Marble Slab ice cream is delicious, but of course the fun part is choosing what you want mixed in - getting real fruit is a treat that can't be beat.  Anything chocolate with raspberries is a sure winner, but kiddos are more likely to go for the multitude of candy available.  I have to admit that gummy bears and ice cream pair surprisingly well!

Seating is very limited, and because the store is small, noisy children will reverberate more than usual.  Luckily eating ice cream lessens their need for talking, at least for a while.  And is anything cuter than faces that have obviously been deliriously happy smearing chocolate from grin-edge to edge??

Be aware they are pricey, so without a coupon, taking several children will amount to a bill larger than you might expect for a treat out, but the flavours make it totally adult-worthy.

Have to admit a few things first....

First, I'm not much of a coffee fan.  I have never in my life thought, "Gee, I'd really like a cup of coffee."  

Second, I'm from Seattle.  Starbucks originated in Seattle.  For me, the bar is set by them.  

Third, after eight years in Canada, this is actually the first time I've ever been in a Tim Hortons.

And lastly .... no, i didn't order any coffee here.  

Okay, having 'fessed up to all that, my visit was fine.  I was told there was a recent renovation, and the setting was pleasant, clean, and comfortable.  The service was speedy and the array of donuts was impressive.  I decided to try the much-advertised new steak and egg on cheddar biscuit.  On TV, the "stack" of steak is promoted, but I found it to be a rather thin layer instead.  And my TV must magnify things, because in person it seemed considerably smaller.  However, the same can be said for a Big Mac, so I won't hold that against them.  It was warm and tasty, but I doubt I'd order it again.  My companions seemed happy with their coffee and steeped tea, which I was told was volcanically hot and didn't become a drinkable temperature until after we had left, so I'm not sure what the allure is to simply sit looking at it while there, but then I don't see the allure of coffee at all, so who am I to judge?

All in all, I feel like visiting a TH can be checked off my Canadian bucket list and doesn't require a second experience.  I do appreciate their involvement in community and youth activities.  And, ok, a last confession .... it never fails to amuse me when my small grandson is asked whether he wants a whole donut or a donut hole.  Long live Timbits!!
One of my favourite donut places to go to great drinks and food very busy on Sat and Sun morinings

First time eating here and ordered a large meat lovers pizza. We received water right away and the waitress was there in a timely fashion to take our order. She was friendly and personable.
We did have to wait what seemed like an extra long time for the pizza to arrive even though the restaurant didn't seem THAT busy. Not a big deal but just wanted to note it.
The pizza arrived fresh & hot and was truly delicious! Has now become my favourite pizza place after being a Royal Pizza fan.
I have no idea what the other food items taste like but we both loved the pizza.

We had Socrates cook up our Christmas dinner complete with all the fixings and 3 pies . One word = AMAZING   . So well organized and packaged for  10 people . No dirty pots and pans and no slaving over the stove and spending the day in the kitchen . Instead we had family visit time on Christmas day while the tin foil trays warmed up in teh oven .
Lots of left overs and a Lemon Meringue Pie that you would absolutely die for . These folks are the best . Helped us carry it all out to the car on Christmas eve and away we went . Love Socrates and their crew are fabulous

Took my daughter and granddaughter for a pedicure and was completely satisfied.  The salon is clean, tools are in sealed packages for each customer, and staff listened to what we wanted and watched our faces, especially the 6 yr old, to see if all was well.  I was impressed with their friendliness and attention to detail, and plan on returning.  Tammy was my technician and I definitely recommend her, but all the ladies seemed very nice and I don't think you could go wrong with anyone.

Prices are reasonable - $25 for a regular pedicure, $45 for a spa pedicure, which included exfoliation and massage of legs as well as feet.

This Tim Hortons on Hebert road in St. Albert is usually a busy one, the drive thru line cuts across the entrance to a gas station right beside it. There is minimal parking around the building, park in the parking lot between the strip mall and Tim Hortons. I went around 10:30 am on Saturday, the service was quick and still had many fresh bakery items to choose. Lots of empty tables to choose from.

I went there once to get my nails done for a friends birthday.
it was terrible, the lady would file around my nails, but she did it too rough, and it was quite painful.
I chose a lavender color, but got Barbie pink. 
the lady also put a few nails on not straight and it was terrible.
a waste of $80

Been coming to Joe's now for over a year and have never been disappointed. Hands down, the best donair I have ever had and I've had a lot of donairs in my day.
Bill, the owner/chef, uses ample amounts of meat, customizes the donairs however you like and are never greasy. Also, ask for the garlic sauce and his special salt if you order french fries. Every order is made fresh right in front of you and doesn't ever disappoint! My favorite donair place of all time!

We ordered the chicken "souvlaki platter" and the "signature burger." The souvlaki platter came with 4 pieces of stale factory-made pitta bread. The chicken was burnt, dry, and lacked any sort of flavour. The greek salad we ordered with it wasn't even greek salad-- just limp lettuce sprinkled with olives and tomato. 
My burger was wet. I don't know how else to describe it-- it was dripping when I picked it up. Also, the burger contained an entire chunk of onion(?). The burger itself had flavour, but the texture was honestly disgusting after I bit into it and the entire thing was *dripping.*
I wouldn't really care about any of this if I had ordered from a fast food restaurant, but this costed close to $40. I thought Socrates was one of the "fine dining" restaurants in St. Albert, but I was wrong lol. I'm pretty shocked with the horrible quality of the food and I'd definitely encourage people to eat anywhere else. There was no care put into the meal, so yeah i'm pretty disappointed :/

These ladies were amazing and gave me exactly  what I wanted which was purple cat style nails but not too long . When I expressed I was worried the purple would be too dark she whipped out a slightly lighter combo and the result is cat eye coloured kitty claws.  STUNNING! Also just so awesome and friendly .I truly felt welcome a a will be back for a pedicure very soon
 Thank you guys! I had.a rough day and you turned it around

We tried Socrates pizza and were really impressed. Tons of toppings, quick and friendly service and lots of leftovers for the next day. 

We had the vegetarian and meat lovers pizza. Both were flavourful and very filling! 

Socrates used to be my go-to place for breakfast but I will definitely be returning for the pizza.

This veterinary clinic was great from the first time I called and walked in. I've seen doctor Amy Kachurowski plenty of times in the last year for infections in the ears and paws, and weight management. She is so patient with my very excitable dog, and informs me of every possible option for medication/future procedures and potential recurring problems. The assistants and receptionists are also very nice and make for a great overall experience.
This is the best pizza I have had in years. Really good pizza best crust. I love it. Good service nice family run restaurant.
They do a good job for being how busy they are in the morning, and if the lineup is ever too big. They will give you your order for free if it takes to long.

Ordered a cake on Friday went to pick it up Sunday and it wasn't even ready. On the top of the cake It appears to be a big piece of white chocolate that says happy birthday on it and the white chocolate piece doesn't even stay on the cake.. And to top it all off the writing for happy birthday is so sloppy. Not worth the amount I paid for this cake. Doesn't look like this place got any better after new management.

Solid breakfast joint. We had eggs Benny on a Sunday afternoon. They had no issues with a few substitutions I made and it was a solid size taste plate of food. 
Coffee refill were quick and plenty. Place is clean and friendly. The rest of the menu looked pretty yummy too. Lots of home cooking dishes. Plenty of parking and easy to access. 
No complaints from me.

Stopped in for a Coffee, I like the place, but the service is pretty sad.  I ordered a couple of coffees and a couple of shots of Bailey's. I noted that we received the tiny 1oz glass, however the waitress was clearly oblivious that a shot is 1.5oz.  I didn't press the issue but its about 6$ a "shot" so I was a bit annoyed.  After we poured our bailey's into our coffees I noticed that one of the shot glasses still had lipstick on it from a previous customer.  That was enough for me.  I pointed out the lipstick, the waitress was polite and apologized and asked if we wanted her to replace it, but I was no longer interested in drinking anything there and asked for my bill.  She at least removed one of the "shots" from the bill, but in the end I paid 12$ for 2 coffees and 2 "shots" of bailey's that we didn't drink. I still tipped her a low 15% which I hated to do because the experience wasn't all her fault.  I can handle slow service and high prices, but it gets to me when I feel taken advantage of (6$ 1oz "shots") and the whole cleanliness thing is the topper. I doubt I'll be back.

Have come in several times and on every occasion found very friendly staff and a very well run restaurant. They are always making sure we are fully satisfied with everything. Always making helpful suggestions and making sure we get the best deal possible. 10/10 will be returning, and will be informing our friends left and right long and wide about how great of a place this is. 

Sincerely, 

A lifelong Wok Box fan.

I don't normally do this, but i've had a number of pretty bad experiences here and want others to know about it.  I get the sense that they're doing whatever they can to make as much money off of you as possible.  Hope you all take the time to read this.... Where to begin...

1) They recommended  their in-house "Vet Diet" Royal Canin pet food (which costs $55 a bag) after belittling Acana (something that has been recommended by many of my friends with the same breed as mine).  Just compare the ingredients on both bags and tell me what you feel more comfortable feeding your dog.  Acana is locally sourced and has all natural ingredients.. I can't even pronounce half the stuff that is in Royal Canin.   It is obvious the clinic gets some back end $$$ from these products they're trying to push.  (They even have 'truth about food' propaganda hand-outs at their front desk justifying all the crap that is in the foods they sell). 

2) I had to bring my dog in for a check up because I noticed some red patches on her belly (apparently fairly normal for my breed and typically goes away and isn't a cause for alarm).  I originally had expected the regular 70 or so dollars for the visit.  Like typical fashion from coming here for a few months, I end up leaving & paying over $300.  The frustrating part about coming here is that they'll tell you what they recommend without telling you the insane costs (markup!!!) on the products/services they charge you with before you leave.  They recommended a special shampoo which was fairly pricey as well as 'Isaderm/gel' for her red patches.  Foolishly, I agreed to purchase these items, when in reality, I am certain polysporin or something much less expensive would've done the trick.  Oh, and the cost for a 15 G tube??..$50!!!  I did some research when I got home and found a website that sells it for just over $20 (and they're probably still making money off of it).  This is the website: https://www.petsdrugmart.ca/ProductInfo/3247/Fuciderm-Gel 

And the straw that broke the camels back, why i'll NEVER be returning, and making sure I let as many friends as possible know about my experience:

3)I had to bring my puppy in to get some pre-blood work before her spay procedure.  The blood work came back with high enzymes indicating a possible liver issue.  So they wanted to run some additional tests (a liver bile test).  Obviously extremely stressful and worried about my pup I really had no choice but to get this done ($200+).  So I book the appointment for September 2nd in the morning.  The receptionist on the phone said I can have her dropped off by 8:20 at the earliest.  Since I worked that day, I came right in the morning at said time.  Apparently they don't open until 8:30, so not sure why they mentioned 8:20.  Anyhow, after the doors open, I bring her in and the receptionist asks her name and I tell her.  She looks confused and says "we don't have you booked in until 10".  Which is odd, because 10:00 was never even brought up or talked about when I booked the appointment.  So she offers for me to come back, which I am reluctant about since you know, I have to work and what not.  She then says they can get me in.  So I end up waiting around about another 30-40 mins from what I originally intended.  They take her in and I'm relieved that I can get back in time to start working.   They say she'll be ready to pick up in a few hours.  (With this particular test, you need to fast the pup for 12 hours, they take blood when you drop her off, feed her a fatty meal and then take blood again to compare the results).  I receive a phone call a few hours later, as expected, HOWEVER... they call to tell me that THEY LOST THE INITIAL BLOOD WORK..and that she'll have to come back another day for the procedure. My heart sank.  I was/am extremely disappointed in them and more importantly, felt so bad for my puppy who was stressed out enough having to go through all this and get blood drawn for absolutely no reason. 

Needless to say, I had them print off my pups paper work and I will NOT be returning.

I've been here numerous times and the service is always very friendly and reasonably priced, $30 for a shellac manicure.  However, I've found the service to be unprofessional at times. I stopped in one day and they were quite busy so I made an appointment for the next morning.  When I arrived the next day the salon was closed and the sign revealed that they did not open for 2 HOURS after my scheduled appointment.  I returned 2 hours later (unfortunately I really needed my nails done) and when I told them what had happened, the two ladies just laughed and didn't even apologize for their mix-up....

I don't live far but it was still an inconvenience and I left the salon quite annoyed at their reaction to the situation.  Other times I have made an appointment and when I arrive at the scheduled time I can see that they have just started walk-in customers and I've had to wait 15-30 minutes despite having an appointment.  Overall decent salon, but don't bother with appointments.

We went to this local restaurant today for dinner we want it to try it as we always drive by it. What a waste of money the place looks old, the menus look ok we found the food was not tasteful at all we spend $120 for 4 of us but the food was not worth the price I order fettucini alfredo with chicken it look like soup and salty I could not eat it. My children order a hamburger and fries and steak only took one bite each and they were upset my husband order the salmon it look dry and old. I mention this to the waitress but she look at me like I was crazy. I will never eat there again it was by far the worst waste of money I'm so upset.

Ordered two medium pizzas for take out.  On-line menu showed $15.95 and $16.95 each.  When I arrived for pickup, I was charged $42.00.  When I mentioned the discrepancy, I was told that I may have been looking at the website and menu of another Capital pizza; they are all independently owned and prices may vary.  When the pizzas were brought out, they were in 9" boxes.  I again mentioned that there was a mistake, I ordered mediums, these were smalls.  (BTW their menus don't have smalls, just medium and large).  Nope, I was told that 9" was indeed a medium size.  I was hungry, so I took them and left.  So......for $42.00 at Capital Steak and Pizza, you get 2 - 9" pizzas.  It was a tasty product, but for that price, I'll have a steak and a glass of wine.  Definitely not worth my repeat business

Expensive and bad food are the best descriptiors I can provide.  I used to run with groups at the Running Room next door and saw that this place was always busy, I took that as a good sign, I was wrong.  I convinced my wife and kids to try this place, with an intent to try something new.  None of us finished what was on our plates.  I don't see us ever going back and I don't recommend trying this location.  The servers were nice enough, the food was sub-par and way overpriced.

I can't remember a time when this Second Cup didn't exist.  I love it here.  I agree with the other reviews that say the patio is not in a good position... but at least they have a patio!

There are so many windows that it's always filled with natural light.  The drinks are always made perfectly and to whatever specifications your little heart desires.

Now... the real shining stars at this location.  THE STAFF.  They are super amazing.  Very friendly and they clearly love their jobs.  They never seem annoyed or overwhelmed.  They are there to make you your beverage, and maybe chat a little.  

There are never boxes of unpacked product hanging around, clogging things up.  Which is a complaint that I often have at other locations.

Although I'm sad that we only have 1 Second Cup left in town, I'm glad that this location is so inviting.

This is an excellent fish and chips joint! I like the seating, temperature and ambient environment. 

Apparently, the place went under a management change and the service is much better and improved from before! 

I had the halibut and chips with calimari. Calimari was delicious, one of the best I've had! Fish and batter were fried to perfection - crispy, just how I like it!

Worth checking out!

order- two super donairs
-phone order taker polite, easy to order
-delivery guy was fast and nice
-donairs could use a little more "stuff" (tomato) but they were really very good and I'm picky about donairs
-value good (but the bill confused me..lol)
complaint..when you send donairs to anyone especially a motel, send napkins!!
I want to try this place again.

Ordered delivery twice now. Lasagna both times. The first time I had no sauce on it. It was just gross noodles. The second time it was all sauce an cheese, no pasta. I do enjoy the wings but honestly, wings aren't rocket science. Meh

LOVE love LOVE this library!

For a small town library, it totally rocks!  The kids area is great - complete with a Arthurian tent to phone a mystery phone recording on, a wooden bus you can sit on with your kids, and plenty of natural light.

They have a phenomenal summer reading program for kiddos!  

The adult sections are pretty good and if they don't have what you want they can order it in from another library.

I love how it's conveniently located in City Hall.  It's nice to stop in for a break from the Farmer's Market on a hot summer's day.

There is a beautiful winding staircase to the second level or an elevator if you prefer - my toddler likes to do both, severl times, every visit!

The only thing that would make this library better is if the memberships were free - I mean come on St. Albert, the taxes are HIGH enough to warrant a free library membership :-)
Simply best donuts in St Albert and perhaps all of the Edmonton area. Always super nice service and great selection if you get their early!

Great seafood place to eat out 
Great service and ambiance.
Loved it
New owners bought a great change overnight.

Stay far far away. This place was good at one time but it has turned into the restaurant from hell. Place is downright filthy. I have no idea how this place isn't  closed by the health board. 

Food sucks, I couldn't  get past the smell to actually eat it.
So its closed now. Had great food but very poorly run. What a shame

So don't get me wrong, but Royal Pizza has the best pizza ever. We used to order it constantly from their old location, but it closed a while back. We were extatic that it re-opened.  The first time we ordered from the new location, we found a hair in the pizza.  Then of course gave them a second chance....our order was completely wrong and the pizza was falling apart and in peices.  The manager was so great and very helpful, thoughtful and apologetic.  He told us that we would get a free pizza next time we order. We though, hey sure that sounds great.  So we orderd for the third time, they looked us up to see what our deal was, and magically it changed to only 20 % off our next pizza.   We ended our St. Albert Royal Pizza relationship there.  :(

I might be a touch biased since growing up this was my family's go-to "we're not cooking tonight" order-in dinner, every couple of weeks or so. I can't hate on family tradition, especially a family tradition this tasty.

I can't think of anything from the menu I've tried and haven't liked. Spring rolls, chicken balls, and ginger beef are a few of my favs, but the sweet and sour pork also ranks right up there. Even the rice is super yummy.

They've never gotten our order wrong, and nothing has been colder than super hot. They always throw in however many fortune cookies we ask for, and often each cookie has more than one fortune - that just means extra lottery numbers for my dad.

45 minutes late.
Order all screwed up
Not edible.
Deep fried wonton changed to wonton "soup" quotation marks used because pasty no meat wonton in hot water is not soup.
Fried rice was white with barely any chicken, did not smell or taste right, one mouthfull was more then enough
Spring rills no sauce, nothing to spring about, just deep fries flour stuff.
Almound soo guy just horrible, processed  chicken???
Chop suey seemed ok.

And we are done!  Never again.

Nice organized store
But they really need to carry more sizes
I couldn't find a nice top piece in a large and they had no stock in the back
Sucked!

Nitzas was a family favorite since I was a kid- since the new owners took over a few years ago it has been awful. Every single time I have ordered delivery it has been over an hour and 45 minutes to come (once was 2 hrs and ten mins on a Wednesday and the pizza clearly had been sitting under a heat lamp the entire time- completely dried out and disgusting). Owner offered to "get hs next time" and the next time I called they refused to honor it and said they have nothing there.  Out of the last six orders, five times my order has come completely wrong. Another important note is that the pizza there is not even subpar anymore- always cold and old tasting. Will never eat here again...

This is my favorite coffee house in St.Albert..
The new owner Tina has done great things with this place. The staff and patrons are very pleasant and personable, and of course the coffee and food is great!

Great experience!  Staff member asks what you are looking for and then starts pulling suits that she thinks will work for you.  You just hang out in the change room while she brings you suggestions.  They provide honest feedback, which I really appreciate.  I wish they had more cover-ups but, honestly, the bathing suit selection is the best in the Edmonton area and so I'm not complaining.  I'm grateful!

While visiting friends in St. Albert we decided to check it out.

I don't usually write these, but the horrible food and lack of service has compelled me to warn other people about this restaurant.

The food was cold and taste like it was full of nothing but MSG. The vegetables were Discoloured and some of the beef strips were still RAW!....This is completely unacceptable and has potential to give someone food poisoning.

Not only was the food sub-par but our waiter was rude and obnoxious. We asked about the discolouration and about the meat but was informed that this is how it is made. Since I am Chinese myself and travel to Hong Kong on a yearly basis I know this is NOT how it is suppose to be prepared.

If I could give 0 stars I would but unfortunately I have to give a 1.
Had pizza twice here and would not order it from there ever again. My only complaint is that they hardly put any friggin toppings on. The pizza isn't cheap either. I would rather have panago.
Best donuts!! My brother picked up a dozen for our road trip. 2 hours in, 5 people, only 3 donuts left.

Had a really weird girl serve us last week. She gave me strange looks and had a weird attitude. Even my boyfriend commented when we left. The quality of the baked goods is consistent across the different locations but service here was interesting and not someplace I would go back for.

We are British, so we know a good fish and chip shop.  This is not one of them.  We both had the cod.  There was not much cod, and lots of batter.  
However, the batter was good.  As good as any English one, although slightly on the greasy side.  
My husband had the mushy peas.  He said they were horrible.  They look like they had been microwaved (yuk!)
restaurant was clean 
Not busy

I finally made it here.  I haven't actually tried anything that I purchased yet, so this review is stictly on the service we received.  

I think they would do well to invest in one of those pull number do-hickeys that you see in delis and bakeries.  More than once somebody behind the counter would say "I don't know who's next".  But once you got through that, the service was great.  The girl serving us was very knowledgeable and helpful.  I can't wait to get into the goodies I picked up.

I have shopped here twice now and both times I have been thoroughly impressed with the service and the selection of swimsuits and beachwear offered for the entire family. The sales staff are knowledgeable, friendly and very hard working. It is obvious that their mission is to please the customer, whatever the age or body type.

This store offers the nicest selection of swimwear that I have seen anywhere in the Edmonton area. Chic, adorable and comfortable swimsuits! It just doesn't get any better than this! Everything from one piece suits, tankinis, bikinis, and monokinis for women. There are styles that simply complement every figure type. I found the perfect beach items for my vacation!

The guy was working the till and hand pressing the pizza dough without first washing his hands.

I just read an article on the widespread ADHD in recent years, and here's an extract that I quote:

"Avoid all paper receipts. Most have BPA or BPS (bisphenol S); they have the same effect. You don't absorb BPA/BPS through the skin. However, if you get it on your hands and then touch your mouth or food--bingo! -- you get 1,000 times the dose that you'd get from food or drink packaged in plastic."

My understanding of why they are popular is because they buy customers by giving relatively tiny sums of money for the publicity they get, to Bellerose School, as seen on photos on their wall.

So it seems the students of Bellerose and their friends and family patronise this place and pay a hefty price for it! Makes me wonder what the ADHD numbers are at Bellerose.

AMAZING pizza!

Nitza's will cost you more than the big chains like Pizza 73 but their tatste and freshness is amazing!  Their price would compare to Panago's.

The best Donair pizza in the world and it's NEVER greasy!  Their wings are delicious and they serve up some mean souvlaki and calamari if that's your thing!

I don't know the owner's name but he is super friendly and always greets you with a smile!  They have a slurpee machine and if you pick up your order you get a free slurpee or bottle of water - and I can assure you we take advantage of that!

And if your'e simply craving a slurpee with your pizza, they will deliver a slurpee to you!

FYI - Their pizza sizes are smaller than most... So an XL at Nitza's is like a Large elsewhere. 

Hands down the freshest and most delicious pizza available in St. Albert!  I tell everyone about this place and I hope you will give it a try!

I have fond memories of walking to Nitza's at lunch in high school...  And now that I'm back in town, it was one of the first places I needed to check out.

I've gotten delivery a couple of times now and haven't had any issues with order accuracy yet.  It's always very fast as well.

I love how cheesy their pizzas are. 

I recently got to introduce my co-workers to Nitza's and everyone was pretty impressed!!

Sublime is where I buy most of my swimsuits. I'm a South Side girl and Sublime is all the way in St. Albert, but it's worth the trip. (OK, full disclosure - my parents live in St. A, so every bathing suit shopping trip ends in a home cooked meal, too!)

This store carries all the popular brands (Roxy and the other surfer-y brands) and tons of other swimwear lines I'm less familiar with, too. I'm a hater of two piece bathing suits that are only sold together (I'm not the same size on top and bottom - who is?) but I found tons of separate mix-and-match type pieces I was really happy with last time I was in. Bonus points: the staff were really helpful. No, I'm not kidding, ladies - I had a really enjoyable swimsuit shopping experience. It exists!

One of my fav parts of Sublime is the ad campaign they had a couple of years ago featuring local women from St. Albert of ALL shapes and sizes modeling their products. Girl power!

I love this store. Although the bathing suits are pricy, you are getting high quality suits. The ladies working here are very helpful as they help you choose swim suits that will you flatter you and still stick with your style. I went to Mexico with my bathing suit and most of the time I walked around with the bathing suit strapless and also went swimming in the ocean with big waves. I didn't have to worry about the suit falling down because they helped me choose the perfect size and also because the bathing suits are such good quality.

Was house-sitting in St. Albert and our original plan for dinner had fallen through, so I looked online for a decent pizza place that delivers, and Nitza's kept coming up, so we decided to try it. They do a 2-for-1 which is awesome, but like the other review said, their pizza sizes are misleading (M = 10", L = 12", XL = 14" - they should really just rename them S, M, L).

We ordered a 'special pepperoni' pizza (special pepperoni sausage (which when I asked, turned out to be the same as their regular pepperoni), asiago, green peppers, mushrooms), and a donair pizza (donair beef, mushrooms, onions, fresh tomato slices, slathered with donair sauce) since it seems to come highly recommended from many other reviewers. Both come with mozzarella as well. I asked if they have a garlic dipping sauce but they only had tzatziki, so I ordered that as a side. The lady on the phone was really nice and actually called me back to clarify if I had wanted the tzatziki sauce on the whole pizza, half, or the side. 

Delivery took the shorter end of the 30-45 minutes that she had told me, which was great. The crust is a regular crust (not thin, but not super thick either), not fantastic but held up the toppings well. I couldn't identify any asiago cheese on the special pepperoni pizza, but it was was still tasty - lots of large slices of pepperoni, real sliced and cooked mushrooms, and cubed green pepper that was neither under nor overcooked. And the cheese was melted just the way I like it - a little bit brown on the edges (I dislike undercooked pizza, where the mozzarella looks white and barely melted - although I find that with better quality pizzas, the cheese can be white and still melted and gooey). The donair pizza was completely slathered in a white, sweet donair sauce, and had a fresh tomato slice on each slice of pizza. The beef was tasty and the onions tasted like they had been caramelized (which I love). Didn't notice the mushrooms? Overall a tasty pizza but there wasn't as much donair beef as expected. The tzatziki sauce was excellent - thick, fresh and creamy with dill in it.

Total came to around $37 - I think the 2-for-1 pizzas were $32 each, and the tzatziki was $2 and there was another $2 service charge. Enough food for dinner for two and leftovers for both our lunches the next day. They do accept credit cards. I'd be interested in trying out their other Greek offerings due to the tzatziki being so good!
Been a family staple for as long as I can remember. Always good pizza made fresh and quickly.

Royal used to be good. Now it's not.
Seriously, Tzatziki  sauce on a donair pizza? PA-YUKE! Never again. Over priced and poor pizza.
PUKE!

This place was so busy! People were coming in non-stop while my wife and I were there. The pizza was great! We got the Donair and Greek Popeye pizzas and loved both of them. The pizzas had mountains of toppings and is worth every penny. You can't get a better deal for pizza then at this place (2 for 1)!We plan on going here again.

Oh Nitzas you are an institution in St Albert. Even way before I lived here I came for pizza or after a night at the crown you were there for me. Our company in Edmonton would drive out for pizza if we needed some for overtime employees. All in all you are amazing. The prices arent bad and the food is great!

I ordered their 3 for 1 pizza, one just cheese, another donair and another beef & mushroom.
(3 for 1 comes with 2 toppings)
The lady said , so just donair meat & sauce on the pizza? I asked her to add tomatoes. She told me she can't do that, I said well the cheese pizza doesn't have any toppings. she said cheese is considered a topping (really??? It's not considered a topping on the others) I asked her to put the one topping from the cheese to the donair pizza. Can't do that she said - if she did it for me, she'd have to do it for everyone. Yes - that's called good customer service. I let it go. Pizza arrives for my kid's after school pizza party. 
Terrible experience. 
Pizza was okay - not great. You

The donair pizza is delicious, and I love the people working there!  Even if I buy just one pizza, they give all four of my kids a slushee.  How nice is that?  Not much on ambiance, but I'm getting the pie to go, anyway.

Nitza's is always our first choice for pizza!

I moved from St.Albert around 8 years ago into Edmonton's Whyte Avenue area which is littered with tiny donair and pizza shops. Not one of these compare in taste and quality to the divine and exquisite awesomeness that is a Nitzas donair. The pita is always soft and fresh, they don't over stuff with donair meat so the flavours of the sauce and cheese are pronounced and they don't put on lettuce unless requested which is the way a donair should be. I have never understood this lettuce idea. Speaking of the sauce, the homemade donair sauce is perfect in consistency and flavour. An excellent sweetness which isn't to runny or to thick and will leave you craving more. The pizza as well is some of the best I've ever had, but of course everyone is the most knowledgable critic in the world when it comes to pizza. It's a medium crust which is fresh light and tasty and never overdone. The toppings and cheese are the perfect amount and of the highest quality. I really recommend the do air pizza and the simple but always satisfying pepperoni and mushroom, with a side of donair sauce for dipping. The jalapeño poppers are fantastic as well as is the ceaser salad and the simple but lovely cheese toast. If you are in either St.Albert or Sherwood Park, and are craving a pizza or donair, Nitzas is the place you want.

Horrible experience for my daughter's tenth birthday party.  Paid for 1 hour of bowling and one hour of table with pizza and pop.  Lost almost half bowling time because of ball jams.  Staff kept accusing our group of jamming the balls due to their equipment malfunctions.  Was promised more time because of this however were never given this time.  When questioned about it they said they couldn't because the lanes were changing over, however they allowed the people beside us to start a new game.  Told us maybe they could find us another lane.  kids barely finished their game before they shut it down.  Brought food out before we were done bowling and didn't even tell us.  So for $166 we received a half hour of bowling and cold pizza with watered down drinks.  Emailed the establishment to state my concerns and again was basically accused of jamming it ourselves.  Offered me a free game to compensate.  meanwhile this was supposed to be a memorable time for my daughter as it was her birthday celebration.  Please don't waste your money at this establishment.  Staff are rude and roll their eyes at you when you voice a problem or concern.  Don't waste your time making these people do their job that they are paid to do.  Will not return to this establishment anytime soon that is for sure.
Ive been here twice. Lots of selection. My daughter loves the decorated cookies. The service was great.

The donuts here are awesome especially when there fresh early in the morning, but the good stuff goes fast so you gotta be here early! The cinnamon cindys are amazing also cant go wrong with just an old school chocolate dipped donut!! Ive also tried a few of the danishes before and found them above average.

Grandin Bakery located across from Target & in same parking lot as Safeway (previously located in Grandin) is a fabulous local bakery!

My kiddos love coming in here and picking out a special cookie or treat!  They have a phenomenal array of themed cupcakes if you are looking for a birthday treat and do custom orders as well.

This past summer, I placed a order for 250 top cut buns for a charity Cookoff (as recommended by D'arcy's Meats) & they were fabulous!  They even let me borrow the bingos to transport the 250 buns!

My daughter's preschool always requested baked treats from Grandin Bakery because they are also a trusted source to do but free baking!

If you haven't checked then out, you need to stop in!

PS - they are closed on Sundays.

The location is prime for this swim wear shop to sustain itself year-round, it shares a row of the strip mall including a cruise travel agency. Smart planning there for sure! 

They have a great selection mainly from Canada, the US and Australia. They pride themselves as being able to sell swim suits that fit any body. Though not the main feature, they do offer familiar boarder suits and shirts including Roxy and Point Zero. The purchase counter is glass and features a selection of interesting jewelry.

Popped in to grab some treats while in the area, and was pleasantly surprised to see it wasn't busy and there were still lots of goodies left.

I've tried their pies and have been happy. Flaky shells, delicious fillings and pretty decent prices. I would pass on their cookies since I think there are better ones out there, but that's because I like my cookies soft and chewy and these lean towards the crunchy, cakier side. Donuts are a good option, as are the vanilla squares. 

Service is always friendly. Today they had a couple of young looking teens working out front and they were very pleasant.

I like stopping in if I'm in the area, but it's not somewhere I go out if my way to get to.

How has it already been 7 years since I last reviewed this location?!?

This is still my kids' favourite for their cinnamon bread.  Come early - it sells out.  They'll slice it how you like and it's so soft, good.  Use it for a snack, toasted with butter, or make French toast - OH.EM.GEE.

The scones here are also a favourite in my household.

They do seasonal breads and treats as well.

If you haven't every bought bread baked fresh at a bakery, you are missing out!

After figuring out that the Grandin Bakery is no longer in Grandin but rather by the St. Albert Centre Mall, we finally made a visit to try their baked goods!  

They had cute cookies and cupcakes - everything to melt a toddler's heart.  As an adult, however, I wasn't overly impressed with a few of the fancier cookies/pastries we picked up.

I'd definitely stop in again when I have my toddler in tote for a treat but I don't think it will replace my usual haunts for baked goods.

they have beautiful swim suits suitable for all woman n guys too i guess, the customer service its outstanding, i went last month n was there for more than an hour trying swim suits, the lady that helped me was patient, honest with her opinions and helped me so much choosing the perfect suit, she literally kept on bringing more n more suits until i was happy, also they had a sale when i went so instead of getting only one top i got 2 cz one of them was from 170 to 70 dollars, they have a huge variety, check them out

Went here tonight for a family birthday party. There were about 20-25 of us, including little ones. My cousin arranged everything, including booking the lanes and the party room and ordering the food. We had five lanes reserved for about an hour and a half, which included shoe rental. We then used one of the party rooms for a couple of hours afterwards.

The guy at the shoe counter was really nice. The place was pretty busy; it looked like almost all of the lanes were full, and we got there at 4pm. 

The only real problem we had was with our lane. For some reason, on two occasions, all of our balls would be used up and just wouldn't come back out. We got a staff member to get them out for us and he was helpful and energetic. 

The glow-bowling was fun. They brought out this weird contraption to make it easier for the little kids to roll the ball, which I thought was sweet. The noise level was pretty loud. Just a culmination of the balls, pins, so many people and kinda loud music. 

We had pizza, which is provided by the bowling alley, and I unfortunately have to say that it was probably the worst pizza I've ever had. I feel bad saying that, because this seems like a nice place, but it was just gross. They have a menu some other stuff on it - I briefly glanced at it and saw nachos, popcorn, wings, etc., and your standard candy and chips. 

I feel kinda bad giving only 2 stars - this seems like a fun place with good staff and I would probably go here if I lived in St. Albert. I would just not order pizza and hopefully would not have any issues with my lane. They have 5- and 10-pin bowling, glow bowling, and apparently mini golf, too!

I love this place. First off it has always been a great place for an after bar pizza. On top of that I learned it is a great place for a pizza any night. Also they are good and slamming together a bunch of pies for big occasions. If you want a pizza that isnt from a big named pizza joint give Nitzas a try.

The food here is really good! And I love the "non-fussy" atmosphere, its a nice place to spend a Friday night. 

Everything on the menu is really delicious. Although, the service can be a little slow at time. But overall its pretty good value for money.

Okay, I heard some hype about this place so I thought I'd stop in. It's a tiny bakery and the bread looks as though it came out of a domestic bread making machine. It smelled like burnt raisins - not one of my favourite scents. The breads and baked goods did look appetizing but the staff weren't too interested in answering questions. They seem to do fairly well, several people came in, ordered, and left. That seems to be what kind of place it is.

This is an awesome Second Cup. 

I love the layout of the tables and chairs, no matter where you sit it always feels cozy. This is a great location for studying, meeting with friends, or just going to do the crossword puzzle. The drinks are always made to perfection and the staff don't roll their eyes when you make special requests or double check that they used sugar free syrup. The staff are definitely a highlight here as they are unusually helpful for a coffee shop and very friendly. My favorite summer drink is the Italian Soda! 

I agree that the outside patio is not ideal. It is in an awkward space and sometimes you are breathing in exhaust fumes when you want to be enjoying the sunshine.

However that drive thru does come in handy when you just finished at the gym and don't want to go inside all sweaty!

Eeek!  Ants crawling on the wall next to me and curtains on the windows splattered in food and fly speck.  Flies in the cool/cold food area buffet :-(

Some items were okay and others were the worst I have had :-( specifically the wontons tastes like dish water broth.  The beef in the beef and broccoli had a texture unlike anything I've had before although the broccoli was juicy and crisp! I also would not recommend the hot and sour soup which had so much gelatin in it and was hard to scoop.  The spicy chicken was okay and both the rice and noodles were a hit with my kiddos.  The stir fried veggies and fried mushroom were pretty good.  The pork skewers were probably my favorite.  The spring rolls were disappointing filled with mostly noodles.

Our plates were slow to be cleared and my water wasn't refilled.

I wish I could say it looked like an off night and we would try again but given the dirty walls behind the buffet and filthy window blinds, I'm afraid we just won't be giving this one a try again.

The breakfast is decent and pretty big for under $5. I will say to stay away from the hashbrowns which is unfortunate cuz that's sometimes the best part of breakfast. I think you can sub it for tomatoes or pancakes.

The previous day I had dinner there and none of the food looked very pleasant. They tried to force the buffet on me but I have a rule against eating from a trough so I ordered a one person combo plate. It came with fried rice and 3 meat/vege dishes. Maybe I should have gone with the buffet since when the owner/server brought out my dish she stopped off and dished some buffet food onto my plate.

The decor is probably the same stuff from the 80's and some chairs had armrests while others did not. :( I don't know of any other Chinese in St Albert but I would chose them over this place.

Second cup will always be one of my favourite coffee houses, I used to work there and I know how everything is made. I have no problem with the coffee, or there food. But since there has been new management and all of the old girls quit, it hasn't been the same for me. They really knew what they were doing, and I know that it takes time to learn everything, believe me- but twice in the last two months, going through the drive through and trying to redeem free drinks has mysteriously taken 500 points off of my app each time. I know the glitch, I know how it happens, and both times the girl in the window has tried explaining to me something that makes absolutely no sense, just talking away trying to confuse me. When I have 1200 points, and I want to redeem 1000 on two drinks, and you scan my card 3 times to try to get them and then tell me I can only redeem 1 because I don't have enough points- I know that you didn't click on the drink before clicking on 'redeem free drink'. I'm sorry, but the new girls need to be trained a bit better in customer service and fixing their mistakes.

YUM! Pizza is big competition in this suburb and so far I have to say that Royal Pizza is a clear winner in my books. 

I've heard good things about the local (Edmonton) chain in the past but hadn't tried it. My soy allergy prevents me from enjoying many of the chain pizzas and so far several of the locals I've tried. Hoping for a positive change but still wanting to satisfy my craving, I took a chance.

The entire experience was great. They have a good selection of toppings, the price is reasonable, the delivery time as promised (about half an hour). 

I ordered a 10" (med) lean beef and mushroom pizza. The crust was golden and cooked to perfection, the cheese had a baked appearance and the beef was certainly ground - no globs of burnt stuff like some I've had. The sauce had the right amount of tang and the mushrooms just the right compliment. 

I think I may have finally found a favourite pizza place to order from in St. Albert. Thank you, Royal Pizza.

Unfortunately, my love for Nitza's Pizza has started to wane.

We've probably ordered pizza a dozen or so times from here over the past year.

If we pick it up, it's okay because I can review the order but about 50% of the time when delivered - something is wrong.

Last time they left off an ingredient.  They wanted to offer me an ingredient for free next time but no.  My jalapeno pineapple pizza missing jalapeno is just not yummy.

Another time the donair sauce got left off the donair pizza?!?  They brought me donair sauce 45 minutes later but by then the pizza is cold.

Why wouldn't you just make me a new pizza?  

Ugh... Their donair pizza is still delicious and I highly recommend a bacon, jalapeno, pineapple pizza... but only if you get all the ingredients at once while it's hot.

I'm more upset than anyone in here finally it was my friends turn to pay for a meal and  we ended up in this crap hole of golden dynasty  I understand people have to make a living,  but not by poisoning customers with a kilo of salt !!! Every tray was just warm. no free re-fills of any kind not to mention the food that was stuck on the walls from who knows when!! Don't waste your time or money I wish I would've never find this place for f*%# sakes

I ordered their 3 for 1 pizza, one just cheese, another donair and another beef & mushroom.
(3 for 1 comes with 2 toppings)
The lady said , so just donair meat & sauce on the pizza? I asked her to add tomatoes. She told me she can't do that, I said well the cheese pizza doesn't have any toppings. she said cheese is considered a topping (really??? It's not considered a topping on the others) I asked her to put the one topping from the cheese to the donair pizza. Can't do that she said - if she did it for me, she'd have to do it for everyone. Yes - that's called good customer service. I let it go. Pizza arrives for my kid's after school pizza party. Driver takes cash - doesn't give my son any change and takes almost $10 tip for himself. Really!!!!????
Terrible experience. 
Pizza was okay - not great.

My family and I regularly purchase our bread and baked treats from Cobs.  We've been coming to this location on a weekly basis for nearly a year now.

Our favorites include Cinnamon Bread (without raisins...) - my toddler calls it Picnic Bread and loves to eat it plain as a snack.  It's quite good toasted with butter of course, too!  (This loaf is just under $5)

We also LOVE the Pane di Case loaf!  So good plain or with the kalamata olives in it!  (The plain Pane di Case is around $4 and the one with kalamatas is slightly higher in price and slightly smaller in size).

We first discovered the Pane di Case when I asked for their recommendation for a great panini bread.  It's also excellent with a scramble for breakfast! The kalamata olive loaf is also excellent for panini goodness - but you pretty much need to make 2 panini sandwiches with this one because it is smaller than the plain version.

We also love their scones - they have a variety that varies day to day.  Our favorites are the Apple Caramel and chocolate chip banana!   They also regularly have chocolate chip, cinnamon, raspberry white chocolate... Mmm... I think I need to go have one now!  (If I'm remembering correctly... scones are $1.80 each or sold at a better price in multiples of 4 or 6).

They make delicious croissants - ham and cheese, spinach and feta, chocolate!  They are a little pricey ranging from $2.50-$2.85 but oh so yummy!

And of course they have danishes, cinnamon rolls, buns and bread galore!  All made fresh daily!

First off I need to admit to y'all that I'm a Starbucks girl through and through (born and Seattle raised and transplanted to Canada about 14 years ago).

Phew, okay.. Now onto Second Cup.

This location has friendly staff, an efficient drive through, and they even give you free copies of the Newspaper!

Lots of glass windows for natural light if you'd like to have your coffee inside and an overall pleasant atmosphere.

Also if you are going to be a regular be sure to download their smartphone app so you can collect points towards free drinks and even receive special offers.  The app is kinda cute in that when you make a purchase it fills a coffee cup with drips of coffee :-)

Stay Calm and Coffee On!

Ah, the St. Albert Bowling Centre. The site of so many awkward high school dates and birthday parties. Memories, sigh.

When you're the only bowling alley in town, you don't need to be fancy. I'm almost positive that's the mindset of the owners of this place. The employees are often local high school kids, making their way through their first after-school job.

It's actually quite big, but when the scoring machines break frequently, that isn't a pro, because it can take a while for the staff to come over.

The food isn't very good, but at least they have beer running on tap. And if you book in advance, you can have your own private room for food, hang outs, and jackets.

A friend accidentally walked out with a pair of bowling shoes from here once. I would be surprised if the staff ever noticed.

All I can say is just DON'T! Congealed layer on the barely lukewarm hot and sour soup. Almost no beef in the beef and vegetable dish and every single dish in the "hot" trays was only slightly warmer than room temperature. Totally unappetizing.

My friend is always raving about this bakery so when I needed a cake for my son's party I thought I'd give them a try.

There is lots of parking out front bit the parking lot is busy. Staff were super friendly.  My son wanted a Terraria themed caked. They had never made one before but we're happy to give it a try. I gave them free raign with the decorations other then that. The cake was light and fluffy with 3 layers. Unfortunately the icing was wayyyyy to sweet. One kids said he never says no to cake and had to through 3/4 of his piece in the garbage. 

The cake itself was about $40. To feed about 16-20 people. I thought the cake looked pretty cool but my picky son said that some of the details were wrong. Whut wah.

We also picked up hamburger buns for a bbq we're having on Sunday. The buns are super soft and just the right size. I hate buns that are so big you can't even taste your meat.

Also the donuts are pretty great. Light and fluffy. My favorite is the sugar glazed but if you don't go early on Saturday you'll miss out.

The food lacked flavour. I bought the family of four meal, with a side of satay beef. the sweet and sour pork, lemon chickn, and ginger beef all lacked flavor (minus the sauce). However the rice was OK. Not worth $60. I won't be going back. The "chinese food" they have at Safeway around the corner is better quality.

First time ordering. 
Called and asked if they delivered to the Garrison (which they do) because Goggle said it was the closest to us. Unfortunately because they were so busy - the young lady gave me a delivery time of 90 minutes! It was explained cause they were in fact very busy and wants to give ample time for the delivery guy, in case he didn't know the area. We didn't care - followed raves from both YELP and other members on the base and so we could wait.
Pizza arrived in 1 hr 43 minutes and was still surprisingly hot. The pizza reminded the family  of an old pizza joint back home, where toppings are stacked high and the cheese is on top! 

Pizza was worth the wait - HOWEVER ..... delivery time needs to be addressed and $60 for two pizza's ??

I have been on a search for the best burger and the best pizza. I was introduced to Royal Pizza in December 2011. Two things are the basis of a good pizza, the crust and the sauce. Toppings are individual but if the first two are bad then the pizza will be bad. Royal Pizza is in my top 5 and I've eaten a lot of pizza in my lifetime. My favourite is pepperoni and pineapple. I drive from NW Edmonton to St. Albert to get takeout (it's the closest). I love this pizza and highly recommend it to all.

A great family owned and operated pizzeria - with a splash of donairs, pasta, and slushes. The current owner took over the business after his father passed away. The pizzeria is very involved in their local community with sponsorships of various volunteer events. 

My brother-in-law took us there. We were a family of three adults and five kids. The interior was pretty basic but you can tell they are used to accommodating big groups so we easily had seating room amongst the table and chairs. Seemed like an ideal place to have a sports team outing. 

All pizza are 2 for 1 and very affordable. So it's a good deal.  We had a Donair and a Vegetarian's Nightmare pizza.  The kids received slushes as well.  The pizza crust was good - moist, crunchy, and tasty. The donair pizza was unique - good helping of meat and a LOT of their homemade donair sauce. The Vegetarian Nightmare was loaded with meat - but didn't feel excessively greasy. 

The owner was very friendly and the staff extremely accommodating - helping out with hot sauce, parm, and chilli flake extras. Next time you are thinking about ordering from Pizza Hut or Panago, I would recommend giving these guys a try.  

We love supporting locally owned and operated businesses - and will definitely be back. Five stars  as a recommendation for you to try it.

We love coming here on weekend nights for neon bowling, which is two hours of neon bowling on Friday or Saturday nights after 10:00 PM for like $17 plus tax.

There is a games room here to kill time if you arrive early, and a full bar with highballs and pitchers of beer to take with you to your table.

The place is a tad outdated but that just adds to the appeal for me. It's a bowling alley. The only two complaints we would have is that las night when we went for neon bowling they have switched to music videos on big screens above the lanes with the songs they play. Cool in theory, but they literally had twelve songs/ videos they rotated through repeatedly. Hearing the same songs 3 or 4 times during your two hours of bowling is irritating.

As well, eat before you come. The food here is reasonably priced but awful. It's deep fried fast food you would expect from a bowling alley. Take a pass on it.

All in all we have a pretty damn good bowling alley in our city, check it out!

We have eaten here many times over the past years and never had a problem with the food or the service  we travel a hour and a half just to eat here because we love there food.  We have had other Chinese buffets that were Not as good as this one.  They are my favourite   Took a friend with us and she really enjoyed it as well. Thanks again fir the great food and service

As the only bowling alley in the area, this place has not changed since the early nineties. The machines, bowling balls and chairs/tables are a tribute to my childhood. 

We had a few drinks which were pretty steep in price for a bottle of beer ($6.75) and there was visible dust on the bottles. I guess not many people order a bottle of beer just jugs here?

The price for the bowling was also high, $15 per person for an hour. We were there on a Saturday night and not during the neon bowling.  My bowling shoes were also falling apart at the seems but hey who likes bowling shoes anyways?

I really love this librairie the staff are so friendly, knowledgeable and helpful. First you need to know that the library cards are free this year and even for 2019. So I highly recommend you get one. At first I found the layout of the library a bit confusing but once you understand it it's the best place ever. They offer tones of services and activities. Like career resource, computer, internet, book club, genealogy club, author talks, computer and technology training, teen hang out and a bunch of things for kids to. You don't even need to go to the library they have a great selections of e-books, e-audiobooks, e-magazine and e-music. Oh and if you wonder why would I want to listen to a book?, well let me tell you I love listening to my book while doing choirs in the house, taking a walk or even while driving a long distance. Then they have a great selections of movies, shows and games you can rent for free. Another thing I love about them is the service. They are so nice there and let's say you want a book that they don't have you can ask for it and usually they get it for you. I've ordered a tons of books and the best is you can ask to be first in line to get it. They even let you know by email when it has arrived. They also offer interlibrary loans. The parking right by the library is really small but if you park across the street it's a big one. I really recommend this library.

This might just be my favourite Second Cup in the Edmonton area (but as a St. Albert girl born and raised, I might just be biased)!

The staff here are great, and always try to get through multiple customers in the line-up at a time. The drinks come quickly, and they always make sure to ask if you'd like it in a to-stay mug (three cheers for the environment). I love the Espresso Chillers and nanaimo bars!

My one criticism? The patio is awkwardly positioned between the cafe and the drive through, meaning your outdoor conversation is constantly interrupted by car engines in summertime.

I really enjoy this library. It's very user friendly, has a decent multi media section and is really close to my condo so it's easy access. Coming from Vancouver I am a little surprised that I had to pay an annual membership of $30. All of this kind of stuff is free but I guess BC'ers also get taxed a lot more to pay for these services.
I will be coming here often and I can't wait to check out the St Albert Farmers Market in the parking lot across the street!

I'm not sure if I'll ever find a good chinese restaurant! Asian Connection may be better then most but I guess my standards are too high coming from Little China (Vancouver).

Pros: They deliver, include chopsticks, soy and fortune cookies.

Cons: Smallish dishes, could barely see the beef inside the szchewan beef dish, and the noodles in the vegetable chow mein were of the instant variety. And for those two dishes I paid $22?! 

I will say it's better than the other place across the street but honestly that doesn't say much. No more chinese food for me!
Do NOT rely on this place to open after bar. They close early even with paying customers. Do not bother to go here

I'm a touch biased. I love this resto. i grew up in St.A and went here for years. I'm a slave to their green onion cakes, fried rice, wonton soup and ginger beef. 

Go now. Go back. Go often. I'm still searching for delicious green onion cakes in Toronto. ho hum.

The library is so popular in St. Albert that they're looking to branch out! That's such good news that people in the suburbs value reading so much that this library has become overcrowded with books and that there's a demand for another branch. 

As I approached the library, there were tables outside with books on top and underneath them. There was a sign saying the books were a dollar each except for the kids' books which were fifty cents. I can never pass up a good deal on a book so I was drawn to this and browsed for a bit. I found two books that looked interesting - one about dream interpretation and tarot cards, the other was a classic, "The Feminine Mystique." It was like hitting a goldmine with that one! I'm all about finding certain rare and out of print books.

I noticed another sign above the tables saying that if the library is closed to insert payment for the books through the book return slot. Interesting. Yet another sign said the library can't take anymore book donations, they simply don't have the space.

I went inside to pay for the books, set off the alarm. The guy at the counter said the total for the pair was one dollar. Cool! I scrounged my pockets and change purse but didn't have a dollar. He asked how much I did have. Turned out I had fifty cents. I offered to use debit but he said that fifty cents would be fine. Wow! Best deal ever! 

I did a brief walkabout of the library for old times' sake. Aside from some technological advances such as self-checkouts (cool!), it looked very much like I fondly remembered it. It felt good to be there. I went upstairs and saw students on laptops and at the internet terminals, a coin-op coffee dispenser and loads of wonderful books. 

The library is home to a book club that anyone is free to join. There are storytimes for the kids. Every summer since I can remember they've had the infamous summer reading game to keep the kids busy.

Ok.. how many people think 5 pin bowling is harder than 10 pin? Whoever invented the 5 pin system obviously could not knock down 10 pins so they created this instead ! Probably thought the regular bowling balls were too heavy as well.. so let's make them really small !  Well let me tell you.. 5 pin is harder.  My sister and her family and I were here yesterday for an hour of bowling ( neon bowling.. lights out, all blue neon and flashing lights ).  
The first ball I picked up had a huge dent in it.. picked up another one.. another dent. 
We had lanes 1 and 2 . Our machine to enter names did not work so we had to go to the counter to have staff enter our names. But thats OK.. as long as it worked. 

The flashing lights are a bit distracting but once you get used to it, you dont notice it as much. 

They do have 10 pin bowling but at different times ( Saturdays, it's 5 pin until 7 pm ). 

So in between waiting for my turn I took a quick look around .. 

The place is outdated and really could use an update in the décor.  The music playing was so-so. You could barely hear it but thats OK by me.  The bathroom was filthy though. 
We did not get any food but I did walk by a table that had pretty much every item on the table - party of 10.  It looked good but when I asked a guy at the table how the food was, he replied so -so.  In other words, typical bowling fare- pizza, wings, fries... blah  !  looking at their menu , a large pizza is $28 or 2 for $50.00 ( I doubt it is even made fresh considering I looked at it on their table and it looked like it was not worth the money ). Actually now that I think about it , it looked like it was one of those frozen ones you buy at a grocery store. Just like all the other deep fried items.  Based on that, eat somewhere else or afterwards.. it did not look at all appetizing . 
Overall it was pretty fun and the place was a bit busy . But then again, I think this is the only place in St Albert so that helps. 
Like I said,, overall it was pretty fun to bowl for an hour - but when your time is up, that's it ! You could be in the middle of a great game ( or in my case a really bad game ) and it could suddenly end ! 

One nice feature is you can book your times online to save you a few minutes.  The cost to bowl is around $18 for an hour but if you go with a group , they do have group rates.  Prices do include shoe rental .

Believe me... My husband and I are shocked that we gave this place 4 stars!  We only came here as part of my quest to find the best Fish 'N Chips & Clam Chowder in Edmonton - Figured we had to try Joey's Only as it's our main "fish" chain.

We were promptly greeted upon entering the restaurant and asked to select where we would like to sit.

After looking over the menu, my husband decided to try the 3 piece Haddock & Chips for $15.99 with french fries and cole slaw.

I ordered a Bowl of Joey's Boston Style Clam Chowder for $5.99 as a starter and the Shrimp & Fish for $14.49 as my lunch entree.

There was one other table in the restaurant at lunch time on the Sunday of Canada Day weekend.

Unfortunately our server wasn't very attentive and completely forgot that I had ordered clam chowder.  When our food finally arrived after around 10 minutes I was still waiting for the chowder to start.

She promptly brought the chowder and we were pleasantly surprised by the classic Boston Style Clam Chowder with large chunks of potato in it!  My husband even liked it and he's not a big "clam" fan.

His order of Haddock and Chips was surprisingly the best Haddock we have had so far - the batter was light and flaky and the fish was tender and quite moist.

I ordered the classic Joey style fish which my server advised was Pollock.  I wouldn't recommend that to anyone who is a true fish fan - it didn't have very much flavor and is not something I will be repeating.  The shrimp were okay... I chose cajun style.  My husband's entree was quite a bit more tasty than my own.  We were really shocked that we enjoyed the freshness of his Haddock and batter here more than at Brits or Back Home... We still have a few more place in the city to try before we crown Joey's Only the champion of (Haddock) Fish 'n Chips.

For my entree, I got to select 2 sides - I tried "Mushy Peas" and "Bourbon Baked Beans."  The beans were excellent  but the mushy peas were actually crunchy... I don't think they had been soaked long enough prior to cooking.

All in all - 4 stars - Hubby's best Haddock 'n Chips to date in Edmonton and the price was reasonable.

*Uploaded pics of all the food*
Good for their fries, but their pizza isn't anything to brag about. Also the pasta prices and sandwich prices are way too much.

UPDATE!!  I figured I should come back and update this once I actually tried the goodies, and the quality of the food has absolutely bumped them up to 5 stars.

I wasn't a fan of their snickerdoodles... but that's a matter of personal taste and not their fault.

The sausage rolls were delicious.  I had beef and my mom had pork... we were both very happy.

My new favourite thing in the world though..... is the mini mocha cake.  I almost cried it was so good.  My family is now very aware that that is the only cake that I'm interested in having for any occassions haha

I will never buy a bating suit elsewhere again!! The staff are friendly and knowledgeable which I really appreciate, being a larger woman. They helped me find the perfect suit! They have a nice selection of cruise wear and jewelry as well. Worth the drive to St Albert!

Brought Grams and the fam jam here last week for a Canada Day lunch date after we were rained out and the outdoor Canada Day events were cancelled.

The we opted for the share 5 for $25:

Calamari - rubbery meh
Pacific shrimp - lacking in flavor despite the "hint of jalapeño"
Lobster and shrimp Mac 'n cheese - none of us even wanted to finish it :-( Think noodles with fake cheese sauce on top
Fish tacos - Really quite good!!! Same fish as fish n chips meal with fresh salsa and a soft tortilla that held up!
Sweet coconut shrimp - okay but not exciting

Kiddo meal $7
Fish n chips, drink, and worms and dirt - She gobbled them up and the fish was the same as adult fish. 

Deal of the day - $22
For 2 - 1 piece fish n chips, 2 pops, and a dessert
Fish was good!
Fries - not a single one of us liked them which is a problem in a fish n chips joint 
Mud pie was good. 

Clam chowder - $7 bowl
Okay but nothing to write home about 

For $70 we all agreed we'd rather of eaten elsewhere.  We all agreed that fish tacos and fish were good but the rest left a lot to be desired.

This particular location is smaller than some others I've seen, so the choices are more limited, but it's still worth a visit if you're in the neighbourhood.

If you love scones, try the Apple and Butterscotch chip, or the White Chocolate Raspberry - truly delicious and fairly large.  Order in multiples to save some money and please your tummy  ;-D

This bakery is horrible if you don't like those crummy grocery store cakes made with that gross buttercream. In fact, many grocery stores like Save On have been realizing that people don't really like those cakes, because they are nothing like homemade and so they've been making better cakes and charging more money for them. Grandin Bakery charges lots of money for a little cake-- that tastes like those crummy sheet cakes no one ever REALLY wants to eat. My coworkers told me I must have picked a bad item, so I went back and tried some lemon tarts. They were basically shells filled with lemon buttercream frosting. I was yet again disappointed. I'd honestly rather go to a grocery store bakery.

This is the best pizza in town. They have  great selection and the delivery is quick.  I have ordered pizza from places all over St. Albert but Nitza's is consistently great and my husband, who doesn't even like pizza, enjoys it as well.  The Donaire pizza is great and we love the Tropicana (with spinach instead of pineapples). They are great about substitutions and their delivery time is quick. Any guests who come to our house and try it fall in love with the pizza.

I've had two cakes ordered from here. (Both customized designs) the first cake I got was beautifully decorated and looked identical to the photo I had shown them. The second one wasn't decorated quite as well but it was still delicious! Service was great! Price was pretty decent. I've never bought any of their other items. If they carried Keto items I'd be here all the time!

Unfortunately, I'm afraid I walked away from dinner wishing I hadn't walked in.  I'm having a hard time thinking of anything positive to say.

Hmmmm......

We ordered the buffet, which had only a few dishes that I thought were satisfactory - too many of them were just plain unpleasant.  The soups were of the "one spoonful is more than enough" variety - the Wonton had almost no flavour to the broth, and what little it did have was not good.  The beef in the beef/broccoli, usually my favourite in any buffet, almost had a rancid hint to it and I decided not to tempt my stomach with a second piece to see if it was just a fluke.  The spring rolls were lacking vegetables or any texture or real taste, just the oil and what seemed to be mushy rice (or something unidentifiable) inside.  There were several dishes I decided not to try at all, based on their looks alone.

Service was not good, either - our plates were slow to be cleared, causing a pile up on the small table, and our water was never refilled.  There was one cheap, thin paper napkin at each place setting, none more available at the dish/utensils station.  At the end of the meal, the waitperson commented to me that we had left too much food on plates uneaten.  I managed not to tell her WHY with great restraint.  I completely agree that people shouldn't waste food just because it's a buffet, but I also believe the food should be flavourful enough that you WANT to eat it.  Even though we take small servings at first to see if we want more of a dish, too many just didn't earn more than one or two bites.

My other issue was cleanliness, or the lack of it.  The window blinds had fly specks all over them, right at my shoulders, dirty enough to make me shudder.  More napkins would have been handy to dispose of creepy crawlies on the window and wall next to us.  My chair seat was quite stained and the padding on all the chairs seemed dingy from long usage (you know that kind of straight chair you see in waiting rooms - blue padded seat, chrome legs, etc - made me wonder if they picked them up from some business going thru an upgrade twenty years ago or so).

Oh dear, still haven't thought of anything positive to say...   

I've never given a one-star review before and feel badly doing it now, but I just can't manage to give it a two.    It was truly a "Methinks not" for me.  I'll continue hoping to find a great Chinese buffet, but this was not it.

Well this place is highly recommended overall for a reason. From my limited experience and reviewing the previous Yelper's comments I am going to say that:
1) Stopping in and ordering is way more effective than delivery. 
2) Great for kids...substitute your toppings and not a lot of grief.
3) There is no silly topping combination  which makes my heart warm.
4) Eat it hot and love it even more 
5) This is a long standing business in St. A and deserves a try!

This is one of 2 second cups in st Albert and I visit both. This location has a great patio and cafe. Comfy chairs and newspapers make you feel like you're in someone's living room. The patio faces south so you get a lot of sun. The funny thing is that the drive thru goes right around it so if youre lounging you do hear the order being taken by the staff. On that note the staff do a good job taking and making your order. I went back and asked for more ice in my iced coffee and got it no questions asked. 

I like a few of their food items but they are usually over priced and just go into a microwave to be heated.

I've heard great reviews for several years but never happened to be "in the neighbourhood," so when I saw their sign in a little shopping centre I was visiting, I was delighted to actually get a chance to visit.

So much to choose from, so attractively displayed, and such friendly service - what more could a person actually ask for?   Well, i'll tell you what to ask for - the lemon bismarks - best in the land!!
Great place to get books you need briefly or movies and video games(1week) very helpful staff...willing to help find books and use the self checkout.

The St. Albert Bowling Centre offers standard blowing, neon bowling, and bumper bowling for the bowling challenged (toddlers or the intoxicated).

The prices are pretty standard for bowling alleys but the food is overpriced and nothing to write home about.  

The staff are friendly but the place itself can use some updating.  There is a mini golf portion outside as well but it is quite weathered from our harsh seasons.

They participate in summer children's bowling programs which offer discounted bowling rates for kids to help keep them active!

There are some league nights here as well, so be sure to check out their website or phone ahead to make sure there are lanes open and available for public use.

Bowl on!

Best donair pizza. Fast delivery. Reliable. Fresh toppings. 

I love nitzas because it is reliable, fast, consistent and delicious. I have ordered here so many times in a bind starving at work and they have delivered us pizza within 30 minutes. Their delivery service is outstanding and they are always on time!

Toppings are always fresh and plentiful. Crust is crunchy. Dough holds well despite the plentiful toppings. They make a wide variety of pizzas and I have been lucky to try most of them (generous doctors). But my favourite by far is the donair pizza with extra sauce. Its outstanding and I almost cant resist it if I drive by this place bc its that's good. It sounds weird but it works. I have gotten the whole sturgeon hospital addicted to this pizza. Nobody ordered it until I did at a nursing event...and now it's a must order whenever nurses want pizza. Try it. You wont be disappointed!
Excellent fresh product baked daily. Lots of bread and other pastry delights to indulge your sweet tooth.

I love libraries in general, and smaller ones really make me feel "at home" and happy.  This year the library cards are free for everyone - what more could a bibliophile desire?
