The online site is fantastic, very detailed, easy to navigate, allowing you to browse not only books but lists compiled by staff and borrowers to help you find items similar to your tastes as well as introduce you to books you may never have considered.  You can create your own lists, maintain a "for later" section, place holds, and be notified via email when they are ready for pickup.

The library itself is bright and cheery, with comfortable seating, an extensive large print section, lots of dvds and movies, a fun childrens area, multiple self-checkout kiosks, and helpful staff.  Couldn't ask for more!
This is the best pizza in St.Albert after moving away for a year I can honestly say I missed it so much!
Great place to get Donairs or pizza, have being in business since 1989. Have a loyal following from nearby students of V.J. Maloney and St. Albert High.

I remember when this bakery actually was in Grandin Mall. Considering the store has been around about as long as I have, it's no surprise that I'd have such a memory. 

Now they're by the Crown & Tower and still doing rather well. The first thing I noticed when I walked in was to the left there was shelving stocked with imported Dutch foods and treats. Most of the displays were filled with pastries, cookies, cakes and pies. Behind the counter were bread and buns. I checked out some muffins but discovered they contain soy and was rather disappointed. So I looked for sausage rolls. Another disappointment because they didn't have any, only "veggie" rolls that looked the same but likely contained soy.
Wonderful bakery they even have Neapolitans! But every time Ive been there the service has been surly, otherwise I would have given 5 stars.

Staff is really nice. Pizza used to be better in my opinion but the fries and way the staff treat you still means I'd recommend folks go to this restaurant. Not my go-to anymore for pizza. Again, would recommend to others and happily eat here though.

Amazing pizza at a reasonable price. If we are getting pizza this is where we get it from. Plus the people there are awesome. They always remember us by name and chat with us when we come in. I definitely recommend this place to anyone That asks.

Friendly baristas and great coffees!!! Ordered the flavoured coffee today which was maple cream (omg yum) with steamed milk.  The wonderful barista told me it was called something like "white coffee" (I'm butchering how he worded it).  Regardless it was heavenly!!!

We ordered the 2 for 1 pizza deal this weekend and got the donair and the mushroom, pepperoni pizzas. We used to love Nitza's as it is local but unfortunately the toppings on the pizza were practically non-existent leaving everyone to be hungry after their usual two pieces. 

Considering the pizza market is a highly competitive segment, you would assume Nitza's would look at their local competitors, such as Socrates, and keep their pizzas well made with a fair amount of high quality ingredients. I get things are tough right now due to COVID, however, I also think reducing the quality and quantity of your food does more harm to a brand long term.

Will not be returning anytime soon.

Going to this Library for 20+ years for school project information, easy reads, and my favourite authors as well as renting movies for the weekends

Unlimited number of movies and books to takeout at a time, just need new movies back in 3 days older movies keep longer.

To be honest I have never set foot in the place but have eaten there pizza a tons of times thanks to my husband who is on pick up duty. 

But beside that I have to say these guys make a damn fine pizza. Of all the pies of tried I have to say the donair pizza is by far my favourite. It is loaded with donair meat mushroom and topped with fresh tomatoes. But the best part is how they literally drown the pizza in their sweet creamy donair sauce.  It is just so freakin fantastic. Yum yum yum.

They basically have an option for anyone, including those with allergies. I kid you not they even have a vegetarian option that is cheese less and can be made on a gluten free crust.

Other options I love are the Tropicana pie. And my kids absolutely love their cheese pizza. 

Little Caesars got nothing on this place.

Anyway now that I've written this I know what I'm having for dinner. Haha

The food is second to none but the likelihood of having your order delivered correctly, the first time, is a crapshoot at best.

If you can pick up, you're good to go and you get a free slush.

Their hot wings are exceptional especially if you eat them fresh and if your wife lets you have any.  And I don't normally like hot wings.  Our hot wings rarely make the drive home intact.

Expect to pay a little more here than your average pizza joint.

Support local and give them a try but I highly recommend picking up your order.

Quite simply - Nitza's is my go-to. Their calamari is superb, dipped in a lovely tzatziki sauce - hits the spot every time. I always get the ceasar salad - one order is enough for two people and more. Since I can never make up my mind, I usually get the wings and pizza - just means I don't have to worry about lunch the next day. No waiting for 2-for-1 Tuesdays - their 2-for-1 pizza is everyday. The pizzas at Nitza's are sturdy - substantial crust - not overly thick - but solid and can easily hold whatever toppings you have piled on. Personally, I like a pizza that doesn't fold in half half way to my mouth. The chicken ranch is particularly good, in my opinion.

I usually order pick-up or delivery. The staff are always friendly - but they go over and beyond for me these days. I'm a bit compromised walking with a cane just now and when I picked up my last order - they carried my food out to my car and put it on the seat for me. COVID safe and all. That's great service. And, as always when you pick-up from Nitza's, I appreciate that they always offer me one of their epic lime slushies - on the house. With delivery - they are fast, they food is hot, and they get my order right.  

On all accounts - 5 stars - well deserved.

I love the fact that I can take my kids here and plop them in front of a computer.  We go to the kids section and pick out books and usually come out of there with some sort of Thomas the Train or Barbie DVD.

My 5 year old has recently taken to choosing music to sing to.  The Frozen soundtrack is definitely part of our repertoire.  

Spacious, clean, bright, and the staff are extremely knowledgeable and friendly.  The only downside is that the library itself is too small.  Even city council has commented that St. Albert would benefit from a larger library.

My children will be partaking in the summer reading program again this summer.  If you have kids and aren't signed up, you are missing out!

Not impressed, not again.  We ordered an extra large pizza, and were told the price was under $30.  We were happy with this...until our 12" pizza arrived.  The quality of the pizza was fine, nice crust and quite tasty, but we ordered an extra large, weren't told they didn't have an extra large, and the quantity was lacking.  We've had other pizza for around the same price, but there has always been more for the money.  From now on, when we travel through Red Deer, we'll be stopping at Western Pizza.

Came here for Father's Day. 

This place has not changed since I was little and came here.   The workers were kind and helpful.  The place was busy which was good to see.  

We all had fun on the lanes and the kids were having a blast.  

Beverages seem very pricey though...but nice afternoon bowling.

What an amazing place. Fresh, super delicious and full of flavour donuts. Nothing fancy and not as huge, if this is what you know as donuts. Totally worth the drive to St Albert. The staff is welcoming, there is so much more to try at this bakery. Go check them out if you have not. Support local!

I stopped here on a whim after work one day because I had a craving for fish and chips. The staff member that greeted me was pleasant and my order came out quickly. I ordered the two piece fish and chips with a side of gravy. The fish was tasty but the batter was greasy. The fries were well cooked and the side of coleslaw was good. The tartar sauce was above average. The gravy was tasty but a little too runny for my taste. I especially liked the added touch of when I was handed my to go bag it was folded so the logo was facing outwards.

This park is small but beautiful. A great place to have a picnic. They do have a small gift shop and bathrooms beside the parking lot. Parking is never usually a problem. It's a nice way to spend a sunny afternoon walking around and looking at the different types of flowers. The botanical gardens are very well-kept. They also have some fun events so check out the website

The St. Albert Botanical Gardens is a completely under-the-radar location and perfect for an intimate, elegant wedding in their rose garden.  I am particularily fond of the garden in mid-late May, when the cherry blossoms are in full bloom and their sweet fragrance weighs heavy in the air.  For local green-thumbs, it is THE place to go in the spring to pick up award-winning roses, dhalias and lillies to plant at home.

This may not be the most fair review for this place as we didn't actually stay here. We attended a Christmas party here. But here goes. The buffet food was decent but they ran out or just didn't refill. The bar was good, service was great there BUT more than one table complained the wine glasses were dirty. Mine had lips marks on it. The bathrooms were nice, well kept. The people bussing the tables seemed to hate their job. We never did get a water refill. I mean all in all it was good. If you have a function this place might not be a bad venue to try

The hotel was decent. Bed was ok, although it was only a queen. The room's configuration was weird. The bed did not face the TV and the bedside lamp and alarm clock were powered by extension cords (unhidden) running from the wall opposite the TV. The water pressure in the shower was pretty bad. The room had a wall mounted air conditioner that let cold air in (and moisture out so the room was very dry). The wirelss internet was horrible (most of the time the sites timed out) and no wired internet was available in my room (only certain rooms have that). There were also lights on the outside of the building pointed at it and the curtains didn't reach the bottom, so it was pretty annoying at night.  There is a fridge in the room which is handy and the staff was friendly. There also didn't seem to be sufficient parking available. If you're staying in St. Albert though the location is good (Starbucks, supermarket and a bunch of fast food places around).

Beautiful, gorgeous, a hidden gem - is how I would describe St. Albert Botanical Park. The park is made up of several different sections to show plants grouped mainly by type - I think the prettiest part is the rose garden. For the most part the names are at the base of each plant so if you want to go home and grow it yourself you know what to get. An interesting note is that they only grow what is in our zone (meaning you actually could go home and grow the plant you saw and have a hope of watching it flourish). Don't forget to check out the area of shade plants - it is hidden behind the trees. I also enjoy the gift shop - there is plenty of local artists that are sold here and some of them are exclusive to this location.

A very relaxing afternoon can be spent taking a stroll through the gardens, admiring nature in an organic way. Plus if you bring a book with you there are plenty of benches to sit on and spend some time outside.

Worst taxi service ever! Was told driver would arrive in 3 minutes, waited 20 minutes. Called back to cancel and the dumb prick didn't even ask my name/number or pick up location! Just said, "Ok thanks bye." Thanks for what, you dip shit!

My experience was definitely not as bad as everyone else's it seems.  Though, had I read the reviews first, I wouldn't have bothered.

However - I don't like being confused.  And this place is confusing.  Is there signage that I just didn't see?  From the parking lot, you can access the wand wash area.  But if you go around back (go out onto the road and then into the little driveway in the back) you'll find the automatic wash.  There was a big sign back there with the prices, but I couldn't see anywhere that said if we paid back there, or had to go inside.  So to be safe, I drove back to the front and went inside to ask.  There's nowhere to park while you run into the office - so you have to leave your car awkwardly in front of the door, while cars are exiting the car wash on either side of you.  While inside - the guy kept suggesting that we should do the wand wash instead of the drive thru, because it probably won't get the car as clean as we want.

Wait... what?  Why do you have the drive automatic wash if it doesn't do what it's supposed to do?  

To be honest though, I was feeling very lazy and didn't actually care if it got 100% clean - I just wanted to get some of the dirt off before the snow fell that night.

So finally he sold us the Alpine package and I head back around to the back of the building.

I actually don't have many complaints about the wash itself.  It seemed very thorough and I was satisfied with the quality based on the $14.00 I spent.  

I sure miss Rock N Wash on the southside though.  It might be worth the 40 minute drive next time I need a car wash...

Considering St. Albert is a small town, the Botanic Park is amazing!

Brought the chitlins and Gramma out today for their annual Canada Day celebrations.

We partook in strawberry shortcake, lemonade, a scavenger hunt through the whole garden, and brought home a FABULOUS glass bird bath for our garden.

I could not believe how many lilies they had!  Three giant gardens!  You can even buy/order plants/rose bushes here for your garden at home.

This would also be an absolutely smashing place for a wedding ceremony or engagement photos!  There is a beautiful rose garden with a water fountain in the middle and a good sized gazebo as well! 

Check out my pics :-)

Nice central location in St Albert, very clean hotel with modern appointments.  Staff seemed excellent and very friendly.  Comfy beds and a nice pool with waterslide.  Nice little coffee shop just off lobby.  VERY pricey small town hotel at around $185.00 per night however.

This location is a good place to shop for groceries and floral arrangements.  They have well priced, unique floral arrangements for those special occasions.  
It's a typical grocery store with a large deli that has a good selection. The only negative at this store is that they close down their self checkouts about 3 hours before closing time.  This seems to be a common thing at all Safeway locations.  It makes it very frustrating when you are just stopping in for one or two quick items but end up having to wait in line behind someone with a cart full of groceries.  There is a Sobeys across the road (same company as Safeway, yet their self checkouts stay open later).

I chose the wand wash to wash my Not so dirty truck. Not too happy about paying for time before I start washing. That's an extra minute per customer and that's just crooked. The lighting was so bad that when another car came in with it's daytime running lights on I was briefly able to see where I missed. The antique mercury vapor lights haven't seen new bulbs in years and it shows......or doesn't show. The only positive note was it had hot water rinse. After $22 my truck still looked dirty. There was hardly any evidence that soap was being drawn into the sprayer. It's the only $22 they will ever get from me.
Nice alternative to Uber they seem to care and also text you when car or driver near. Good experience
I go here for 1 litre lactose-free milk, organic sugar, organic fruits and carrots and grain fed chicken. These are some of the things I don't find at the Superstore.

I wasn't that impressed. The rooms were not as clean as they should be, the linens had stains, and what put me over the edge was the family across the hall let their kids run screaming up and down the hall for about an hour. The good part was the service was excellent, and the response was fast when we complained about the excessive noise. The one recommendation (other than hire new cleaners) is the housekeeping staff need to be reminded to knock on the door before entering. I didn't like when the housekeeper walked in at 9 am when I was getting dressed.

If I have a favourite Safeway this would be it!! The prices keep me from shopping here too often but if you need an item and/or shop the sales it can be a very rewarding experience overall!!! 

The floor plan is set up in such a way that I which my doors for entry and exit based on what I need and it seriously improves efficiency due to the location of obstacles. The produce, dairy and dried goods are best suited to the right hand side while the left is bread, frozen goods and the deli!! 

Under all circumstances I avoid the pharmacy as the one lady is entirely toxic and seems to enjoy making her coworkers and the customers alike miserable!! 

My advice for Safeway overall and not just this location is to ensure you know the price point before you shop for a family!! Take the flyer seriously...don't impulse meal plan and always leave your kids at home.

This car wash fits the bill for me. I use the touchless section that you just drive into, park while the machines squirt soap and spray water, then drive out slowly through the dryers. Yes it is a bit more expensive than washing your car by yourself, but this is fast and I don't have to get dirty. And, while my car is being washed, I can be multi-tasking. There are three options with varying services; I like the middle of the road option called The Meadow.

Also this is close enough to my house that in the winter I can wash my car and make it home before anything freezes!

Dubbed "a garden in progress," St. Albert Botanic Park is maintained entirely by community members. Admission is free, and although the site is small, it is full of different kinds of plants and flowers. The sections for roses and lilacs stand out in particular. There are bushes, trees, and other kinds of flowers too. Open from dawn to dusk, this is a great reason for a short road trip to St. Albert.
My taxi, ordered the night before, was very prompt, Carter was very nice and the taxi was nice and clean. I will use them again

Called for a cab - my first in about 8 or more years.

Cab arrived on time: 
- weather was a warm 24+ and there was no A/C
- windshield crack in direct line of driver's vision
- cab driver can only open and close the front passenger window
- interior of vehicle is FILTHY
- van exterior is quite "dinged up"
 
I mentioned to the driver that I'd called for a cab several years ago and, I believe it's quite possible that I got the SAME CAB.

The New owner (June 2018) has made BIG changes. Firstly, he's really friendly and agreeable unlike the last owner (Mr. angry face). The lights have been upgraded with super bright LED lighting, the water is always hot and the cleaning chemicals actually clean. Alpine is better than ever.

Took my truck there today and one side did not get a rinse so it was dirty when finished.  The wheels were also very dirty.  Asked the manager, an oriental fellow, to look at the truck.  He immediately became defensive and said I should have pre washed in the wand bay first.  I mentioned I never have had to do that in any other wash and he just walked away.  Obviously not the owner I hope.

Came here today for the first time with a coupon. Cost is 75 cents per minute with one minute to get set up from the time you take a ticket until you finish and pay. No coins or tokens! Clean and upscale environment for a do it yourself kind of carwash. The teenage boy cashier was polite and friendly. The only reason they get 4 instead of 5 stars is that this place ends up costing me $3-4 more than the timed token locations. I will however, definitely return!
This wash has great pressure, lots of soap and handles larger vehicles easily(even my Excursion).

Great place to shop. Just RUN (don't walk) away from the pharmacy!
They are rude and have picked up and sent home 3 times in the past year with the wrong prescription. I don't think Blood Pressure medication is what treats Tonsillitis! HAHA!

Warning do not go to Alpine car wash in St Albert, since under new ownership they are awful and rip people off. They over charge for the timed washes even if you time yourself they still overcharge you! Past owners always charged once you started washing your vehicle, as per the timer on the machine, now they start your time before you enter the wash! Even if it is busy and you have to wait in line to pay they charge you for the time you waited in line! They don't care about customer service and then all of a sudden pretend they don't speak English when you voice your concerns about being ripped off!!! FML for being charged $70 for a car wash!!! There goes my grocery money!

This is a volunteer-run botanic garden/park type thing; nothing huge or fancy like the UofA botanic gardens further south, but in the spring and summer there are nicely labeled flowers and plants to enjoy, and there's a beautiful rose garden that must be lovely when they're all in bloom. During the winter there's not a lot to see, but starting from the botanic garden you can easily transition to the walking trail along the river, which will take you all the way along the river into St. Albert. There are little picnic benches along the trail also, so this is a great option if the weather's nice to bring a picnic or pick up some food from a local place - the trail will take you past a few, depending how far you want to go and in which direction. A good pandemic option when the weather's not too cold, and pleasant views.

If I could give zero stars I would. To start off, at first they seemed nice. They replied to emails at a decent rate. The problem started when they failed to mention a very important rule: no outside chairs. But wait, nowhere in their brochures, or their website states no third party chairs whatsoever and also in person, no one mentioned this very important rule of theirs. Taylor was the one who got our paperwork done when we gave our deposit. When I asked if we could bring in gold chiavari chairs, Patricia said someone should have mentioned it to us. Nope. Not mentioned. We were also told we were the last slot for a ceremony on our wedding date on a Saturday. We even tried to accommodate and make sure it wouldn't interfere with anyone or anything that would wreck the flowers in their garden. Then Patricia told us we weren't the last slot. So, based on their lies, we decided we didn't want to give our money to this company. I guess the one star can be for them returning our deposit money. If you want to save yourself a headache, stay the fuck away from this venue. Their garden isn't even that nice so no wonder they love their ugly chairs and won't let anyone change it. My first choice was muttart conservatory but unfortunately they're closed for renovations until 2021. Personally if I was a business owner, I would first own up to my mistake, then second, I would try to make the customer happy if I was in the wrong but hey, to each their own. They didn't seem like they wanted our money with how rude and unprofessional they were towards my fiancé and I. They were basically pushing us to get our refund instead of trying to fix the problem. We will take our money elsewhere.

What a gorgeous place! So glad I checked it out. 

Obviously Mother Nature decided autumn was going to happen TODAY, but we we still got to enjoy the rose garden. Many plants were still in bloom and the variety was stunning. 

It's such a lush and quiet beauty, I couldn't help but falling in love with it and dreaming of next summer's picnics there. I can't believe how meticulously this park is maintained. There's a lot of pride put into these gardens. I'm a little jealous of the perfection!

I previously used Alpine Auto Wash exclusively.  They are now under new ownership and I will never go again.  Since new ownership came in they: 
- Turned off the water heater (cold water out of the wands).
- Reduced the soap concentration in the wash coming from the wands.
- Completely turned off the radiant heaters that heat the building (I used the wash at about -15 C and it was approx. 0 C in the building.  Not one of the radiant heaters was running.  Freezing cold. 
- Self brush foam now ejects foam/soap intermittently.  Previously ran soap constantly, now it seems to turn on for 5 seconds and off for 15.  Frustrating. 
- I can't confirm this, but they seem to have increased their rate per minute since they installed the credit card pay system. I washed my vehicle countless times previously and the average price was $17.  My one wash there was $25 and I believe the time spent was similar. 

Bottom line.  Go elsewhere.  You'd be better off using your garden hose on your driveway in the middle of winter.  It's practically free and the experience is unchanged.  Cold environment, cold water, no soap. I'd give 0 stars if I could.

Terrible. I went through the touch less wash, it hardly cleaned my car. When I went inside and mentioned it the guy brushed me off and said that is the kind of job it does. I left and came back to get the mangers name, it was the owner I had been talking to! He really doesn't have a clue about customer service and I've never had such a poor cleaning when the previous owners were running things. Don't waste your money!

I have always liked this car wash as the tools are much easier to use than other places. However under the new ownership this place is awful and I would suggest no one waste their money at this business. The current owners are money grubbing lazy crooks. When they went to a pay per stall operation I was not comfortable but I did get used to it. But I found the lighting has even become worse with the new owners and I can hardly see my car to see if I have cleaned it. And I'm pretty sure that is deliberate of the new owners.

Second very upsetting development was their wax. I spend an extra 2 mins washing over my car with wax to get the streaks of water off. But since the new owners have taken over there has been no wax at this place. But they continue to list is as a services and charge you for it even though they know they don't have it. I have gone to them to complain many times. The owner comes to look at my car and claims it is working. I show him that it should bead off my windows and he sits there dumbfounded. He goes back to his utility room to check his wax and comes back to claim it is fully loaded. But he is completely lying. I  assumed that maybe it was just a one time bad occurrence but I had returned and used different stalls and again the same thing. Always speaking to the owner and he love to lie and claim it works. I was so frustrated I drove across the street to the shell where their hand wand wax works perfectly. Spent another two minutes there to properly wax my car. 

Then the other day I was rushing into town and wanted to wash my car quickly with their brushless automatic system, and on a car that is not too dirty this system has always worked perfectly. However my first time using it under the new ownership has proved to me that they have also taken the wax out of the automatic system as well. Even though they clearly state on their signs that they offer it and I paid for it. They are complete crooks. You are better off finding a new location as the current owners are only interested in taking your money without proving you the promised services.
Great service and wash. The owner was super friendly and helpful with the auto wash, and went above and beyond to ensure my vehicle completely clean before leaving

Awesome cashier, Reese today. Very attentive to each person he dealt with asked about there day and how they wanted there items packaged. I would come back to this Safeway location again. I was here around 11 am on Feb 15, 2020

So we had an unfortunate experience at this Safeway last week.  But rather than just stew over it, I picked up the phone and gave them a call and asked to speak with the store manager.  I'm very pleased to say that the issue was resolved and for that they get 4 stars from me!  See below if you want to hear the story:

I sent my husband to the store with my toddler to go pick out some fancy cupcakes for my birthday dinner.  We already had a grown up Marble Slab ice cream cake set aside for adults but wanted our daughter to have fun so we thought this was a great idea!

When they came back from Safeway, she handed me a box of 4 beautiful Tinkerbell and Winnie the Pooh cupcakes.  I have always been impressed by the selection of children's cupcakes at Safeway: various Disney characters, Sesame street characters, etc.  Many times the character's face is actually a ring the child wear after eating the cupcake!  They are always quite pretty and VERY reasonably priced at $1.50 a piece.  There aren't flavour options like the gourmet cupcake shops - but gorgeous and perfect for a toddler!  Also a great idea for birthday parties since they are only $1.50 a piece, come proportioned, and usually come with a party favour in the form of a ring!  Anyhoo, she handed me the box of 4 - and I was happy for her - but then she told me she had gotten more.  Okay, where are they?  She handed me the grocery bag with 3 more cupcakes each placed individually in a plastic square container that WASN'T tall enough to stand the cupcake up in nor small enough around to prevent the cupcakes from rolling all over the place!  So the cupcakes had naturally rolled all over the place and Piglet, Winnie, & someone else I can't even recall was decapitated and smushed!  

I asked my husband if they had run out of containers or if he had packaged them up like this for some reason and he said that the Bakery clerk did this!  He advised that they had originally selected 4 cupcakes which were placed in the APPROPRIATE cupcake packaging but then my daughter kept seeing more cupcakes she wanted and they ended up adding 3 more - but 1 at a time.  Well, regardless - even if you were only buying 1 cupcake it shouldn't be given to you in a container not designed for a cupcake!  This looked more like a sandwich box!  

I fumed for a bit and then decided to call the store and ask to speak with a manager.  First, I spoke with customer service who didn't offer any suggestions other than putting me through to the lady who packaged the cupcakes for my husband - Uh, no thanks!  So then I spoke with the store manager who apologized and said he would have the bakery manager get back to me asap.

Approximately 15 minutes later, I received a phone call from the Bakery manager apologizing and stating that he spoke with the employee and asked to see what she packaged our cupcakes in.  He said he didn't need any further explanation because as soon as he saw the containers he could imagine how the cupcakes looked by the time they got to their final destination.  He asked if I would like to come back to the store to replace the cupcakes.  We only live a few minutes away so that wasn't a problem.  I asked if he wanted me to bring back the 3 decapitated cupcakes or if I should just give them to my toddler (rather than my dinner party guests) and he offered for her to keep them.

Upon arriving at the store, I was greeted by a not too friendly bakery clerk - I figured out later that it was the same one who had packaged the cupcakes earlier.  None the less, I had my daughter say "Please" and "Thank you" to the, ahem, "nice cupcake lady."  I was pleasantly surprised to find that they had a variety box of 6 character cupcakes waiting all packaged up for us free of charge.  

Now, while I wish the cupcakes hadn't been poorly packaged in the first place - it was nice to have the customer service issue corrected promptly and thoughtfully.  I stopped on the way out of the store to thank the manager and we took our cupcakes home.  

So in the end - I had sent my husband to the store to pick up 4 cupcakes - he came home with 7 - then we got another 6 free of charge - for a total of 13 cupcakes, good lord! We packaged up 4 cupcakes and delivered them to the neighbour girls and went on a car ride to deliver two adorable cupcakes to our nieces who were sick and couldn't come to the dinner party.

Thank you, Safeway, for correcting an unfortunate experience.  The least I can do is give you credit where it's due!

NEVER go here!   I had a Gift Card that still had about $200 on it and they would not honour it I believe the ownership changed hands and the new owner is an absolute crook.   I hope he suffers from his actions and is put out of business sooner than later.

Please note, any positive reviews are left over from the previous owner.

Garbage. Touch-less wash is useless. Card reader wouldn't work so the attendant came out with a code; nice, but he saw my truck and had nothing to say. When I complained that the truck looked pretty much the same after the wash he stated "touch less wash won't clean this kind of dirt". I had to rewash by hand (and pay for it). I don't expect perfection from a touch-less wash, but I expect the bulk of the road grime to be gone. Terrible service, terrible attitude. Save your time and money and wash by hand elsewhere.

Close by on the way home from work, I have usually gone to this location not the one further North on St. Albert Trail with the gas bar. Great Service and helpful staff. 

Always asking if I found everything I needed today.

The St. Albert Inn is pretty much a landmark of the suburban city. They've recently done extensive renovations and it looks pretty good. 

My sister had her wedding reception here in the summer. She was a little concerned that the carpeting in the conference room was still pretty dated but once everything was set up it was the last thing anyone would notice. The catering was decent though they did mess up on the midnight sandwich order which left a few people including me and my sister without bunwiches. (My sister loves that word, her husband not so much). 

I was glad that I'd booked a room in the hotel so I had a place to retreat when things got overwhelming. It was very convenient, I just checked in, went for dinner, went back to the room to nap while they were doing the speeches and stuff, then returned at my brother's urging and bribing me with free drinks. 

I was happy with my room which wasn't in the renovated part but still nice. The free wi-fi was awesome! It was also great that I didn't have too far to go in my too-tight shoes when the night was over.

We called St. Albert taxi to take us to the village transit center as we are not locals and couldn't figure out where the stop was for the nearest local bus. I agree with Derek about the dispatcher being a bit brisk on the phone. He seemed to get a little impatient when he tried to get me off the phone quickly and I stopped him mid goodbye to ask what doors they usually pull up at at Servus Place. I understand with it being the weekend and there also being a festival in town they were probably busy but again I am not a local and they should be prepared to get questions from out of towners.

The timing of the cab however was right on the dot. I mean literally on the dot as I was quoted 20 minutes and the driver showed up exactly at the 20 minute mark. The vehicle was a little older and had that "old car smell" about it but it was still clean and comfortable. The driver was very nice as well as very professional. He didn't attempt to make any awkward small talk and took us right to our destination without trying to take a more scenic route to pad his fare. He even went to the trouble of getting out and opening my door for me as according to him the button on the door required extra force and he didn't want to see me break my nice nails. I definitely appreciated the extra courtesy as well as the compliment.

If you can forgive the chilly reception of the dispatcher on the phone I think St. Albert Taxi is a great choice for getting around (alot better for sure than some of the companies in Edmonton) and we will definitely use them again next time we visit.

I have gone here a few times and never completely cleaned my car.  Yesterday I went again and couldn't believe how dirty my car still was.  I went back and requested a refund.  The attendant -John - no last name given - was completely rude, didn't care that my car was still dirty.  I have seen several negative reviews on Facebook.  I have contacted the Better Business Bureau and hope to get the word out about this terrible business.

i am done with this safeway.  I have tried and tried to shop here but it doesn't seem to matter what day of the week or what time of the day i go there is NEVER ANY FRESH PRODUCE!  They rarely have lettuce, or vegetables to purchase or any big selection at all.  I attempted several times to go in one week to see if i could pick some up fresh but no way and majority of the items on sale are either sold out or they never restock til after the sale.  i could give many examples of this.  After 8 years of running around trying to get groceries at multiple stores i decided NO MORE safeway.. I will shop where i am guaranteed to find what i need when i need it.  
Thank you Sobeyes for being so close and having a HUGE selection of fresh produce.

On the plus side, it's kept very clean. And the credit/debit card usage right in the bays was a great enhancement.
However, you cannot get a vehicle clean without using a brush. Not everyone likes to use a brush on their vehicles. I prefer touchless. The reasons for this issue are:
1. Very little soap is dispensed on "Soap".
2. The water stream isn't aggressive enough.
As a result, you will pay about 2x vs another local car wash.
If you like to use a brush, go here.
If you want to spend half as much, maybe not. You can get a vehicle clean elsewhere without using a brush.

We spent part of Canada Day discovering the beautiful gardens at the Botanic Park, as did hundreds of others.  For a $5 donation, they served a "Strawberry Tea" under a sheltering awning.  Lovely ladies brought us cake, ice cream and strawberries, and we chose lemonade for our beverage.  They had quite an organized system going for seating and serving and all were very friendly.

This organization was evident everywhere, with lots and lots of volunteers on hand to help you enjoy all the areas.  Children were invited to participate in a scavenger hunt with a map to affix stickers found throughout the park - it was set up so that you wandered the entire length and could view everything.  Along the way there was even a violinist in the gazebo, and benches along the paths for resting and viewing.  At the completion of the hunt, kids could choose a prize and then a petunia plant to take home.  I was impressed they had added a ribbon handle to each pot so wee ones could carry them safely.  It was obvious a lot of thought had gone into the day.

The flowers were amazing, with so many varieties.  The lily beds were especially impressive, with many of them waist high - I need to return in a few weeks when they are in full bloom.

Be sure to stop in at the gift shop.  Although small, it has lovely items and you're sure to find something your garden or home will appreciate.

Scammer alert 

Just wanted to let everyone know that Alpine car wash has obviously got a problem with topping up there wax I've been there twice in a row now and both times there was no wax but yet there's no signs saying there is no wax they just keep letting you think that there is and you waste your money. Also the place looks like they're not even keeping it clean the ground underneath my truck last time I was there was all muddy I know it's a car wash but the person working there should be maintaining it

The new Enjoy Centre is far more than just the reincarnation of Hole's Greenhouse. It is intended to be a hub for people and businesses interested in reducing their carbon footprint, locally produced items, and sustainable living. 

When you first enter, you are in the midst of the greenhouse, with lots of plants, gardening supplies, and books lining the shelves. Prairie Bistro is one one side, featuring locally-produced ingredients in items like sandiwches, soups, and baked goods. At the other end is a gallery paying tribute to the history of the Hole family is at the other end. A high-end home and cooking supply store is in the centre. Downstairs is a market with a deli and bakery. The products are largely local, organic, gluten-free, or some combination thereof. There is also a spa and an event centre that is available for bookings for things like large dinners and parties. 

The look and layout of the Enjoy Centre is very natural and earthy, and the staff members I dealt with were very friendly. It's beautiful, without a doubt. Just be prepared for some sticker shock - sustainable living does not come cheaply, at least not in this case.

Definitely worth a visit if you are in St. Albert.

I'll be blunt - I don't have previous experience with Hole's Garden Centre but  I liked what I experienced.  The Enjoy Centre looks beautiful, and it offers fantastic views.  Boasting a spa, health food store, cafe and nursery, there's definitely quite a bit to do here.  These elements all seemed to blend together rather well into one atmosphere - for examples, just because you were in the spa didn't mean you felt like you were in a different business.

However, it does not feel like a close-knit nursery.  It just doesn't.  Partially because a great deal of the nursery is outside, and perhaps partially because they have too much room to work with.  I'm used to the nursery's I visit being cramped and full of product.  In fact, I'd go as far as to say that Enjoy Centre had less plants than I was expecting, considering it's size.  If you can get past that, you'll find a lot here to entertain you.

Great service
Great staff
I enjoyed my experience here and the pricing is really good, I don't feel like I'm being ripped off like most vet offices.
Clean calm lots of seating for waiting times
I will likely make this my go to vet office since it's the second time I visit and I'm impressed with everything
Always have room to squeeze me in last minute
If you debating, looking for a vet , need an ear cleaning or nail trimming definitly give this spot a try! I doubt you'll b disappointed

I've been in to Privada quite a few times in the last year (I actually thought I had reviewed them already) but recently I came in for dinner with 2 very important people: My retired Aunt and my Vegan cousin from Van.... Now, that's when you actually see if a place is 5 stars; can it please everyone? Would we all love it? 100% YES!!! 

From the excellent service, phenomenal wine list, quaint patio, it was just amazing. And then there is the food... Chef Tony and his SO soux chef Chelsea rocks my culinary world!! The food is always unique, avant-garde, and most important: delicious! The breadboard is a must. Four fabulous loaves with 2 in house made butters - including a sea salt encrusted brow butter that never fails to give me the "O" face... And I have never written that about any food, ever. Other must haves are whatever meat Tony is currently curing in-house. As well as the cheese board, which features local Alberta cheeses, from 4 or 5 different spots. As well as the outta-this-world apple tartin for dessert. 

St Albert, you definitely have the Patron Saint of Culinary Creativity and love in your backyard. Edmontonians, get out to St Albert. NOW!!

Very disappointed. I ordered the Teriyaki beef and rice. Very stringy beef, and the rice was dreeenched in sauce. It was edible, but won't be coming her again.

I also tried some sushi. I've never before had sushi with DRY seaweed on it. And I mean dryyy.

Made Edo Japan look like a 4 star restaurant.

I really should not review this amazing tapa and wine bar as I would like to keep this hidden gem a secret. This place has a cool atmosphere and great vibe happening. The food, presentation and wines are all so tempting. They source local ingredients and make fresh baked breads. The sharing plates are so delectable, I can't name all my favourites. You can check their website for the current menu. The staff are very friendly and professional and are happy to help with pairing a wine or explaining the items on the menu. This St. Albert wine bar which is located in the heart of downtown has become quite a hotspot so be sure to make a reservation. A great place to eat either before or after a performance at the Arden Theatre. If you have a passion for food and wines you really should visit Privada. Perhaps I should be quiet now, so I can still get in for a date night. 

The short version: A YUMMY SECRET hidden in St. Albert.

Never been here before, but got invited to see a live Performance by Group Called Quartango and Tango dance experts Fabian and his wife. Amazing performance and sound. Stage visible. All well organized. Very small space but no matter where you were seated, front row or back, could not be disappointed. Attached to City Hall and Library.  Events are always running.Restaurants are all around and the theatre itself has consession.
The only thing is the one tiny bathroom in which the line up for women seems never ending ;)! 
Overall the space was clean and staff were very organized.

Our absolute favourite place to go. Whether for dinner or just to drop in and have a drink sitting at the bar chatting with bartenders Kayden and Mike.Congenial host Kaylen is great as are servers Chelsea and Melissa . 
For something different in an amazing atmosphere this is the "Go To Place"

Love this place! The staff are knowledgeable on all the wines, great with suggestions. Food is unique, not super big portions.  The burnt butter is to die for!
Definitely the kind of place to hang out with a couple girlfriends for the evening, great atmosphere

Oooo, I just love the Enjoy Centre!! I have been out to by flowers and plants in the greenhouse/nursery. I have dropped in to grab lunch at the Glass House restaurant. Sipped wine in the wine bar area. Bought amazing cheese and meats in the deli department of the grocery store. Poked my head into the yoga studio & spa. And my favourite part; shopped the decor/home stores! I especially enjoy how at Halloween or Christmas, etc. they have so many lovely decorations and gifts.... I want it all! 

Recently I was in for the Sturgeon Valley Food and Wine Festival. I have to say, having an event in the huge glass ceiling events centre is just fabulous. It was airy and light. Warm and inviting. The Enjoy Centre is most definitely worth the trip to check it out. Trust me, you're going to Enjoy it! Well done Hole Family, yet again you have made Alberta proud.

One of my favorite places to go for a night out. Relaxed, intimate atmosphere, great tapas (their charcuterie board is delicious  - the browned butter is not to be missed). The selection changes - have never had anything that isn't exceptional. The oysters are delicious and fresh. The tart is HUGE, worth the wait - I would recommend sharing this dessert. Great cocktails, huge wine selection. My husband loves their scotch selection. I would definitely recommend Privada and cannot wait to try their sister restaurant Revel.

The tapas here was surprisingly good. Usually, I associate tapas places to be expensive and i'm still hangry after the entire meal.....BUT NOT THIS PLACE. The 6 of us that went here got everything off the menu that had some kind of meat in it. The ones shown are just some that looked decent to show as an IG picture.

So all of these menu items don't have a real title name but just what's in the dish. The top left one is "scallop, rabbit croquette, seabuckthorn gastrique." Despite just the long name, this was delicious for a small plate, as a well as the "mushroom ragout bone marrow, sourdough toast." The bone marrow one i thought wasn't going to be all that good but the addition of the mushroom had all of us scoop every bit of marrow with the toast. "Crispy pork cassoulette, root vegetable slaw" was another small plate which had a good crunch, flavor and was gone instantly. The last picture is the best large plate we ordered, "stuffed rabbit saddle, black garlic stuffing, barley, burdock." I don't even know half of the things in the dish but it was tops. Every large dish was delicious but the only one we didn't think wasn't that good was the one with a single sausage on it, weird but it was just a sausage.

Located in St. Albert, this place was a nice surprise. Service was fast,friendly, and prices weren't too far off from other tapas places. Definitely going to try their brunch that I just found out existed.

Sal says: Just Eat It

Ben says: Good company good food good atmosphere

Literally, The Enjoy Centre is my happy place.

We just love it as a place to spend the afternoon as there's so much to see, do and eat.

You can easily wander around for over an hour, checking out the great stores within like Hillaby's, Evoolution, the bakery, the market, the liquor store, the spa and of course, the greenhouse and garden area (and more!). It's the perfect place to find gifts for everyone on your list as there are a ton of unique items at every price point.

Pop in and grab a latte and enjoy time in front of the funky wall or enjoy some locally sourced food and incredible eats (my favourite meal to eat here is brunch) at the Glasshouse Bistro & Cafe. 

Every time we've gone, the staff have been incredible. The selection of food and products in The Enjoy Centre makes you want to stay longer and it really turns into a great place to spend time with friends. Bonus, there's tons of free parking as well.

They also have multiple spaces for events and they run them like rockstars. The Hubba Hubby and I had the opportunity to get married in front of that funky wall, plus take photos throughout the Centre. Having the opportunity to work with Julianna was so wonderful and we loved being able to source our wine from the on site liquor store, as well as all the food from The Enjoy Centre for our evening appetizer and wine wedding was perfect! I would definitely recommend hosting your event here too - it then makes your visits to your happy place even more special!

Glasshouse Bistro, nice ambiance, menu. Unfortunately our waitress couldn't be found to take our order and service went downhill from there. Not sure where she kept disappearing to as there seemed to be few other customers in her section. Our pleasant lunch turned into one long painful wait after another. Tip reflected.

How do you even start to write a review of a venue that holds so much sentimental value to you?  For the first time in my yelpy life, I'm afraid that my words are not going to do justice.

But I'll try!  Like Michelle H, I have a plethora of childhood memories in this theatre.  I lived in St. Albert from the time I was 10 until I turned 20, and was involved in choirs, solo singing, and plays during that time so I was lucky enough to get to stand on that stage a time or two.  I never attended the summer camps myself, but I always looked forward to the show they would put on at the end of the season.

Last night, a friend and I made the long trek out to St. Albert to see Brent Butt at the Arden.  It was my first time back in that theatre as an adult.  When I parked the car, I immediately had a rush of memories in my head.  

If you get to the theatre early enough for a drink, there is plenty of room to enjoy a cocktail.  But if you don't want to sit/stand and visit, you can also walk down the hallway and look at all the pictures that line the walls of performers over the years.  That's my favourite part.

The staff are really remarkable here too.  Everyone from the bartenders to the ushers - they all have smiles on their faces constantly.  I don't remember if they are employees or volunteers, but either way, they love their jobs.  

I was late in hearing about this show - usually when Brent Butt comes to town, I'm one of the first to get tickets and am in the first 5 rows.  The opposite was true in this case.  Our seats were in row O.  That's the second row from the back.  I was a little disappointed at the thought of being so far away... but once I sat down, that disappointment melted away.  People always say "There's not a bad seat in the place!" when talking about most theatres.  But it's absolutely true of the Arden.  The rows are slanted so perfectly that your view is NEVER obstructed by the person in front of you.  You NEVER have to lean to one side to see around someone.  And the sound in the theatre is really great.

Back to the staff for a second.  I noticed that any time a guest had to sneak out to the bathroom during the show, the ushers were IMMEDIATELY on their feet to help you find the door.  And then they stand by that door until you come back to help you back to your seat.  They're like ninjas....

I can't wait to go back and will definitely be looking into more shows I can attend.

I was excited to support my friend Cynthia McLaren who had her art displayed at the Night of Artists Art Show, which was held here. 

Having never been here before, I found it a bit confusing which entrance to use and once inside it would have been nice to see a sandwich board to tell you where to go.

It's a neat idea to have as many stores as it does all under 1 roof. It was pretty quiet when I was there, so I'm not sure how busy it is normally.

The selection in Amaranth Whole Foods Market and Sandyview Farms is quite impressive! Amaranth also has a vitamin and supplements store within their store. There was a wide variety of options for both stores... it was worth walking up and down the aisles to see all the different items they carry.

If you wanted to come for a spa treatment, there is Wellness Within Health Center and Spa... and then you can grab your groceries before you head home.

Upstairs, was Evoolution Olive Oils, Vinegars & Tasting Bar... it was awesome to try before you buy... and not only that, they also have written suggestion cards to help with pairings and ideas! The staff is super friendly too :)

Hillaby's Tools for Cooks is a neat little store with again, a wide variety of unique items to choose from.

I have to say... the service was the slowest ever at the Glass house Bistro & Cafe!! It was also super expensive for 2 drinks... I'd bring my own next time to save the aggravation.

If you've got a green thumb, there was a nice selection of plants and gardening stuff as well.

I attended the Art Show in the Moonflower Room, which is a pretty sweet venue. The glass let's in a tonne of light and the ceilings are high so it's very spacious and bright. It would be a great spot for those looking for a venue with the outside feel in our 6 months of winter... while being inside. I was curious what the room rental rate was and asked at the information desk where they gave me a card to the person who books it as they didn't know.

Overall it's a neat concept, but just a bit pricey for some of the stuff they have to offer.

I grew up in St. Albert. So naturally, this theatre was my second home when growing up. I've done at least a dozen shows, dance and singing competitions on this stage. I've done summer camps in this building. This is one of my favourite theaters. But keep in mind, I'm biased. Childhood-attachments, you see.

But in all honestly, it's a great theatre for a city of this size. Plus the theatre is attached to the same building as City Hall and the city's public library.

Wow.  Outstanding wine bar in St. Albert.  Kalyan is a great host. Had the Gazela Vinho Verde for half price on Wednesday.  A very interesting wine.

Had the Duck Confit Cassoulet.   Absolutely outstanding.  It worked incredibly well with the toasties.

Then the Bahn Mi as a follow up.   Saigon never had it so good.

As an appy, Iberico Ham.  Good luck finding it somewhere else in the Capital Region.  Holy imported, Batman.

Bring a first date here.  You'll get a second one...

Phenomenal little Deli in St. Albert!  They specialize in deli meats, cheeses, and products that are sodium nitrate free, filler free, glueten free... and all around amazing!  

My neighbor had recommended this place to me the other day because I mentioned to her that I have been craving pepperoni during my entire pregnancy but can't have it because of the sodium nitrates!  She told me to go give Grapevine a try!

My husband and I immediately hopped in the car to go check it out!  And lo and behold they had all kinds of goodness!   They had farm fresh eggs, little red and yellow cherry grape tomatoes from a local farm pesticide free for $3.50 (awesome!) and all kinds of goodness.  They had shelves stocked with local and organically made glueten free pancakes, muffin, and bread mixes.  I could go on and on!

I also noticed that about 6 people came in while I was there and every customer was greeted by their first name!

They also serve sandwiches made fresh and soup to go!

All their deli meats were reasonably priced... no specials of the week... but $2.99 for 100 grams was pretty typical of their prices which is great for soidum nitrate and filler free deli meat!  I was able to get my beloved pepperoni in sodium nitrate free!  They even had quite a variety - honey garlic, spicy, turkey, ham and & ??? can't remember...

I left there quite impressed and looking forward to becoming a regular!

I tend to avoid fast food, especially KFC and Taco Bell, BUT I was starving. I was actually impressed! This place is clean, has friendly staff, fast service AND the food was fresh. Yes, shocking, I know. I came at 7:30 so was expecting the worst (as I have had at Edmonton locations). Everything was great. I am recommending this place.

I miss the old Holes Greenhouse.  This feels cold and pretentious.  The high prices just aren't justified.  I will go here occasionally in the winter to get my fix of light and a greehouse feel (when I am ready to spend 8.00 on a coffee.

I love this place. The service is great (at all the shops and services) and I find it such a relaxing place to be. That was really the point of the place to being with, after all. We ordered a large quantity of soda from both Amaranth and Sandyview for our wedding at the end of the month, and everyone that we've dealt with has been pleasant and more than accommodating. I love coming in here just to have a wander, and we rarely leave empty handed.

What a great place to visit once! Yeah it would be tough for me to go back there time and time again. I've been there twice now since they've opened and although the place looks very impressive, I want a real garden centre experience. I want to see dirt on the floor, knowledgeable staff that approach you. Really what I'm saying is, I like the old Hole's. I know things change and this is a state of the art European design but I don't think it fits here in Alberta. 
I have bought many plants and gadgets in the  past at the old Hole's, but they seemed to have gone away from those products. Now it's all about displaying it correctly with them. 
I also hate the fact they want you to walk through their extremely expensive food store first before moving upstairs to their small plant section. I must admit the food was great in the restaurant, great service and thoroughly enjoyable. Perhaps they should move into this area completely and drop that they're a garden centre!

Privada is so amazing! The staff are incredible! The only thing better then the lovely atmosphere is the food. Oh man! I could live on the bread, dairy and charcuterie from there. The brown butter is to die for and the condiments on the bread board are delicious! It's such a treat to get to mix all the different meats and sauces with the homemade breads! I can't wait to go back!

I first discovered the enjoy centre through the tomato, a free food magazine. I find that I go weekly. I really can't say anything bad, the staff is always helpful. They offer interesting samples in there deli. The bacon is amazing. I'm always discovering new products which I enjoy immensely.

Staff are way to bossy about sauce. I really like to spice up the flavour in my taco but the staff won't let me have what I want. I think you can buy more but why should I have to pay at one location and not at another. Avoid this Taca bell at all cost!

I ate here for the last time the other day. When I walked in, the workers were eating their own meals, which is fine. But I noticed that after eating their food and handling my money, they prepared my food without washing their hands and without the use of gloves... the worst part is, I ordered California roles, and I noticed the fish smelt kind of odd. I ate it anyways... I then had probably the most painful bowel movements of my entire life for the following 12 hours. I have never experienced food poising that severe. DO NOT eat here. There should be a health hazard sign right on the front door.

This one is kind of tough because I don't even think I've seen or experienced all of it yet. 

The cafe is expensive and the staff don't seem too well informed about the ingredients of the food. I don't even try to eat there after having asked once. I went with my sister and mom for Mother's Day and ordered a drip coffee in my travel mug and they filled it three-quarters full. I asked them to top it up because I drink it black and that seemed to be quite the request. I got a bit of a glare over it. The coffee wasn't even that good. My sister and mom ordered specialty coffees and food and seemed rather pleased. 

The natural food store is kind of a mixed bag. Some things are pretty expensive compared to the same product I have purchased in other places. Other things are not bad. Of course, as always, it's important to read the labels as things aren't as healthy as they appear. Just because they're "natural" or "organic" doesn't mean you don't still have to consider the whole ingredient list. But that's always a given for me. The line-up was long but they do get people through reasonably quickly. 

What I really LIKE about it is that it still has the old Hole's Greenhouse vibe to it which I think Lois Hole would have really appreciated. I was fortunate enough to have met her several times and she was a wonderful woman and a gardening pro. There are a lot of innovative gardening implements like wall planters and such. 

There are some unique crafty items for the home and yard. A lot of it reminds me of suburbia. There are a number of little niche shops within that I can't remember enough to name off. I know there's one for kitchenware - like pots and pans and that sort of thing. They have a spa - apparently my sister and mom will be having massages there. I was turned off by the makeup they sell in the spa because it has tea tree oil in it which I'm quite allergic to.

I love looking at the old pictures on the wall of Lois and her family on the farm. It reminds me of what a kind, giving person she was throughout her lifetime. She genuinely cared about people and smiled at everyone.

Came here for the Indie handmade sale and it was the first time to this facility. It is a beautiful building. I love the open and zen feel to this place. There's so much here with all the cute home décor and greenhouse. Wandering further you find a great restaurant and spa. The show itself was in a hall off the main entryway and everything was very organised and plenty of room to wander.
The thing that was not so organised and a complete gong show was parking. I would think for a place this size they would have a bigger parking lot. Especially being out on the edge of town. People were parked all over the place and they had opened a field just south of the building to park but of course there were no markers or crowd control so once you went in you weren't sure you won't get blocked in. Maybe instead of an empty field they should expand the parking lot. But this was my first time coming and maybe this was a rare occurrence.

A tiny little bistro with room to barely sit 50, Privada is stylish, comfortable, and homey - everything you want in a tapas restaurant. With low lighting and beautifully ambient music, the atmosphere is delightfully charming - enough so that even the TV's insistence on showing the fireplace channel can't dampen the mood. The wine selection is excellent; even the 'lower-end' malbecs are full-bodied and smooth - perfect to pair with a charcuterie plate.

Taner and I started out with the seared maple scallops, served with white wine corn puree on marinated roma tomatoes, as well as the prosciutto-wrapped asparagus. The scallops were perfectly cooked, with the puree acting as a hollandaise-esque sauce that complemented them nicely.

The asparagus - oh, the asparagus! I would return to this restaurant simply for the asparagus. I read several reviews before visiting Privada, and almost all of them (the smart ones) made mention of this amazing dish. Please go there. Please try them. You won't regret it. Also, several of my friends tried the Asian Chicken Skewers, served with wasabi dressing, and pronounced them delicious. However, the Garlic and Artichoke dip (served with the Chips and Dip) wasn't the best we've ever had, and the chips tasted too much like the oil they were cooked in. Oh well, can't win them all, right?

I'm completely obsessed with cured meats and gourmet cheeses (thanks to my fantastic UK MA friends, who showed me the way) and it was my birthday, so I went Double Butcher. The charcuterie plate can work three ways: select three cheeses, select three cheeses and two meats, or have one of everything. The Double Butcher, as you may have guessed, was a smorgasbord of all the tasters Privada has to offer. Our plate consisted of:

Dairy: Le Triple Creme (soft), Sir Laurier (soft beige), Bleubry (blue), Le Cendrilon (ash-covered goat), Contonnier (semi-firm), and Le Saint Raymond (soft).

Butcher: Westfalin Ham, Prosciutto, Pepper Salami, and Coppa.

Our tasting plate was accompanied with crackers, breads, chutneys, and spreads; my only regret was that we didn't get one tasting plate each!

The dessert shots - served in shot glasses - were delightful. At $2 a pop, you can try a couple of different ones without breaking the bank or having to eat a mammoth-sized cake, as is too often the case. I tried the Lime Cheese Cake, a mini-dessert perfect for lovers of key lime.

All in all, I would definitely visit this restaurant again. The food, the wine, the atmosphere, even the service - all perfect. In fact, writing about it now makes me think I should book myself a table again sometime soon...

Great service. Great sandwich. My new favorite lunch spot downtown!  I ordered the Pastrami on light rye. Tons of meat, fresh veggies, and the bread is super fresh. Not to mention, the deli has all kinds of pickled veggies, oils, vinegars, spices, etc.

Honestly this is the best place to eat in St. Albert. Food and service are exceptional.  We are regulars here and it feels like a second home as you are treated like family.

I encourage you to stop in and try it out for yourself, you won't be disappointed.

We have tried everything on the menu and have yet to find something we didn't love.

They have opened for brunch in Sunday's and again they didn't disappoint, what a great experience!!!

So this was an awful place. First of I come for fast sushi. If I wanted a half hour wait I would go to a better sushi joint. Sashimi was overpriced and onion cake was over done. I have never given a 1 before so I feel kinda bad but I wont return

The new Enjoy Centre is alright..it is technically a really nice place..looks great and there is lots to see and do....but it has certainly lost alot of the original atmosphere that Hole's always had. Which is a real shame..

Also one thing that kinda earked me was how expensive the cafe was..and it was self server (aka, you had to clear your own tables etc..) but for the high price you pay, you'd expect they should.

I was so impressed by Privada that I had to come back and experience it all over again.

With the sun out, we came around the dinner rush and were quite pleased to be seated on the patio. I really enjoyed having a front seat infront of St. Albert's main street; there was a certain charm of main street's building that you would be hard pressed to find in Edmonton. My only compaint was the loud trucks that like to tell you how their mufflers work but that really isn't the fault of Privada.

We started off with some flavored citrus and grapefruit beer which is refreshing when on the patio. For entreés we got the bread plate which had the always great fresh in house baked foccocia and other in house bread samples. The salted butter gave the fluffy spread an extra graze of flavor enough to make the mouth water. The double charcuterie board had pork sausage, duck prosciutto, pork belly bacon, and cured pork shoulder: all of which excellently sliced.
The meat was extremely light with savory dancing on your lips and the bread added that extra comfort.

For small plates, we had these fried potatoe pastries which gave more of an earthy taste. The texture albeit starchy was still smooth and mixed well with the harder crust. We also ordered a plate of asparagus wrapped with parmesean and thinly sliced cured meat drizzled with a butter aioli. It literally is a party on the plate which wants to move to your mouth. I forgot to mention that a perfectly balanced 65 degree egg was sitting nicely on top of everything. Such consistency! Such Flavor!

We had a chance to speak with chef Tony and he also presented us with a tomato tartare with a cream that defied gravity because it was so fluffy and light. I was glad this came out last as it gave our mouths a chance to ground itself instead of being further beaten into flavor overload.

Service was again very good as we had excellent suggestions and were checked up on to ensure we had a great experience. I would love to return again to see what other magics chef Tony will conjure.

Very pricey for a car wash, but you can get by for $15 in the early mornings for a basic external wash. I go for the external wash that includes undercarriage spray, triple foam and hot wax, but no Rain-X or tire dressing; $29, but you get your next wash within 7 days at half price with this package. If you have a high-end car and want to pamper yourself to a 99% spotlessly clean car, I would spend the money. I only wish they would let us drive through, rather than have to let them drive through the wash.

I wasn't sure what to expect when I visited the Enjoy Centre this past week but I was very impressed.  Impressed that something like this is in St. Albert as well as with the overall ambiance in such a huge place.

I was a bit confused, at first, as to where Hole's left off and other stores started but it didn't matter....I wandered around aimlessly enjoying how I felt...relaxed, happy and filled with wonder.

I perused and touched and bought...it is quite the experience.  Very home-oriented so don't expect to find clothing, although there is a jewellery store that was intriguing.

I love it and want to bring my husband back to experience it together....i can't wait!

Taco Bell has been a guilty pleasure of mine since I was a child. I noticed that this location was less tidy than I'm used to but I still went regularly. Then on one occasion, the fellow charged me 2$ extra for sauce (at the drive through). I won't be going back. I think my health is better for it, so all good!

For a special event, we had the pleasure of trying Privada for the first time this week. The decor at Privada was an ideal space for the event. The staff were friendly, attentive, and helpful. The space was clean and cozy with a nice mix of rustic and modern. I hear their patio will open soon with their propane heaters, which is an added plus. They are in a great central area of St.Albert with nearby walking and shopping.

The chefs at Privada know how to cook and the meat was all excellent! The presentation was perfect and I couldn't have had a better time.

I am back at work today and can't stop talking about the amazing fresh bread, the mushroom and apple spread, the charcuterie board, the kale salad with fried garlic, wild rice, and mushrooms - with just the right amount of vinaigrette dressing. 

And the Pièce de résistance was the amazing crown roast of pork, supplied by D'Arcy's Meat Market and cooked to absolute perfection by the Privada chefs!! Tender juicy and not a moment overdone! 

I wish we could have stayed for desert, which I'm sure was equally as amazing. 

We would gladly return to Privada if in the area and will surely recommend them to others.

We had quite an enjoyable evening. Being from St.Albert it is great to see a nice little place like this, and even busy on a cold January night. I really liked the wine flights - the 2oz sampler size of 3 flavours - it is a great way to taste different wines. My girlfriend did not enjoy one wine on her flight and it was replaced with a different one - on offer from the young woman looking after us. The service was great, very friendly and personable - although we did sit up at the bar. We shared the butcher plate and the mini sandwiches - both were great, though the butcher plate could have done with a couple more pieces of meat in my opinion.

Good prices, very good selection of wines and cocktails, great atmosphere and environment. It is great to see a place like this in St.Albert. 

Visit here and check it out for yourself.
Review on Google... can't say enough negative things about the deli and even more so the staff and owner.

Went through the drive thru for a later afternoon lunch.  Drive thru line moved at an acceptable pace due to the double ordering speakers.  I found the staff at both the payment and pick up window very friendly.  The food is what you would expect from a McDonald's.  Overall it was a good drive thru experience for a quick, inexpensive, lunch.

The Enjoy Center is a home/gardening mecca of sorts, they have the same square footage as some malls. I like that they have diversified since opening and now include a delicatessen (Sun Valley Farms), a scratch bakery, Whole Foods Grocer (Amaranth Foods), Spa, Yoga Studio, Liquor Store (Liquid Harvest), kitchen ware store, Restaurant and a Bistro. They also rent out some of the space for events like craft shows and of course the massive green house section they are famous for.

Their prices at the bistro and the restaurant are to high for the service and the quality of the product ($9.00 for a Panini that makes hot pockets look gourmet and it took 30 mins to get). The staff are inexperienced and it comes through in their service. I have been asked to move seats because I was eating my bistro food in the restaurant area even though there was no one in the  restaurant which is pretty ridiculous. It was not like I climbed over a fence to get there.(The chairs looked more comfortable so I wandered over)

I haven't used the spa or the yoga studio but the décor of the front looks very relaxing and the staff are fairly pleasant. The kitchen ware store is like downloading the food network's celebrity chef's Christmas catalogue which is great except for the celebrity price tag. I did however find a few items I wanted that Call the Kettle Black was out of within my price range so that was a bonus.

Their liquor store, Liquid Harvest is a great little spot they often have samples for you to try. The last time I was in they were offering whiskey which made my boyfriends day. He got to try stuff that he would never buy a whole bottle of and the staff really knew their stuff! Their price point is also very reasonable, I would compare it to Sherbrooke pricing.

I have purchased a few loaves of bread from the bakery and all of them were great. My favorite, although I can't remember the name was the Texas toast loaf with sunflower seeds. I also get the chocolate croissants when I go because a) they are AMAZING and b) they are amazing! Good enough not to share, nuff said!

Sun Valley Foods is a solid delicatessen with a great variety of sausage, cheese and both fresh and frozen meat. Along the back wall they have a shelf of sauces, chutneys, pickled products and a few other items that you expect to find in a deli. I love their knackwurst as well as elk smokies. Their nitrate free product range is also growing and includes bacon which is great as I know people with sensitivities. On the weekends they often have hot and cold samples of their sausages and a if you are lucky they offer cheese too.

But by far the main reason I visit the Enjoy Center is for Amaranth Foods. It is a wholefoods / organic grocery store that gives Planet Organic a run for their money in terms of selection but often beats on price. They carry pretty much everything that you could want in the genre and also have a health and beauty section that is separately manned so you don't have to ask the lady stocking mangos which facial cleansers are vegan. The staff (Amaranth not the rest of the Enjoy Center) have to be some of the happiest and most pleasant people I have ever dealt with in retail. I spent almost 20 minutes speaking to two ladies about their favorite hummus recipes and they even took me to their favorite products to use if I needed to substitute. 

I pretty much do all of my grocery shopping here even though it is more expensive than the mega chains organic section. I like to support local and if I can help keep happy people employed in retail while doing it, I consider it a service to humanity!

First, let me say that they have a fabulous selection of plants. You are guaranteed to find whatever it is that you need here. And I recommend getting everything you need in one trip, as this is not the type of place you will be keen on navigating on a regular basis (more on that later). It would be wise to set aside an entire afternoon, as there is much to look at, and you wouldn't want to feel rushed.

I was skeptical, as the prices are more than what you would pay at a place like, say, Superstore. However, after seeing how my plants are flourishing in my garden in comparison to the cheaper plants, I would say it's worth it - especially if you are investing in some bushes and/or trees. 

However navigating the centre is not "Enjoy"-able. Their staff is very friendly and helpful, though, and always pointed me in the right direction. It's utterly confusing and, if you need shrubs, bushes or trees, I would recommend getting them first. Why? Well, that particular section involves nagivating down multiple, circular, sloping levels, at which point you have to push your heavy cart all the way up again (not fun if you have bags of soil weighing you down). 

Anyway, I'm luke warm on The Enjoy Centre. I love the concept, and I think it's a great addition to St. Albert however, being from Edmonton, I'm not sure I would ever make the trip there more frequently than once a year to get the important garden stuff.

Dirty Yo! 
From the floors that haven't been properly cleaned in weeks to the staffs uniforms that have not need laundered in as long . 
This place needz to be closed for a week long cleaningz.  
Mikey wont be back as a place that serves raw seafood should have better standardz
