Great service
Great staff
I enjoyed my experience here and the pricing is really good, I don't feel like I'm being ripped off like most vet offices.
Clean calm lots of seating for waiting times
I will likely make this my go to vet office since it's the second time I visit and I'm impressed with everything
Always have room to squeeze me in last minute 

I gave it four stars because they are very expensive compared to some places

I held my wedding ceremony in the Park Room in the Enjoy Centre. I loved the look of the room and when I went to check it out (after looking at many, many venue options), I was greeted by one of their many courteous and helpful staff, who then continued to be amazing throughout my planning process. 

When I came for rehearsal, there was miscommunication about timing, and one of the staff members ended up having to stay much later than she had anticipated, but she didn't complain, she remained professional and helpful. The day of my wedding was even better. 

The enjoy centre offers many indoor locations for beautiful photos if you are afraid of what kind of weather may come your way, and also offers many fun & unique things for your guests to do & look at while waiting for wedding events to start. There is a ton of parking and it's right at the edge of St Albert coming in from Edmonton.

My one and only complaint is the crazy price (for a ceremony spot alone). However, for me it was worth it!!
I really enjoyed going to Hole's but I love spending time at the Enjoy Cntr....I can't wait till the garden is done.

Went for Sunday brunch. The place was not busy but the service was not very good one water refill and it took 45 minutes to get our food. People who were seated after us got their food first.  Food was ok. Not much vegetarian options.

Came here for the first time since the remodel with my 4 and 1 year olds.

Spotless and modern for sure and the playground is state of the art with a staircase parents can easily walk up within the structure!

My only complaint is the toddler area was not to my 1 year old's liking and my 4 year old wished the slide came down to the floor rather than the 4 thru 2nd level of the play structure.  Pros & Cons but really a lovely remodel!

Another yuck is the parking lot and parking at this location is a little tricky but c'est la vie!

As a random aside, my 4 year old was thrilled with the Hello Kitty Happy Meal you today!  Sometimes the toys are so weird and random but today was right on par!

I so tried to purchase some if the Valentine coupons (like the Halloween ones) but was told they did not get any at this location.

It's always scary bringing your pet in to be neutered and I was impressed how caring everyone was, Amanda was great she was knowledgeable and gave me a call before and after the procedure to let me know how everything had went, highly recommend!

Hands down the BEST place in St.Albert!

The experience is always amazing and we are noticing more and more customers are becoming "regulars"..

We go to the Arden most months during it's regular season. The performances we've been to have been consistently entertaining and have included an eclectic variety of performers. We've seen Canadian and international touring musicians and a few modern dance performances. Always worth the money and the venue is fantastic. 

Located on the river in downtown St Albert, there are several good choices nearby for dinner before the show. Beverages are available before the show and during intermission. Performers pretty much always come out at intermission and after the show to sell CDs and sign autographs. A very intimate and reliable setting for artists on the road.

Like all music venues, sound depends on the person at the sound board.  Sometimes too loud or muddy, but when a skilled engineer is at the board this location has fantastic acoustics.

The building was designed by Douglas Cardinal and also houses City Hall and the local museum. It is an excellent example of Cardinal's beautiful and flowing lines.

The theatre is also used by local groups and schools and can be rented for a reasonable price.  I volunteered there many years ago and learned a lot about backstage logistics and sound for music and theatre.

I was introduced to this wonderful place last night while attending an Elite event. I can't even begin to describe how wonderful the experience was. The Foccacia was baked fresh and served with their signature brown butter, the inhouse smoked meats, and cheese from the local cheesery. The kale salad was wonderful with both garlic and onion helping create and interesting taste sensation that left you wanting more (and I am not a salad person). The biggest surprise was when the crown roast pork showed up. Truly beautiful to behold and so tender it could be cut with a butter knife. Our final treat for the evening was an amazing chocolate trufle and caramels. 

If the food isn't enough to make the trip to St. Albert then the owner and the staff are. Our server was delightful and extremely attentive regardless of the full house. Both the owner and the chef moved about the room chatting up the guests. Recieved the warmest hospitality from every part of the team.

The restaurant has a beautiful decor, and although we weren't on the patio I can't wait to experience it also. 

Altogether a truly amazing experience!

Hooray for the arts in St. Albert! The Arden Theatre is by far the greatest entertainment venue in the city. 

It's an intimate yet still somewhat formal theatre that seats just over 500 people. I've been several times for a variety of reasons. I saw Jann Arden play at the Arden (how cool is that???) when she was just starting out. In fact, her dad was selling her concert T-shirts in the lobby. I saw the Nylons perform there. I've performed on that stage many times for music festivals through school and Christmas concerts. I've assisted adjudicators while other nervous students took the stage. I recall taking many field trips there as a child to watch live performances. 

Their box office is also a Ticketmaster location. Back in the days before the random number system, I recall freezing my butt off in the wee hours of the morning to get the best seats for some big name artists playing other venues.
Went to try some new whiskey. Very knowledgeable staff. Recommendations were great.

I'm new-ish to Edmonton. When I first heard of Lois Hole Provinicial Park, I thought it was named after an actual physical hole, not a person. I never visited the original Hole's and the garden is more of Sarah's deal rather than my thing. So essentially, I have absolutely no connection to the old Hole's that a number of reviews refer to.

Because of this, my review of the Enjoy Centre is a review of the building itself - which may have the most pleasant interior of any building in the Edmonton region. Sure, the cafe may be a bit expensive, and the Hole's Garden Centre may not live up to the old location, but the building is full of light. And the Amaranth Whole Foods Market in the basement actually offers decent prices on its food, at least compared to Planet Organic and Blush Lane. The liquor store also offers free wine tastes. Though when I went, I tasted a wine I wanted to purchase, and they happened to be out of stock.

But it can be your happy place in the winter time or any other time you want to spend inside.

A true GEM in St.Albert!!

We went there for our 1yr anniversary and we will definitely be regulars there.
We were greeted by the owner upon arrival and I must say what a great layout (small and intimate).  When the owner new it was our anniversary he let us know there was a complimentary glass of champagne when we wanted it (very nice touch).
We tried a variety of dishes and everything was excellent!!! (You have to try the popcorn at some point in the night!!!).
This is just the place that we need in St.Albert, perfect for a first date, anniversary or a night out with friends.  You can't go wrong with this place.

Privada adds style, variety, and late night wine/dine to St Albert downtown. 

Don't let Privada's curb appeal fool you because everything changes when you walk in the door. The 44 seats are a mixture of regular tables, hightops and bar stool and the faux brick walls give it a warmth that reminds me of Montreal. Located right on the corner of Perron and St Anne at the heart of downtown it's surrounded by many other dining options but none can offer what they have. Tapas has grown in popularity and is one of my favorite ways to eat since variety is the spice of life (and food). I wanted to order many different items but were told that the charcuterie board (called the Butcher Board) was large enough to act as a meal for one so we split this and each had a feature entree.

The Butcher Board was so full of goodies that a cracker fell off just as he set it down at our table (5 second rule). Four types of cheese, 3 types of cured meats, 3 types of crackers, 5 types of fruit and 2 jams topped off with micro greens and edible flower petals all arranged beautifully will ensure eye-gasms for any diner. There were so many possible combinations that every single bite was unique. This is true variety and I will probably order this every time.

For our entrees we chose the weekly features: Turkey Burger and a Flatbread. Both come with a side salad and were $20/plate. Two new features are introduced bi-weekly so there's always a new dish to try and more variety! The Turkey patty was handmade in house and had good flavor. The flatbread was also handmade and the toppings were tasty yet balanced.

Now I couldn't go to a wine bar without having a glass and they offer 5oz or 8oz options. I asked for a French Bourgogne and they had a Bourdeaux which is from the same region. I was told that they had a bottle that hadn't even made the menu yet but was recommended by a regular. I'm happy they take recommendations because it was a great blend.

Finally being open till midnight may not be considered late in some cities but for St Albert it's huge! This is probably the only place open that late without counting the sports bars.

Great food, excellent service, variety in food and wine and open late makes this my new favorite spot! Try it out for yourself if you don't believe me.

So The Enjoy Centre is not at all what I thought it would be like.  I'm not a gardener. My green thumb has resulted in me killing a bamboo plant and a cactus, so I really was like, why would I want to go to a garden centre? But people had said The Enjoy Centre was, well to put it, enjoyable. Plus there was a LitFest event I was volunteering was being held there so I thought I would go in a bit earlier and see just how enjoyable The Enjoy Centre was. 

Yes, turns out The Enjoy Centre isn't just a bunch of greenhouses. Yes it has a gardening section (a huge gardening section), but there are also other parts of this gigantic store. Like how downstairs is this huge organic (I think?) market with a large section of Sandyview farm meats. There is apparently a liquor store (which was at the back and I didn't visit). There is Evoolution, a store specializing in olive oil and vinegar store - and they have little sample cups and pieces of bread so you can try before you buy. I know there was an event space, which was being used for some sort of Youth Festival that was going on. And I saw there were signs for a Yoga studio, but I didn't exactly see where it was. When I needed help finding out where the LitFest event was being held the lady on staff I asked for directions was very helpful. 

I spent quite a bit of time at The Glasshouse Bistro, since that's where the LitFest event was being held. It's a big open cafe, and I was a bit confused at how to order (seemed like cafeteria style, but I didn't know what side to stand on since the lineup wrapped around two sides - might be a good idea if they had an "order here sign"). They did, however have lots of lemon water available, and the cafe itself was bright and airy, with lots of tables and chairs to sit down at. There is also free wifi (for an hour). 

The Enjoy Centre is like a mall/a giant store/marketplace all in one. It's very open and bright, and while I'm sure it gets busy it didn't feel super crowded when I was there on a Saturday afternoon.  If I lived in St. Albert or close enough to it I would probably be a regular visitor. It's right on the edge of St. Albert and it's pretty straightforward to get to from The Henday. If you haven't been to The Enjoy Centre it's worth a stop.

The service is great! Thats the first thing to know about this place. Next the selection is good and the pricing is good. We should probably go here more often because it is so good. The only problem is like anything in downtown St. Albert the parking is shitty!

Refreshingly unique for St. Albert.  Unique tapas and the chef really puts outs unique dishes.  
Food : One memorable dish was the fish head : fried and tossed in a sweet chili sauce.  Delicious and not something I've had in a "Canadian" restaurant.  Oysters were fresh, bread plate was really good ( especially with the brown butter ), pasta, prawns, charcuterie was well done, mushrooms on toast were delicious.
Wine : very good but I was hoping for some higher end wines served by the glass.
Atmosphere : quaint, fun little spot.
Will be back...surprisingly not as soon as I thought I would be.

The Enjoy Centre is a great place to spend an afternoon. I enjoy (haha) the restaurant and the ability to shop for a ton of beautiful plants at the same time. 

I was also impressed with the great service I received throughout the whole building, from the restaurant, to the nursery, to the grocery store. 

If you are looking for something to do on a Saturday morning stop by the Enjoy Centre and seep in the great view while eating a quality meal.

Beautiful space. We attended an event here recently and I was quite impressed by the lighting, the many options of spaces to host events and activities, and the numerous stores and shops to frequent. While at first I found the organization of the space a bit confusing, we quickly found our event venue and the space was well-lit, large and had a good stage with good sight lines. Staff were very helpful for this special event and the washrooms are well labeled and quite accessible for this special event. If I lived in St. Albert, I'm sure I'd visit more often for events and activities. The greenhouse aspect is great also though we weren't here for that purpose.

The Enjoy Centre really is a unique space, and that always makes me happy. 
There is a grocery store with plenty of locally supplied products, gluten free and vegan options, fresh deli,  and so much more. It's pricey, but I believe in most cases worth it.

The Glass House Bistro I was less impressed with, and that's where I docked a star. It's a cafeteria style, so you get your tray, and you pick from sandwiches and salads in clam shell containers, pre-packaged. I find the prices somewhat high, but what really made me cringe was when I pushed my cafeteria tray up to pay, ad debit machine gave me a tip option. Eye roll. Do servers everywhere find this to be a slap in the face to hard work? Does Ikea ask for a tip in their cafeteria now? I doubt it. Excuse my rant, but these tipping options are getting a little ridiculous. Tips are meant to subsidize the incredibly low wages that servers get, and also to show appreciation for the service and food. And I'm not anti-tip anywhere but a restaurant. I tip my coffee shop that I visit every morning quite decently, but I can see them standing there making me the perfect latte. Anyway, I'll end my rant and move onto something positive.

The indoor plant section is super nice and has lots of unique gift ideas. You can get a tiny terrarium for $20. They are really adorable and would sure make a nice gift. They also have lots of garden decor type items like statues and signs.

I haven't used the spa here, but I have heard good things about it from people I know.

I attend a tradeshow here and it was super easy to get into, and out of. Maneuvering around the cluster of strollers was another story.

Other interesting things within the Enjoy Centre: Evoolution Oils & Vinegars, Hillabilly's Tools for Cooks, Liquor Store, and a Wild Earth Bakery.  And of course, the greenhouse :)

Overall, the Enjoy Centre is really great place to spend an afternoon shopping. And look how much of my review I dedicated to being asked for a tip at a fancy cafeteria. I still maintain that is a little ridiculous.
One of the best charcuterie boards in the Edmonton area! Our favorite St. Albert spot!

My go-to for fresh deli foods. They have a sandwich service counter which features their own deli-fresh meats and locally grown and purchased vegetables. They are also family-owned and operated, which makes it an easy choice to support this local business. Be on the lookout for featured items on the counter. Scones, foccacia bread, buns - everything super tasty!

I really tried hard to like this place. I went there three times and can honestly say that I never left there completely satisfied with the meal. The restaurant is nice. Generally we've had good service and presentation of food. None of the dishes were so good that I would return. 

The first time we went there I went with my family (4 people total). We ordered two orders of the fresh bread. Each order comes with three pieces (and ones a thick corner slice) so for four people 2 is necessary. The bread is nothing special. The butter is really good and unique! We had the gnocchi, bbq octopus, chicken breast, and banger and mash. I think we had something else but can't remember what it was since it isn't on the menu anymore. All were fine, but no dish was anything to write home about. For dessert we had the chocolate creme brûlée and the peach cake. The chocolate creme brule was good. The peach cake lacked in flavour and was dry. 

The second time we went for brunch. My mom and I both ordered the eggs benedict. I love eggs benedict and try to order it as often as I can. I appreciate they are going for something more unique, but I can honestly say it was the terrible. The sourdough was too thick for the amount of toppings. The greens were cooked so I can't tell whether they tasted off because of that or because they were going bad, and the bernaise sauce wasn't good and is definitely no substitute for hollandaise sauce. My brother had the chorizo breakfast bowl and he said it was really good. My dad had the chicken and waffles. He said it was good. Although, it looks quite boring. 

The third time I went I went at about 9pm on  a Saturday. I really enjoyed the drink I had (but I can't remember what it was called)! My boyfriend and I had the chefs board. It may have been the charcuterie. Whatever one it was it had meat and cheese. It was good. We had the gnocchi, pickled snapper, and the banger and mash. Presentation of the pickled snapper was nice. Other than that nothing notably good or bad with the dishes. I like that they try and minimize waste, especially since Saturday evening is their last dinner meal until Wednesday. But I think it's unreasonable to go out a few hours before closing and for them to be out of the roast lamb sirloin and crab and corn stuffed pasta. If this is the case then you're stuck ordering from dishes you've already had and you don't get to try things that seem more appetizing. 

I think Privada is ok just not my type of food. I don't think they are your usual tapas place. Their big dishes although they say are for sharing are quite odd to share. For example the chicken breast or banger and mash dish (like others) you're served the meat uncut so you and the others at your table have to portion it yourselves. Although it may change presentation (which they are good at) I think they should cut the meats into pieces that people can more easily grab from the main serving dish.

When I think about it, y'know, the very first show or concert I ever went to must have been at the Arden Theatre. This place is nestled inside the much larger St. Albert City Hall/library building, but it's got a certain charm that's all its own.

You can catch an amazing variety of shows here. Because it's not a huge venue, only a few hundred people, you can catch tons of upcoming acts, especially local (Edmonton-area and Albertan) acts, from country to indie rock.

I may have even been in a few high school musicals that debuted here. Just sayin'.

If you're looking for a unique date night out, this is a lovely little spot with a huge variety of performances in a gorgeous, historic building. Great for family shows, too!

I like finding little restaurants with intimate settings.  This place doesn't disappoint. I had the privilege to partake in the YelpofThrones event and was absolutely amazed at the food presented to us.

What we were served I hope will be put on the menu at some point. But if this is any indication of the Chef's skills, you are in for a treat when ordering food here.

They make their own breads, cure their own meats and feed you well. If you are looking for a cool spot to take your special someone for drinks and some eats, I highly suggest going here.

We brought our senior cat here for the first time. They were able to book us in on the same day, which was a huge relief. Being open until 9 pm on weekdays is a huge benefit for those of us who work regular business hours. The clinic staff seemed genuinely sympathetic and concerned about our pet's health issues. The actual clinic was a nice setting. The waiting area and exam room that we were in were clean.

The vet was definitely one of the best vets we have ever taken our pets to (in 12+ years of seeing various vets in BC and AB). He was very gentle with our pet and she didn't seem as fearful with him as she has been with other vets, even when he was completing his physical exam of her.  He took the time to educate us on our treatment options and we didn't feel pressured at any time. He was very thorough and didn't seem rushed. We left feeling confident and comfortable with the treatment our pet received and the bill was very reasonable. We will absolutely be bring our pets back here again and are relieved to have found a great vet clinic so close to the city.

WEDDING VENUE REVIEW

DO NOT BELIEVE THE ENDORSEMENT IN BLUSH MAGAZINE. It was based on previous management and ownership and no longer applies. 

The venue itself is beautiful and unique, however the owners and management are a nightmare to work with. They will promise you all kinds of things before you book with them, and then will turn around 3 days before your wedding and threaten to cancel the event unless you pay an additional 80% for things that were supposed to be included in the original agreement. This includes items like staging, podiums, water glasses, sufficient tables, rafter speakers, cloth barriers... even access to certain amenities for your other vendors/caterers... the list goes on.

The executive manager/head chef in particular should be avoided at all costs. He was extremely disrespectful to myself and my parents, and refused to honor promises and assurances that his previous event coordinators had made, suggesting instead that they had done so without the current managements approval. He lacks integrity and decency, and brings up these issues days before your event, when he knows that it is too late to arrange for these items yourself. This is the dirtiest kind of business and should not be trusted with your wedding or special event. 

We went through seven different event coordinators between the day we signed the contract and our wedding day. Each of these individuals were either fired or quit due to disagreements with senior management. And after having directly dealt with the executive management, it is not surprising.

On our wedding day itself, the staff were exceedingly rude to our guests, stole bottles of vodka and craft beer, refused to provide water glasses to my grandparents and family, and tried to shut down the party early. They refused to return boxes for the cake and favors, and were exceedingly aggressive with our other vendors who were trying to clean up.

Do Not Book With the ENJOY CENTER. And if you have already booked, cancel it. Your wedding day will be stressful enough, without having to worry about whether they will try to cancel your event or over charge you. 

And if you think this is an isolated event, please note, that we have encountered 3 other individuals with similar experiences. The enjoy center has been deleting unfavorable reviews and flooding their web pages with adds and positive messages.

I normally like Taco Bell but this particular location is the cheapest one I have ever seen. This location wants to charge you for hot sauce if you ask for more than 2! Unbelievable! I use 4 sauces per taco! Avoid St Albert Taco Bell if you like hot sauce!!

My first Yelp review was inspired by Tokyo Express, sadly. I come in here regularly, as it has more variety in 'fast food' sushi than the Edo in north St. Albert. It's a special trip, as Edo is closer to home. On this particular occasion, my boyfriend and I were gazing at the digital menu, deliberating on our order, when the young chap behind the counter snapped at us to hurry up as they were closing soon. Not cool, man. This is not the first time I have experienced poor customer service here, mainly in the form of overt rudeness from staff. Lost my appetite...

Everytime I come here with my Significant Other, It makes me happy. From the healthy and local groceries, delicious oils and spices, amazing kitchen shop to the delicious and flavorful restaurant overlooking the country side and Big Lake. I love it here! It makes me breathe better when I come through those doors!

One of my favourite things to do in life is take a personal day here. I'll put on some comfy shoes, turn my phone off and just have a leisurely afternoon to myself.

I will start my time there with a massage booked at the in-house spa, Wellness Within. There's no better way to ensure that you're really really relaxed during a personal day than by starting it with a massage. The spa space is lovely and they also offer yoga classes if you're into that. After my massage I will head upstairs where I will start the second part of my Enjoy Experience with a killer iced vanilla bean latte from the cafe, seriously one of the best iced lattes around.

I currently live in a condo so I live out my gardening dreams as I wander through the greenhouse where the air is thick and heady with pollen and sunshine. After I've had enough of that I will spend another hour trying out all of the patio furniture on display before taking my sweet time wandering through Hillaby's, the kitchen goods store (I usually want everything in there, so if you ever have to buy me a gift I recommend you start there). And now that they've opened up an Evoolution outpost here I can sample and try out some new oils before I head back downstairs.

Downstairs I'll wander the butcher and deli before heading across to the organic grocery store. After I've hit every aisle I can grab a crusty loaf of bread to eat with the olive oil I purchased upstairs and start making my way out the door, back to the real world where I have to turn my phone back on and people can reach me once again. If I'm feeling like I really deserve a treat I'll pick up some flowers for myself on the way out the door, because let's not forget why this place exists in the first place--flowers.

I went to the Enjoy center to attend Glow Edmonton on a Friday December 1st. They had great crowd control and despite very far parking they had a very efficient shuttle service. We didn't wait long to and from our drop off locations. Glow was a great way to kick off the Christmas spirit and the best part was that it was indoors so you don't have to freeze while taking photos. They had a scavenger hunt for children and adults to complete. This is the perfect place for Christmas pictures with your loved ones and you can even take pictures with Santa. There was a makers keep market to shop from as well as a booth filled with random Christmas Knick knacks. My one and only purchase came from Holes greenhouse, a little whoville tree all done up for $30! Go enjoy the Christmas spirit with gorgeous lights!

Very very dissapointed.
I would suggest that Lois would have disliked this cold unwelcoming place.
Thats all about ripping people off.
To call it this place overpriced would be an understatement.
The $9.00 dollars sandwiches, $3.00 cookies, and $5.00 soup is such a rip its beyond words.
This is a place for a different class of people of which I never want to become one.
High priced stores that should be in Vegas or New York trying to gouge people who think they are rich living in St Albert Alberta.
They even block the view of some swamp across the road for those that sit eating their overpriced sandwich in the cafeteria, You have to go into the dinning room to get really clipped to get the view.
One could only imagine the prices they charge in there.
I bought the sandwich a bowel of soup and two coffee's for just under $20.00 only because we can afford it and I have never had a $9.00 sandwich except when I am in New York.
We went, we saw, and we will never go back.

One could enjoy oneself here, if one: 1) lived in St. Albert; 2) had lots of money to burn, and 3) had low expectations of this Centre acting as the greenhouse it replaced.  Beautiful space, but better suited for elderly mall-walkers and special events. 

Truth be told, there are few actual plants, particularly annuals, on offer. They seem to focus more on specialized seasonal plants, like poinsettias and Norfolk pine at Christmas, and decorative items like pumpkins, terrariums, and tropical plants.  I came in mid-September for fall bedding plants and was shocked to find there were almost no plants, a few potted mums with tightly closed buds, and that was it. Not even a marigold in the whole place! What perennials they had left were leggy, there were a few scraggly trees and some sad looking pansies. Quite a pathetic showing, shocking that Home Depot and Canadian Tire have better selection! All this greenhouse space, and hardly any plants. I was pretty choked that I had driven all the way to St. Albert and left without a single bedding plant, what a waste of my gas and my time.

The Enjoy Centre is actually a wannabe high-end shopping mall, out in a middle of nowhere industrial park. One of the reasons I chose to come out was to hit Evoolution, but I can do that closer to home. There's a spa onsite, an overpriced kitchen store, an overpriced health and wellness shop, and a specialty grocery store akin to Loblaws City Centre market or any Planet Organic. I'm not sure why anyone would come to the Enjoy Centre for such services, and indeed anytime I've visited, these stores are all but empty. The cafeteria is also overpriced and very average.

Honestly I'd only come back here for the special events and would maybe do some gift shopping. But I'll never make the drive from Edmonton again just to peruse expensive items I can purchase elsewhere, or to buy plants, if there were any to buy!!

This used to be a great place to walk around for hours.  But it has slowly been losing its appeal.

First - the closure of the deli area downstairs.  I understand that it probably didn't have enough business to justify staying open, but it is a real shame.  They had a great selection and was a main reason for me to come here.

Amanrath is still open, but who knows for how long.  Lots of gluten free and organic items for sale here, but I wonder how many people know about it.  Prices seem reasonable, but I don't have much to compare it to, so I don't know for sure.  I love that I can find things here that I can't find anywhere else - like Coconut La Croix carbonated water.

If you've never been inside, you wouldn't know which entrance is best for your needs.  There should be better signage.  The parking lot up top is often crowded because people don't know about the additional parking and entrances down the hill.

The shops are cute but expensive.  Good for browsing, but not so much for actual shopping.

The plant selection seems to get smaller and smaller, and I don't see much here that you can't get elsewhere.

Things have grown downhill fast . No more deli ,needles in the bathroom and plugged toilets .Too many empty spaces ,very rude cashier . What a let down . I used to love coming out here for the day .Clean up the place I won't be back for a long time .
I hope this place stays in St. Albert! amazing little place and the service is fantastic. any wine and cheese places I have high expectations and this one blew my mind! will be back forsure!

I come here all the time because the sushi is usually fresh and very delicious. It's also very clean and well kept. Although, I have experienced good service here only once. The staff is very rude and abrupt, often pressuring me or my friends to make an order as soon as possible. The sushi is the only reason why I keep returning.

Why do I keep coming back here?

I guess once upon a time when I was new to Maki, I thought Tokyo Express was pretty good and I did quite enjoy their salmon bowls with the sesame sauce. 

However, my last 3 or 4 visits here have been subpar - times overcooked, not fresh, and altogether incorrect.

On my most recent visit here, I ordered a Maki combo to bring home to hubby and a Salmon bento box to share with my toddler.

Upon arriving home and distributing the meal, I discovered that the sauce was left off the salmon in my bento box so it was essentially a steamed piece of salmon on white rice. 

Ugh... I tried to eat it but it was so bland.  So I hopped back in the car, headed back down to Tokyo Express, waiting in line behind 8 people to advise of the situation.  Their response - to hand me a cold little tartar size cup of sauce to take home?  WTF?!?  Seriously?!?  First of all, by the time I reheat that little cup in a microwave safe container I'm going to have about 1 tbsp of sauce of my meal.  Secondly, my salmon is now cold and reheated salmon is a no-no in my books!  

I could tell they weren't going to cook me a new piece of salmon and I didn't feel like having a tantrum at Tokyo Express so I asked if I could have a 2nd mini tartar size cup of sesame sauce of my salmon to which they wanted to know WHY?  Seriously... Yep, seriously!  So I explained that by the time I reheat it in another container at home there won't even be 1 full tbsp for my now cold salmon.  They discussed it amongst themselves for a minute and and then brought me a second mini cup of cold sauce.

No apologies - nothing.  They acted almost as though I was inconveniencing them by expecting my food to be as pictured.

Sigh... If I go back again, it's my own fault!

This past weekend, I was up in Edmonton visiting some friends. One of them suggested we go check out the Enjoy Centre. As I'm an avid gardener and plant lover, she didn't have to ask twice. I was also excited to see this place since it is the dream child of Lois Hole, and if you know anything about her, this place would be fantastic.

After a fairly lengthy drive, we arrived at the Enjoy Centre. It's quite an architectual creation. It has tons of windows because it is mainly a greenhouse. As we walked up the front, we were greeted by a lady who gave us a map. Down the stairs and in we go. 

First off, we come to a natural/organics store, I believe it's Amaranth. The one side is food, the other is more pharmacy. Off to the side is a spa and wellness retreat. Nice.  We continue further to the moving sidewalk thing that takes us upstairs. That's where all the plants and flowers are. 

There didn't seem to be a real structure to the layout of things. You kinda just wandered down one side and then back up the other side. You would find bougainvillea, some other plants that I think will not survive our climate, coleus, some annuals, ornamental pepper plants, tomatoes, peppers, then up the other side you have some perennials, herbs, geraniums, pots, and all the other cute garden decorations. Down the middle you'll find lots of other neat things like watering cans, tie-backs, hand tools, and a zillion other things you might need for your garden. 

Off on each side of the building are these HUGE areas that are filled with plants and flowers. But the thing is you can't go back there. Yes you heard me right. You can look at all the pretty flowers but you can't get at them. You have to make due with whatever they put out. That is very very disappointing not to mention annoying as heck. They do have this really cool automatic chain thing rigged up that all the hanging baskets are on. It slowly moves the plants along so you may actually get to see more of what they have hiding back in the greenhouse areas. I did see an employee back there pulling out some huge fuschias to give to some customers. So perhaps if you see something you like, you may be able to get it. Otherwise, you might have to stand around waiting for the plants to slowly come by on the automatic moving apparatus. 

The prices of the plants were actually not bad. I got a tomato plant for $3. My friend bought a nice ornamental pepper plant (which was really popular) for $10, a lemon scented geranium for $6 and some herbs for $4. I figure that they are grown organically and probably good quality if Lois Hole's name is attached.

Once outside, there is a fairly large area that trees, shrubs and larger plants are sold. We didn't go in but it looked pretty popular.

Overall, I was pleased with the Enjoy Centre but not totally blown away like I had hoped. It's a hell of a drive and there are many places in town that you can get most everything I saw here at the same or lower price. In my opinion, it's a bit over rated.

Given our previous experience into "Tapasland" food experience, I wanted to try again and hope for the best.  Thank goodness we did!

On a nice and easy spring night, we drove to St. Albert to have dinner at Privada.  At first glance you think it can get quite noisy because of the size of the space (a la Canteen, Corso 32, Woodwork).  NOT so :-)  In fact, there is a nice buzz of chatting, but nothing to make you need to lean over to hear the person sitting across from you.  As well, it definitely is a "neighbourhood gem" as I looked around the room and noticed many folks sitting who knew each other across tables.

Our hostess was quite nice and was very helpful with the menu for a few things.  We ordered the small Chef's Board, the mussels dish (LOL....and they were actually ;-) ), the small tomato and mozzarella salad (with peaches and pesto....no, the combination was actually quite nice because the early season peaches are not so sweet, rather have a bit of a less sweet taste to complement the pesto), the small dish of fried octopus and the larger size green salad with soppressata.  The preparation and plating was very good and there is attention to detail.  Also, and it is something I do pay attention to, is the salt content.  Salt is good when it brings out the flavour of a dish, NOT so good when it hinders the flavour of a dish.  In the case of what we ordered, the only place where I feel it was over salted, was the green salad.... there was too much balsamic vinegar with the saltiness of the Feta cheese used.

The sauces used in the dishes all seem to have a creamier base than what I expected, which means that when you dipped your food into it, it stuck to the food versus dripping off (hurrah!).  The sauces also didn't overwhelm the dishes with which they were served, another plus so you can taste the food with the sauce versus the sauce with the food.  

We also ordered desserts.  Here, my companion picked better than I did which is funny since I am usually the one who picks the creme brulee.  He did, it was chocolate, and it was quite good :-) I ordered the apple tart tatin which was also good, however, here I feel it was too much "tart"and not enough apples and a bit too sweet (which was fine for my companion but not so much for me).  Again, it was enjoyed and each palate is different.

My only "real" critiques are: (1) that for the Chef's board there were only two small wedges of cheese and the rest was meat.  I feel it would be better balanced if there were two more small wedges of cheese and perhaps a little less of the meat and maybe one extra slice of bread, one for each person :-)  and (2) that there are a few more fish selections since most are meat based.  The hostess did indicate that they hadn't gotten in any Sturgeon and they usually have it, however, it would be nice to see a few.  Aside these, it was a delicious evening with very nice service.  

If I can, I hope to return and enjoy the food and the space again soon :-)

The Enjoy Centre is, in a word: Enjoyable. This place is just absolutely wonderful to come to. Whoever designed it was an absolute genius, because I can't think of another building I've been in that has a more positive or calming energy than this one. The spacious, open concept layout with its many many windows allow for a very nice shopping experience. The upstairs is where you'll find the nursery, while the downstairs is where they've got the food- including a deli (I LOVE Sandyview Farms), an organic grocery section, and a liquor store with all types of specialty wine and beers (some of which are available for sampling). The Enjoy Centre is the perfect place to go on a lazy Sunday afternoon and to browse at your leisure while getting some shopping zen on.

It's nice to see it and experience it once.
We went there for their Christmas special event, "Glow" and I'm not sure if they have the same issues all the time or this issues were related to their Christmas special:
Parking is a disaster. I was driving around for a while to be allowed to go to one of the parking areas and it seems the traffic was not planned or controlled properly.
Then the parking was all icy which is a safety hazard knowing a lot of young and older people walk there.
Then we got inside and although it was nice, it wasn't worth the money and energy.
I personally didn't feel Christmas spirit and originality.
Everything about the setup was very mechanical without soul. Like a robot maybe!
I think something like "candy cane lane" is a lot better experience and it gives a feeling that your in a Christmas painting.

I will go back there for the market itself after holidays.
I think I may enjoy the market better.

This place has got to be one of the best vet clinics I've ever been to in my life!

When you walk in there the staff is always very friendly and always willing to help you and answer any questions you have. 
I've recently had my dog bullet neutered there and had a problem (Little bugger chewed his stitches) and found that it had nothing but the best of help over the phone. They told me to simply bring him in any re-stitched him up and they didn't charge me a single penny. 
I also went on vacation recently and brought back three puppies from Cuba. I had absolutely no idea what to do with them and the staff and the veterinarians were nothing but helpful kind and sweet and helped me so much I can never repay them for that. The puppies are now nine weeks old and healthier than I could ever imagine them to be.

I would recommend this place to anyone looking for a great veterinarian and veterinarian clinic. 
Plus they give you free Soda, Starbucks Coffee, and water! WooHoo!

It seems like fall is in full swing at Privada and I was informed that they were launching a new menu tonight I loved all the dishs that I tried and cant wait to come bqck and try the rest of the menu.

Lois Holes is rolling over in her grave!

This place went from being the temple of plants and inspiration to a veritable museum of overpriced crap and god awful food!

Whoever is running this place has no focus and his intent on losing a heck of a lot of money! Save yourself the time and a lot of money go to a real garden centre even a Canadian Tire for that matter.


This is a lost cause and should be part of the University or some public space. It is definitely not a viable business

Just checked out the Enjoy Centre for the first time to see Glow as well as eat at The Glasshouse Bistro. The food was awesome! I had this beat salad that was almost too pretty to eat and my husband had a burger with these amazing fries! I also had a hot chocolate and him a latté. Everything tasted really good. I thought the prices on especially the drinks were a little high but it all tasted good! The greenhouse portion was pretty. Lots of plants out, even in winter. The Glow event was super cool to see. It was pricey but when you see it (I can't imagine what their power bill is!!!), you can see the reasoning for the price. The Christmas store was alright. I thought there were more vendors than there was. So much of the stuff was for kids and babies! If you're looking for a date night, fun for the kids, or some awesome photo opportunities, I would definitely recommend checking it out!
legally blonde - best show ever!!!

Looks neat, couple interesting businesses, not that many of them were actually open.  3 pm on a Tuesday and this place was like a ghost town.  

Bizarre.  

Not sure I'll go out of my way to stop in again.

My spouse just stopped into this McDonald's. When She got home with our food the fries were half empty & beyond stale; I can deal with stale fries from time to time but this was over the top;  the burger bun was also hard. I'm not usually one to complain, but this quality of service was deplorable.

Our wedding was held at the Enjoy center and I would not recommend it to anyone. We had a terrible experience with management and our day was partially ruined by their overly agressive attitudes towards ourselves and our guests. We were forced to renegotiate our contract on numerous occasions and at one point consulted a lawyer to ensure we were fully aware of our rights as patrons. 

Don't book with this vendor. There are many other venues that are equally as beautiful in Edmonton and nowhere near as difficult to work with. I regret holding our wedding there.

I got to experience Glow at The Enjoy Centre. There was definitely a lot of lights to walk around and look at. Most people were on their phones snapping photos. The venue is perfect for bolstering your social media accounts with pictures, but as for a date to walk around hand in hand it falls short. $29 a person is quite pricey for a 20 minute walk through.

This past holiday season was the first year that the enjoy centre held their venue called "glow" that features indoor Christmas lights, shows and little train rides for totes. You can even purchase holiday drinks with liquor while your children wonder around and explore the festivities close by. This is a great place to be when you want tonchecknout lights walk around without your big coat and freeze outside. They even have a coat check by donation. If you ever get bored, you can even go downstairs and shop for groceries or check out their garden section.

I love everything about Privada! A lovely personal space, great staff, and amazing food. Every time we have visited Privada we were warmly greeted, and served promptly! They always offer great recommendations, and every recommendation has been top notch. The service really speaks to what a locally owned business represents. On our anniversary, we visited and this night they were very busy with a very large reso and it appeared a little short staffed, and for the delay we experienced they gave us our duck entree on the house! We will always return and you should check this downtown gem out!

Bistro staff  are not very accommodating and often have an edge to them that makes you feel more like a nuisance.  On the other hand, bakery staff are very friendly.

Also, it's a shame that you can't choose your plants in the greenhouse.  They have it roped off so you can't go in and they bring plants out onto tables in another room - not very cozy and fun.

This is a great little gem in St Albert... They have a great selection of deli meats including triple smoked european bacon! This stuff is smoked so much that you can almost eat it without cooking! It`s also only a few cents more expensive per 100g then the regular bacon which is only smoked once.

I must say that it was quite busy in there and I felt a little ignored at the beginning. I guess they have their own system on how to manage their customers but it seemed a bit disorganized.

Once I did get some service I realized how much they knew about their products. I think they also realized I knew what I was talking about as well. I was really happy when they let me try the smoked bison tenderloin because it was amazing. I immediately ordered 100g because it was so good and they actually gave me close to 200g for the price of 100.

I will definitely be back here to get the triple smoked bacon and I will have to try some of their other offerings.
New fav place for pho and vermicelli! So nice to have a good Vietnamese restaurant close to home

Thought we would try this place for Vietnamese pho when it was cold and chilly the other day. The food was ok, but the service was the most odd experience. The tea was only 1/4 full (had to ask for more water after 1 cup) and when my daughters soup came I was told the soup i ordered they had run out of. So I sat and watched her eat while they started over with my order. 1 hour after arriving at the restaurant I received my soup. 
Not sure I'm willing to give them another try. Was hoping it would have been better.

Piss poor customer service... couldn't find one person on the floor for indoor plants. Found someone in outdoor plants but they couldn't help as they worked In outdoor plants. Yes they were busy but still no excuse.

I have heard great things about the Enjoy Centre for years and FINALLY got to check it out in 2018 after attending Christmas Glow.

The little coffee shop is fantastic. They make your order lightning fast and the latte's we got were amazing. They also have an Evoolution location here which was a nice surprise. The ladies working there really seem to know their products and offer good customer service. A bit of a sad vibe going on the day we visited though as well as it looked like a little kitchen accessory store was going out of business. Regardless of what part of the building your looking in things do seem to be a bit on the pricey side and in this economy I could see how people might be struggling to make a go of it there.

I also have to agree with other reviewers who commented on the parking issues and lack of signage. The lot was quite icy the day we came which was a great source of anxiety for me as I have issues walking due to a health problem. I was not expecting it to be in the condition it was in for how busy the holiday event was. Also we could not figure out which door lead to what area of the building as there was just nothing outside for signage so we picked a door and just kind of wandered around till we found what we were looking for. If your not going to post signs at least have people walking the sales floor to help people out and get them pointed the right way. For those without their own transportation I also noticed public transportation seems a bit limited in this part of St. Albert.

Still I would definitely give it another shot during garden season as I love plants and flowers just to see if the experience differs/improves in warmer weather when it would likely be busier.

Corporations are much like people.  They can easily lose their way in life when they decide to "re-invent" themselves.  If you don't think this is true, I invite you to visit the Enjoy Centre and compare it with your happy memories of the former Hole's Greenhouses.  My own happy memory of the old Holes included the smells, the enthusiastic customers and the overflowing abundance of top quality plants.  It was easy to find a cart for purchases and the parking was convenient to the entrance.  As soon as you entered the old Hole's, you knew right away that these were people who were good at what they did and they knew their business. 

The Enjoy Centre is located as far from the old location as it could move and still be in St. Albert, as if it was distancing itself from everything it once was.  It's in an industrial area on Riel Drive.  It's easy to end up in the wrong parking lot because the address isn't in my year-old GPS.  Once in the correct parking lot, there's a sign that directs you to the entrance, down a wide, curved stairway.  DON'T BE FOOLED BY THAT SIGN!  It just leads to the restaurant, an organic food market and other high-priced things I didn't come to buy.  Just to the left of that misleading bit of data are two doors, one labeled "Exit" and the other "Business Entrance" I suggest that you enter by the Exit because that's the only way to get a cart to carry out all your purchases.  There's a third entrance called "Events" but I assume you need to be a lucky soul with an invitation to get in that one.

If you're an obedient soul and decide to enter by the entrance, it's a long walk past all that overpriced food, drink and bric-a-brac to the good stuff in the nursery.  I know that Allan Kellogg gave the Enjoy Centre a good review in the Journal recently but he only ate there and even he had to admit that it was expensive eating.  As for us, my wife ate there once and wouldn't go back.  When I trek all the way to a remote area of St. Albert, it's because I have limited time to get my plants for my garden.  I have enough organic food and overrated restaurants in Edmonton, thank you very much.

The nursery is a miserable remnant of what Hole's once was.  It's difficult to find the specific plants you want.  They seem to have rearranged everything from the previous year so past knowledge won't help.  There's something called a "concièrge", which for me conjures up that cranky old man/woman who guards the entrances of Parisian apartments and makes the lives of visitors absolutely miserable.  This particular concièrge was disguised as an empty kiosk, so they weren't any help to find what I wanted.  Fortunately the staff do know the layout but they spend all their time answering questions.  Half of what I wanted was out of stock and I ended up making two trips to get everything.  Yes, the nursery is also expensive but I concede that what they have is of good quality.

Overall, the Enjoy Centre has forgotten that it was the nursery that made them great.  I find the change of name and format especially disheartening when the Hole Family has such a revered name in the Edmonton Area.  By adding unrelated businesses to their portfolio, they haven't concentrated on their core competencies.  It makes for a frustrating visit or visits in my case.  Lois Hole, where are you when we need you?

The waitress was very good at describing the food but to a point where she over-sold some of the dishes and the food under-delivered. There was a limited selection of tapas. I had several dishes:
-The brussel sprouts were not exciting and rather plain; I wouldn't recommend it unless you need to get some greens in your diet
-The charcuterie board was good; had several assortments of cured and aged meats. It was nice to know all the meats are made in-house. If you're getting other tapas dishes no need to buy the $5 bread for the board because you'll get plenty of bread with the other dishes
-The tartar turned out to be lamb meat (menu didn't specify and I had assumed it was beef); I'm generally not big on lamb but the truffle oil masked a lot of the usual lamb taste so it turned out to be good
- I love bone marrow so I was pleased with the bone marrow here as there was miniature diced pickled vegetables to garnish the bone marrow and absorb/break through a little of the fatty taste
-Escargot was good but simple; seems like it was mainly the butter that made it taste good
- Cassoulet (I think it's French-style chili) was good; I wouldn't have ordered it had the waitress not sold me on it. Felt like a good home-cooked dish
-Clafoutis for dessert was made to order; it took long (almost 30 mins) to come out but you could see it sinking as it sat and cooled at your table because it was freshly baked. Could've used a more generous side of ice cream to go with the portion but overall a nice ending to dinner

So this venue aesthetically is quite beautiful. It truly is an elegant setting for a any large party or event (my sister's wedding in our case) as the flower, trees, and high ceilings make it quite stunning. The kryptonite of this beautiful venue, unfortunately, are the staff and management that conduct business here. Having been involved in planning numerous weddings and business events in the past. I have never met a more unprofessional group of managers and employees.

Our relationship with the Enjoy Center began approximately 1 year prior to the wedding date where we began negotiating our contract. At first discussions were quite professional and to be expected from a large business as this. Over the course of this year, the centre had changed event coordinators 7 times. That should have been the first tip off of worries to come. 

3 days prior to the date, their most recent coordinator attempted re-negotiate our contract culminating in an increase in overall cost on the level of many thousands of dollars. Despite our negotiations with past coordinators, they would not honor what the previous event coordinators had agreed upon. They even threatened to cancel the entire wedding if we did not agree to their demands!

At this point we had to seek legal consultation from a corporate lawyer such that we knew what steps to take. Thankfully we had documented the details of each meeting prior to confirm what had been said and agreed upon. After a lot of "hard ball" back and forth we came to a compromise so as to not risk the chance they would cancel the wedding.

That was just a flavor of the heart ache we experienced from the management. At the wedding, the servers were rude to our guests and the bar was understaffed. Bartenders refused to shut down the bar at certain times during the night and ended up delaying the events of the wedding. I physically had to stand behind the bar to stop them from serving after asking them 4 times to close the bar such that people would return to their seats and the bride and groom would enter. Beyond this I strongly suspect they stole much of the alcohol. Much of the craft beers that we had purchased had not been drunk by any guests. When I asked them to show me any empty craft beer bottles or boxes, they refused. 

When we brought this up with the Event Coordinator and Owner, they claimed we didn't purchase enough alcohol. They claimed that we ran out of beer and the guests were upset because we no longer had beer to offer. The strange thing was that the bartenders did turn over some beer back to us, the generic molson canadian. So we hadn't actually ran out as they claimed, and yet the expensive drinks had all gone missing.

For any who would like their wedding at this venue.... I would strongly urge you to re-consider. It will only plague you with heart ache. If however you truly feel the venue is worth it (because it is stunning) I would recommend bringing your own bartenders, or making them keep a tally of the empty bottles to ensure that things are not stolen. I would also recommend recording conversations with the event coordinators such that you have clear documentation to hold the center liable on their agreements. Also be sure to discuss every detail you can (whether there will be water served, whether there will be glasses for said water, whether there will be ice for the water, whether servers will serve water or only the bar, etc) as they will attempt to price hike you later and claim that these were services not included in the previous contract. 

Good luck!

This is my new favourite place to eat! Omg we had the cauliflower appetizer my friend raved about, I was extremely sceptical. Like how can cauliflower be that good? Well I tell you the way the chiefs elevated it is unreal I'm literally mind blown at how delicious it was! I'm still dreaming about it today. Than I had the short ribs which was equally delicious! The new chief they have Lee is an absolute maestro in the kitchen creating a symphony with flavours! I highly recommend!

Okay, this is totally embarrassing but I'm a fan of the basic soft and hard shell tacos at Taco Bell!  We're no stranger to swinging by on a Wednesday when tacos are 69 cents and picking up 1 of each kind for our family for a snack or a quick side to dinner.

I'm not a fan of fast food in general but something about their Taco Wednesdays keep us coming back when we're out and about.

And I like to douse my tacos in both their hot and mild sauce!  Now, if only we carried the same sauces in Canada that they have in the states at Taco Bell!  They have over 5 varieties there! Chipolte, verde (green), mild, hot, and fire if I remember correctly!

Popped in tonight, on Mother's Day (yep, you read that right), at the kiddos' request as we just cane from Avengers End Game.  When Bruce Banner/Hulk have tacos to Ant-Man, my 7 year old leaned over with doe eyes and asked for Taco Bell.

We weren't expecting much as this is Canadian Taco Bell, but Raj really went out of his way and showed extreme patience with my overly tired yet wound up kiddos. 

The food has improved in the 16 years since I moved to Canada.  Do f get me wrong, it's no Calle Mexico.  But my kids love the simplicity here and no one at Taco Bell gives them a hard time when they customize their tacos to boringness (one only wants meat and cheese and the other only meat and lettuce).

Thanks Raj for making tonight's impromptu Taco Bell Mother's Day Visit a success! 

PS I can't get over the French on the sauce packets in Canada, even all these years later ;-)

Came for lunch one day and tried the lemongrass pork on vermicelli ($11.95). The pork was delicious - very flavourful and cooked well. Spring rolls were hot and crispy but the filling was a little bland. I wish there was more fresh vegetables and noodles in the bowl as I found that to be a little smaller in portion size than other places. 

I also ordered an iced coffee ($4.95) and it was delicious. Strong and with the perfect amount of condensed milk.

Service was a little slow, albeit friendly. It took a while to get our food although we were the only table. I would come back and try their soups next time.

Every time I come to Privada, I know it's going to be a great night whether I'm coming in for a glass of wine with a girlfriend or a group dinner party.

The menu is always changing and focuses on fresh, local, and sustainable goodness!

Popped in yesterday during Rock'n August Nights to a completely full restaurant and patio.  Luckily, I was meeting a girlfriend who had space saved at the bar.

Bartender, George was quick to come up with a sour mojito for my request of bubbly and sour and it did not disappoint.  

The look and layout of Privada makes the most of the relatively small restaurant.  With wall length and corner windows, you get a good view of what's going on downtown and plenty of light.  The patio outside wraps around the block (L shaped) and easily seats another 20ish people.  I love the dark colours inside and the hanging lights strung above.  

I ordered the sous vied octopus which was AH-MAZING!  So tender, so flavourful, just perfect with housemate tomato sauce, salsa verde, and chives.  

I also nibbled on the house made breads, smoked meats, and cheeses offered on the bread plate and charcuterie board.  The house made brioche was outstanding! The house cured meats were fabulously paired with artisan cheeses.  I was quite surprised by the honey and food grade pollen on the board - phenomenal!   

You can check out their current offerings here:
http://www.privadawinebar.com/#!menu/ch8j

As always, a great night.  Looking forward to my next visit.  Thanks Privada!
Oh My God you guys... it's Legally Blonde the Musical! A few (but only a few) seats left... and with a surface, and many deeper, messages for all...
Outstanding service and the food was excellent. Highly recommended! They don't have a lot of staff, so please be patient if you're a large party!

I have yet to eat a sandwich here BUT I am willing.to bet it would be just as amazing as the actual deli. Good selections and great meat. On top of that the customer service was amazing! After stopping in once coming back a week later they still knew my order. Though a bit pricey it is well worth it

When we moved from Calgary, I was worried about finding our JRT a new vet. The move was very stressful on her and right away I did some research and found Tudor Glen. From day 1 they have been awesome. Today we had a bit of a scare with our dog, and the staff went above and beyond to make sure she was taken care of, we had a treatment plan and that we also followed the steps that made the most sense, for our dogs sake and financially. They also always follow up after appointments to make sure everything is going well, which means a lot. I 1000% recommend them to all pet owners!!

I have been to visit the clinic twice now.  It was recommended to me by a friend that brings her cats there all the time.  

The clinic is comfortable and inviting.  They have drinks and snacks for the people that end up having to wait for test results or procedures to be completed.  

First dog was a very bad ear infection.  The staff was fantastic about squeezing me in between appointments because of the urgent nature of his condition.  The doctor was great about explaining all of the steps that were being taken and they were able to clean up my little guy really well before they handed him back to me.

He is a special case when it comes to meds because he only weights 3.5 pounds.  They managed to find an antibiotic that we were able to administer.  

Second dog had blood in her urine.  They were able to squeeze me in between appointments again.  She is a rescue so she has some personality problems as well.  The staff managed to clip her nails, which is almost an impossible miracle and they were really patient with her when it came to her flipping out about other dogs.  (Poor girl pooped herself)

The doctors seem to genuinely care about the animals.  My dogs didn't seem to have a problem with the vets, although it is hard to tell with chihuahua's because they shake all the time! 

The website, newsletter and educational nights they have are incredible.  You can upload pictures of your pet and information about him/her to their profile.  They have a monthly educational night where you are invited to the clinic to hear a talk about the subject of the month.  They send you an electronic greeting card on your pet's birthday as well.  

The clinic is now open 7 days a week.  They are even open late on the weekdays.  This really helps when you have an "after hours emergency" with your pet, or if you are a worrier like me!

I bring my kids here on a semi-regular basis. As we all know, McDonalds is McDonalds. This one has the new automated kiosks and is also quite well maintained, cleanliness-wise. It also boasts a Playplace. (my kids say "yay.")

Today, they played Huey Lewis and the News over the speakers.

That is why they get four stars.

#heartofrockandroll

I met my girlfriends for tapas and wine. The wine list is good so there are lots of options depending on your taste. We shared a few tapas but the cauliflower, ricotta gnocchi and charcuterie were our favourites. Great place for sharing and trying new dishes!

Red Brick Wall opens 4 days ago in the old Yuzen sushi spot next to Game OVR and Ace Liqour.

Hubs and I were super excited to check them out.  They've updated the space and given it a bright cafe feel with 12 tables and bench seating along the walls. 

The aromas were heavenly from the moment we walked in, the instrumental music played softly, and a waterfall by the door trickled calmly. 

We were greeted by the young owner and chef, Cathy.   They are offering a free appetizer for the month of March with a minimum purchase. 

The menu is a bit sparse currently but she noted that a full menu will be coming shortly. 

We opted for the following:

Large Spicy Beef Noodle Soup for $11.95 - raw beef steak, shank, and pork sausage.  Hubs devoured this - flavorful and filing. The normal plate of bean sprouts, basil, and hot pepper also had mint and culantro.  The noodles used in this dish are of a thicker variety. The spice was good but we could easily handle more.  There is sriracha on the table and they will bring you additional options such as hot chili oil.

Charbroiled Lemon Grass Beef for $11.95 - on vermicelli or rice with 2 spring rolls.  Clean cuts of meat (she brought some chicken because they were didn't have enough beef).  Lovely spring rolls and dichon (?) and mint instead of usual basil. 

Shrimp & Pork salad rolls for free today (regularly $6).  The shrimp were the LARGEST I've ever had in a salad roll aside from when we make them at home.  I appreciated that the order came with 2 ramekins of peanut satay sauce.  The pork was lightly BBQ'd.

Oh and tea is included here - two thumbs up.  Dana - you reading this? ;-)

We will most definitely be back and look forward to seeing what new additions will pop up on the menu!  (Fingers crosses for a Spicy Satay Pho!)

This is the worst Bubbles in the Edmonton area. The slick talking sales guy had an attitude when I brought up my previous experience of a poor interior clean. He is focused on the up sell and not the customer experience. The focus should be on the customer, not how fast you can push vehicles through the tunnel. This will be my fifth and final time at this location. It will be an inconvenience to go elsewhere, but other car washes in Edmonton do a much better job...and with less attitude.

This review really deserves 0 stars. 
My husband got his car detailed, and It was the 200.00 pkg. I wasn't there, or I would have noticed how bad of a job that was done on the inside when it was finished. His car needed a good cleaning, and he was willing to spend the money.
 We ended up cleaning at home , the areas that were neglected to say the least. There was 4 pails of extremely dirty water from he inside.  For us to go back would take at least  an  hour.
 I'm not saying all bubbles are like this, but St. Albert is not the one to go to!!!!

We had a birthday party there with over 30 people in attendance. The food was awesome and the wine selection great. They also serve beer and hard liquor. This place has a gret atmosphere and attracts a good group. The chef is great and changes up the menu often. We recommend this wine bar as a great experience. Next party in November, we have already booked ahead.
Over priced yuppy place . Going down hill fast Bistro sucks.I can see why they were losing business

I had the opportunity to attend a private event at Privada recently. They have a new fan!  

They try to source all of their ingredients locally.  This shows immediately in the quality and taste of the food.  Fresh is always best. 

The patio is lovely with the chrome heaters and a nice view of downtown St. Albert.  They are located very near where the Farmer's Market sets up.  

Inside is comfortable, cozy and clean.  Great for an intimate meal for two, or small groups. 

I highly recommend the Charcuterie Platter.  All of the meats are hung and cured in house.  

The menu is always changing to keep up with the trends and the fresh, seasonal ingredients. A nice variety and some great pairings available. 

Plating and presentation is beautiful and imaginative. 

Privada would make a great date night.  The Chef and staff make it an experience rather than just another visit to a restaurant.  

Try them, you just might like them!

This place has gone downhill. Half the drink items on the menu were unavailable, not the first time this has happened to us.  Also, the place was not clean.  Very disappointing experience, will give our business to better local options.

This has got to be the friendliest little market I've ever visited!  Not only were they greeting everyone by their first name, on our second trip in, they gave my little granddaughter a crafty kit and invited her to come show them what she made when it was done - so cute!  She was thrilled and I was very impressed.  The walls were decorated by children's drawings as well - this really felt like a neighbourhood favourite.

I've not found anywhere else with so many choices of nitrate free meats and organic specialties, plus lots of delicacies to explore.  It feels like you are in for a treat!  With healthy choices! If you're anywhere downtown, stop in and take a look, you'll definitely like it.  Try one of their sandwiches and munch happy  :-)

First off - it's hilarious that Kristin K called me out in her review to let me know that tea is included here.  She knows how much I love a free cup of tea!  Sadly... it was not free :(  Maybe that was a special thing just for the opening.  We were charged $1.50 I think.

But that's okay.... I'm coming to terms with the fact that I have to pay for tea.

Prices were really reasonable and the ingredients were really fresh and delicious.

I had the grilled lemongrass beef and i've been dreaming about it ever since.  talk about tasty.  I can't wait to get back there and try more!

I was pleasantly surprised when I visited The Enjoy Center two weeks ago. It's not much to look at from the outside, but the upstairs greenhouse is fantastic! There were plants there that I never thought I would find in Alberta and everything looked very healthy. The selection was vast, although a little disorganized. They had some very creative ways of displaying plants. It was overall a good experience in terms of finding products I liked and having something nice to look at.

In terms of customer service, I found it to be rather abysmal. My order was close to 300$ and I asked to have a 6$ plant taken off after she ran it through (I had not paid yet). The cashier gave a sigh of disgust and begrudgingly had a senior employee void the item. Got a bit of a bitter vibe from the other employees as well and  didn't see anyone out and about giving people advice. Luckily for them their plants sell themselves..

If you're in the mood for fast-food Maki, rice or noodle bowls, and other usual offerings, this is a pretty good solution.   Although it's a chain, I've found that quality varies so don't judge the whole shebang by any one storefront.  This St Albert location is a fair example of their food, although it can still deviate by who's on shift when you visit, which can be disappointing.   

I like their rice bowls with either teriyaki beef or chicken, and if you order double meat it can actually feed you and a child quite well.  Maki is good for fast-food standards, but they are sadly chintzy about providing much wasabi or ginger, and often our takeout boxes will not have any even when we specifically request it and they PROMISE it is included.  I highly suggest opening the boxes before you leave and then making a second request!  I have no idea why this is a constant issue, but unfortunately it happens over and over. There are also bento boxes, stir frys, green onion cakes, sushi .... it's a good amount to choose from and is quickly ready to eat.

The Enjoy Centre is the new Hole's located in St. Albert.  

I think they are still calling their "Greenhouse/Nursery" Hole's but have named the entire place The Enjoy Centre as they will be housing an art gallery, spa, and bistro.

It's now open to the public but parts of the centre are still under construction (such as the spa).  

The Enjoy Centre is a nursery combined with a bistro and capaccino bar with plenty of space to sit and lounge while overlooking the outdoors through 3 stories of glass windows.

The inside nursery is beautiful and has the most interesting display of hanging baskets I have ever seen back in the Annual section.  They hanging baskets are on a motorized pulley that wheels them slowly across - back and forth - zig zagging - kind of like a conveyer belt so that you get to see all the available baskets.  

The greenhouses where they grow and nurture the plants are off limits to the public but you can view them from the area where you are shopping and it really is quite breathtaking.

The quality of plants at the Enjoy Centre is high - as is the price.  Of the 5 nurseries I have visited this spring/summer, the Enjoy Centre has prices amongst the highest but the quality is also amongst the highest I have seen.

They have beautiful starter plants for vegetables - an amazing assortment of tomatoes!

Outside they have 4-5 levels of terraces that you can manuever your shopping cart through for perrennials, trees, shrubs, etc.

They have lovely nick knacks galore for your garden - actually this is where I spent most of my $200 on my last trip there!  Beautiful sculptures, animals, old-rusted style hooks to hang on your sheds, vegetable markers, sun catchers, birdhouses, I could just go on and on and on...

I did notice that they are having a special this Sunday for father's day -
Noon - 4PM - A beer, bratwurst, and a biggie tomato plant for only $10!  I think I may have to swing by for this - a great deal for the biggie tomato plant itself!  There are also drawings and giveaways... I'm pretty sure they will be doing this sort of thing for most holidays.

Their website is:  www.UnearthThePossibilities.com

Their hours are:
Hours of operation!

Hole's
9 to 9 -- Monday to Friday
9 to 6 -- Saturday, Sunday & Holidays

Prairie Bistro
8 to 9 -- Monday to Saturday
8 to 6 -- Sunday

I give the overall package 5 stars because the ambiance, beauty, and majesty of the entire centre is quite breathtaking... Now, maybe I'd lean a little towards 4 stars because of the slightly higher prices?  But then again, they have to pay for this breathtaking building and landscape (complete with a pond outside with trails and benches to sit and view nature...)

A definite must see in St. Albert!  

*Note* they can get QUITE busy on the weekends, so if you are able to sneak out there during the week - you'll find it much less busy!

Absolutely delicious! We have been searching for a Vietnamese place in town since moving here 2 years ago, we have ordered many times and love it every time! The people who run it are so lovely and happy to accommodate all our little requests. Would highly recommend them to anyone and everyone

We had the vermicelli bowls (beef/spring rolls, and chicken/spring rolls), and they were excellent.  They are on par with some of the best Vietnamese food we have had in Edmonton.  The sauce that came with it didn't have the little red flakes that I generally see in it.  That was great for me, but if you like it spicier, you might not like that  (maybe you could ask for them?).  The service was a little slower than some other Vietnamese restaurants we go to, but it wasn't bad, especially compared to other types of restaurants.  There were more vegetables than most, and they were really fresh.  Overall the quality was very good.
Great oysters, excellent cheeses & charcuterie. The hosts and staff are fantastic.

I have mixed feelings about this veterinary location.
