Granted they give out free granola bars and slushes for the kidlets and provide superb care, I also found that I was pressured here to do more and more for my cats.

I had a kitty who had a stroke and by the end of treatment (2 days in house) she passed away and I was left with a 2k vet bill... Yikes.

I found that their services were consistently more expensive here than at my previous vet and my current vet (yay Morinville Veterinary Clinic).

While the atmosphere is beautiful, I'm just left thinking that it's a bit too on the extreme end for me.  If you're good with paying top dollar for above and beyond treatments or service, this could definitely be the vet clinic for you.  But as a mom of two young children - spending excessive amount of money here when I can consistently save 25% elsewhere just doesn't make sense.

I adore the Arden.  Do I wish it were bigger?  Of course, I do!  BUT the flip side is there just isn't a bad seat in the house! 

Chairs are comfy, staff are attentive, sound and visual access is great!

For everything from a cozy concert to a high school play, the Arden is perfect.  My most recent visit was for a dance festival.

The concession area serves both alcohol and standard treats - small but perfect for a venue this size.  It's located in St. Albert City Hall enclosed with the library and city hall stuff.

My mom did trip on the stairs once and the round ramp to walk up to the entrance can be a bit much for those with mobility issues but otherwise this is an absolute gem!

Arden, I'm sure I'll be seeing you soon!

P.S. Parking is limited depending on the event going on so keep that in mind when guesstimating timeframes for arrival.  You likely won't have to pay for parking but you may need to walk a bit.

So I've been going to this Bubbles location for years as they've always done a great job on my truck.  Normally just your basic inside/out kinda detail and I'm happy.  Not this time.  The young salesman outside up sold me to a$100 plus tax clean and then the truck came out terrible.  Over Promised and under delivered.  The right side of my front windshield, mirror and truck window didn't even get wiped down on the inside.  Where the "kid" said the dirt would be removed...nah ahh didn't happen , came back.   So I won't be going there anymore to say the least.

Seems that they care more about pushing unnecessary procedures and the terrible food they carry than the well being of your pets. Very disappointed about that since they seem so popular and have a nice office. There are much better vet clinics out there.

Don't waste your time or money here. Aligned with the past reviews, this place is still WAY overpriced for the sad quality of work they attempt to pass off as being professional. Charging $400 for a detailing package where the finished product arrives with dirt and dust that's clearly visible in the interior is unacceptable. The customer service is substantially lacking, which is a direct reflection on the management who needs to get it together. Would've have given 1-star, but after complaining onsite, they did lower the cost, so perhaps there's still some hope for them? 

Step it up Bubbles, you're not the only game in town!

The Enjoy centre to me used to be a one stop shop for a variety of fresh healthy food, a place for a lovely lunch and a spot to just spend some money. Over the years the Enjoy centre has lost the deli it once had and some other grocery space that turned into office space from what it looks.

While the upper floor has also lost some neat tenants it used to have, it does have the Makers keep which is a great option for gifts of just a neat place to find something unique for yourself.

The spa on the main floor is beautiful and they have great yoga classes at Wellness within. There is also a little play area on the main floor with things for the kiddos. So while it still has things to do, it just feels to me like it lost some of it's magic. Altogether, I still will go occasionally just to check in and see what has changed but it does not have the same draw it once had.
Vietnamese food at its finest!  Love the spring rolls and vermicelli bowls!  Small family owned business with the most incredible authentic tasting food.  We will definitely be back!

I closed my dog's file today because of growing frustration with the front desk giving the wrong dog food for the second time
I've called and and requested them to correct it. However, they gave the wrong food again when I asked my brother to pick it up. They are so disorganized and careless about correcting the file, I no longer trust or want to support this awful business. Don't let the free drinks and snacks fool u. When I called today, they did not care. It's inconvenient when I had to ask someone to help me pick up food and then I have to go back and exchange it. My dog has a strict hypoallergenic diet. I've decided after today to close my account because of the horrible experience since it was repeated.

Looks like I'm gonna be the one that disagrees with the other reviews here...

If you have read any of my reviews it's obvious that we love Viatnamese food... it's our "go to" for dining. We love Pho and Bun, and go almost weekly it seems. We have our favorites in Edmonton but are always hoping for a great spot in St. Albert. So when we saw that Red Brick Wall opened near Ace Liquor off Hebert, then saw reviews here, we were excited.

The excitement ended with our lunch visit the other day. This just wasn't a good experience in many ways. Where to start?

- the glass doorway you walk into was FILTHY (which was NOT a reflection of the rest of the restaurant, which is very clean and tidy). An older lady was walking in the same time as us, saw the door, winced, and left before walking in. Might want to address that ASAP...

- it was incredibly slow to get our food, at lunch time with only about half the restaurant full. When ordering we were told it would take about ten minutes... no problem we said. Our meals took almost a half hour. Need to be quicker when folks are on work lunch breaks. The part that was odd about this is that one guy was cooking, a lady was serving and helping everywhere she could, then a younger guy was for the most part sitting around by the drink cooler scrolling through his phone. Bad look.

- the food was below average. Heather ordered a lemongrass beef vermicelli bowl (she was informed they did not have any beef, so she switched to chicken). She received a half full, lukewarm bowl a half hour later that was missing the spring rolls. I ordered Beef Satay soup. Again lukewarm, and the peanut flavor and spice was underwhelming. Also, they had shrimp in their Beef Satay soup (never had that before) that gave the soup a bit of a fishy flavor that I was not fond of.

  We ordered the grilled chicken salad rolls to start, which were fantastic (although the dipping sauce had no flavor, it was literally a brown paste that we could not discern what it was supposed to taste like).

  I hope they get their ducks in a row as we could again use  good Vietnamese spot in St. Albert. But for now we will continue to drive into Edmonton and hit our regular haunts where we know we will be happy.

Privada Wine &Tapas... "Tapas" are a wide variety of appetizers, or snacks in Spanish cuisine according to Wikipedia. 

In Privada, in St. Albert, it's of Argentinean cuisine origin. Doesn't that sound so Old World, so romantic... 

Not only the type of cuisine sounds romantic and adventurous...the experience is absolutely amazing to the taste buds.

I'm Vegan and this review is from my experience and perspective. Though I did come along with my trusted carnivore companions to tell let you know what they thought of the food as well.  Truth be told were not so far off from one another.

The Menu is a one pager. No specific gimmicky names but the specific components of the dishes. Which in itself is very beautiful in its simplicity....cause what you get is what you get. 

"Simplicity is the ultimate sophistication" - Da Vinci

It's vegetarian friendly but vegan is a little trickier.  And of course, absolutely caters to the carnivore. 

Our server,  the beautiful girl with the blue eye shadow was so friendly and helpful,  I couldn't help but feel she was a long lost friend. Told me she will ask the kitchen staff if they can do something for a veganite.  My long lost family in the kitchen said yes and accommodated a long lost relative into dishes they were able to make vegan.

That is the ultimate in customer service!
I have pics but no names of the dishes.  The ones I ate was wonderful and my trusted ones told me the same. 

It's a plate sharing thing. To which many agree 'sharing is caring'.

My carnivore family told me their oysters were divine and the house-made butter tasted like Christmas.

The vegan dishes they made were elegant which were a bounty of flavours.

The Privada staff was wonderful! 

The atmosphere felt like some place where grape vines nap and where old friends come to unwind to have a laugh.  

It's where one enjoys the comforts of that nice warm feeling you get in your stomach ....a meal shared with those you care about most in the world.

Definitely a place to come back too! 
It's an indulgence you won't forget.

Parking found along the the street in downtown St. Albert. Easy to find.

I love hearing that an event I want to attend is held at the Arden - it's definitely my favourite venue for viewing  :-)  The seating is very comfortable with sufficient leg room, each row is easy to access once inside the theatre, parking is free (although across the street, so be prepared for a short walk), there's a snack bar, it's next to the library with indoor access, there's not much more I could ask for!

My only concern is that for those with mobility issues, you either have to go up a lengthy flight of shallow steps, or up a winding walkway that is difficult for anyone on crutches or with leg/foot issues to manage.  I found that ushers were willing to allow early entry for anyone who needed extra consideration which is much appreciated.

Now don't get me wrong, they make exactly the food you'd expect from a Taco Bell. This review is more about the employees and service than anything else.

The employees are  polite enough to customers, if sometimes curt, but between themselves it's somewhat uncomfortable to watch and hear interactions. Hearing the veterans berate one of their new hires over something that isn't their fault doesn't necessarily make for a pleasant wait for food or stay-in dining experience. Not the quickest service, and there's a Taco Time across the street that does almost the same thing better and keeps their employee conflicts to a minimum. I have to call this a skip.
I had the supreme crunch wrap and it tastes like someone used the ingredients in a shitty bowling alley to make this, severely disappointed. Awful, the only good about Taco Bell is the baja blast.

LOVE LOVE LOVE this venue - I went out for a girl's night for the Glow Winter Festival, and I'd have to say they could not have picked a better venue for the event. The free parking was great, but the free shuttle to and from the parking lot was even better - would have been a very long, cold walk without it. I found it easy to navigate around the building as well and thoroughly enjoyed the event altogether.
Great food and service as always, best place to get subs in town.

I am a huge fan of anything Vietnamese.  So when I heard about this place from a friend And fellow Yelper Dana I knew I had to go.  As usual I got their beef satay.  I found it to be milder than most that I've had.  What I love is that you can choose the size you want.  I went with a small and of course it's still a large portion. It was still good though.  The place itself is quaint and nicely done.  They have a decent amount of seating for a Vietnamese place.  You come you order food comes quickly you eat and you leave.  They have a small menu I was expecting a bit more.  I will definitely be coming back to try a few other items on the menu.
I always want to support this company but the prices are out of hand!!! 70.00 for just a wash inside and out. Went next door and spent 7.00 for everything and too about 25 mins.

I'm not one to leave bad reviews. This place is pretty bad though. I work construction, so I usually stop and order a coffee and breakfast sandwich on my way to work. I can't say much for the afternoon or evening crews, but I can say 100% the morning crew either has no idea what they are doing or don't care. 5 mornings in a row they've messed up a triple triple coffee. Not in a minor sense, in a "there is 1 cream and no sugar" every time sense. You could spell out your sandwich order, and they'd still get it wrong. The English muffins are burnt about 70% of the time. Until something changes, it gets a 1/5 from me. Highly wouldn't recommend.
Best Vietnamese subs and spring rolls I've tasted since coming to Edmonton from Winnipeg!

One of my favourite places to go to just write. They have a great Cafe / bistro. Good and beverages are good. Bit pricey but a lot of it is green/sustainable food so I don't mind paying that little extra. 

The service was a bit slow when we arrived but friendly. The atmosphere is what keeps me coming back. Despite it being in the middle of no where it seems - the ability to feel outside even in the depth of our cold winters is golden. 

The place has a bakery, fantastic market/grocer, green house, indoor plants too!, and a liquor store. Definitely recommend to check them out!

I LOVE this place. It has the most zen environment, filled with plants and sunlight. It's wonderful. Honestly, you will feel so relaxed strolling through this place or sitting and enjoying a snack. The ambiance is fantastic. It would be a great place to take a date and browse through.

The grocery store is cool. It's filled with a mixture of foods - local, organic, non-mainstream brands. For a little space, it offers a vast amount of selection for reasonable prices.

The greenhouse was beautiful. Filled with rows and rows of different plants, gardening accessories, and knick knacks. Plus there are plenty of cute little houseplants in ready to purchase plants!

Dont live in St Albert but was heading there next door for a cocert at Arden theatre. Saw the reviews online and decided to try. We were lucky to get a  reservation early friday evening before the show. Staff were welcoming, decor was elegant and definitely worth trying again. It has style and class and a great dinner menu with great cocktails and wines. They have specials so check online or ask when making a reservation. Its a mix of high seated tables and low. You never truly feel crowded.
There is multitude of tapas to choose from and if you like Oysters, its worth ordering. If you like Chacuterie, the Butcher board has variety and definitely sharable. The main dishes are feature items that change bi weekly so you are never getting the same thing if you choose to go more often than not. 
Parking is available all around and the place is open until midnight. Highly recommended.
Great service by knowledgeable and polite staff!

My dog was having some issues recently and I decided he needed to get checked out. Not near my regular vet but felt it was more important to get him in than to wait. Called in and they were able to fit me in quickly that day. All staff were friendly and helpful, especially they veterinarian. Love to see people who work with animals having a genuine love for them and doing everything they can to keep them relaxed and comfortable. Definitely will be back, very satisfied.

I've been going to Tudor Glen for 10 years. My cat is a special case "spicy" and they are completely understanding of the situation. They take his temperament into consideration and make the experience as positive as possible. Thank you to the staff at Tudor Glen from the front counter to the techs and the vets! I feel like my furr baby is safe in your hands.

Moving this from an original 2 star review to a 4 star review. We gave Red Brick Wall another chance and it's since become a favourite of ours. Awesome food and super friendly owners. Our first experience was lacking, but every other visit (dine in and take out) has been excellent. Credit where credit is due and I have to adjust my original post.

Being an avid gardener, I'd been wanting to visit The Enjoy Centre for the longest time, but I don't get to St. Albert very often, so it took a concerted effort to make my first visit. 

I recently won passes for the Sturgeon Valley Food and Wine Festival, so Allan G. and I visited for the first time. What a great place! I fully intend on coming back when I have more time to browse, and am husband-less. It's more of an Electric Laini-land kind of place. 

The festival was in the large open event space, but we also browsed in the kitchenwares store and took a quick run through the grocery market downstairs. Imagine a sort of Planet Organic, with all sorts of exotic products. I'd love to go stock up on interesting cheeses, chocolates, and goodies when I have more time. But I fully expect the prices to be astronomical, simply because of the products themselves and the environment in which they're being bought. 

Didn't make it to any of the eateries this time, simply because of our destination, but they could definitely use a few more vendors. I was still hungry afterward! Should have gone earlier and stopped in for a snack. :)

And I definitely need to come back during the summer when the greenhouses are bursting at the seams. With us hoping to buy a house next year, I'll need plenty of plants to pretty up the garden!

Nice little theatre in St Albert! We came here to see the Post Secret live event and it was a really great size for it - nice and intimate, fitting about 400 people. The lobby and washrooms were clean and there was a concession. 

My only gripe was that parking is a little far (across the street in a PACKED lot), and the only reason I'm complaining about that is because it was -30.

The Enjoy Centre is one of St. Albert's brightest gems. Visit the place on a weekend and grab a beautiful brunch at the Glasshouse Bistro, a cup of delicious Iconoclast coffee from the cafe, some decorative plants from Holes, and a wheel of Sylvan Star gouda from the Amaranth Whole Foods Market.

There's plenty to see and do at the centre for those who love to eat and shop local! The centre also hosts some great events, such as the Sturgeon Valley Wine and Food Festival, and produces some great programs and workshops for budding gardeners, sommeliers, and much more.

Well worth a visit!

The food and service were both excellent and the atmosphere was very good but the prices were ridiculously inflated. The bread plate cost five dollars and was five (for two people) half slices of nondescript bread with a spread so disgusting looking I didn't dare try it. My husband said it might have been brown butter, but that isn't normally cold!! The tapas sized fish of the day (market price) was yellow tail tuna and turned out when we got the check to cost $28 for a very tiny portion. I don't think we would return.

Whenever I am meeting friends or family in St.Albert this is always my go to for delicious tapas and drinks! 

The owners and chefs believe in serving everything as seasonally as possible, with means a rotating menu, and for me generally different things to try each season! I have honestly never ordered something I didn't like here.  They have a great selection of wines, local beer and cocktails, so anything you want is covered.  

One of my favourites, if you're looking to indulge is the apple tart-tatin which is baked fresh to order and it comes out all warm and amazing.  The charcuterie is definitely a winner too, they even make the charcuterie in house, and the quality is amazing! 

I'm looking forward to trying the new restaurant the owners opened downtown Edmonton called Revel!

2007 Jeep Cherokee 35K KM Absolutely the worst Auto detailing service in the Edmonton area, Truck was fairly clean to begin with had been Detailed in Jan 2013 went in for spring cleaning in may 2013 after just 4000KM they missed so much stuff could not even list it all. Had to go back 4 times and they still did not get it all.  Finally just gave up.  Will never ever use again for auto detailing. Save your money and go elsewhere. In fact go anywhere else

Okay.... where to start....I showed myself today Sept 26,2018 to that particular DETAILING SHOP which is supposed to be a professional car detailing... First at my arrival NO ONE came to me for a detailing service I had to go inside to ask for service so...first sign that it wouldn't be a good move but I decided to give it a try....and go on with it !!!! Well, it was my first mistake. Second,my car wash and detailing omg....I should have went to the next car wash ( Do it yourself ) because the detailing on my truck is a mess and I don't exaggerate carpets were not washed and cleaned, side,rear,running boards on my truck has miss and hits like if the work was butchered they just simply did a sloppy job for $79.00 it was just throwing my money to the trash. I have so much spots of dirt that if you want to waste or throw your money away its the place..... I am not bashing but I have to give my reality check and also advise people like me that wants a professional place for your money to inform people that if you want a decent detailing done well thats not the place ( anyways for me ) So disappointed of the work that was my first and last time for sure..I should've read the review before I went there !

I hope that my review will help others to make a wise choice !

This is a KFC & Taco Bell combination store. I ordered a cheesy  Gordita Crunch combo with fries supreme and a 7up.  I went for the fries supreme first, there was almost meat and it tasted old. I couldn't even eat 3 bites of it. (And I always eat all of my fries supreme) so I opened my cheesy Gordita crunch and the wrapper was so dirty it looked like it had been used before. Again there was almost no meat on it, or lettuce, there was cheese on top, but it  also tasted old and wasn't hot all the way through. I am done with this location. It's such a disappointment now.

This is a review for the Glow Winter Festival that is currently being held until mid-December.

They have beautiful displays worthy of pics with family, loved ones or just selfies.  The only bad thing is that some will have a bit of a lineup to get your turn.  The other thing which can be frustrating is the crowd, if you're trying to get a decent pic of something without people getting in the way.  Can almost make a game of it.  I went on a weeknight and it was very busy, so I can't imagine what it will be like on the weekends.  There are a few things to keep the kids entertained, like a playground and stepping stone lights or the most popular was running through a bunch of hanging lights.  They also have Santa there too.

They also have concessions inside, outside food and drinks not allowed.  The prices I saw were typical of fair ground prices.  $2 for bottle water, $4.50 for small popcorn, $6.50 for mini donuts etc..

Also be warned, the lineup to get in the parking lot was long and took awhile.  But we went at 6.  I would suggest going around 730 or after, as I left at 8 and there was no lineup of cars any more.  You only need like 2 hours at most I think.  It goes 4-10.  And nice it's all indoor so weather doesn't play a factor.

Buy your tix online as it is a bit cheaper.  It was cool to check out once, and I'm glad didn't go on a weekend since was pretty busy this night already.

This was our second visit here with my son, he enjoyed his meal the first time but has been bugging me to go back to try the satay soup so off we went. We happened to go in during St. Albert dining week and they had a couple of specials, one included the satay soup so we went for it! The salad roll was super good, very light without the noodles inside and I loved the added crunch of the spring roll wrapper inside! We "shared" an order of green onion cakes (my kid adores them) which are also delicious. My son really loved the satay soup and was telling me the whole time that it was so good that he didn't even want to pick out the cucumber (which he normally doesn't eat lol). I had the lemongrass chicken vermicelli bowl last time and it was delicious so I ordered it again.  The service is wonderful, they are so friendly. They use quality ingredients and the prices are very fair, we will definitely be back!

Honestly not my favourite. I love Vietnamese food but I find this place to be sub par. The people here are very friendly but I find the flavour lacking and they get so busy that you usually have to wait a while for your food. I don't mind waiting if the food is really good but I just find their sauce isn't the best and the spring rolls could use more filling.

Ordered ahead (due to covid) and glad we did.  I arrived 30 minutes after placing the order as the lady said. They were crazy busy and it took an extra 30 minutes on top of that. 

Now my last few days have been hectic so I appreciate kind and happy service.  They gentlemen and ladies were fantastic and nice.  My food was fresh and hot.  

Ordered tuna maki, cucumber maki, shrimp bowl and green onion cake. Everything was really good.  

3/5 because of the extra long wait....but I'm glad it all tasted good and service was great.

Well I had the pleasure of going to this lovely restaurant.  This is a cozy, sexy little restaurant with probably the friendliest staff I have encountered in a long time.  This is a family run business and everyone seemed to really care that you were having a great time.  

More importantly the food and drinks were creative and fun.   Our waiter recommended a new cocktail that he told us he invented.  He called it "Vancouver Island Ice Tea".  It was a mixture of brewed ice tea and grey goose vodka.  It was refreshing and delicious.  It was a very muggy August night so the recommendation was well received.

The owner recommended the baked peppers.  A Classic Italian dish that was very savoury.  It had a bit of minced veal in a bruschetta / tomato sauce.

I took my final recommendation from my most awesome waiter and that was the fresh rack of lamb.  It came with seasonal vegetables and a home made tomato sauce.  

The rack of lamb was cooked perfectly.  It was delicious.  I only wish I was offered some mint jelly or sauce.  I know that is a Greek thing and I asked one time in an Italian restaurant and felt like I committed a crime, so I will never do that again ;).

In closing this restaurant was a delight.  St. Albert is lucky to have this beautiful restaurant.  I look forward  to my next visit.

Simply the best Farmers Market in Alberta! I enjoy heading out to the Farmers Market every year.  Everything is fresh and there is a wide variety of veggies,meats,baked goods,crafts,spices,breads,etc.  But make sure to be there at 10:00am when the bell rings, since some of your favorites tend to go fast!  Let the shopping begin!

I am very pleased by the two shingling jobs we had done by Protec (Home and Cottage: May and June 2015).  The estimates we got were complete, accurate, detailed and done quickly. All available options were explained. The friendly crews arrived as scheduled. The quality of workmanship and materials was outstanding. The work was done cleanly and quietly and the final cleanup left each worksite perfectly clean. We have had many houses shingled over the years. Our experience with Protec was the best and most professional I have seen.

To market, to market to buy a fat pig;
Home again, home again, jiggety-jig.

This would be my almost every Saturday morning during the St. Albert Outdoor Farmers Market season. The market is incredible, the diversity of the vendors and best of all it is in beautiful downtown St. Albert.

The market is on St. Anne and St. Thomas streets, the horn sounds at 10 am Saturday mornings and the vendors start distributing their goods. The crowds are always large and the vendors usually sell out early (some are sold out as early as noon), quite often by two o'clock very few vendors have any product left.

Are you looking for that unique gift, well you will probably find it here amongst the hundred of vendors on site. But never fear there are plenty of every type of vendor you could think of from produce, baked goods, ethnic foods, stained glass, and considerable number of gluten free vendors. Most important to me is the cupcake lady! :)

Come early so as not to be disappointed. There are ATM's on site and if you can't find parking, head over to the St. Albert Centre parking lot and they have a free park 'n ride shuttle to and from the market.

The St. Albert Farmers' Market is so huge, it was like being at a festival. Two large streets are filled with vendors on either side. There is an excellent variety of just about every kind of produce, food, craft, or gift item available here. Several of the vendors are also recognizable from the various farmers' markets in Edmonton. 

If you want a snack, the food carts are all arranged in one area, about halfway through. A few buskers added music to the atmosphere.

There are literally hundreds of vendors - and thousands of shoppers. My only complaint is that I could not get close enough to many of the booths to get a better look at the goods. I'm not a crowd person - what else can I say? But it is definitely a lot of fun and worth a visit if you love farmers' markets.

Canned pasta served up by the cast of the Jersey Shore. Sound good? It wasn't. There are 5 Italian restaurants in St. Albert, 2 are in walking distance of this place. Do yourself a favour, keep walking. Pasta did not taste fresh, sauces were bland and metallic (can) tasting, and there was way to much parsley on everything. All that and it was over priced.

I am a huge fan of the farmer's market - all farmer's markets anywhere and everywhere.  I wouldn't call myself a regular or a die hard by any means; simply because the prices are too high.  As much as I strive to support local, fresh, organic; sometimes the price tag is just a little beyond what I can consider to be reasonable.  And although I can certainly see the justification for the higher prices (given the much better quality - in most cases), I just simply cannot afford it.

Now maybe I am taking this the wrong way but here's my story - you be the judge:

You know how Venus Fly Traps are just the coolest looking plant ever?  We sure thought so when we saw them at a booth selling a variety of plants and various greenery.  I thought the $10 price tag was a little high, but we just couldn't resist.  Well resist we should have; at least until we went grocery shopping the next day and found the same EXACT type of plant (identical packaging - and it was pretty unique so it was no coincidence) for $6.99 at Safeway.  I felt genuinely ripped off, but maybe I am just missing the point.  I thought the point of the farmers market was for local 'entrepreneurs' to promote & sell the fruits of THEIR labour (not Safeway's).

The farmers market to me is more about the experience than anything.  We usually treat ourselves with some type of fruit or vegetable to snack on, and often find some unique item that we just can't pass up.  I would love to purchase my produce exclusively from places like this, however, in my current financial state, I will regrettably have to choose the less expensive options.

I went with a group of friends and ordered a type of spaghetti with Italian sausage dish. The noodles were undercooked, and the sauce definitely tasted store bought. A friend of mine ordered the same and we both agreed that the only good thing about the dish was the sausage. The price was also way too high for what we got - around $30 for a small plate of pasta. I won't be going back, which is unfortunate because the staff were all friendly. It was just the food and prices that were off.

fair prices, convenient paying options and lots of room. This car wash is just off st albert trail, you can't miss it. 12 self wash bays at 2 touch less automatics. Touch less prices are 10,11,12,13 dollars I usually go with the 13. Check em out !

The mussels were fantastic!  I wanted veal which wasn't on the menu & to my surprise the owner brought it out & said made especially for you. Wow I was so impressed!  The meals were so flavourful but simple. The tiramisu was the best. We paid for our meal & was heading to our vehicle & the owner caught up with us to see us off & thank us for eating at his restaurant. I have to say you never see that now a days!!!  I was so touched that we would be treated with such respect & treated as a valued customer!!!!

Aw, the SAOFM! (Even though no one calls it that.)

I grew up in St. Albert (or Stalbert, or St. A) so I'm pretty familiar with this market, which just happens to be the largest in Western Canada. My hometown's claim to fame, I suppose.

Picture any other market in Edmonton. Doesn't really matter which one. Terwillegar, Callingwood, Strathcona, even Downtown, which I think is a pretty substantial market. SAOFM blows them all outta the organic, locally sourced water. From one end of St. Anne street to the other, I always find myself walking the market twice through - once to visit booths on the east side of the street, and once to visit west side booths.

The best part about this market is deal hunting. There's not just one or two booths selling ripe tomatoes, but close to a dozen. Same goes for peaches, lettuce, and meats. Plus crafts, handcarved wood, pies, meat pies, a balloon artist, and of course, the strawberry popsicle lady.

You won't do efficient grocery shopping here, especially if you intend to run back and forth between stalls to price check, but on a gorgeous day out, it's the perfect family-friendly activity.

This is by far, the best outdoor farmers market I've been to. It's huge! There is so much to explore, so make sure you have at least an hour or more to spend there if you've never been. 
There's lots of options for produce, local and organic meat, pasta, desserts and local artisans and crafts. 
I would recommend the fresh pasta and pesto place- their pesto is so flavorful and they have the coolest shaped pasta. I'd also recommend the homemade pie place and Sunworks organic  meats sausage. 
Buying local really is worth the extra cost-you just can't get the same quality of food from a big supermarket. 
My only regret is that we can't have outdoor farmers markets year round with the same selection.

There is something so wonderful about the months in Alberta without snow and one of them is this market. It is so large that you have to dedicate a whole morning and early afternoon to really take it in. Samples and wears. There is a huge variety of everything. It definitely becomes an occasion when you make the effort to have lunch there from a vendor.

I always leave with a sweet treat and a pair of earrings at the very least. 

Support the locals!

You want it? You got it! I think almost anything you might want you can find here. It might cost but it is here. From wine to entertainers, food trucks, arts, soap and of course foods. The only problem is it is only half a year!

My husband and I were in St Albert for the art walk a few weeks ago and stumbled into this quaint little restaurant. The waiter that we had was so attentive, witty and knew the menu and drink menu completely by memory! I need to eat gluten free and he was so knowledgeable about all of the items I could eat and the substitutions and changes that could be made to items so that I could have them. He really was such a hard worker and it was so obvious that he loved his job.
The owner came by and recommended that we try the calamari for an appetizer and he would make sure it was made gluten free. It was fantastic! Highly recommended .
Our meals were great. Ample food. Took some home for lunch the next day which is perfect. 
The owner took time to meet us and join in to our conversation about European soccer and since it is such a small world we realized that we knew many of the same people. I loved how personable he was, how relaxed the environment was and we will definitely come back again.
Excellent choice of stalls.  Go with plenty of money as lots to spend on and rarely come home with any money left
Highly recommend this wonderful restaurant in downtown St. Albert!

I don't usually go to farmer's market but once a year I'll make a special trip to this one.  I find they are the same, mostly fruits, vegetables, bakery and other food items and jewelry.  But this farmer's market is the best as it has so many vendors that I'll always find something to buy and enjoy.  It's good when you spend more time perusing than the time it took to drive there!

You can tell the fruits and vegetables are very fresh so they might be a bit more expensive than the grocery store but it tastes better.  I don't buy large quantities of fruit and vegetables from the market as I find they will go bad quicker since they came straight from the garden/orchard.  You will find unique items too from something crafty to articles of clothing.

This market is quite easy to get to if you don't know St. Albert very well.  Located in the downtown area, there are various shops and restaurants too so you can easily spend a whole day here.  There is parking around the area, just following the people and cars and be patient.  Even if you don't find anything you like, you can enjoy the beautiful sunny day, music or lunch from the food trucks.  Definitely worth to check out!

Thought I'd do a quick update.  Since my last visit, the self wash bats have changed a bit.  The system to select what you are washing with (soap, wax, rinse, brush, etc.) is now a switch and easier to operate than their previous touch key pad. 

You now have to start with a minimum of $2 and can add a $1 at a time.  I prefer not having a minimum $ start amount as I'll often take a break for 30 seconds or so to switch between foam brush or rinse and now I feel a bit rushed to get my $'s worth. I realize it's a small $ amount but a change that costs me more in the long run regardless.

I haven't been here in a while but when I was it was often. It's better than the Whyte Ave one too and I think it's because it has more of that small town atmosphere. The out door singers are a treat too.
Awesome place to get fresh produce on Saturday, go when it starts for best choices

I prefer Sparkle to Alpine for the self-service bays because you are charged for the time you use the equipment not from the minute you drive in to when you exit.  So all in all, my wash here is usually $2-$3 less than at Alpine.

That being said, the equipment is sticky and sometimes I struggle with getting the right option to start on their keypad (telephone button) system.

I really hate writing negative reviews about local businesses but, I feel other consumers need to beware of this company. We had our Eaves,downspouts and soffit  replaced last year in September. They literally showed up one day after promising they would be there 2 1/2 weeks prior to that date and began replacing them. Although we were not prepared or expected them we still proceeded with the replacement. At first we were thrilled to have the replacement done as they were originals to our 1973 built home. As it began to rain we soon found out that new was not always better. We literally had waterfalls pouring off the side of our house as if there were no eaves's at all. We made several phone calls to the company asking them to come and have a look at what was going on. We fully expected them to come within a week of our phone calls, to assess what needed to be done, nothing could've been further from the truth. It took eight phone calls my husband finally going down to the actual address of the company and  demanding  someone come to look at our eavestroughs. We consistently got the runaround, empty promises not showing up as promised by this time we had already paid in full, so we have no leverage to use against them for poor workmanship. When they finally did come they blamed it on other people in the company telling us that they forgot to add a crucial component to stop the areas from seeping between The roof itself and the eaves. They did replace that after our continued threats and by that time winter had arrived and we thought everything was good.

Fast forward to 2016 springtime runoff melting water again was seeping out of areas where they had said they had fixed the downspouts were completely unsealed and water was dripping in all four corners horribly I even took video footage of The awful mess that these downspouts created. 
We have now left two messages for the company to come and look at the workmanship again and we have been promised by one gentleman that they would come and have a look we have heard hide nor hair from them so as a result I phone leaving a message today and told them that I was going to leave this review. Buyer beware do not use this company and save yourself huge headache and out-of-pocket expense. We will have no choice but to have these poor eaves replaced by a more reputable company.

Went to the opening day of the St. Albert Farmer's Market 2011 season today!  It was pouring cats and dogs - and we got quite wet - but oh so worth it!

Stocked up on Happy Camel hummus and pitas, mennonite farmer's sausage, guacasalsa, grabbed one of Little Jack Horner's Curry pies for dinner... and of course kettle corn, fresh squeezed lemonade, and tried Eva Sweet Waffles for the first time!

Peas on Earth had the most beautiful organic produce - that's the same place that much of my former Organic Box deliveries come from (mixed lettuce, etc.) and I noticed their prices were lower than what I had been paying through the Organic Box!  I think I'll be cancelling my Organic Box now that summer is here and stock up every week at the Farmer's Market!

Can't wait for next week!

We love going here with our family. The staff make you feel so welcome and treat you like you are royalty. 

The food is always top notch as well. Definitely my favourite Italian place in St Albert!

St Albert Outdoor Farmers Market is such a fun place to visit during summer months when it's too hot to eat, and all your body craves are  fresh fruit and vegetables. The vendors sell everything from fresh produce, baked goodies, honey, sausages, olives and cheeses to handmade clothes, jewelry and home décor items. Most of the fruit and vegetables are grown locally, while some are brought in from British Columbia. There are hundreds of friendly vendors who are happy to assist you and answer any questions you may have about the products they sell. The best time to come here is during early morning as by midday most fresh produce is sold out. Yet, I never feel rushed when I shop here, and I really enjoy the pleasant experience of shopping outside.

St. Albert is often on my way into the city from work and I frequently stop at Sparkle Car Wash to clean my vehicle. Always have had great service, never have to wait too long to get in and prices are reasonable! I am aware there has recently been a change of ownership/management and I'm surprised by some of the negative reviews since I believe they are doing a great job. Would recommend!

An absolutely fantastic Restaurant offering in St. Albert!  Busy on a midweek early night is certainly a sign of a successful business. The service is amazing, with the owner checking up on you and your meal several times during the course of dinner, and they are very accommodating to any wishes you might have, gluten-free variation, or kids-size portion. They prepare their own ingredients, even grow some of them, truly a gem worth trying!!!

The Outdoor Farmers Market is the quintessence of a St. Albert summer Saturday well-spent. Delectable edibles, handsome handicrafts and punny business names abound! 

Plan to show up first thing in the morning (and later in the season) if you truly want first pick of all the fresh produce. Some booths get VERY busy very quickly, so plan ahead if there's a certain something you're after. 

The Farmers Market is best met with an open mind, a curious palette, comfy shoes, and good company. It's a great place to try new things. The vendors are all very friendly and are happy to tell you about their products. Free samples are everywhere (and somewhat dangerous - it's difficult not to walk out with a case of whatever you try!). 

Make sure to bring some cash with you - not all the vendors are equipped to handle debit/credit transactions. There are ATMs onsite, but come prepared to avoid paying high withdrawal fees. 

The Farmers Market is fun to revisit all summer as different vendors come and go throughout the season. It's a great place to shop for unique gifts, and you'll be sure to discover some new favourite snacks & spreads. It's extremely family friendly, and with live music from local buskers the atmosphere can't be beat. There's no better way to support the local community.

This new Italian restaurant in downtown St. Albert is truly a jewel! We had an absolutely lovely evening in this beautifully renovated space. The service was warm and welcoming and our meals were outstanding. We started with the bruschetta, then continued on with lasagna and penne rosa. Divine! We also took home an order of arancini which were heavenly.  We are so glad that San Remo opened here. It is truly a welcome addition to the St. Albert restaurant scene. Reservations a must!

This market is WORTH THE DRIVE!! From south-side Edmonton, or out of town, you will NOT be disappointed making the drive to this market. You might be disappointed by the parking situation (lol), but it's worth it!

This has to be the largest market in the Edmonton area. They have over 250 vendors!!! It's insane, and I love it. The market is laid out perfectly, and is in downtown St. Albert so you can make this an entire day outing. 

Check out the website for a full list of vendors, but trust me... they have EVERYTHING and more. It's a great market to bring kids to as well.

The St. Albert farmers market is a fun outdoor stroll on a warm summer's day. I've made the trip into St. Albert just for it. They have tons of vendors selling fresh produce, baked goods, meats, gourmet foods, jewelry, clothing, and other unique artisan items. It runs all through the summer and is the biggest outdoor one around. By be cooped up inside a grocery store, when summer's so short in these parts? I like the vibe of an outdoor market. There's usually music, lots of families and kids, and vendors very happy to be connecting with the people who will eat the food they grow. It feels good to support local farmers and put money back into the local economy. It's social, and it's also is a great excuse to slow down and enjoy the process of shopping, instead of just plowing through the aisles of a supermarket with your cart and shopping list. Farmers' markets are a great compliment to conscious shopping and eating. You can find out exactly what's gone into making what you're going to put into your mouth right from the people who produced it. That's cool.

This has to be the best Farmers market available within the Edmonton area. It is held outdoors in the heart of St.Albert. Ive never had an issue with finding parking, theres actually a parking lot just down the road by an old folks home that has a nice walk to the market. Its along a river that is full of wildlife. The market itself is rather large and has a wide variety. I never leave this market empty handed. Theres a concession (foodcourt) located in the middle of the market. Theres alot of unique crafts and fresh produce and plenty of pies mmmmm I love pie mmmmmm. I always look forward heading to the SAOFM and cant wait till the slow melts and the market opens again.

used to go weekly but never again.  It was nice that they had machines that took quarters but they eat 50% of what you put in without registering them.  When brought to the attention of the worker he could not care one bit.  He said "that never happens" to which I responded well yes it is.  

Usually if something goes wrong the owner makes it right.  This fellow had the audacity to say "well the owner is not here"  In fact as I was leaving the worker decided that he would give me a two middle finger salute as I was waiting for the door to go up.

Needless to say that is not how to treat a once a week customer for a long time.  Plenty of other places to support and that I shall!

This quaint little bistro was pretty much the best lunch I experience I have ever had.  The wait staff was attentive and friendly. The food came and it looked amazing.  It tasted even better.  The waiter said most of the menu is made fresh daily, and it certainly tasted like it.  I highly recommend this place.

Lovely staff.  Some might find the level of attention a bit overbearing and perhaps even intrusive, but it's par for the course in small Italian bistros like this.  

The menu prices are laughably high for this type of cuisine and this style of dining; they should be lowered by a minimum of 25% across the board.

I was seated at the bar and the tiled area on which I dined was obviously dirty, with the residue of some kind of sauce/dried tomato stuck to same.  Meh.  I'm unlikely to try San Remo again.

This Farmers Market spans a good portion of the Perron District with a wide variety of different vendors ranging from homemade crafts to fresh produce. If you're looking for a bite to eat, they also have a few food trucks throughout.

This Farmers Market has become my favourite by far with the wide variety of things to purchase or peruse. Many of the vendors I've come across are also very friendly with pretty fair pricing.

The only issue I have with this farmers market is parking; if you don't come early enough, parking can be quite the gong show.

However I'll definitely continue going to this farmers market!
I just had lunch from this restaurant.  I am disappointed.  Chicken parm was gooey, not the best flavor and the Alfredo pasta was bland.  I won't go again.

My company works in oil and gas production operations.  We drive on some very poor roads, with lots of mud.  We have 7 vehicles that are routinely washed at Sparkle, we typically spend in excess of $500. /mo at the that car wash.  We have been bringing our vehicles exclusively to Sparkle for washing for the last two years, in that time we have noted a change in the operation of the car wash since ownership changed last year, but nothing really too bad (we find it's not as clean, the staff not quite as helpful (there are some language issues), but I still think it's a good facility, and the prices are still pretty good). 

Today the young man who works as an attendant at the car wash told me my truck was too dirty and muddy and suggested that I take it to Big Toys to wash it.  He suggested it was too much work for him to clean the mud off the floor in the bay as he couldn't just wash  it down into the sump.

I would like to apologize to the management of Sparkle Car Wash, I didn't realize that we should only bring clean vehicles into the car wash.  I'm sorry for bringing my muddy truck in, but don't worry, it probably won't happen again, not for my truck or any of the other six vehicles we own.

I'm not very happy about being asked not to come to a car wash because my vehicle was too dirty - IT"S A CAR WASH! it's sole function is to clean vehicles.  I'm pretty sure I can find somewhere else to take my vehicles, my mud, and my money.

Been going here for years. Last week there hose fell off the rood and smashed the tonneau cover on my truck and put a dent in it. Gave them my information so their insurance could contact me to replace the $1200 tonneau cover their equipment damaged. Still havent heard from them. I would not recommend this place to anyone terrible service and a death trap

Went here with a good friend of mine a few nights ago and I was pleasantly surprised. I was expecting it to causal but the decor and atmosphere was very classy. I had that rigatoni with the red sauce and my friend had the gnocchi in house cream sauce. My pasta was perfect, the menu said it was spicy and most definitely was. Maybe a bit too strong? My friends was great very creamy. Although our food was fabulous, the staff was a bit off. My friend stepped out to to use the washroom and her food had arrived. The female waitress then waited with the cheese and other dressings until she was back. It was quite strange and uncomfortable.  However the manger/owner was extremely welcoming and should be very proud of his establishment! Would definitely come back!

I ate here with the family last night and the food was fantastic! Very nice place and friendly staff. They even shook our hands and thanked us for coming in! I have lived in the area for over 15 years and this was my first time stopping in. I can tell you that I will be eating here again!

I think Sparkles is great. I have never had a problem there. Also remember you bubbled socialites of St. Albert, it's a business and they need to make money too. If it's too expensive buy your own equipment and clean your car yourself at home. Overall you will save more money and your car will be cleaned better.

The employees there have always been very helpful to me and I always go out of my way to wash my car here!

Keep up the good work Sparkles!
We went to visit the in laws in Edmonton and they took is here. Absolutely wonderful. Had great hotdogs and cotton candy. Lots to look at. Felt like I was a kid again.
Favourite car wash to go to with friendly management and super cheap prices! I've already recommended this car wash to my friends & family

Highly recommended by friends and this place exceeded all expectations.  From the wine to the appetizers, main course was amazing as was the chocolate mouse!!!  Very classy touch was the restaurant giving us some peach grappa to end the night.   We will definitely include this place on our usual St. Albert stop moving forward!!!!

The service was excellent but the food was VERY expensive! About 2X normal prices! My steak and pasta was $45 and my wife's spaghetti was $32 . 5he steak would have been just OK but all I could taste was the coating of salt on the top even after I scraped a bunch off! Wires spaghetti was not fully cooked! House red at $20 per half liter.

This place is HUGE! Vendor after vendor, block after block, so many things to do, see, and taste! Take your time, wander around, sample some goodies! 

This market is very well laid out with the vendors spread out nicely. I won't bother listing all the items for sale, because there is SO MUCH! I always love the fresh veggies/fruit (we picked up some Taber corn), distilleries/craft breweries, and fresh baking (PIE!!!). The quality of the items often shows in the price of the goods. Yes, some great items, but a bit more than I was willing to pay. That's more of a reflection of the individual vendors rather that the Market itself. 

I was impressed with the number of food choices available, and happy to see food trucks there. 

All along the market there are incredible musicians performing. Lemme tell you, you're not getting serenaded in the grocery store! This is a treat! 

They also had a Show & Shine going on which was a nice break for hubby. We also saw a fun area for the little ones to hang out and play as well as face painting. 

Market days are the best!

Arranged a lady-minute dinner w my sweetie and she suggested San Remo - and it was fabulous!

We started w a glass of wine and a couple of starters, their specials that night were bacon-wrapped scallops and an eggplant parmigiana... the scallops were perfect, so moist and soft (so many places overlook them, but not here!) and the eggplant was huge and tasty - could almost be an entree in its own.

For our mains we did the half rack of lamb, and the veal scallopini - the lamb was incredible, VERY tasty, and the gnocchi was good and the veg on both our plates was awesome, quite crunchy yet not raw - and the only reason this is a four star review and not five was the veal, I was less impressed, lots of oil/butter. Maybe that's how many people like it, but it was a little too slick or me! :)

To finish? Chocolate mousse, again tasty and creamy, and a small shot of peach grappa closed it all off well... We will be back! :)
They seem to be falling behind on equipment and building maintenance and the washing chemical quality seemed to have changed. This used to be my favourite car wash.

A bit of an interesting experience. I went with my father for a night of fine dining. There happened to be a large party celebrating a family event - approximately 25 other people in the restaurant with us. Despite the event, the service was very attentive. In fact, the service was a little too attentive to the point of being overbearing and feeling like we were getting pestered over every little thing. About 5 people came to check on us (the chef came out and shook my father's hand - would have been a nice touch, had the servers not been all over us already) every 5 minutes over the course of our stay.

After riddling off a massive list of specials, the server allowed us to order.
For an appetizer, we shared the mussels and the mushroom bruschetta. Our first choice was originally the regular bruschetta, but the server strongly recommended we try the mushroom variety instead. It tasted fine, but my father and I concluded we would have much preferred our first choice.
My dad ordered the Linguine ai Frutti di Mare. It looked pretty great and as far as I know, it was very tasty.
I ordered whatever lamb special was on for that particular day - 2 lamb shanks paired with gnocchi. It was very delicious and the meat was tender. The presentation of the food left something to be desired, though. My plate looked a bit sloppily put together, however I could tell the intention and the effort was there. 
We concluded our meal with a dessert (chocolate mousse, if I remember correctly.)

Overall, the dining experience was alright, but I did feel like I was being watched over a little too closely. I understand the desire to serve your customers well, but I strongly recommend the staff to back off and stop over-stimulating those who are dining.

This is without a doubt the best Italian Restaurant around.  We were in Rome this summer.  When we visited SAN Reno tonight we were transported to that magical culinary city once again.  We wanted two dishes not on the menu, vongole and spaghetti carbonara and the chef produced dishes that rivalled our Rome experience.  We live in Vancouver but always visit every time we are in Edmonton!  Well done owner Romano!!!  Delizioso!!  Grazie!!!

It was a beautiful sunny day today, so I thought I should be out. I decided to check out this farmers market in St Albert. Well it took me 20 mins to find parking, but it's worth it. 
I have been to few farmers markets in Ontario, but this one stands out. There is some " Zing " in the air. This market has a Character, it's full of colour and life. Despite being a big market it's very well organized, it's just like a carnival.
Some really good counters for Locally grown Organic fruits and vegetables. The colour of fresh organic fruits is just a treat for eyes and taste buds. One counter was selling fresh dips, Tomato Basil Hummus and Roasted Veg dip are really good. 
Everyone is so friendly here, mostly all of them have free samples. 
One of the highlight was the street performers, it's well said you will find best of the talent on streets!!
I will definitely be there again next week

Visited the Farmer's Market today for the 2nd week into the season - got there before 2pm but nearly all of the food stands were already "sold out!"  Happy Camel, Kettle Corn... So sad!  Did still get a lemonade of course and tried Molly's International Eats for the first time.  Ordered the Spicy Chicken Tortilla described as "seasoned chicken with jalapeno spiced chimi churri." for $3.75.  Flavor was great but the portion was REALLY REALLY small for the price - I uploaded a pic!  I would rather be charged $3 for such a small morsel or charged another $1.25 upcharging to $5 for a bigger portion.  The chicken was moist and cooked to perfection - the heat from the jalapeno was mild and salty sweet!

Today just gets an A-OK rating because the 2 items I specifically went there for were "sold out."  The farmer's market runs from 10am - 3pm...  next week I'll listen to my own advice and get there before noon!

Still a fan for life!

I must say that The owner did make efforts to contact me and that is admirable.  He was not the problem but an employee and we can't always be on hand to make sure things happen properly.  I will give them a second chance but just not for a bit.

I hope others have better expereinces due to the sharing of this last visit.  :)

I don't frequent this market but I was here recently and it was the same day as the Rock'n August so it was busier and parking options weren't close by.  We didn't mind walking after parking in the residential area. 

The variety of vendors are great.  There will also be the ones selling produce, but there were also plenty of food vendors sampling tastes and some options were ready to consume.  If not, there are numerous food trucks available and some seating which is always great when you don't have walk and eat.  It can get crowded but I find the layout is not too congested and I was able to walk around and see the items I wanted to.

In addition to food, there's jewelry, clothing, and home decor.  here's a kid's play area and the library was also open inside.  There are porta potties but also toilets inside too. 

Great place to spend a Saturday morning or afternoon!

I went to San Remo with some friends for dinner one evening and was impressed. The service was great, no complaints. The food was also really good. I had the gnocchi and it was great. The portions are a good size too, I took the rest of my gnocchi home. The only thing that I didn't really like was the tiramisu. It was served in an glass and seemed to have a bit of a film around the edges, like it was prepared days ago and sitting the fridge. Not fresh. However, I would definitely go back.

This place is small, but it is actually nice and adds to the ambiance of the place. I would say maybe make a reservation, just in case. And yes it is $$$. But well worth it. There is parking right beside the building and that is nice since it is downtown. The calamari we had to start was delicious. I had the chicken parm, I wanted seafood pasta but $$. Either way it may have been best I have had, ever hands down. Fiancé had the cannelloni. The meat stuffing yum! Also the red sauce on both tasty tasty. We had tiramisu for dessert and it was perfect, authentic. The service was phenomenal. No it isn't a weekly stop but perfect for special days!

The food is fantastic! I have come here numerous times and still can't get enough. They have nightly specials, which I highly recommend. Lamb shanks, seafood, pastas; they have something for everyone. I have tried various dishes and I love the 4 cheese pasta and the braised lamb shank. The service is friendly and prompt and the atmosphere is welcoming. It is normally pretty busy, especially on the weekends, and I recommend reservations. I can't wait to go back.

Definitely one of my favorite markets to hit up in the summer months. Even the last market of the year, the street was full of great local vendors! 
Everything you can imagine from home baking, fruits and veggies, homemade birdhouses to essential oils! St. Albert Farmers Market has it all! 
They have free park n ride at the village transit station so it makes getting there a breeze!
They always have ATMs on-site for those of us who forget to bring cash & plenty of food trucks to pick up a meal. It's a big market so that's usually a must! 
I always feel a little bummed at the end of the year when this market finishes off for the season but I'm always equally excited for the next year!

One of my favourite parts of the St. Albert Farmer's Market is the live band.  Every market starts out with a local band or orchestra playing our National Anthem followed by awesome musical masterpieces like Star Wars or Hockey Night in Canada.

Another plus is that it's located by City Hall with easy access to indoor washrooms and the library for an escape from the heat.

Food trucks are a plenty and local fare is abundant.

I'll be seeing you there...

Love this place! Family run business and the owner is so friendly and personable. We got our pizza delivered in 35 minutes hot and fresh. Crust, sauce are delicious and they arent skimpy on the toppings! Nitzas used to be the best place in town but I can easily say this place is ten times better.. :)

Best authentic Italian pizza you will ever have! The owners John and Angela are the nicest (and funniest) people you will know, and very well-respected - John is known as Mr. Pizza Man in the neighbourhood! Great 2 for 1 deals, homemade lasagna, pasta and doners (with their homemade secret sauce!) I especially loved the atmosphere - you feel like you're walking into an Italian guy's home with posters of his favourite Italian soccer teams, Italy flags, and photos of his family back home from the village! A Must-Eat! This place will not disappoint

Just reading all the other reviews puts a smile on my face and increases my impatience for opening day - this place is so much fun.  As everyone has said, it's huge, so the possibilities seem endless when you start out and there's literally something for everyone.  Like fresh local produce?  Check!  Handmade jewelry, yard deco, clothing? Check!  Delicious meats and fish? Check!  Homemade pastries, cookies, fudge?  Check! And i love the ethnic offerings I don't find elsewhere, always getting to sample something new.

My own favourite, gotta get it, is the Bees Wax Moisturizing Skin Cream from Coal Lake Honey Farm - great for feet wanting to get sandal-ready, and smells divine.  Thank you, little bees, for your hard work!

We always have to get a few treats like the kettle corn, flavoured almonds (try bacon!), and fresh lemonade, and usually include a visit inside to the library.

For the kids, there's face painting, balloon lady, street musicians, singers - room to run a bit and lots of energy buzzing around.

If Saturday starts out with a drizzle, don't hesitate to go anyway -it's less crowded and you might just discover special bargains offered.  Anytime is a great time to go!
Had and excellent night here with friends. All the food was excellent. Staff is super friendly. The owner was a delight to talk with.  Will definitely be back with other friends.

I really like supporting this business. It's family owned, in our neighbourhood, the owner is a great guy, and the pizza ain't half bad either!

Heather and I disagree on the crust. I'm a fan, because I find greasy crust (think Pizza Hut) disgusting. Heather finds the crust here too dense and dry. It reminds me of the homemade pizza crust my mom made when I was a kid.

The toppings are plentiful and fresh, and the sauce is good (not great). Delivery is always faster than quoted which is great! It's not pizza I would necessarily rave about but it's always solid and I love supporting the local little guy. The friendly service boosts a 3 star pizza to a 4 star rating. Give them a try!

By far my favourite farmer's market EVER.  Even though I moved from St. Albert to Millwoods almost a decade ago, I regularly make the trip for this market.  It's so well organized, and even when it's packed it's still enjoyable.  

I also love that there are so many return vendors year after year.  It feels like coming home! :)

This farmers market was so hyped up that I thought it would never be able to meet my expectations... instead it blew them sky high! If that was confusing to anyone then let me be clear: St Albert Outdoor Farmer's Market is a MUST VISIT!

The amount of stalls, options, buskers, food trucks and customers makes this weekly event feel alive and at the same time useful and fun. I was a little overwhelmed the first time so I only bought farm fresh eggs and the tastiest hothouse tomatoes. I learned quickly and made sure I brought my reusable grocery bag next time and filled it up with market goodies.

I also ended up taking the shuttle from St Albert mall so that I wouldn't have to deal with the parking snarl.

If you forget your cash at home or run out you can use the portable bank machines provided on site! 

This market closes in October so check it out while you can!

Went today and spent 14 bucks on an a Premium wash. The only Premium was the price. After I was done I gave it a once look over. Well the windshield  was still dirty so was the hood of my truck. The box of the truck was still full of soap as there wasn't enough water to rinse it out. Then I looked up and saw the blowers were already going for 8 seconds before the so called rinse was going on. Then when I pulled up to the blowers, the middle one was pointed off to the left side not drying the truck.

I spoke to the attendant about the issues ( that he already knew about the way he talked and pointed to the correct wash I had used). I was told to come back later to get more time next time. I don't think so.

I really don't like giving bad reviews but I have to in this instance so that others can make their decision armed with opposing views. Having never had it before, my boyfriend and I ordered pizza from Pisa Pizza because of the great reviews on yelp.

We ordered two kinds:  Greek and Meat Lovers.
The Greek pizza was not good....at all. The crust was very thick but more like bread (stale bread) than a good pizza crust. The meat lovers was only slightly better but not that good either; almost tasteless.

The pizzas arrived almost cold and had to be heated up in the microwave.
I would have to say that this is one of the worst pizzas either of us have ever had....and we eat pizza often from various pizza joints.

I don't know if they were having an off night.....the delivery guy said they were really busy. But I honestly can say I will never order pizza from here again. Sorry.

Cold water, poor pressure, not enough chemicals, relatively expensive and not well maintained. Heavy fog on cold days makes driving in there treacherous. Used to really like this place but it has gone down hill real bad in the last 12 months. Now bad enough I won't go back.

Owner is exceptionally friendly and conversational, always glad to stop and chat for a bit before I leave. As for the food; the crust is light and soft inside and crispy on the outside, likely the best I've ever had. The sauce has a nice subtle sweet taste to it I very much like. Cheese is fresh and tasty, and meat/veggies are fresh and used in ample amounts. This is my favourite pizza place now, ever.

Received a brand a new roof installed 3 years ago and recently called to check on some of the materials that have come off the roof.  Apparently this is a new owner. After waiting for ove two months for them to show up and after several calls.   He said he wouldn't come check it out.  He was rude and worst customer service i've ever received. Also said that i lived way too far (my location is 5 minutes from downtown!).  Also said that he didn't care if i would not recommend him to others as he has lots of business.  I find that this sort of service is unacceptable! POOR RATING!

If you want an authentic Italian dining experience go to San Remo's in St Albert
Absolutely delicious food and 5 star service.

This market is the best! It's a Saturday outdoor market that's open from June till Thanksgiving every summer. They blow a fog horn at 10am when the vendors are allowed to start selling their wares and it blows again at 3pm when the market closes. 

There are so many vendors at this market and they rotate from week to week and year to year. Some booths are consistent and show up every year while others may come only a few weeks of the year. Of course there is the classic food vendors: garden produce, fresh seasonal fruit, hot food/drink (food trucks), and custom foods (pies, cookies, beef jerky, fresh/frozen meats, perogies, etc). But there are a lot more hand made items: wooden patio furniture, jewelry, garden items, knit clothing, and other knick nacks. And there are the alcohol suppliers now: craft wines, craft beers, distilleries, mead, and doesn't kombucha even have a little bit of booze in it? ;)

A few of my favorite anchor booths are listed below. 
Viravongsa's Farms: they have a legit farm near Red Deer and offer the freshest locally grown produce. Family owned and operated and their prices are fair.
Confetti Sweets: They offer a great selection of cookies. You can buy them as a single or get a volume discount if you buy 3 or more. My favorite is the Oatmeal chocolate chip.

I am a market person. On Saturday morning you can usually find me at one of the markets in town. So why had I not yet ventured to the St. Albert Farmers Market, the largest outdoor market in Western Canada? I don't know, but I made sure to change that this summer! 

In the super cute Perron District of St Albert, the market is found on St Anne street, St Anne Promenade and St Thomas street. It's huge, and it took us over 2 hours to walk to one end and back, hardly stopping for a break. And it's popular, drawing huge crowds, so don't expect to be able to power walk through the place. There is very limited parking on site, but check on their website for parking areas within a 6-8 minute walk (including north of the river). 

I found the vendors very friendly and there is way more sampling to be had over other markets in Edmonton. There is an area with food trucks in front of St. Albert Place. Plus indoor bathrooms there too!

Biggest downside is that there are so many vendors, it's hard to comparison shop - if you have an inkling for something, buy it right away because you'll probably forget about it and not be able to find it again! Or it might be sold out by the time you find it again.

In any case, worth cheating on the City Market (and Strathcona) every once in a while!

One of my favourite Farmers markets! It is big, it is easy to walk around which is a bonus. Some of the other markets do not have this luxury. There is a great variety of vendors- crafts, fresh produce, meats, fish and seafood. I feel like a child at a fun fair every time I go there. there is so much to see, to try and of course, to buy.

Wanted pasta and this place looked very authentic with a decent score on Google and Yelp. A little out of the way for just a takeout order and might have been better for dine-in but I had plans to watch TV and eat my fancy Italian dinner at home. I called and was quoted 22min which I thought was quite long but it took me that long to get there anyway. There was lots of 2 hour street parking available. Very nice decor inside - fancy, classy, romantic would be how I would describe the decor. The restaurant was completely empty at 5PM although they did just open at 4:30PM.  My order was ready when I arrived (20min later).
I got the Arancini appetizer, Gnocchi entree, and Tartufo (choc + raspberry ice cream) dessert all for ~$40.
The food survived the 11 minute drive home (even the ice cream). The Arancini was delicious - like a deep-fried risotto ball should be. I liked that it came with a touch of tomato sauce which gave it a nice acidic kick. The gnocchi were larger than I expected and therefore hard to eat in 1 bite so I had to try to cut each one before eating. Not the best I have ever had. I got it with the rose sauce which was nice but nothing special. Creamy but not a lot of flavour.  The tartufo was promising - like a black forest cake but ice cream style. Too bad it had such a miniscule amount of raspberry. 95% chocolate ice cream; which was good chocolate ice cream for sure but not enough acidic to balance out all the sweet for me.
Place and menu look great and promising but unfortunately, I was underwhelmed for the price and can't see myself back anytime soon.

We had a superb dinner at San Remo tonight thanks to the wonderful staff . Deep fried cheese and stuffed mushrooms appetizers both very nice.  I had the Osso Bucco (a special for the evening)which was so tender and flavourful  , my better half had the chicken parmigiana which in our opinion was the best that we have had anywhere( melt in your mouth goodness)One of the other good thing was the fresh pastas and sauces served with our meals it tastes like someone cares about quality.

I am scoring it a 3....however, it is closer to a 2.75.....  

We went to SR on 9/19/14...it was my turn to pick and I wanted to pick a place outside the City of Edmonton limits.  I read the website and thought that the restaurant would feature Italian food from the region of Liguria given ALL the information the website featured, AS DOES its menu when you go there.

Alas, there are NO dishes from Liguria.... with the exception of the Linguine ai Frutti di Mare which given the country, EVERY region is on the coast so they is a staple dish :-)
What did surprise me is that the restaurant features dishes from OTHER regions, but not even one dish of Spaghetti al Pesto (Spaghetti with pesto (basil) sauce)....basically what the region is known for in all of Italy.  With that said, I was a bit disappointed, however, the one thing that did impress me was the attention that the wait staff and owner paid to ALL its patrons.  It is quite obvious, happily so, that San Remo is a "neighbourhood gem" and for this, I am glad :-)

For the appetizers, we had the Arancini di Riso and the Stuffed Mushrooms.  Bite size, the arancini were FRESHly made and basically the size where you don't need a fork....and it is probably best to just pop them in your mouth.  The sauce served with it was fresh tomatoes, not too herbed and NO parmiggiano all over them :-) (hurrah!).  The stuffed mushrooms were not great, but were not awful.  The mushroom didn't have any distinct taste.

Our entrees were quite good, the only drawback was that there was TOO much sauce :-(  My companion had the Gnocchi alla Casalinga and they were quite good and well made, however, there was too much sauce (though he didn't let it go to waste and had a "scarpetta" once done with the gnocchi).  Mine were the Penne Rosa Peperoncino Picante.  They were al dente and the amount of spicy sausage was just right and the pieces were small so they didn't overtake the penne.  Again, too much sauce but very good, nonetheless.

Dessert was okay.... My companion ordered the Chocolate Mousse which he enjoyed :-)  I ordered the Tiramisu'.  :-( It was soggy and unfortunately not as good as I had hoped....  

The surprising thing was HOW FAST everything came out....our reservation was at 6:45pm....we were out of there a bit before 8pm.... ?  Not sure what to make of that part....

In all, a pleasant evening as the staff that served our table was very nice and personable to be sure :-)  It seems like a spot that would be fun to go with a small group of friends :-) And perhaps we will go again with friends :-)
