The steak was 10 ounces so I wasn't able to finish it but I took it to go with some of the potatoes and the complimentary bread and it was a great lunch the next day.

Finally, the service was great. Maybe it was because I was Chris's only table but I would like to believe I would get that service everyday.

I would go back but only when I'm craving steak.

Campbell Liquor is a fabulous liquor store located in St. Albert.  We popped in for last month's spectacular 18th anniversary wine and liqour tasting featuring more than 60 offerings!  There were lovely meat and cheese platters to accentuate the offered tastings.

Found some lovely new dessert wines and a port to share this Christmas season.

The store is always clean, the selection broad, and the staff friendly.

Campbell Liquor also offers weekly tasting selections, usually on Fridays and Saturdays.  If you need some help picking out a bottle of wine for an upcoming dinner or gift, I highly recommend you stop in and try a few sips and talk with the knowledgeable staff.

This trick with this place is that it's great for pick up or delivery, but not that great for a sit down meal. It's essentially a hole in the wall cafeteria with great pizza. It's a great alternative to the usual Panago or whatnot. They seem to have good combo deals, but I have never tried anything else apart from their pizza.

This place is A-OK. The food and drinks are definitely good, but I think it's overpriced. The decor and atmosphere is great and I would definitely recommend trying this place out if you've never been, but honestly there are a ton of restaurants with the same quality food for a lot cheaper.

"Yay! I'm a fan" for brunch on the weekend. 

In the month of March, I came in for brunch three times on the weekends - separate occasions. And I thoroughly enjoyed it, a complete 180 from my first visit here for dinner. Their brunch menu offer half a dozen varietions on each of ... pancakes, omelets, eggs, bacon, sausages, steaks with hash brown and toast etc. (see their website for exactness)

This establishment does not have the chandeliers, candle lit centerpiece etc - it's just a simple, comfortable community diner. If you show up on the weekend to find that there's only a couple tables available for seating - you'll see why the "regulars" keep coming back week after week. It's reasonably priced, convenient for the Castledown/Oxford and St Albert communities, ample amount of parking, good hearty food, and can comfortably fit a group gathering (6 to 12 people). 

Portion wise - I always have a bit to take away in a doggy bag to snack on in the afternoon!

Menu says breakfast is served until 10AM, but on the weekends it's till later - not sure when exactly.

This is a good place to catch Oiler's games. The crowds a bit older so you don't have to worry about having to deal with an obnoxious crowd. They have plenty of big screen TVs that allow for good views of the game.

I like how they have a countdown clock for the hockey games and they have free pool on Sundays! It is definitely a pub but allows for more space than the norm. It doesn't get too loud in here either so if you are looking to catch the game in a relaxed environment, this is the spot.
I had steak, my wife had... i don't remember what she had! anyways, my steak was AMAZING. My wife's food was good but not amazing. I would have given them 5 star if their prices were reasonable.

Today my friend and I went here for lunch, I am 6 months pregnant she is 3 months pregnant. The waiter was nice, but a little awkward, not what you would expect at a nice restaurant. My friend ordered a virgin caesar, little spice, with a lime. First he brings it with no lime and table salt on the rim, then he brings it back with celery salt no lime, then he brings it back again looking right. I tell him I would like the exact same as her. My friend finishes 3/4 of her drink before mine gets there and she realises she is starting to feel DRUNK. We complain to the manager that our virgin caesars have alcohol in them and that we are both pregnant. He says the meal is on him. I had the chicken club sandwich with clam chowder. Food was fine, nothing special and the price was fine ($15). We ordered the cappuccino cake for dessert, it came with some of the paper from the packaging it was in still stuck to it. I gave this place 2 stars instead of 1 because the manager was very nice. All in all this was a bad first impression and I won't be going back. Which is to bad. I'm sure with a better waiter (who was also the bartender) I would have had a better time.

This place has all the makings of a great night out.. Neat interior design, live jazz Thursday nights, patio, downtown St. Albert, nice ambiance. 

Despite all of its positives the food is so bad it far overshadows everything else. Steak runs 30-45 a plate. It was cooked perfectly to order, had no exterior sear, spice was the ubiquitous Montreal Steak spice. Ordered a "Silver Cut Rib Eye' and it was virtually tasteless. My wife's strip loin was the same. Corn on the cob was so over cooked it was mush. The peppers, carrot that came as vegetable were also overdone. My fries were not fresh cut, they came in a bag, and tasted like rubber, also over salted despite asking for no salt on anything. My wife's stuffed potato was actually quite good, the only thing we had that was. The bread they served before supper was ROCK hard on both ends. Inside was softer but again zero flavor.

I would have been disappointed in this meal at one quarter the price and I have had far better steaks in many places around Edmonton. Peter's Pizza Spruce Grove, the Roustabout Ft Sask and Franco's on 50th St to name a few.

Honestly, I think Ricky's breakfast place could have done a better job.

The Jazz wasn't bad but it must be a volunteer team. They played less than 20 minutes out of the hour and a half we were there.

It was far too hot inside despite it being only 22 outside. The place needs a make over, starting to look pretty tired if you look close, particularly the rest rooms.

One upside, they have a very extensive wine list and the prices aren't to bad for that.

Service was okay but nothing to write home about for a place that sets itself up as higher end dining. We won't be going back given how many much better options there are. There are three restaurants within a stones throw that kick Ric's butt.

There were some great write ups on the wall from back in 2001 but they have definitely not kept up to there old press. WAY overpriced for the quality and service.

Wow, this is one quite Chapters! Like ghost town quite. I guess if you need to buy a book with complete anonymity this is your place! Its large and has a nice children's section. They have quite a lot of gift item sections as well throughout the front and all down the middle of the store. The only reason I went in was because I was in need of a place to work with free wifi. I had driven around St Albert and found 2 locally owed coffee shops, one was closed, the other did not have working wifi. So, I knew I could count on Chapters and their Starbucks, so headed in. The Starbucks was ok, 2 people working scatted tables and chairs, non that had a plug in! So I worked until my laptop died, then wandered around the store. At one point I heard a pin drop and decided it was time to leave. (Okay, I made that last part up, but seriously... It was crazy how quite the place was)

Our go to spot in St. Albert. Pub food is always steady and what you expect, great for wing night on Tuesdays. Staff are always friendly. A great relaxed atmosphere,  no BS here. Awesome spot for St. Paddy's Day, Eskimos bus, etc. Wish the beer tap selection was a bit more diverse  (heavy on Molson products) but good specials.

I grabbed some lunch while checking out the Century Casino. 

In my opinion most casinos have pretty darn good food and this place is no exception! 

I ordered a coffee (hot & fresh) and a prawn rice bowl. It arrived without much of a wait and looked delicious! Big prawns, snow peas, broccoli, carrots, hoisin sauce over fluffy jasmine rice. I was pretty happy the veg was prepared perfectly (cooked but still a bit of a crunch). It tasted delicious, and the portion was pretty generous too. 

The menu had lots of offerings such as appies, sandwiches, some desserts and a good variety of entrees. I also noticed there were a number of daily specials available at a great price! 

My waitress was very nice and gave just the right amount of attention to me. Good service, a quick meal, honest and fresh food at a reasonable price make this place a winner in my books.

Not happy with my last service (note all others seemed ok).  A bunch of yahoo youngsters with their pants slung low working on a Saturday should have been my first clue to leave.  I had the oil change done and they seemed confused like they didn't know what they were doing. At my next oil change at a different Jiffy Lube I asked for 10-30 synthetic since this is what St.Albert talked me into switching to.  To my alarm the guy at the new location informed me they don't carry 10-30 synthetic and none of the Jiffy Lubes do!! This makes me wonder what they put in my car? And maybe that's why I was burning two liters between oil changes and having engine lights come on for various emissions issues?  AND the new location read the notes and noticed the yahoos put a note in about snapping off one of the clips on my air filter cover. Thanks for telling me.  Since I now have the right oil my car is no longer burning oil.  Needless to say I won't be back.

Always well staffed with people ready to help you find what you need.

Nice selection of gift-y sort of stuff.  If you're lost on what to buy somebody (especially for a housewarming gift!), this is the place to come.

The starbucks is fine, but it seems that they are always training somebody new.  The sitting area is pretty small and crowded, but it's fine to grab a cup and go.

Staff are definitely the draw here though.  Very friendly and helpful.  And there's never too big of a crowd here, so you can quietly shop and sip your coffee.

So..... we went here as part of a walking pub crawl and although it felt like we stepped in to a bit of a time machine we had a great experience!  The staff was really friendly and attentive, the prices were great, and the food was perfectly tasty pub fair. We will definitely be back!

I have been coming to this liquor store for over 10 years. It was such a great find, and I make a point of going there whenever I am in St Albert. I would give it a 4.5 stars if that was possible, but I can't give it a 5 star mostly just because of cost. I think most of the liquor is fairly priced there but some of the scotches we buy are quite a bit cheaper at Superstore Liquor Store. When we want to try a new scotch we always go there and sample quite a few before making a purchase. A couple of the guys there are very knowledgeable about scotches and when making a purchase that is 70-100 dollars it is really nice to be able to sample and talk about it.

I love wandering around in the store.....there is ample selections of wines from around the world, a large wall filled with different Scotches, many kinds of ciders and beers. ....and much much more. 

Great store... And great staff!

Neighbourhood pub in mall in St. Albert.  Medium size with older decor.  Open with large round bar counter which is quite nice. A n of TV screens and some slots.  Beer is cheap.  Food is good and had nice green beans with the entree.  Definitely an older crowd.  No wifi.  Seems to be popular with locals.  More of a quiet place with some ACDC playing in the background LOL!.
Fantastic service Every Time !!!!! Love those guys !! Cassidy is so darn amazing !!!! 5  Service all the way !!! Will not go anywhere else for oil changes on our vehicles !!! Thanks Jiffy Lube !!!

Bj's turn around was good for a typical tune up. They did unauthorized work on my mower and wouldn't listen to reason. My bill went from $60 to $180 with no phone calls or emails. I wouldn't recommend this shop to anyone because they have no integrity. The worst part is the extra that they charged me for doesn't work as designed. Go somewhere else!

This is our neighborhood liquor store and that probably rings true for more than a few. It has a casino, great restaurant pub and the Servus Place near by. 

The staff is very approachable and give great choices in various price ranges. I am always pleased with my choices and always impressed by their selection.

Stop by for the wine tasting and vast range alone but you will likely will be impressed with the entire place. 
My best reviews are a four star but this almost deserves a five, next best hing to a unicorn for me
Good service.  Decent diner fare.  About 30% more expensive than it should be.

It was a Saturday morning and we wanted breakfast.
My friend suggested that we go to Campbell's in St. Albert because she had a 50% Groupon.

The restaurant is not easy to spot because most of the buildings are the same colour and there's no big signs that points to this restaurant.
Boring atmosphere and unusual one of a kind clientelle.

It's a small family owned restaurant with only one waitress on the floor, so there was quite a wait for service. 
It was a standard breakfast menu that you can find at any diner.

We both had the egg benedict with hollandaise sauce. I had a fruit cup as a side. I was plesantly surprised by how good it tasted. It definately cost less than Coras!

I don't mind coming back again if I happen to be in the area, but I'm really impatient and would really like the waitress to come around more often!

Tried another breakfast place in St Albert this weekend.  I thought the menu had quite a few things that sounded good to try.  

We shared the Ole omelette - Mexican omelette with avocado, salsa, cilantro, bacon, sour cream and freshly aged cheddar 

The omelette was really tasty. If fact was it was one of the best omelette that I have had in a long time.  I was not a fan of the shredded potato. The only down for the omelette was that it was not very hot,  but that happens often when you add salsa and sour cream to hot food.

Nice restaurant in St. Albert. Classy, warm and welcoming interior with interesting food choice and very good quality. Service is excellent too, just the price level on the high end. Would definitely come back here!

Went out for dinner with friends. Service was friendly and the Tuna carpaccio was tasty. The ceviche is wrongly labelled, more of a poached shrimp and scallop. My entree was simply terrible. The pistachio crusted halibut sound intriguing but the halibut was way overlooked and super dry, and the topped with a horrid lemon sauce. This sauce tasted like lemon meringue pudding and was god awful sweet. The manager was very attentive and took it off our bill- do not think we will go back despite the friendly service. My husbands ribeye was not seasoned at all and not cooked evenly.

The beef barley soup starter was quite good.  So was the cilantro chutney served with the 3 small samosas which looked homemade.

My wife wasn't thrilled with her steak sandwich which was a bit over done and under seasoned, served with what seemed to be frozen fries.  She mentioned that the steak didn't seem like a fresh steak and was probably from frozen. 

My salmon was a very small portion (looked like about a 4oz portion, but description was 6) of adequately cooked salmon served with the smallest baked potato that I've ever had at a restaurant!   Instead of the cilantro, there was a small piece of parsley topping the salmon and the described green tea and char flavours were absent and the promised mango and pineapple salsa were no where to be found!  Passable as a simple salmon meal, but not as described, and certainly not adequate for an $18 main course.  

We used a Groupon that she initially only credited $36 of the value of $40 until we asked her to double check the printout that we had given her.
 
Unlikely that we would return given our experience today.
This place is under new management and it isn't as good as it was once upon a time.  It's unlikely that I'll stop by there again.  Meh.

Really great!  It was Michelle F's pictures and review that made me bookmark this restaurant.  And I'm so glad I remembered that when my mom and I were in St. Albert with my nephews and brother this afternoon.

We were there at 1 pm on Saturday afternoon, and the place was unfortunately fairly empty (except for 2 or 3 other tables).  I think they're just too far from downtown to take advantage of the Farmer's Market crowd.  However, our server was extremely friendly and attentive.  She had light bruises on each side of her jaw, making me think that she recently had her wisdom teeth out, or maybe some other kind of dental work/surgery.... but you'd never know it.  She was on top of drink refills and made great recommendations.

3 of us had the donair poutine.  I had originally ordered just the regular poutine, but I asked her if she thought I'd regret not getting the donair version.  So on her suggestion, I changed my order to the donair poutine with no veggies.  My youngest nephew got the kids flap jacks (menu described it as 4 mini pancakes, but his plate had 4 on it).  And my mother had the senior's fish and chips.  You'd never know that it came from the seniors menu... it had two pieces of fish, lots of fries, and really delicious coleslaw.

I should mention that my mom does not usually eat the slaw on her plate... but she really enjoyed it and ate most of it!

The 3 of us were all very satisfied with our poutine.  Even though I had mine without the veggies, I observed that those who did have it, had crispy lettuce and fresh tomatoes.

All of our orders were correct.  And everyone really enjoyed it.  We all had leftovers.  The value can't be beat and I will definitely be back (even though I live in Summerside!!)

When people go to the casino, their intention is to usually gamble, not eat. However, casino restaurants are a good place to satisfy your hunger even if you didn't intend on going to the casino in the first place! Hidden inside Century Casino St. Albert is a restaurant that goes by the name of Vee Restaurant & Lounge. Switzerland-born Executive Chef Michel Rey serves casual favourites and comfort food. On Friday and Saturday nights at 9 pm, you can find live entertainment. On weekdays, there are daily specials which usually lead to a full house of locals, such as Prime Rib Thursdays. You can also find monthly feature specials if you want to stray away from their menu.

I started off my meal with an order of yam fries. Served with chipotle mayo, these fries were fresh and crispy with the right amount of salt. They were honestly some of the best yam fries I've ever had! Would recommend ordering this as an appetizer or even as a quick bite.

My friend had the mac and cheese which came with naan bread. We found the naan bread pairing to be a bit odd but no complaints on the taste. As for the mac and cheese, it had a creamy blend of brie and swiss cheese. It wasn't overwhelming cheesy, and the noodles were cooked well with a nice chew to it.

Our server told us that the steak sandwich was the most popular item on the menu so I decided to try it. The steak itself was cooked well, it was tender but I wish there was a bit more seasoning on it. I liked the garlic baguette that came with it as you really can't go wrong with garlic bread. For my side, I decided to go with a baked potato which came with the usual fixins.

My friend's main dish was similar to mine, except his steak came with vegetables, mushrooms, and mashed potatoes. He also thought his steak was cooked properly and enjoyed the fresh vegetables that came with it. For his side, he went with the mashed potatoes which he said weren't anything special but did the job (when do you ever go wrong with potatoes?).

If you're looking for a sweet ending, there are a variety of desserts offered. My friend and I shared a lemon meringue pie which was the monthly feature dessert. Other desserts that they have are carrot cake, tiramisu, turtle cheesecake, and chocolate pecan bread pudding.

Vee Restaurant & Lounge is a good place to grab a bite if you're in the St. Albert area. They also offer banquet facilities and private dining.

I am am happy that this restaurant is close to home.    

I ordered menu items for pick up on two occassions and have not been disappointed.  My last order included chicken quesedilla and a large meat pizza.

The chicken quesedilla was moist and hot.  The cheese was not overpowering and the chiken tasty.  It came with salsa and sour cream, a must for quesedillas.  It also comes with your choice of fries or salad. I chose the salad which was full of fresh vegetables and crispy lettuce.

My husband and daughter had the meat pizza and it was dimolished.  The puzza was not greasy and the toppings were generous.

The first time my husband and I ordered we had the beef dip.  It was also delicious with lots of beef and a soft bun. We both had fries with gravy as our side.  It was very filling!

I would definitely recommend Appetite Global.  The staff are very friendly and helpful.  The food Is well prepared and reasonably priced.

My most favourite bookstore/Starbucks to hang out in. Love the store, the employees, the merchandise but most importantly...the ambience and feeling of utter escape from the harsh world.
Love you, my Chapters!

We stopped in for brunch on a Sunday and aside from 1 table, we were the only ones there. Walking in, there is a small buffet area to the right and a fairly simple looking dining area. A little dated, even.

We weren't going to get the buffet since the menu online looked pretty extensive, but the menu we were given was significantly smaller with maybe 1/2 the options on their website. My guest ordered the coconut french toast combo (add a side of bacon or sausage plus 2 eggs for an extra $4) and I had the buffet since I wasn't super excited about anything on the menu. 

The woman working the front of the house (cash, taking orders, clearing tables) asked if I needed anything fresh from the buffet. To be honest, the buffet didn't look super fresh, but she offered me fresh pancakes, eggs and I asked if toast was part of it (it wasn't) but she had the kitchen make me fresh toast and didn't charge me for it. That was very nice! Basically I had a mostly made-to-order fresh meal with an unlimited supply and it was pretty good. The other options on the buffet weren't my favourite as they were pretty dried out.

Service was very friendly and I really appreciated her offering me fresh food from the buffet. I

Just had one of the best dining out experiences I have had in some time.  A very friendly staff, able to make good reccomendations and provide excellent food.  We had a varied meal that everyone enjoyed.  Kid sauce portions are a little small for us but very tasty.  

Prices are very reasonable.  Cannot say anything else but that we'll be back.

Great place for a beer and a little bit of a hole in the wall which I really like. Had the food for the first time and not impressed. Wife ordered potato skins and it ended up being 2 potato's cut in half baked with cheese and raw bacon. I had the clubhouse and it was not the best. No mayo, very dry, bread was hard as a rock, fries were covered in tons of salt. Waitress didn't come check on the meal once. Oh well, We have been looking for a good pub food joint and this place is not it. The search continues.

Having been to Mr.Lube in St Albert and found their service and advice useless, I wanted to try something new. I got the basic oil change for my kids runner (2009 Patriot) and was served by Cassidy. Outstanding service. Quick and professional and also reset a few warning lights free of charge! Great customer service and will be definitely going back. Give them a try and you won't be disappointed.

Quaint little place in a mostly retail strip mall area.  The staff were really friendly and attentive.   Let's be accurate though. This is a straight forward no nonsense cafe. For what it is, the food was good, clean and presented as you would expect for a 'diner'.

I must give them praise for the cleanliness of their washrooms.  For those of you that have gone to the odd diner or two, usually the facilities are not the best. For this place, they were a very pleasant surprise.

I had a Reuben Sandwich,  it was correctly.  The rye bread was grilled (not just toasted) with Swiss cheese and smoked meat, with just enough mustard. This gave the bread just the right crunch. Give it a try it worth it.
Plenty of tvs and good service at this great dive bar.....drink prices are awesome...didn't eat there but will be back to try the menu...
Outstanding service plus a wonderfully varied menu. The prices are very reasonable too!
Popped in for a quick lunch, quickly seated not many customers. Ordered chicken, received fish. Gravy lumpy and bland. Service was good.

Summary:
- new food option in the area; part of Apex Casino
- simple pub food with a few other options; lunch specials during the week

Detailed review:
Vee Restaurant/Lounge is attached to the Apex Casino in St Albert. The Casino was renovated in recent years and I believe the lounge/restaurant is fairly new. The space is quite comfy although it is adjascent to an area with a bunch of slot machines so you need to be able to handle the typical sounds coming from slots. There are lots of TVs which typically have an assortment of sports on. 

Food is standard pub food although they also have an entrees section that has simple steaks, stirfried dishes with rice, etc. Nothing will blow you away but they do have good onion rings! Great place for a snack if you are gaming in the building or want to have a drink in a non-busy environment. They also have lunch specials every weekday - I sometimes work around the Apex Casino and this is a welcome addition to the few food options in this area.

We came here with a Groupon and it was nothing we expected to be perfectly honest. The only good thing I have to say is that my Chicken Parm was AMAZING. The service was atrocious though. We were sat beside the bathroom, forced to order drinks before we even actually sat in the booth, had to wait 20 minutes to have our order taken, and then I watched our waitress give our order to the chef another 10 minutes after she had already taken it. All in all, we waited about 1 full hour to get our food. They only had one waitress on the floor, who was also acting as the hostess, so I felt kind of bad but she literally walked past us 8 times while we were waiting to give our order and she couldnt even muster up a "I'm really sorry, I'll just be another minute". I would really rather give this restaurant a 2.5 stars, but that is not an option. It is definitely NOT a date night spot, but okay to go to for a home cooked style meal with family. I heard every other table that left before us complain about the service as well while they were paying. We were also not impressed with the portion size. I think we got about 15 fries each and 1 cup of frozen veggies (they weren't too terrible if you're not too picky, as they fry them in butter and add lots of seasoning). There is no way we would ever go back and would definitely NOT recommend this place to anyone that asked. I really do hate to leave a bad review, but i dont want anyone wasting their time or money.

I love going for breakfast here with friends and family. There is a great atmosphere and very friendly staff. We bring the kids and dine on the pancake combo or hit the morning buffet line. The naan bread is incredible, second only to the delicious pancakes. It's a great place for a post workout meal to catch up with friends!
Quick turn around!!! Dropped off our mower at 1 pm and I was called to pick it up by 5pm.  Reasonably priced- highly recommend.

My husband and I enjoy the Crown and Tower. Just a good, solid pub. 

It's spacious and comfortable. It's quite big, actually, but gets busy during hockey games and other events. The crowds have been older and well-behaved when I've been in during the evening so it's a fun, comfortable time.

We have been in around lunch time often and it's a terrific place to sit back and relax a bit and have a good lunch.

Give it a try if you're looking for a place to chat, watch a game and relax with a beer.

I am so angry. Ended up bringing my lawnmower in and it was tuned-up, but still would not work. I paid them for the tuneup. Staff tells me they will recheck it for no fee. Then they went ahead and fixed it a second time, for a huge bill that I did not and would not have agreed to. When I complained, Brian was rude and refused to stand behind his work. He also would not stand behind the promises made by his staff, just said they were wrong. Stay away from this place. I will never ever use them again.

This is similar to a cozy pub only super sized! It seriously has that pub feel with a dartboard on the back wall, coin pool table (free on Sundays) and lots of tables to sit at. They have several big screen TVs to proudly show the Oilers in action. There are a few VLTs in one corner. They've got a decent sized patio - a bit of a surprise for a strip mall pub. 

It wasn't very busy when I arrived which according to the countdown clock on the wall was half an hour before an Oilers' game. The demographic is 30+ I'd say. There were couples that came in that looked about my parents' ages. A table had some guys around my age, but no one younger than that. 

They offer a full menu. I ordered an appetizer - mussels - which were pretty tasty though had tomatoes cut up into the dish which I totally wasn't expecting. They offer daily specials so either check out the board on the way in, ask the wait staff or check the menu.
Went for lunch; excellent food, great service; highly recommend the butter chicken with naan bread.

I'm often on the lookout for quick meals, and I won't stand for food that's merely functional. There's no reason a low-brow meal can't be delicious and totally enjoyable and, in most cases, in a pleasant setting with friendly vibes. Appetite Global Cuisine is a charming restaurant that offers value and is perfect for your next date night or dinner with parents.

The atmosphere is warm and inviting, and the friendly service is knowledgeable and efficient. And above all, the food is excellent and it's very reasonably priced. You really can't go wrong here. For something tasty and Italian, their seafood linguine is packed full of flavor and they use as many fresh ingredients as possible. The Moroccan beef kebabs were perfectly seasoned and tasted amazing with the couscous. For the price point and the quality of the ingredients they use, it's hard to beat Appetite Global Cuisine. Where else can you have enjoy Italian linguine, Austrian schnitzel, Korean BBQ ribs and Moroccan kefta all at the same restaurant?  

What's also awesome about them are the great people who run the restaurant.  Chef Reggie has an impressive career spanning Asia, Switzerland,Germany, Belgium, Montreal and Edmonton with previous work experiences that include working for 5 star hotels and was the former Executive Chef of Chateau Lacombe. His Swiss trained culinary background definitely shows in the selection and quality of dishes here. 

Everything is made from scratch and if you have gluten sensitivities, Chef Reggie can also prepare meals to accommodate.  He also bakes gluten free bread for those who want to have bring home some fresh baked bread.  I highly recommend!  This is definitely our new favourite restaurant in St. Albert.

This is your friendly neighborhood diner if you live close by. Bazinga!
I recently discover this diner after getting sucked in by their 50% off Groupon offer.... and ..... it probably wouldn't be my first choice in "lets head out for dinner!" unless my company just needs a burger fix. 

This restaurant may be hard to find for the first timers - it's right beside the sports lounge. They have a dozen or so tables for seating - the waitress (friendly & polite) allows you to seat where you please. Their menu is nicely presented on their website with the typical steakhouse/diner offerings. But if you're looking for that "one of a kind" meal - you may have better luck elsewhere. 

One thumb up for the few choices of cakes on their dessert menu - however I am not entirely confident that they are as freshly made as say the Safeway bakery. 
There is a widescreen centered in the dining room for those die hard sport fans. But if you're looking for the "happening" atmosphere, this establishment may be a bit quiet & deserted. 

Portion wise - the standard entree is guaranteed fill you up, even if it will clog up those blushing arteries in 0.5 seconds.
Requested they pick up my mower to service it. Guy said they would pick it up that night between 5 and 8. 8:30 still no show or no phone call. Sad customer service.

I visited the pub for the first time last week with 2 friends. We were there to catch their happy hour starting at 4:00. We are seniors and were glad to see many others in our age range. There was no music and that was fine with us. The selection of beer was adequate.  However, if you are looking for craft beers this may not be the place. The Supercans on special turned out to be a good choice. Two of us ordered the Ukrainian Nachos (perogies) which were delicious. The server was very friendly and knew the beer and the menu well. All in all a good place for a beer and a snack or a meal.

Thank you Chapters for having a Starbucks inside, having a children's section with a few items out to enterain my monkeys, and for having what I was looking for.

So why only 4 stars you ask?  Perhaps it is not Chapters fault and just my HATRED for Canadian pricing on books.  Seriously!?!  $22.95 for a hardcover copy of a Dr. Seuss book... Really?

Chapters is clean and bright with friendly staff.   They have some excellent sale sections but alas... I'm still peeved at having to pay $24 for a children's book.  So, 4 stars it is.  If Yelp would let me, I'd give you 4.5.

You are still my go to and I will remain forever loyal.

Signed your book loving book worm but CDN publisher price listing hater,

Kristin

Had not been in this restaurant in at least a couple of years. Remembered the breakfasts were always good so decided to stop as I was going right past. This is a place with a large crew of regular customers and the very friendly waitress knew all of them by name. 

Had the early bird, before 11, breakfast special, $8.00 without coffee. Two eggs, hash browns, toast and bacon, sausage or ham. Eggs done perfect, soft boiled, bacon crispy and the hash browns had great flavour. A little garlic, green onions, and home shredded real spuds make hash browns that have flavour and body. 

They were also getting ready for lunch. They have  $13.95 buffet  Friday and Thursday. Thursday is Ukrainian buffet. Looked great and had a pile of people showing up for lunch. Definitely a place worth trying.

I had a previous oil change done in BC where the oil filtre was not on properly and we drove to alberta, so needless to say, I was a bit apprehensive to go to another quick oul change shop. Thankfulky I found the Jiffy lube here in St. Albert.

The customer service was awesome there. They were friendly and fast and I felt welcomed there. Also can we mention the awesome displays they have when you drive by?! They seem to be a festive bunch.

Altogether it was a great experience and my car is still in one piece. That reminds me, I better go back for the next oul change!

I've never been to Campbell's before Sunday. It was super easy to find and in a great location for anywhere. I live on the West End of Edmonton and because it's right off the Henday, it literally took 13 minutes. The waitress was prompt on drinks and was very friendly. The food didn't take very long to get to us, and I could hear the burger/food cooking while we were talking so it was fresh. The food was delicious. Just like most diner foods. I really liked the chicken quesadilla. The gravy was really good as well. After we were done eating, there was no rush to leave, it was very relaxed. I would definitely go back again as there are so many things on the menu I'd love to try. My boyfriend's "Bigger Boy Burger" looked delicious as well as my Bestie's Beef dip and poutine! nom!

I was experiencing an oil leak and returned to Jiffy Lube to check the problem. He assured me that it was not their service that was the cause of the problem. He sent videos showing the oil change I had received from Jiffy and was patient in explaining the cause of the leak and even contacted the car dealership to rectify the service charge for repairing the leak. Even though I still had to pay the full cost of the repair at the dealership, I think the excellent customer service Jiffy provided was above and beyond and I would certainly recommend their shop.

My husband picked me up for work for my one-hour lunch break today, and we headed to Appetite. We got there around 1, and were seated within two minutes. There was nobody else in the restaurant, and as far as we could see, only one employee. The server came over and when we mentioned our Groupon that expires on November 11th, she stated that they no longer accept the Groupons, and that I "received an email". I did NOT receive an email. She said I could contact Groupon for a refund. 

My husband and I left the restaurant with NO food, and no desire to go to this restaurant again. I am not looking forward to having to contact Groupon about a refund, because a restaurant could not follow through on a commitment.
Great Service, knowledgeable staff, and hours till late in the day. Great selection of beer, vodka, rum, tequila, wine, brandy. Reasonable prices.

Ask the server for off menu items such as whole wheat pancakes with nutella and bananas.  We had fish pakkoras (off menu) with cilantro mint yogurt.  

Servers were friendly and motivated, as they were both owners.  Lots of free parking and just minutes from Henday freeway.

I searched up an item on one of the computers to see that there were 21 copies in the store. "Consignment" was the location of all 21. Not knowing what that meant I seeked help. After searching for about 5 minutes for a store associate I was finally able to pinpoint one only to see that 3 others were together chit chatting at the back of the store. I asked for assistance, and after an awkward moment of exchanging looks to each other to decide who would help me, one of them finally takes initiative. It seemed that she too had no idea where the 21 copies were so she had others look as well. I decided to have a seat while I waited. 15 minutes had passed and I began to grow impatient. As I stood up to search for the original staff member who was helping me, she casually walks by with a Starbucks coffee on hand and walks straight to the break room. Why hadn't she bothered to update me? Irritated, I went to look for another staff member, only to find all of them huddled together chit chatting ...again!
"Oh, she didn't tell you? We don't have any."

Thank you St. Albert chapters for wasting my time with your unprofessionalism and lousy staff.

This place sucks and is dangerous to your cars health.

First couple of times I went there I was pretty impressed with the service. Last time I went there however I took my wife's 1992 4runner in. It is in pristine shape, 130,000 original Klms.

The guys that tried to change the oil obviously didn't know you have to remove the front splash panel to get at the filter. They tried to access it from the wheel well and ended up ripping the protective skirt out. No offer to replace it, just zip tied it in place and tried to say nothing. Told them they had to access through front and showed them where.

A couple of months after I notice oil spots on the garage floor. Look under truck and appears to be dripping from around the oil filter. Take off splash panel and sure enough the filter is loose, not only that, it is the same NAPA filter that was on it when I took it in the be change. Obviously loosened the filter to remove and either forgot to finish the job or didn't have a filter to fit.

Service has really gone in the toilet here. No way would I let them touch another one of my vehicles. Will go back to doing them all myself. At least then I know it was done right, all the zerks were greased etc. This could have been a very expensive mistake if the filter had come the rest of the way off

Tried going there on February 13th with my family for dinner. The website stated they were open until 8:00 pm. Arrived at the restaurant at 6:30pm and the door was locked and the restaurant already closed. The sign right next to the door also said they were open until 8:00pm. This was my first time trying to go to the restaurant and will probably be the last. The family and I went to a different restaurant that night and thoroughly enjoyed the meal. Appetite Global Cuisines loss!

Home decor! Books! Toys! Chapters really has it all. This location has been awesome to visit during the restrictions because I feel like they really have nailed down all of the protocols. 

The curb side pick up is also awesome. I particularly like to scope out the on sale racks because there is always something to find there. The kids section is pretty good as well, with a nice selection of books and toys for the little ones in your life.

Went there today to purchase a bottle of liquor. Despite the claim that GST & bottle deposit are included, my price after special discount was more than the sticker price! Seemed to go over the head of the cashier as he wasn't able to figure it out. Didn't appear that there was any management in the store. Received only a small credit after arguing that still did not reflect the correct price.
Close to home great layout and selection of products Awesome service from staff ahead of May long weekend 2020.

Our wedding is coming up and I don't drink, so choosing a wine has been a very overwhelming process. After going to about half the liquor stores in the city, I came to Campbell. The Sales Associate spent a very long time with me going through all of my options at my price point. The selection was far better than any other store, with lots of unique wines you don't see everywhere. The Sommelier came in too and together they found me the perfect wine, and under budget! Thank you so much and if I will definitely be coming back here!

I wasn't exactly sure what to expect when I came to this restaurant... It's located within the Apex Casino in St. Albert and that place is a definite eyesore from the outside. The parking lot is dirty and the building looks pretty sketchy...

But then you walk in.

It's clear that this casino has undergone some major interior redesign. It's actually really trendy and well down. Everything is super clean and new. Completely opposite to what it looks like outside, which was a relieving surprise.

Vee Restaurant and Lounge is on the inside, it's open concept in between all the slot machines. One side is more dining room, and the other side is more lounge with a sit-up bar. Our server was very nice and went above and beyond to answer our questions. 

The food came out relatively quickly, which is good! I had the beef dip with soup. The beef dip was delicious, although it didn't come with horse radish - so I stole some from my mother-in-law and then it was really good. My soup was really bland. Some creamy white perogey bacon soup which sounded good in theory but wasn't that good in reality.

My in-laws both got this prime rib, but it was extremely fatty. They don't like fat so they lost about half their entree just cutting off this thick slices of straight fat. 

So ya, other than the food only being so-so, it honestly wasn't that bad. It's not the type of place I would normally go to but it really wasn't terrible. The service was good and that's usually all I ask for in a place.

Been a customer for 8 years.  Nice atmosphere with excellent staff & nice people.  On Tuesday wing night I thought I would ask for an order of wings to go for my sick wife at home.  Ownership has a rule where to get the 00.35 cent special, it pertains to eat-in only, not takeout whereas the full cost is applied.  So I thought I would double the order for the eat-in & what ever was left over ask to package up to take home.  Ownership said no to the doggy bag request, even though I had spent 4 hours here with friends & many pints during this visit. 

After 8 years as a regular, I was ticked-off at Ownership's  cheap, cheap mindset & silly rules. So I have decided to take my money elsewhere.
Chapters a great place to pick up knowledge, escape to your fantasy world, enjoy the words of famous personalities in a memoir. And enjoy a chuckle in the humor section. Enjoy the gift of words.

BJ's Fix It Shop in St. Albert completed unauthorized repairs to a snow blower we own. My husband called the shop and explained the machine likely had bad gas in it, as it's pretty much brand new and we couldn't get it to start. Along with fixing this - they also did a tune up on it - Kevin didn't realize till he got home the bill seemed unreasonably high. He went back in after work today and explained we did not ask for a tune up, the snowblower is brand new. They refused to refund the difference in the bill insisting Kevin asked for that work. When he again explained he didn't, they still refused. Really!? Beware folks - this is not the first time we've seen questionable work completed that was not authorized.

This place is a great hidden gem in St Albert.  I think lots of people don't realize it's even here because of the bar next door (Bourbon Room).  We have been coming here for over a Year now and love it.  The owners are super nice and attentive to every table.  A year ago they were just using the old Campbell Restauraunt menu but were making their own flourishes with the menu items, the food has drastically improved from the previous owners.  Over the past year they have renovated the place, replacing the tables and chairs, and launched a new amazing menu.  We have had the fish and chips (freshly battered fish that melts in your mouth), burgers (homemade tasty patties and fresh toppings), and the Korean ribs ( super tasty and a good sized portion), Donair (Tasty big portion), Stuffed mushrooms (exploding with stuff), Steak Sandwich ( Good size on a garlic bread), and their appetizer soups of the day (all obviously homemade).  There new menu has so much on it and we can't wait to try other new things.  Also the prices are all reasonable for what you get, you won't leave here hungry that's for sure.

Unbelievably BRUTAL experience!  Seriously, avoid and save your evening.

Here's a quick summary of my Feb 14 disaster.
- arrived at 7pm for my 7pm reservation
- seated at waiting table and purchase a bottle of wine
- my gf and I are seated at 9.10pm (had no other reservations!!)
- manager comes by at 9.30 to touch base.  We still hadn't seen a waitress! He takes order
- food comes in time.  Wrong dessert.  Gf complains. Manager says I can keep the wrong dessert for free given the disastrous evening!!!! 
- appears all or most of the female guests leave with a rose; however, no rose is presented to my date.  We dash and never look back!

Unreal wait time. Never saw a server all night.  Expensive dinner. Wrong food.  Insult. No rose. Never again

I went here with my family, a group of 6 people including my parents and grandparents, and the menu had something for everyone. They have a small seniors' menu with a few options on it. The menu offers lots of options, including pasta, sandwiches, salads, burgers, pizzas, steaks, etc.  

A few members of our party asked for some alterations to their meals, and it wasn't a problem. Everything came to the table accurately. Plus the portion sizes were good. Three of us shared an XL pizza and it was definitely too big for us. It would have been enough for 4, or 3 people who were very hungry.

Service was good and quite quick. Servers were owners of the restaurant and eager to please. 

As I mentioned, prices were decent. Total bill came out to around $100 for 6 people, and that included 2 alcoholic drinks and one appetizer.

This place is definitely worth a try if you're in St. Albert.

Great place

Location and food is one of the best. We booked a reservation through yelp and I found that be be a super easy experience and I would do it again. We chose to sit on the patio. We had the crab cakes to start which were fantastic. I had a tough time choosing a entree as most of them look good. The rib eye won my eye and it did no disappoint. Dessert I chose creme brûlée. It was good not the best I have had but tasty. 

The prices were decent for portions given. I don't drink but I did appreciate a half price refill on soda. 

I will be back for sure

St Albert Centre has recently undergone renovations adding a wing/hallway and modernizing. 

The new look from the outside is much more esthetically pleasing - Winners in particular is quite attractive from the outside now. 

My tween daughter lives that Ardene's is now giant and in the old Winners location.

Best addition was the rethinking of the Primary Care Network here which makes these invaluable mental and physical health resources much more accessible to the public. 

The food court continues to be utterly disappointing - ever since Rocky Mountain Chocolate Factory left, there's not much for me to get excited over.  

There's quite a few empty or still under renovation spots in the mall as well. 

I think fellow Yelper, Joy K. accurately portrayed the Black Friday event in her review so I won't go into as much detail but I will say that it was a huge disappointment and they changed the program or the event specifics AFTER tickets had already been sold.  There were no special deals for the attendees only and people waited in line more than 30 minutes to get into the roped off area for a glass of sparkling fruit juice, chocolate, charcuterie board, and to fill out the ballots for giveaways.  Nothing was as originally advertised and left a really bad taste in my mouth for both the misrepresentation (almost bait & switch) and then the extremely poor customer service.

Overall, there's been some positive design updates to St. Albert Centre but there's a lot of room left for improvement.

2 stars on Yelp is described as "Meh, I've experienced better" on their ratings guidelines and that would most definitely be the case here.

I find myself making the 10 - 15 minute trip to St. Albert, more often than not, on my days off now. Either to deliver experimental baked goods to my coworkers or to find good eats! Two weeks ago, Joe managed to find his way to St. Albert to join me at Yuzen, one of the few sushi places in the area. (You can read about it here). Right across Herbert Road, located in the same parking lot as Safeway, lies another sushi restaurant, Ohana-Ya. With a couple of friends favoring Ohana-Ya over Yuzen, I decided it's only fair if I try both to compare, and soon too! When my coworker, sushi-crazy (or general-crazy, if you know her) Jessica, was free for dinner, it was a no-brainer.

On a Wednesday evening, the place was sparsely filled although by the end of the evening, most of the restaurant was seated. To compare, Ohana-Ya seats more than Yuzen, although I preferred the decor of Yuzen. Bare walls made Ohana-Ya feel barren. Our spicy tuna tataki came out first. I liked this dish a lot better than Yuzen's tuna tataki although I do have a preference for spicy dishes. The ponzu sauce had a nice kick, although Jess barely detected any heat at all. Some of the heat comes from the seasoning on the tuna as well, so there's no escaping it. If this dish is consistently made like this, I say watch out when smothering your fish into the sauce!

When first introduced to sushi, I was born a roll-girl at heart. Over the course of the last few months, I've learned to eat more sashimi and nigiri, appreciating the taste of fresh fish rather than overly complicated rolls of tempura bits, tobiko, and fancy sauces. I ordered the hamachi and Sockeye salmon nigiri to try. I found the sashimi to be oddly cut, almost twice as long as the rice given, although very fresh. I've also learned that I prefer the Atlantic salmon much more than the Sockeye salmon, the Atlantic having a creamier texture. With a hint of wasabi under each sashimi, the nigiri was mediocre. Something about the rice is also different from other sushi place in town. Undercooked? Super soft? Even Jessica agreed although she didn't dwell too long on it and proceeded to eat and enjoy.

Moving to rolls, which Jess prefers when eating in town (she's experienced the authentic Japanese sushi and only orders sashimi and nigiri when visiting the motherland of sushi). We ordered the seafood sensation roll (avocado, crab salad, scallops, shrimp, tobiko, spicy mayo, fried in tempura, oh my!), sweet tuna roll (tuna, sweet sesame sauce, avocado, tempura crumbs), hanabi roll (spicy tuna, soft shell crab, crab salad, masago, lettuce), and Kamikaze roll (spicy chop chop with tempura bits). Ohana-Ya's selection of rolls is extensive, a must-go for those obsessed with finding different kinds of rolls. They even have 8 varieties of fully cooked rolls, great for those who shy away from the raw stuff (you're missing out by the way). My favorite was the Kamikaze roll, moreso because it was simple, fresh, and a good amount of heat. The other rolls were almost as delicious although minor criticisms were made for a couple: the hanabi could use more spicy tuna mixture, and perhaps avocado instead of the use of lettuce, throwing both of us off. The seafood sensation was mostly filled with artificial crab, something I'm not a fan of, but dynamite roll fans might find it a good alternative. Overall, a good variety of rolls available and something for everybody! I knew we were ambitious in ordering but Jess (differing from my usual companion, Joe) has no restraint when ordering. Love it, more items to try, plus leftovers for others after!

With some of the rolls going home to Jess' hungry significant other, I decided to try the tempura banana with mango ice cream. Why not? Freshly fried, it was delicious! The mango ice cream and whipped cream cooled down hot banana bites and was greatly appreciated. As long as the tempura is crispy, I'm not sure how you can go wrong with this dessert.

Verdict between Yuzen and Ohana-Ya? If you plan on ordering only sashimi or nigiri, I'd recommend Yuzen. If you prefer unique sushi rolls, I'd recommend Ohana-Ya. Both have a good selection of appetizers and entrees and both are around the same prices. Or, if your sushi cravings are more like mine, you'll have time to try both and add both to your cycle of sushi restaurants in the future.

For reference, my favorites are still Ichiban (west side Edmonton), and Sumo Sumo (Sherwood Park).

Very good place to come for sushi as the fish is very fresh.  Also their hot food selection is very good.
Rolls - one of the best on the menu would be the California in snow.
Hot Food - Sea bass is very good, really fresh.
Raw - one of the best toro in the capital region.
They sometimes also carry very fresh Uni which in Edmonton is not easy to find.
Great food, good prices. I eat here very frequently, and the quality is always top notch.

This is a place where the chef and his staff make a genuine effort to ensure that diners leave satisfied. The food is all excellent and dishes are prepared with care. Local sourcing is a priority and the care taken to select the best ingredients shines through in the freshness of the flavours.

love the food. great wine selection, the only thing is that the room always clears out super early.  The staff always look at you like you should be leaving and they want you out around 10. 
we like dinner and drinks to take a few hours so its unfortunate we always feel rushed. I figure if we are spending heaps of money why not stay and serve us with a smile? if you want to have dinner? great place!
if you want to have dinner and drinks and relax?.... go somewhere else! or the staff will stare you down until you're so uncomfortable you leave.

Absolutely hands down the best donair's in Alberta!!! Absolutely love this place. The portions are huge! And very reasonably priced. The staff are on the ball and friendly, service is fast. Sweet sauce or Tzatziki, donair poutine!!!! Highly recommend:))

This restaurant offers great service and delicious food. I went for my birthday back in November and really enjoyed the experience. Great selection of Italian-inspired food and friendly servers. 
My only complaints is that the restaurant is quite small and because of the close quarters, it can quickly become quite noisy on a busy night.

Came here to try a new sushi place.  We had miso soup,  beef tataki,  baked seafood,  chef choice of sashimi,  butterfly roll,  kamikaze roll,  and seafood sensation roll.  

The beef tataki's ponzu sauce was spot on,  with a hint of spiciness.  However,  there was no seaweed - I love seaweed on my tataki.  And the meats are small and very thinly cut. 

The baked seafood came out in a bigger dish than I expected it to be.  I was excited,  but soon was disappointed.  The seafood pieces are probably from those assorted seafood bags the u can make the seafood salad with,  from tnt or superstore.  There as lots, lots and lots of mayo? As the sauce. There it wasn't thick either.  Very watery,  and ended up using it as a topping on one of the sushi rolls.  

The sashimi was alright.  But with the tuna,  you can tell was still slightly frozen.  The red tuna was defrosted and lost the texture the it usually has. 

The rolls were good,  especially the butterfly roll.  It was very light, with the tobiko and the lettuce.  The Kama, kamikaze roll was basically a chop chop roll with tempura on the outside.  I used the baked seafood as a topping.  I liked the seafood sensation,  but honestly it tasted like an upgraded dragon eyes.  

I'm also happy to see a sushi restaurant have a section  for just gluten free meals.
It's an older mall, that's filled with several different stores, your standard offerings including a food court.

First thing first! I saw few negative comments when I searched this place in google and was a little skeptical and kept them in the bottom of the list of shops I wanted to try in buying a new bike. I did manage to go and was pleasantly surprised with my experience with the shop and its personal. No pressures from the sales folks and I was able to get the bike that I wanted with all the information, I required. I also bought a new helmet and they seem to have good selection. I was extremely happy with the bike and the purchasing experience. The bike was fitted to my specifications with little wait time, which is understandable. I returned to the store to buy some good bike U lock in two weeks time. I did not mind the distance having to travel from West Ed to St. Albert. I will go again for other gears and accessories. I would highly recommend this place as it has a personal touch to it without the sales pressure I had seen in big bike shops.

Intimate and romantic yet still appropriate for a family, business meeting or gathering with friends that enjoy good food and wine;) I would definately take a client here if I wanted to impress them. The staff was youthful and friendly and helped make the whole experience enjoyable.

The decor was a little dark for me personally but it had a nice mix of old meets new.

The locally sourced food had decent portions (not big, just filling) and the menu was modern and fun yet still enjoyable for even the simplest of palates.

My husband and I can't wait to go back for our 5year anniversary in July!

I've dined at the River House several times now but most recently I sampled their Crab Cake with pepper sauce on arugula with a lemon oil at the Sturgeon County Wind and Food Festival this past Saturday, on 2013-10-05.

I must say that of all the restaurant/food vendors at the festival, the River House had the best item to order for both value and taste!

The crab cake was cooked to perfection and complimented perfectly by the pepper sauce. 

A+ River House.

Bites like these are the exact reason I will continue to pick you for special nights out!
Super fresh sushi, friendly and laid back atmosphere. Absolutely worth the trip to St Albert. Can't wait to go back!

Oh WOW.
Their large is almost the size of a NERF football. If you can finish this EXCELLENT donair by yourself, GOOD ON YA.
Myself, I needed two tries. I was frickin' STUFFED.
Best donair ever. Period.
Bring a friend and take extra napkins.
Now called 'New Asian Village'. They served the best Indian food I have had in Alberta. As good as any I have had in SF Bay area. Good variety and fresh dishes.

Okay before the food, takes in and I fell asleep let me tell you how amazing this food was. I just moved to the area and wanted to see what the hype was all about this place, let me tell you it is freaking amazing. That's sweet sauce they put on the poutine & Donair just cuts through the Savory aspect. Definitely coming back here

Take your family to enjoy a great new sushi place. My entire family (parents, brother, sister, brother-in-law, and 2 nephews under age 3) enjoyed the atmosphere, the service and most importantly, the food. Even my dad, who does not try anything new, loved the tempura shrimp and yams, and even took a dive into the world of sashimi. Portions were generous and the price was excellent. If you like a lot of variety, get one of their bento entree boxes, you will not be disappointed.

The staff was great and accommodated our baby carrier and a booster chair for my young nephew. 

Make sure you try the Flamingo roll if you like it spicy! 

My only suggestion is that they start accepting American Express cards.

Recently came to Ohana-ya with my mother and daughter.

Loved the variety and different options - like Shrimp miso.

It's like a Japanese Asian fusion - I know that sounds silly but think Sushi house with additional Asian influences.

Everything, absolutely everything we had here was absolutely delicious.

My mom's favourite was the maki roll with salmon and cream cheese - wish I could remember the name.

I really want to come and try Ramen here!

Service was friendly and efficient despite us popping in 50 minutes to closing.

We will definitely be back!
The owner took the time to call me about my service concerns...very impressed! Thank you!
i had the donair poutine, wow it was awesome and extremely filling (huge portions) & extremely clean environment.

Haweli's is one of the best places for friendly and reliable service. The server comes often as they can, even when busy to make sure everything is good and the customer is happy.
The food there is PHENOMENAL! Easily the best place for Indian cuisine. I've tried quite a few dishes and have no complaints. My personal favourite is their Butter Chicken. Be sure to ask for Coconut Naan bread if you would like to enjoy a sweet treat, as it is not shown on the menu but they will make it for you if you ask. 
I have not once been disappointed by this restaurant and am a frequent visitor.

Ramen. Ramen. RAMEN. You know there's going to be a new post whenever there's new ramen in town. Let's try and keep this short and sweet, if you want more details, check out my first review on Ohana-Ya

Five types of ramen on the menu but they are all in the $11.00-12.00 price range.

Trip #1
- Bento box A ($12.00) - beef with mixed tempura. Comes with edamami, maki, steamed rice and choice of miso soup or a salad. They forgot to bring out my buddy's miso soup but I think there was enough food for him. The bento boxes are great value here.
- Pork gyoza ($7.00) - six pieces of fried pork dumplings. They were tasty but nothing out of the ordinary. If they gave more gyoza, it'd be worth it. But they don't.
- Shrimp shumai ($5.00) - if you're going to go with an appetizer, try the shrimp shumai. Nice and light with a Japanese twist. Yeah, that's a dollop of mustard on top of hoisin sauce.

- Shoyu ($11.00) - soya sauce based broth. Two pieces of cha sui, egg, green onions, bamboo shoots and corn. The noodles had a nice chewy bite to them and the bowl is decently sized. My broth was a bit lacklustre, especially compared to the tonkatsu. It reminded me more of Chinese herbal soups. Lacking depth and flavour, the broth tasted watered down.
- Tonkatsu ($11.00) - pork bone based broth. Pboy was in l-o-v-e. The only time I've been to lunch where he wasn't chatting your ear off. Too busy diving into that bowl of creamy, flavourful pork broth. He would have swam in it if that was a possibility. This was probably the best broth out of the three.
- Tan tan ($12.00) - spicy sesame minced pork. D-Bone ordered this one. He didn't realize there wasn't any cha sui in his bowl, otherwise he would have ordered some. I had a taste and you get hints of peanut in the broth.

Trip #2
- Miso ($11.00) - soy bean based broth. I decided to try out their miso the second time we came for ramen. This one was much better than the shoyu I had previously but again, the broth was still lacking any real depth. I guess it's passable for Edmonton standards but meh.

Overall, I think the ramen is pretty average at Ohana-Ya but hey, it's another option for all you ramen eating lovers out there. Especially if you can't make it out Saturday morning to Yuzen and are craving it for lunch!

I love coming here for brunch on the weekend. The Spa Bennie is like no other! They have a large selection of coffees, teas and lattes as well as a menu that changes seasonally! Definitely recommend this restaurant.

Lunch buffet is incredible. All the food in the world to eat but such limited space in the belly. The food and the service both are very good, and the na'an bread...WOW. For the carb conscious, this is NOT the place to be. Otherwise, indulge and enjoy. You won't regret it.

I was a loyal customer for a year almost and after a while I started subscribing to different series. One week I asked the owner, Roy if I could stop subscribing to all of them and he started asking me why and all of this other stuff and it as because I didnt have enough money to keep buying them so I stopped and he told me i had to keep coming for another two months because that's how far he orders in advance. After two months I asked him it is was over now and he said it would be another month! One week I came in on a Thursday when comics come out on Wednesday's and I asked what i had and he said nothing when it said on the Internet one of the ones I was subscribed to was out! After I asked him he told me I thought you wanted to stop in a rude way and told me to never come back to his store again. If the owner finds out you went to another store he will kick you out. You can get the same stuff for cheaper PR the same amount at other stores like comic king and happy harbor. Go their instead the owner here is a rude man.

I'm upgrading my review from 3 to 4 stars.  While the selection and number of stores remains limited, there are a few staples that keep me coming back like Target and The Children's Place.  The mall regularly runs promotions where you earn free gift cards on a certain day of the week or purchase gift cards and receive a bonus amount free.  Customer Service has stroller vehicles you can check out with your driver's license.  This is a great location for Santa & Easter Bunny pictures without a mile long lineup. And last but not least, they do fun things in the summer like free drive in movies with complimentary treats, balloon animals, etc.  

It's not a one stop shop like West Ed but I'm loving the small town charm and community giveback!
I have eaten at Haweli a number of times and it is always delicious! I have only been there for dinner and would like to try the buffet lunch sometime. Highly recommended.

Okay, I admit it, I was sceptical going in.... Let's start at the beginning: I met the new Head Chef of The River House at an industry event, he said his goal was to be "the best restaurant in Edmonton within the next year"... Ya, that's what I though too: good luck buddy! I mean, in life you have to be your own biggest supporter, your own number one fan (y'all know I'm the Prez of the I Heart Jennie M. Fan Club!) so I immediately admired his tenacity, his brava, his well, prairie oysters at making such a bold sentiment. He and his words stuck with me over the next week, and when I was long over due for a date night with my BFF, whom resides in StA, I figured time to see what this place was all about!

Now being born and raised with family that lives out in Etown's trendy Northern burb-city, I have seen the River House. How could you not? It's a gigantic, old fashioned mansion on the side of the Sturgeon River, smack dab on St Albert Trail! Entering the place I was struck by the gorgeous veranda that wraps around the side of the building, as well as the structure of the place. The River House its self is separated into two smaller rooms, a dinning room that is quaint and has a 1920's feel to it. As well as another room that that looks like it was perhaps redecorated in the last 10 years and it is well, not good. There is no delicate way to say this, the light fixtures look like sperm ready to shoot off from steel holding bays. And the art work clashes garishly with what the feel of the building is emitting. But, we all know it is All About The Food; I don't care if I'm on a park bench or a back alley, if the food blows me away (pun not intended), I'm a fan!! 

The food, simply put, is spectacular. Chef Steve has been well trained, has vision and creativity is pushing the limits as what this sleepy culinary town has seen before. He has taken your Grandfather's steak and potatoes and gastronomically exploded it into this decade! The menu is well balanced, although utterly lacking in the true description of how elegant and amazing each dish is; I'm thinking serious re-write! 

No matter what you order, or if you are just in for wine, order the in-house marinated olives. The are encased in jars with peach hickory smoke that oozes out as the jar is opened; it is an experience that stimulates and delights  taste, smell and sight all at the same time. Amazing! By far my favourite dish is the baked Halibut topped with crispy prosciutto, bathed in a smoked tomato broth with goat cheese, basil and fire roasted sun dried tomato house made ravioli. I have had this dish 3x now, I dream about this dish! I also love the Fois Gras; with toast and red grape reduction - So smooth, buttery soft, crazy amazing. And my final major mention is to the soy lime Beef Short Ribs on garlic mash with green apple puree and julienned snap peas. It is a delectable carnivore's dream!! And to top everything off, there is always an outstanding amuse bûche sorbet to cleanse you pallet. From Pineapple, to Earl Grey & Lavender, to beet & wild honey, they are always fantastic. 

Well done River House, well done!

Best donairs  in the edmonton area. They are very clean. Service is friendly, the donairs come.loaded with lots of meat and whatever topping you want. I usually ask for sautéed  mushrooms  and onions. The sweet sauce it's great perfectly balanced. I never had any of their other stuff because one donair it's more than enough to fill you up.

Not usually do I do updates on restaurants but when I give out 5 stars, it better be as good as when I went there the last time.

Foie Gras & Toast - changed the brioche from my last review which was a huge disappointment as what they gave this time did not pair as well with the foie butter.  The foie was still very good but changing that element really changed the flavors of the whole dish
Chefs special of duo of lobster - it was very good but not to the 5 star level
Steak - sous vide which you don't see this technique used very often around here.  Very tender and excellent flavors.

Wine Selection - good.  We ordered their best wines and the price on them didn't make you feel like it owed you a free meal
Service - excellent.  Our server was very attentive, friendly and knowledgeable.   

Sorry River House but this time the food did not hit the 5 star mark but I will be back, maybe you can earn it back.

Had a mixed donair it was OK but really nothing great the meat was a little too spicy for my liking and the donair itself was pretty greasy it left me feeling kinda gross afterwards. Also waited a really long time to get my order and it wasnt even busy. Owner seems very friendly though might give it another try sometime.

This is the location for St. Albert mall.  The mall is quite clean and has friendly customer service but it needs a face lift - the outside basically has no windows and looks like a giant paved/rocky wall surface.  The mall has a Zellers (soon to be a Target), Bay, and an assortment of typical mall like stores inside.  It doesn't have the traffic to warrant high end stores or chains like Victoria's Secret, Disney Store, Apple store, etc.  For those you will need to make the 15 minute trek to West Ed. There is a fairly decent food court, Please Mum, Cars store, Sports store, Winners, Payless Shoes, Dawgs, and more.  It's nice to have this little mall in our city of 60,000 people but it's not a one stop shop yet :-)

If you sign up on their website for e-mail updates you will get coupons and monthly special notifications in advance.  

I'm really excited and looking forward to the Zellers transitioning to a Target next year!  Hopefully, the mall will get a big of a facelift at the same time!
What a great find, a restaurant where there are real chefs, everything made from scratch and fresh. Even my mother would be imoressed.

THE BEST COMIC STORE IN ALBERTA!

I have been coming to thunderground for over a year know and I can honestly say, it is the best store in Alberta. The staff are so friendly that there are often complimentary cookies or local chocolates for free! Also on your first day there you get a free can of pop! They have an amazing Magic The Gathering collection as well a various Warhammer stuff. Really I cant even think of a better store to spend a weekend at

Had to update my review: Second best sushi in St Albert. The best is across the street. 

I'd suggest sticking to the most commonly eaten fishes (tuna, salmon, shrimp, etc) instead of being adventurous. The spicy Tuna roll is especially tasty because they use Sirracha. 

I would order more often except that it's pricier then I'm used to. But I'm sure it's expensive to get sushi grade fish into land locked Alberta.

Wow. What a pleasant surprise. A buddy and I were looking to grab a bite before a movie and, on his suggestion, it was decided that this would be the place to go. I've never been a sushi nut but I can tell the difference between what's good and what's mediocre and the menu here rates a 12. I really can't wait to come back again.

If I could, I'd deduct half a star for the atrocious muzak.

Simply the best.

Cant put it any other way. Miles ahead of Swiss donair. The meat is seasoned and cooked to perfection, and the spicy option is a game changer. Open till 3-am on weekends, the donair king knows how make the best donair in the city.

This is the biggest garden center I have ever seen. An aerial shot of it looks like it's a farm. I discovered this place when I was shopping for a garden Inukshuk to give my parents for Christmas. I'd looked around a lot and found nothing I liked, and this place had several beautiful options to choose from in their garden accessories mega-section. Seriously, this place is loads of fun, even if you're not the green thumb type. Though you can imagine, if you are a herbaphile, you will find everything you could possibly want or need for your garden sanctuary here. I highly recommend coming here at Christmas time. It is so festive, and you can get a fresh-cut tree, fragrant wreaths, miles of beautiful ribbon, home decor, poinsettias, pots, and so much more. There are four or five giant greenhouses attached to this place, so take some time to come roam. This isn't the kind of place to rush through. You'll want to stop and smell the flowers.

This was a tough one to rate...the food was really good and fresh and my girlfriend and I nice time.  I had the gnocchi and she had the "pasta of the day".  But I felt it was really over priced for what we got.  The bill was over a $100 and all we ordered was 2 appies, one drink each and our meals (which where the cheapest on the menu).  I could be wrong but I personally feel it was over priced.

I have been going to Thunderground for several years now and I have to say that this is the best store in the Edmonton area, at least for playing Magic: the Gathering which is what I do. The owner Roy is extremely friendly and always is ready to help customers, and will always help new Magic players get started. It is a very small store but even still there is always places to play your games of choice or read comics or just hang out. There is always MTG events going on from booster drafts every Wednesday to Friday Night Magic every week (standard is always available, modern is available if enough people sign up, so come play modern with us!). Thunderground is the best hangout for us nerds, so I encourage you to visit!
The best donairs in town simply put hands down. Portion sizes are big and do not let that fool you for quality

Great little candy shop with loads of British imports.

My kids could spend all day here but Mommy's walker can only take the occasional visit.

Expect to pay a premium here so don't let your kiddos talk you into something you could get at the grocery store.

Phenomenal bulk gummies behind the counter and of course salt water taffy - my fave is pear! 

As mentioned by another reviewer, the layout/organization isn't visually appealing but the content is great!

See you soon Candy Boquet!

This is a belated review, but a month ago (or so), my husband took me out for dinner and we tried Luisa Ristorante, based on other positive reviews. It was small, loud and busy the night we went, and it seems like a good idea here forth to make a reservation, but it was a wonderful experience. 

The decor in this place is not modern and the atmosphere makes me think of a cozy little unheard-of place, but wow! The food is great! All I can say is BRUSCHETTA--order some. It's the best! We were totally fighting over it. 

My husband had a herbed chicken pasta dish, which he said was great and I had some cannelloni. Mine was very good! The food was definitely better than your average Italian place, but it was a bit more costly. I do think it is worth it, though. We scoped out other people's meals and they looked awesome too.

This is the sort of place that I would prefer to try on a weeknight, when it would probably be less busy. Go for the bruschetta! I promise you won't be disappointed!

Every time I have been to the Riverhouse Grill my expectations have been raised, and always equalled. The food is superb, the service is even better, and everyone is super nice, from the staff down to the chefs. Highly recommended.

Update (only on ramen): 

Edmonton's ramen race has begun. There's been an influx of ramen lately, from pop ups to storefronts and I could not ask for anything else for my hometown - ramen is my absolute favourite thing to eat. Hands down.
