Ohana Ya Japanese Restaurant in St. Albert is the latest to serve up ramen, an addition to their sushi centric menu. Unlike its competitor across the road with Saturday lunch-only ramen, Ohana Ya offers ramen during the weekdays for the lunch rush. Who would have thought that St. Albert would have a small ramen culture of their own!

Five kinds of ramen are offered, $11 a bowl: shio (salt), shoyu (soy sauce), miso (soy bean paste), tonkotsu (pork bone broth), and tan tan (spicy sesame minced pork with peanuts, $12). All bowls, except for the tan tan, are served with char siu, bamboo shoots, beansprouts, sweet corn, fungus, and a boiled egg. For an additional $2, you get two extra pieces of char siu, and for an extra $1, you can have an extra side item. I assume that means another egg.

Josh was my lunch date this time around, his (questionable) first time eating ramen! He ordered the tonkotsu ramen and paid extra for the char siu. The noodles aren't made in house but were wavy, good consistency, and one of the better noodles I've had in Edmonton and area. Ohana Ya at least is sourcing delicious noodles! A sip of the broth gave me a taste of creamy, rich, and salty pork bone broth. I understand that an "under-seasoned broth is a crime" (high-five to you, fellow ramen lover, if you know where that quote is from), but whoa. It was a touch harder to finish and drink the broth near the end.

I ordered the miso ramen, the fermented soy bean paste a favourite style of mine. The char siu was moist and very nicely done. I hate it when I get lean char siu in ramen. The half egg was medium-hard boiled and very lightly marinated. The menu pictured different bowls, one with a perfectly cooked soft-medium boiled egg, whereas the next photo showed a hard-boiled one. I'm going to assume that the kind of egg you get is a surprise! I really enjoyed my bowl, a good portion and loaded with toppings. I appreciated the two different kinds of seaweed.

I would have preferred for a slightly less salty broth to enjoy the bowl from start to finish, but otherwise it was a solid bowl of ramen for a good value. As they just started offering their ramen menu, hopefully this was just a part of the kinks that need to be ironed out. Comparing it to Yuzen's weekend ramen is a hard sell, seeing that you'll never have to choose between the two on a given day. Ramen is a labour intensive dish to make and I appreciate Ohana Ya Japanese Restaurant for serving it up daily, let alone offer five different kinds. Definitely a must visit when you're in the area or if you have a free weekday lunch. Try it out!

Today was my first time eating here. I went in to get take out using a groupon. They told me the groupon was only good for dining in, I told them it didn't say that in the fine print so they allowed me to order take out. All the staff I talked to were very nice and polite. The food was good. I'll go back. I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 because I think it's a little overprice. Perhaps the buffet is a better deal, I don't know.
PS If you like butter chicken I have a great recipe. Message me if your interested.

Great food! We have been coming here since it opened. The portions are a little small for the price but we always enjoy the quality and taste of the food. We have noticed the rice portions have gotten smaller. The service is excellent and the people are very friendly.

In my experience, there are not many quality restaurants to choose from in St. Albert. Luisaâs is located right in the heart of downtown, and itâs a tiny space with romantic lighting, paintings, Italian music and plenty of smaller tables for intimate meals. The food here is wonderful. You just know by the smells emanating from the restaurant. I start with red wine and their bruschetta, which is overflowing with fresh garden tomatoes, garlic, Parmesan and fresh olive oil. Sometimes I come here just for this appetizer and a coffee. If youâre having a main dish, anything with their signature tomato sauce is a safe bet. You wonât be disappointed. Prices are reasonable, and service is friendly. It has the feel of a small neighbourhood restaurant in the heart of Italy.

River House Grill is located in a converted Victorian House in the heart of St. Albert and is Known for regional cuisine with exquisite presentation.  Most of the salads and entrees are made using local ingredients (both vegetables and meat), and the desserts are prepared in-house.  It is a bit on the pricey side, but the ambience and view is spectacular.  Reservations recommended.

After the Yelp Elite event, I had to come back and hopefully taste the creative dishes. Unfortunately for us, chef Steven was not in and to our dismay, the menu had changed and we could not have the charcuterie.

We both started off with a glass of Mascato which I knew could be big trouble. It was was so subtle and mouth watering that you could probably finish a bottle and not even realize it.

We then had the beet and goat cheese salad and scallop proscuitto for appetizers. I'm not a fan of pungent smelling cheeses but this salad has made me a fan of goat cheese. Paired with a sorbet, the cheese just melts in your mouth with the sweet and savory beets.
The scallops were one of the largest scallops I've ever eaten, seared on the tops while retaining the moisture on the insides. It was buttery smooth and had a good contrast to the salty dried proscuitto. What I really enjoyed about the scallops was the dressing and crunchy bread crumbs that were decorated on the dish. It added smaller complexities which forced me to really slow down eating and enjoy the finer details.

Based on the server's recommendation, we had the bison tenderloin and salmon with chilli aoili. I've never had bison before but as far as I could tell, i could not taste any game-y-ness. It was cooked just right to medium-rare and the parsnip puree was an excellent touch.

The salmon was incredible as it was topped with dried shredded brussel sprouts encompassed by a fluffy chilli aoili which reminded me of an Asian influence. It was interesting to see a balance of western and eastern cuisine fused into this dish.

What I was really impressed with was the accomodation the staff was to our meals. The chefs came up with a play on chocolate mint ice cream for dessert complete with candied rose petals. It was delicious to have the mint chocolate ice cream melt in your mouth followed by a fruity candy burst of flavor by the rose petal. I can't stress how much the staff went above and beyond to ensure our experience was memorable.

My only complaint which in my mind was redeemed as the dinner service went on was there was a lapse in time where we were both waiting for our server to return to take our orders. But to their credit, they were quite tentative and accomodating after our orders were taken!

Dinner was approximately $150 for two.

Will definitely recommend and return here.
Very reasonable prices, especially if you go with the buffet. Very delicious food. My favourite is the chilli chicken, butter chicken and naan!

Awesome experience buying a bike here. The owner and staff are super knowledgeable, the shop is clean and organized, and the selection of products is really good for a smaller shop. Customer service here was the best I've had in a bike shop in a really long time, and buying my there felt good. I would recommend anybody go there for road or mountain.

Truly one of best in Indian dining in the city! The Food is absolutely wow! You will not be disappointed in the buffet.  I have eaten at several indian cuisine restaurants in the city from the fancier to the basic and this one is truly a 10 in all aspects.  

The staff are always friendly and it is truly a beautiful atmosphere to dine in.

Food was delicious. Service exceptional. Atmosphere lacking. Seating outside with lots of street noise and wasps (summer time.)  Though the food was wonderful, albeit quite expensive, the portion sizes were not too large either which we liked, but I don't think we'll be going back any time soon. Didn't wow us.

Still love Thunderground Comics!

Roy, the owner, is fabulous and takes the time to get to know his customers.  He's always excellent with my kids and takes the time to figure out what they'd like. 

He runs weekly game nights and tournaments.  

Roy always supports local artists and you'll be sure to see some amazing talent at the events Roy hosts throughout the year. 

Two thumbs way up!

P.S. Happy FCBD2018!

WOW!

I eat out very frequently at high end places in Edmonton and Vancouver. River House is as good as the best in those cities. They cooked my halibut to perfection and my friends were just as happy with their meals. 

Easily the best surprise find that I've made this year.

My family and I popped into Thunderground Comics last week for Free Comic Bood Day (FCBD) located on the corner of Fairview and Sir Winston Churchill.

Roy (the owner) introduced himself to us and our children right off the bat and had a really great demeanor. 

We inquired if he carried the Vinyl Pop figures which he doesn't but no worries.  He showed us some other goodies and even some artwork made by local peeps.

In the back of the store were some adults playing games (maybe D&D or role play of some sort) at a folding table.

He took the time to speak to my children, find out what their interests are, and suggested which FCBD issues he thought they would like and even gave my little guy a mini Green Lantern figurine.  

Roy was surprisingly great with my kids who usually shy away from strangers and was easily available for any questions we had but never made us feel like he was hovering.

Both of my kids picked out their first comic books here (Jem - Yes, that's right and a variety grab bag of 10 super hero comics for only $10) in addition to a few other goodies the husband picked out. 

All in all it was a great visit - love shopping and supporting local!  The kids and husband are already asking when can we go back :-)

Two thumbs way up to Roy for Thunderground Comics & Collectibles - I'm sure we'll be back soon!

PS - They offer a pretty neat subscription service where for a $10 down, they will hold current subscriptions for a period of time until you can pick them up so you don't have to worry about missing out.

My first review of a comic and collectables store. We met the owner named Roy at the store. Wow. Super friendly, very knowledgeable, and extremely personable. Our nine year old son just started playing magic casually at after school care with his friends. We asked Roy for some guidance on how to build decks around Core 2019 Sets. He was great at giving us a run down of how Magic the Gathering started, the different types of play, and customized what we were looking for to match what would work for our kid.  

Comic selection was a list of new releases. I pick up a couple of copies for myself. 

Thanks Roy!  We will exclusively shop for comics and Magic Cards here when we are in Edmonton. Guys like Roy and places like Thunderground are worth supporting.

Ohana-Ya Japanese Restaurant is a cozy, relatively unknown sushi joint located in a little strip mall area of St. Albert.  They are quite close to Yuzen, another sushi restaurant, which is literally across the street from them. Competition, competition. I've been to both now and I can't really say if one is better than another.

From what I've read and tried myself, Ohana-Ya is known for their rolls while Yuzen is all about the sashimi, nigiri and Saturday ramen. I've only been for lunch at both places so maybe I will have to try out their dinners one of these days. Then again, I'm pretty sure I go during lunch because sushi is so much cheaper that way (at least for Edmonton it is).

Anyways, Ohana-Ya has a very relaxed, easy going vibe to it along with super friendly staff. The service was great when we were there on a Wednesday and they are quick to bring out food.

- 2x tea ($1.00 each) - hot and our cups were consistently refilled.
- Bento Box A - chicken with mixed tempura ($12) - my buddy ordered this and completely devoured it. You know when you just craveeee sushi/sashimi/Japanese food in general? Well, that was him and he said that this bento box left him feeling mighty satisfied.
- Bento Box E - sashimi with mixed tempura ($13) - there's a surprising amount of food in these bento boxes (you get to choose between miso soup and a salad)! The salad was delicious, the dressing had a nice tanginess to it. Size wise, the bento boxes are quite deceiving (I was really full, past dinner time). My bento consisted of 6 pieces of sashimi (two each of salmon, tuna and surf clam), 6 pieces of small maki rolls (tuna), edamame beans, rice and a good mix of tempura. 
- Bento Box A - beef with mixed tempura ($12) - got this bento box as a take out order for a co-worker. They packaged everything nicely, separating out the salad, vegetable rolls, sauce and then the rest of the order (rice, mixed tempura, edamame beans and beef). The next day, she was raving about the sweet sauce that comes with dipping the tempura in.

It seems like the quality of sushi restaurants in town are getting better these days. Obviously, nothing like in Vancouver but at least you have a greater selection of options to choose from. But holy, is sashimi expensive! I wanted to try Ohana-Ya's chef's choice sashimi platter (18 pieces) but it's $24 bones. For lunch. Not easy on the wallet, that's foo sure. But if you stick with the bento boxes and sushi & maki combos, you can't go wrong.

Just coming back from 5 star dining experiences out of country, this review maybe a little biased.  But when I was waiting for my wife to arrive, at least offer me some water or ask me if I would like a drink.  I thought my server was just being rude but I came to the conclusion that she doesn't really know what good service is.  Tough start.
Food was good.  Their Bolognese sauce had decent flavour but the tortellini that came with the dish was just ok.  Lasagna was also ok because of the Bolognese.  The Caesar salad was good but had some wilted greens that were served.
Not my first choice for Italian out but not my last either.

Avoid this mall! It is severely lacking in relevant and current stores, and is mostly still up and running because of The Bay. The owners of the mall always ask for new suggestions for stores, decor, etc from local residents but I hardly ever see any changes made. I think they need new owners/management ASAP.

My mom drags me to Hole's quite often, and although I do not have a particularly green thumb, I enjoy coming to this enormous garden centre. During spring and summer, Hole's sells an amazing selection of live plants ready to be planted in pots or in the garden. When winter comes, Hole's stocks up on Christmas trees, Poinsettias and holiday ornaments. Any time of year there are beautiful flower arrangements available for sale.
Hole's consists of several greenhouses each of which houses a certain type of plants. For example, there are indoor plants section and bedding plants retail area. Whatever you plan to plant in our garden be it flowers, shrubs or trees, you will find it here. Apparently, many Edmonton and St Albert dwellers think so too as Hole's is consistently busy.
Great St. Albert spot. Creative chef specials, and a good wine list.

Food is local produce prepared in an excellent manner. Menu changes occasionally so it isn't always the same old thing. Service was friendly, efficient and very professional - in a good way. We ate indoors because the weather wasn't great but have eaten outdoors before. Great setting and ambiance either way. Previous review 
provides as good a description of the food as one could so won't repeat it here.

Top notch place to take your number one lady for a nice evening out or to just go with friends or for business meetings and a meal. Price is not low, but not real high for the level of quality and service. Quite affordable on most budgets. 

It takes a lot for me to rate any restaurant a 5. Highly recommend this place and we go back regularly.

Great lunch spot. Being from the states, we wanted to sample a local donair. We ordered the chicken/beef mix with both sauces and all the fixings, large. The donair was quite amazing and was the most filling meal for the money we have had while in Edmonton.

Ok place 
Clean and family friendly regular place for Japanese with a little bit better quality

Wow, what a find!

We dine out a lot...several times a week...and always say "What could they do better?" and in this instance we were stumped. We could not find any flaws with this establishment. 

The food was genuine Italian cooking. "E" is well versed in Italian cuisine....and  througout the whole meal "E" was saying "I swear my Nonna is in the kitchen cooking!"

I had the best lasagna of my life here. It was perfect. We had a salad as well, again perfect. Nothing complicated...just fresh and the dressing was spot on.

The value for money is probably the best we have ever seen. Or close to it. The portions are HUGE. Typical Italian...love  em!

There are A LOT of good Italian restaurants in Edmonton and area. But this is probably one of the best we have been to.
 
We will be back  as there are a lot of other menu options we can't wait to try.

We had an excellent time at River House Grill, taking in the special menu available for Mother's Day.

My meal began with a seasonal organic greens salad, with a delicious vinaigrette and small balls of fresh mozzarella on the side. My main course was a perfectly cooked piece of arctic char with an amazing sauce, followed by a great raspberry crepe for dessert to end the meal.

The seasonal and local flavors River House Grill is known for were really on display here. I've only eaten there once before, but it wasn't on a day with a set menu. There was enough choice for all three courses to satisfy anyone, and all the dishes looked like they would taste as amazing as the ones I had. I'd definitely go back there for another dinner with a special set menu.

Like last time the service was great (we had the same waiter as before), both friendly and attentive, and very knowledgeable about the menu.

There is nothing spectacular about the food here. It's just another Indian restaurant. The food may not be terrible, but the service is. I was here one afternoon for the buffet and I was pretty much the only one. I asked if I could get roti instead of naan. No, they would charge for it. That is my cue that the service sucks. Only one other place has done this before. Then, I don't remember what, but there was another No for something I asked. Wreaked of the No attitude, so I left without eating. If I was the owner, I would be so ashamed to let anyone leave without eating. That's just my values.

Simply donairs is my new go-to place for donairs! One of the best donairs I have had, and I have tried a lot! Not much for looks, but you want to do take out anyway. Although I actually kind of like the European style 'snack bar' feel that it has :-)

Beautiful cute location. Decent service. But I'm not gonna lie they good was no more then decent. Really disappointing because it's such a cute place but my husband and I ordered quite a bit of things from the menu and we just didn't find anything great.

I had an awesome experience purchasing two bikes last year! Today I took our two bikes in for the one year service. Service was extremely Poor! Whoever the owner is needs to give the staff a lesson in customer service! I would suggest buy your bike somewhere else!

I was so looking forward to going ,Sat in booth beside kitchen just to notice wall and intire back of booth covered in flys so gross. Witch made enjoying the awesome food impossible didn't even get to have dessert because of it.We had to eat our food so fast because of the flys flying around trying to land on us and our food.So disappointed I have wanted to try this restaurants for so long .
Awesome little place. Lao food and Thai food done to perfection. Very cozy. And friendly owners / staff. Exceptionally clean and good service. Will definitely go again!

Clean premises.  Lovely owner.  Nice donair, but in the end, it's just a donair.  

Simply Donair is alright on balance.  Recommended in the end if you're in the area and you're up for a donair.

Huge selection within the confines of the little shop. Tons of British brands of candies as well as food. Staff is always friendly and helpful and know a lot about the products that they sell. Whatever you're looking for, there's a good chance you'll find it here.
Great place for both lunch and dinner.Fresh Sashimi, various rolls,recommand Poseidon rolls and DIY dynamite...and best customer service ever.They also serve Ramen!

Oh, so good ... I could live on the butter chicken and nan in this place, if only they still had their lunchtime buffet!  The staff are friendly, and they have never served me a bad meal.  Lovely look and feel inside.  Haweli remains high on my list!

Yaaaaas, it's so nice having someone that knows all the St. Albert hotspots. My co-worker and I went to Simply Donair on a Friday and got there just before the lunch rush. The place is simple and straightforward - order at the counter and watch the magic happen.

I know Edmonton is overflowing with an abundance of donair and schwarma spots but Simply Donair is definitely worth a try. Especially if you're one of those people that like massive quantities (aka. generous portions here).

We each ordered a donair combo platter ($11.66) with cheese ($0.71 extra). You get a small donair (choice of beef, chicken, mix, donair poutine or falafel), small fries and drink (pop, juice or water). The "small" is easily the size of a regular sized donair. What I really liked about Simply's donairs is that they shave the meat off and then grill it on top of the stovetop. Gives it a slight char flavour. As well, the sweet sauce was goooood. Just be prepared to get messy.

Also, a nice touch was how you can customize what you want in your donair. I added mushrooms and banana peppers along with the usual tomatoes, shredded lettuce and onion. Fast, cheap, and fresh, what else do you want in a donair shop?

My daughters and I always order from Ohana-ya when we want a special treat.  We usually order assorted nigiri sushi, assorted rolls and tempura.  Occasionally we eat in the restaurant, but mainly order take out.  The food is always ready as promised.  I don't eat sushi but my daughter, who is selective about her sushi, says it's the best she's tasted (she's been to Japan).  I was disappointed to find out they are closed until the end of the month.
It's unbelievable.  If it was fiscally possible I'd eat a super with cheese for every meal.

My place to go for donairs.  Large portions and great sweet sauce.  But their meat is the best I've had.  I really like the spice and spiciness of it.  I haven't put my arteries to the test with their donair poutine but it sounds unreal ( with the meat all over it )
Food - best donair I've had
Wine - haha
Atmosphere - it's a donair shop

Probably the best butter chicken I have ever had. When I go to an Indian Restaurant I like to go to the buffet and try new things because I'll never know what to get on the menu. But at Haweli, butter chicken is a MUST. I haven't had better. Would definitely recommend to anyone willing to try new things!

Thai Mekong is a great place to eat Thai food.  Of course, there isn't much selection for Thai food in  St Albert, however, after eating at several places in Edmonton, I found that this was my favourite due to its convenient location and good food.  Although the prices could be lower, the food was fantastic and the service was good, considering there were only two servers.  The place was packed and there was a mistake with our reservation, however, within several minutes of us waiting, we were apologized to and were given a table, crammed in behind another.  

Overall, the meal and service was good, however my only problem was with the prices.  If I could give half-stars it would definitely earn 4.5/5.  So go eat here and help support local businesses!

A group of four of us ate here on Saturday night - after reading the reviews here, I wasn't sure what to expect, but I was pleasantly surprised! Everyone we interacted with was warm, friendly, gracious, and genuine. Two of our party had the Fettuccine Pescatore special, with the white wine sauce. This dish was nothing spectacular, but a good respectable pasta dish. The scallops were much larger than some places! The other two members of our party had the Seafood Stuffed Shells (another special) and the Mediterraneo pizza. Both were more than satisfied. 

The best part of our dinner was a surprise. The owner (I assume) brought us out a plate of Gamberi Alla Sambuca, which is sautéed prawns with white wine & tabasco sauce, flambéed in sambuca. It. Was. Amazing. Since we hadn't ordered it, we didn't know what it was until we asked him about it afterward. We were all expecting it to be a simple scampi. But the sauce is divine - and the shrimp was large and plump, perfectly cooked. The member of our party who ordered the pizza scrapped the plate of leftover sauce onto their pizza to continue enjoying it. 

Definitely check out this restaurant. It's a local independent place and the foods and people show that. Far better quality and service than you get at a typical chain restaurant.

Who would-a-thunk St. Albert actually has some good places to eat?? Well, I found out when we went for a dinner on Saturday evening for my friend's birthday. Luisa's was packed with several large groups (seemed like everyone was celebrating a birthday that night).  Luisa has a down to earth, family run, genuine home style of cooking. It was my first time going and I would definitely go back to try more things!

Anyways, for food, there were 7 of us but I'm only going to talk about the food I tried:

- Bruschetta ($9) - you get 6 nicely sized pieces of bruschetta. So tasty, I couldn't pick out exactly what herbs/spice they were using but it was well balanced. Definitely a great way to start our meal.
- Complimentary bread and oil/balsamic vinegar - our waitress was nice and brought out two plates for each part of the table.
- Agnello ($23) - lamb shank was fall off the bone tenderness. Cooked perfectly with onions and rosemary. My friend ordered this with vegetables (you can also choose pasta instead) and came with a very nice variety (eggplant, cauliflower, potatoes, etc.). Such a good deal especially for lamb!
- Fettuccini piccante ($18) - this was my dish and it came with 6-7 prawns over a spicy rose sauce. The sauce had a perfect hint of spiciness to it and the pasta was cooked perfectly. I couldn't stop eating it.
- Tiramisu ($9) - this was a legit tiramisu, so good. Devoured is probably a nice way of saying how fast it went.
- Birthday dessert (free) - I'm not sure exactly what it was but it came with a scoop of vanilla ice cream and was a sponge almond type cake.

Overall, great place if your hungry for Italian! And in St. Albert! Reservations are a must unless you like waiting. Family run, love how the owners come by to chat and see how your meal went. Only minus we had was our waitress who was a bit odd. Other than that, great food!

Luisa's Ristorante is our favorite Friday night go-to restaurant for dining. This gem of a dining spot is proof positive that high quality food will always trump an expansive menu. The atmosphere here is very welcoming and the food is reminiscent of the Tuscan tastes that we recently enjoyed in Italy. Our favorite item on the menu is the bruschetta. We have yet to find any other restaurant that can top this. Reservations a must on weekends.

Went here the other day as its walking distance from a friends place. I wasn't impressed at all. Nothing we ate had any kind of wow factor. Also they got my order wrong and by the time I got my correct order the table was done eating. I didn't expect the dish for free but some kind of discount would have been nice. Nothing was taken off the bill. 

Needless to say I won't return as there are a lot of other great Italian restaurants.

This past weekend, I headed up to St. Albert for a wonderful dinner at Luisa Ristorante.  It's a good thing we made reservations because the place was hopping, even when we arrived at about 6:45.  We were seated at what must be the best table in the house, right in the front window.

Our server was excellent, very knowledgeable about the menu and the specials.  Speaking of the menu, there were so many vegetarian options, and I don't mean that our server said, "Yeah, I guess we can make it without the chicken" like almost every Italian place in Edmonton.  They had several veg options printed in the actual menu.  We ended up going for the bruschetta (very good), the pasta al forno (excellent), gnocchi (quite tasty), and the tortellini (outstanding).  Their prices are much more reasonable than any place in Edmonton.

We don't get up to St. Albert too often, but when we do, we will undoubtedly head to Luisa Ristorante again.

Thanks, Yelpers, for recommending this place.  Once again, you didn't let me down.

Since moving back to town a few months ago, I have been asking around to find out who does the best donairs.  I didn't want to waste my time with a bad one!

More often than not, this place was mentioned.  So on Victoria Day, I decided to break my diet and head in there.  I went with the combo #2, which is a small donair, fries, and a can of pop.  I think it was about $12 which is right on track with what I would expect to pay.

When I walked in, the only employee out front was on the phone taking an order.  I stood there for quite a while, which was fine because I needed to look over all the options.  After a few minutes, he was still on the phone, but he went into the back and got another employee to help me, since his phone call wasn't ending any time soon.

Was I blown away by flavours?  No.  Was it good enough to keep me coming back?  Absolutely.

Just like the retro comedy show Cheers, it's nice to have a place where: "they're always glad you came". With that in mind, ten of us went for my wife's birthday, through the front door and into this bustling, colourful, St. Albert restaurant - where Rocco, Rosa and their staff proudly welcomed us all into their homey setting. 

This place is cozy; with vivid Italian music, soft lighting and attractive artwork (for sale at a reasonable price). We started our meals with such fundamental appetizers as prawns, salads and soups - and accompanied them with glorious glasses of fine Italian wine. Our exceptional main dishes included veal parmigiana, garlic shrimp linguine, and chicken in spinach pepper sauce with penne. 

The group consensus gave Luisa the nod as one of St. Alberta's best value restaurants we've been to, for its combination of great Italian food and nice comfy surrounds. But when you come here, just remember to save room for the tiramisu, or eat dessert first ;) I think we could best sum up Luisa Ristorante with our parting three words to Rosa: "See you soon!"

When we first booked this restaurant last minute, we expected it to be pretty much the same as before it changed ownership (which isn't a bad thing at all since the food was quite good then).  But when we looked at the menu, you can tell it has been tweaked to be a little more sophisticated and finer dining.

Foie Gras & Toast - more like foie butter than a whole slice.  It was excellent, I could have had another portion of this app.  And really excellent value also, 4 pieces of brioche ( I believe ) and 4 slices of foie.
Crab Cakes - one of the best in the the Edmonton & area.  Not a lot of filler and great flavours with the nice panko crunch.  The sauce adds a nice little kick.
Salmon - well prepared cooked to medium ( I prefer medium rare ) but still really moist.  Great accompaniment of the risotto
Short Rib - fork tender.  Great flavours and balance of savoury and sweet with a spicy foam ( jalapeno maybe? )  And great whipped/mashed potatoes, so smooth and velvety, almost as good as CUT in Las Vegas ( and those potatoes blew my mind )

Atmosphere - nice but not bust on a Tuesday night
Wine selection - ok
Service - attentive and warm.  
Like I said, I rarely give 5 stars but for flavours and price, this restaurant deserves it.

The meat is always hot, spiced to perfection!
The sweet sauce is amazing, if you don't like a lot of sauce (I saw some people complain there was too much sauce) you have the option to tell the person to stop!
Their prices have increased which is unfortunate considering the business is increasing. There is now a Simply Donair open in South Common.
Best Donair poutine ever! This place has large portions and is so delicious, I find it a bit pricy for a Donair stop but it's totally worth it to try at least once.

We had a great dinner here - gamberi and bruschetta to start (OMG the bruschetta was HUGE!), and a Caesar salad for two and an entree was lots for supper - and I was hungry! Not so hungry, mind you, that I was blinded to the tastes - which were superb! Thanks - service was great, too!

The River House Grill is a fantastic place for a special occasion. The locally sourced food is amazing, and although the portions don't look huge (they are definitely well presented) they fill you up!

Have been here twice now and had a great experience both times, but the last time they had the dining room closed for a private function and seated us in the bar area. Not bad but the dining room is definitely preferred. I would recommend asking if you will be seated in the dining room or bar because had I known, I would have saved my reservation for another night.

Also on the slightly pricey side (over $60/person), but worth it.

Tried to go back here to give it another chance seeing as how there a a few good reviews. Service is still just as bad as ever and the food is at best bland, boxed pasta with canned or bottled sauce. There are a ton of much better Italian places in St Albert. You don't need to go here. On the positive side, I rated it two stars instead of the one star I gave it the first time as it was very marginally better.

The food portion is very small. The price does not match the food portion, so it's expensive. Customer service is great. The fried rice taste very delicious. The seafood plate consist of only greasy shrimps and vegetables. Overall it is an ok restaurant.

Luisa Ristorante in St. Alberta is a gem! Went there for the first time last night and it certainly did not disappoint. Ed and Cindy the owners were outgoing and true hospitality people! You can tell the wine and drink menus are well thought through and there is a nice selection for almost everyone. The food menu has great variety and some standard staples of Italy. The price is very reasonable and the service was unmatched. The space is small and intimate but appeals to both families and date night. Cannot wait to go back.

It's hard to believe that I've been coming here since my 2nd was born and he's now almost 6!

Last time I reviewed them was 2012 so an update is most definitely due!

Simply Donairs continues to be outstanding run by the same people and he prices have hardly increased.

Our go to order these days:

Large mixed (chicken/beef) with cheese and lots of hot sauce (on the grill) and a large donair poutine.

I usually get part of the Donair poutine on the side plain for my son because he just wants meat and fries with seasoning salt.

We've eaten at a few other Donair Shops but this is consistently the one requested by my kiddos.  Maybe it has to do with the free lollipops for kiddos?  ;-)

Either way, I'm sure we'll still be coming here 6 years from now!

I had the pleasure of dining here by accident on a Saturday night.
My friend and I originally had walked past, looking for a quick bite closer to our destination. However, something called us back in. It was pretty quiet, but the restaurant is small and cozy so we didn't take that as a bad sign. The ambience is unassuming and homey and had Italian music playing lightly in the background, which was super relaxing!
Our server was very down-to-earth, friendly, and very attentive without coming across as overbearing.
We ordered the arancini as an appetizer, and although a little on the salty side, was still delicious. We had the 1/2 litre chianti to drink and it was PERFECT. In fact, so perfect that we regretted not getting a bottle to ourselves and ordered another half litre.
One of their daily specials was a pork cutlet with mustard sauce and a choice of vegetables or pasta on the side. Naturally, we both chose pasta, as is contractually obligated at an Italian ristorante. In fact, we both got the exact same dish.
We quickly discovered that the portions are extremely generous for the price, which ended in me throwing the napkin on my unfinished plate in defeat.
What was supposed to be a quick dinner ended in an awesome, 2-hour dining experience that made our impromptu night out one to remember!

A small, quaint restaurant, Japanese food here aims to please. It's not what I expect from a Japanese place but that is mostly due to the atmosphere. This is a modernized western cafe of a sushi place. It's warm and inviting but lacks the traditional atmosphere. 

Our order of the chefs platter for 2 was quick to prepare and eye appealing, however when you dive into your food, it often falls apart. A sign of a rushed chef. 

Still worth a night out for a decent price (when comparing sushi).

I booked my truck in one week ago. I wanted an oil change, all fluids checked, there was a squealing/grinding sound coming from (I thought the left front wheel), and a tune up. They asked to have the car in at 7 am. I dropped the truck off at 7 am and the puppy and I walked home. 5 hours later they called me to tell me they managed to get the oil changed but hadn't had a chance to do anything other work yet, but the alignment team did note that my front wheels were out of alignment. They asked of I wanted a wheel alignment, I said go ahead. 

Four and a half hours later they called back and said that they now have the fuel filter replaced and will be doing the wheel alignment next and my truck will be ready in an hour and a half (6 pm). At 5:45 they called and said they didn't have time to do the alignment. I could leave the truck and they could do it tomorrow or I could pick the truck up tonight and rebook it back in.

I picked the truck up and it won't be rebooked back in. 11 hours to do an oil change, replace a fuel filter and rotate my tires.

I hope they have a large customer base, because this kind of service will result in a loss of lot of them.

What I noticed as I walked through the door was the 3 huge slabs of rotating meat. Haha I found it to be quite amusing as I don't frequent donair shops very often. The menu was small, but I already knew what I wanted...the donair poutine, which had been highly recommended by a friend.

As it was Sunday night, the place only had a few customers but it felt good to know that their on-break staff ate where she worked. =) We were greeted by the very friendly chef. Once he knew we were there to try their donair poutine, there was no pressure for us to buy more than what was necessary for us. Instead of us each getting a small for $6.99 each, HE SUGGESTED we share a large one for $8.99 instead. There were 5 of us, so we winded up ordering 2 large ones and 1 small for the friend who frequents this place.

This place was fast food like, so we picked up our order at the counter once it was ready, but it was made quite quickly. What we saw didn't seem too impressive at first, till our friends decided to divide it up on a plate. All of a sudden, half seemed very overwhelming. Eventually only 2 out of the 5 of us actually finished our halves.

It was the best poutine I've ever had! The fries were crispy and remained intact even till the end, where some fries tend to get mushy. The cheese was melted, but not stringy. The gravy was mixed with some sort of sweet sauce which tasted absolutely amazing. There was more than enough donair meat! I started off eating a couple of bites of fries then a bite with meat, but it became obvious that they did not go cheap on the meat haha. Near the end, I was stuffing myself with mouthfuls of meat, meat, meat! =)

We were all ready for a nap after a very filling and greasy, but super delicious meal. When you go, make sure you are hungry and don't expect to need to order anything else.

2 Thumbs up! I need to rest up my stomach for another go some time. =)

Just tried this amazing restaurant. New owners and it still is a family run business. Food is fresh and locally sourced. They will try to accommodate you if they can especially if you have food sensitivities. I mentioned I cannot have wheat, rice or corn pasta and Ed the owner went and got me quinoa... wow!!
My photos are not that great as we were digging in before realizing we need to take some pictures.

Was in St.Albert doing some shopping. Getting very hungry and craving for a Donair. I checked Yelp and this place was highly rated, so I though I would  like to try.
Well the reviews did not disappoint! Their Donairs are awesome and the sweet sauce is to die for. I had the large beef and it was huge. I don't recommend ordering it unless you haven't eaten for a day. 
Wow you have to try this place!

The donair poutine is AMAZING. The portions are generous which makes it ideal for sharing. The beef donair with cheese is also good. You have to eat is quickly or else it can get soggy. 

The staff are always friendly and for the most part the food is always quick. It would be awesome if simply had a drive thru.

My family loves this place! This is one of our go-to restaurants in St. Albert. The pad thai is excellent, and we really like the coconut rice. The staff who run the place are very friendly, I've never regretted coming here.

I brought my trek navigator bike to Crankys to rectify shifting issues on the front derailleur.They did a  front Shimano adjustment and replaced a shifter  cable. I road tested the bike afterwards twice and experienced the same issues, but they were unable to diagnose the problem . I finally took the bike home and had two other cyclists try it with the same results. We finally learned that we had to really reef on the shifter  to shift gears successfully--a definitely abnormal condition which did not exist before we brought it in. Crankys did offer to look at the bike again ,but there's no way I'll bring it back.
There was also one instance of discourtesy from a staff member as well.

I'm a donair snob.  I stumbled across this place and was pleasantly surprised.  The donair meat has flavor and they don't cheap out on the meat.  Toppings are good (lettuce, tomato, olive, hot pepper etc) and they heap those on too.  Best thing on the menu might just be the donair poutine... wow that was awesome.  The gravy tastes great, the fries are crispy, the donair meat is very good, and lots of cheese... I think one of the best poutines in the city.

Ohana-Ya is a dependable Japanese restaurant.  It is not the best sushi I have ever had, but it is most definitely not the worst either.  I think my point here is that you know what you are going to get when you go here.  It is very standard for north American style sushi and it seems to always be fresh, which is pretty important when going for sushi.  Ohana-Ya is one of the better places to go for sushi in St. Albert, although there is not much for competition.  I would recommend it for lunch or even a quick dinner on a week night.  With that said, you would be just as well to make the drive into the city to go to a place like Kyoto, or Mikado especially if you are going for dinner or on the weekend.

Full Review: http://www.holmcooked.com/2011/04/restaurant-review-ohana-ya.html

Just tried this amazing restaurant. New owners and it still is a family run business. Food is fresh and locally sourced. They will try to accommodate you if they can especially if you have food sensitivities. I mentioned I cannot have wheat, rice or corn pasta and Ed the owner went and got me quinoa... wow!!
My photos are not that great as we were digging in before realizing we need to take some photos

Holes Enjoy Center is a one stop shop complete with a casual dining restaurant, bakery, grocery store catering to health food and local made goods, wine store, as well a well stocked garden centre. While some of the prices may seem higher than some others places the increased quality of their products and plants justifies it 'you get what you pay for'. They even have warranty for plant purchases. We've bought a perennial plant that didn't survive the winter and brought it back with receipt from the previous year and the gladly replaced the plant with a new healthy one. Jim Hole also puts on a number of free seminars during the year especially during growing season. These are very informative and always well attended on topics ranging from growing tomatoes to fruit tree pruning and his popular cannabis growing talks. Jim is very personable and is more than willing to stay afterwards and answer questions one on one. I've been going to Holes since the Enjoy Center opened and have always had a pleasurable experience.

Simply the best! Best Donairs anywhere hands down! They definitely don't cheap out on the meat/cheese at this donair shop. Friendly, family run business located in a new location by Save-On-Foods/Wendy's in St Albert. Once you try their Donairs you won't want to get them anywhere else.

I have heard about them, read the YELP reviews and thought I would give them a try as we were in the area. Not our top 1 choice for a donair with sweet sauce and chicken donair with grilled sauce but not bad either. It is a family run business-  the couple and their son are pleasant and quick in putting the orders together.
We will definitely give them another try when they move to their new location. What I and my husband loved the most was their fries seasoning- just wow. Not spicy, not salty, simply amazing. I am pretty sure they make it in house, too. The portions are generous- I could not finish the small size I ordered and my husband had left overs from his regular size donair.

Although I've not had a full meal at the River House, I did enjoy probably the best appetizer of my life here and would encourage you to try the Scallops with Prosciutto.  It was a bit pricey and a bit slow to arrive, but worth both every cent and minute.  Firstly, it's a work of art, and looks like the plate was created by someone who really appreciated the food and wanted to insure that you did as well.   The flavors were wonderful - three large sea scallops with thinly dried prosciutto "chips" or slices, on a bed of bleu cheese ganache - don't worry if that might sound like a strange pairing, it's incredibly delicious and I would definitely order it again with pleasure.

(Also worth mentioning - every staff person we encountered was friendly, helpful, and attentive, happy to answer questions and make us feel welcomed)

Took my Honda in for the out of province inspection. They tried to charge me over 1K saying all my wiper mechanisms needed to be changed and there was an ABS fault. I was very suspicious of this immediately as i could see no issue at all. I changed the wiper blades and took it to Alberta Honda for re-inspection and it passed with no problems. The technicians at Alberta Honda could not believe that they had blatantly lied on the inspection. 
I also had some repairs done on a H2 that I am suspecting now as well in light of this. 
I will not be returning to this dealership.

This store is among the best candy stores in Metro Edmonton. The ladies who own the store and their staff are fantastic and know their stuff.
If you want British chocolate, which is decadent, this Candy Bouquet has the best selection I've seen. Their Turkish Delight bars are British, with very soft turkish delight inside surrounded by a thin layer of British chocolate. It's like heaven in a store!
They also carry British crisps (potato chips) in several different flavours, though some sound almost like an acquired taste.
They also have candy from the U.S. like Necco Wafers, Sky Bars, PayDay, Baby Ruth, etc.
Candy Bouquet is open late on Thursdays, and last I checked they were closed on Sundays and Mondays. They're located right across from the old Post Office in downtown St. Albert.

Came to Haweli with my hubby and baby in tote for a lunchtime buffet.  Was disappointed after arriving to find that they have changed their menu and no longer offer weekday lunch buffets even though I had a coupon for a B1G1 free buffet valid ONLY for weekday lunches.

We decided to stay and try a vindaloo and curry off the menu alongside garlic naan and basmati rice.

They did not offer for us to use our coupon for the lunch specials but did allow us to use it for one free item.

The vindaloo and curry were phenomenal and the garlic naan was to die for! 

The service was incredibly attentive and the atmosphere was beautiful.  I uploaded a few pics and we definitely will be returning.

The only reason they get 4 stars is we were quite disappointed that they no longer offered a weekday lunch buffet but will definitely be back for a date night sans kids!
The shank is phenomonol!

I must say that Simply Donair has gained ground and now passed Famous Joe's for my Donair needs. And that was achieved in 3 consecutive visits.

Visit 1: Donair Poutine delivered by a friend to my work. Fries got a little soggy and there was a little too much sweet sauce for my liking but I ate the whole thing and stopped short of licking the aluminum take out tray.

Visit 2: Regular Donair that I took to go. Very filling and tasty. Standard donair fillings and sauces but done perfectly.

Visit 3: Donair Poutine eaten in the shop. This is definitely the way I'd suggest eating the Poutine. The fries stay crispy and everything is really hot. Also when the takeout lid is put on it flattens the whole thing and takes away some of the goodness. I did ask for half as much sweet sauce though and it was perfect for my tastebuds.

Try this place and you won't go anywhere else for Donairs!
I have been going there since a young boy. This place takes pride in providing kinds a safe place to purchase and play game, comics, etc... I highly recommend this establishment.

Came for my birthday dinner and everything was amazing!  The appetizers were fantastic!  Then the main course arrived and my taste buds hit the truffle chilli sauce!  WOW WOW WOW!!! This is the best sauce I have ever had!  Then Chef Steve came out to offer me a bottle to take home as a gift!  This place is such a hidden Gem!!! Can't wait to come back!

Another go-to donair place, but in St.Albert. If you enjoy Swiss-donair in the north then this is my 1A donair stop. Their sweet sauce is oh so good, loaded with flavourful meat & service is always super friendly. I've had the donair poutine also which is insanely good, but usually way too much for me to handle by myself.

One knock - when the girls wrap it, sometimes it turns into a donair taco rather than a wrap so it's difficult to eat. Still tastes the same although it ends up all over your shirt & pants, but so worth it.

My go to is just a regular donair with lettuce onion tomato & sweet sauce (of course!!!). Boom done, into a food coma where I will inevitably just end up dreaming about these donairs.
Just curious trying their promo of $10 per Ramen on Sundays. If you crave for ramen that is not pricey go in Sunday. Taste is nothing special but not even bad. Staffs were hospitable.

I used to love Holes. The prices were always high but I was always happy with the quality. My boys took me to the new "Enjoy Center" I have to say, the experience was no good at all. The place is just monstrous and the plants are arranged in an order that is very confusing. I saw many of people there but very few with purchases. They looked as dazed and confused as I was. Prices? Absolutely sky high. I wonder where the enjoy part is? Such a tacky name for a tacky place. I won't be back again.

I absolutely love the food here. Its delicious, and I love their naan bread! 

Its one of St.Albert's best restaurants!

Thank goodness I did my research ahead of time because I would have ended up at Ricky's with the rest of the crew - yuck.

This is a cute little restaurant in an older looking building just off St Albert trail. The building itself is only 20 years old, but it had a lot of character. Rivet House Cafe has been around for 10 years. Before that, this place was a home for some commercial housing and an art gallery, so I was told. 

They have a pretty simple menu. All of their starters are either a type of soup or salad which was kind of weird, but it all looked good so I didn't mind. If you want to share a starter, they charge a $3 for splitting it - also strange. I ordered the blended lentil soup with lemon yogurt to start. It was perfectly mild in taste and the lemon yogurt gave it a nice little kick. I got the center cut angus sirloin. It was a huge 12oz steak grilled with pink peppercorns topped with a chipotle butter, balsamic drizzle, mashed potatoes and seasonal vegetables. The best part about a good restaurant is that you get REAL vegetables! Everything was very good except that my steak was a little too well done for my liking.

Last thoughts: the food was good but there were some things that could have been better. However, the service was great, the venue is very cute, and the washrooms? Super tiny!! (just as cramped at Ming in Calgary)

18/30

Great selection of candy including nice brit chocolate like Yorkies. Nice selection of 'classic candy' including sugar straws, pop rocks, rock candy, Turkish Delight, and more. Bit too expensive - 100g of Sour Jelly Beans cost $3.90. The store isn't the most visually appealing but the variety of candy is appealing.

This place is fantastic! My family has been countless times and the food is dependably good, with a few different dishes that always stand out. Sushi pizza is basically sashimi on large slices of yam tempura with a creamy sauce drizzled over top - for $10 you will not find a better bang for your buck anywhere! The Mexican roll (spicy tuna, avocado & mango) is a surprisingly tasty combination, and the crunchy roll is a unique battered and fried roll with smoked salmon and cream cheese inside which will surprise you with the size of the order. Once or twice when they have gotten really slammed just as we got there we have found it to be a little slow, but the staff is always friendly and we always leave satisfied!
They were out of what I went in there for but the variety of sweets is terrific.  So many different things I have not seen in years bringing back lots of great memories!

Oh man, I thought I had reviewed the mall already!  Well... here we go.

This was the mall I grew up next to.  I worked at two different places in the food court, and my best friend worked at 3 different stores.  Almost every store had somebody I knew working in it.  So... maybe I'm a little biased about it.  

I will say that this mall absolutely sucked for a while.  There were no relevant stores for a long time.  I remember when I was much younger and wal mart moved out of this mall up to the newer super centre location, we thought "well.... at least there's still the food court I guess."  When Zellers moved in, it was a nice compromise, and we were happy enough with that.  Nothing else in the mall was really changing though.  Ever.  Same old stores.  Same kiosks at Christmas time.  Nothing new in the food court.

The same cannot be said now.  First off... despite the addition of a Tim Horton's last month, the food court sucks.  It has an A&W, and Orange Julius, and I think the Chinese Food place is still there?  There's some kind of Pizza Kone place opening... seems like a strange choice.  The Smitty's is gone and that was devastating to me.  I said the same thing about Kingsway - I really like to have a restaurant to sit down in when I need a break from shopping.  Also... you could get a glass of wine for $2.50 in the lounge!

Now, the good.  Talk about a facelift.  You can't help but notice the changes as you drive down St. Albert Trail.  London Drugs and Mark's Work Warehouse now find their new homes on the West Side of the mall, and Winners has moved to this side as well.  It looks AMAZING.  and the hallway that connects the new area with the old (formerly known as the "Smitty's entrance") is gorgeous with lots of new stores like Stokes, Soft Moc, and La Vie en Rose.

And it seems like they are ever growing.  The mall was asking on Social Media a few weeks ago what type of local stores we'd like to see.

Does it have everything you need?  No.  But it's getting there.

Haven't bought a bike here but loving my brand new hot coral pink kitty Kat helmet!!!  They even had a matching bell!!!

Like any boutique specialty store, the prices are high n the higher end here but the selection is outstanding and we always receive great service!

They also provide complimentary bike check-ins during the St. Albert Farmers' Market.  Last year they cut off an old lock for us free of charge. 

Two thumbs up!

Stopped in for an emergency derailleur adjustment and was charged $22. I appreciate that they were there and open and could make the repair, but charging that much for literally 3 minutes of work says a lot about the kind of company this is.  I'd avoid in the future unless it is an emergency.

Luisa was absolutely FANTASTIC! We were in Edmonton for a few days, and really relied on yelp for direction. We were not steered wrong when we followed the directions to this lovely little place. The service was fantastic (even though we showed up 30 minutes before closing and  without a reservation), and the food was over the top, delicious!

Wow! Wow! Wow! That's all I have to say! Came by for some bruschetta and left completely full and VERY satisfied. Small bistro with a big personality. Will be my go to spot for Italian cravings from now on!

Cranky's must be happy they're doing so well because they're in the process of expanding. It'll be great to see the store once they're finished. They carry strictly cycling gear with the exception of some skate helmets. They don't have a lot of bikes, mainly due to space I imagine, but that won't be an issue for long! They've got some cruiser bikes and race bikes. Sadly no fold-up bikes which is what I'm in the market for since I have no space for a bike. But the staff are friendly and they have a lot crammed into a small space - yet it all looks organized somehow. They'll be doubling in size very soon and I'm looking forward to seeing the expansion.

My boyfriend and I came here last Friday specifically to try their ramen as I heard they're now selling ramen during their weekday lunch hours. 

We arrived at 11:15am only to find that they don't open until 11:30. Not a problem. We darted over to Cob's Bakery a couple doors down to grab some baked goods while we waited. 

When we walked into the establishment, it was FREEZING!! Sooooo sooo cold with the A/C blasting. I'm thankful I had a jean jacket but still.... I couldn't get warm. I was so cold I asked for hot water as my beverage. There was another guest who arrived at the same time as us, and he actually left the restaurant to go to his car and came back with his winter jacket! Lol.

Anyways, they serve a several varieties of ramen ranging from $11 - $12. Shio (salt);  Shoyu (soy sauce); Miso (soybean paste); Tonkatsu (pork bone broth); and Tan Tan (spicy sesame minced pork). I opted for the Miso bowl while my boyfriend chose the Tonkatsu.

The bowls arrived after several minutes piping hot. Eagerly antcipating my first bite, I found it quite disappointing.The broth was overly salty and lacked depth. There were lots of noodles - almost too much compared to the toppings received. I opted to not get the bamboo shoots or fungus added to mine (since I dislike either); and was left with a very bland looking bowl topped with green onion, bits of corn, bean sprouts, some seaweed, and ONE piece of char siu. The ONE piece of pork I received was soooo fatty that by the time I removed the layers of fat, I was left with a nickel size piece of meat *tear*. Oh well, the char siu itself also lacked any identifiable flavour.

As for the Tonkatsu my boyfriend ordered, it wasn't much better. The broth lacked the umami and depth it should have and he also found the portion of noodles too much (he couldn't even finish).

Overall, a disappointing ramen experience despite having high hopes!  I look forward to a real good ramen place in Edmonton.
Excellent!  Rocco and Rosa make you feel like you are eating at their home in Sunday!  Highly recommend!  Don't forget the homemade desserts from Rosa!

We went to this restaurant when we first moved to St Albert over 15 years ago. Found it overpriced, tired, musty...never returned. Until this past weekend. We'd heard it was under new ownership ...waitress said it's already been 3 years, who knew? Redecorated..warm, inviting, classic, ..fantastic. Yes, it's pricey, but the food was great! I have to agree with a Google reviewer who said they should consider offering the lovely brioche complimentary before the meal.:) The mussels in particular, absolutely delicious! The broth was so complex and flavourful.  We're happy to return with the added bonus of supporting local! Great job!

I phoned Hole's Greenhouses to find out if there was a product I could use to control an insect called "Popular Borers".  They killed my neighbor's Columnar Aspen and have now attacked mine.  I was given a web site where I could send my question to Jim Hole - the expert (so they say).  Just a catch, he charges $20 for his advice.  I should have just called other green houses but Hole's used to have a good reputation so I went ahead and payed $20 for his advice.  Two weeks later I got a call from Jim advising me to call a fumigator that can treat the tree.  Huh?  $20 for a referral?  Even my doctor doesn't charge for referral's made without a visit.  Well, we hired the recommended fumigator and for $400 a summer student came to our house, drilled holes and inserted insecticide capsules.  The capsules were "Medicap Acecap AC1210 Systemic Insecticide Tree Implants" available through E-Bay for about $3 a piece.  Anyone with a drill could have done the same-  Instructions come with the capsules.  So why didn't Jim Hole suggest that as an option?  I suspect he is collecting a referral fee, why else.   This is a service not to be trusted.  It's about taking as much out of your wallet as possible.

I feel like a dirty mistress... I've found a Donair Place to Rival my longstanding love affair with Famous Joe's Burgers and Donairs.

I came to Simply Donairs this past weekend as a result of an ongoing fued with a co-worker who insistes that Simply Donairs is the BEST in all the land.  I snuck a peek at the reivews on here in advance and I must admit, the 4 1/2 star average had me all fired up and ready to go!

Hubby and I popped into Simply Donairs this past weekend, Saturday night at 950PM on the nose.  I noticed on the door that they close at 10pm 7 days a week.  I quickly asked the Chef/Owner if it was too late to order.  He enthusiastically invited Hubby and I to take our time as he needed a good 30 minutes to close up the store anyway.

There were two young men line also waiting for their orders.  I asked them if they were regulars, and YEPPERS, of course they were!

FYI:  I uploaded PICS of the items reviewed below:

Hubby and I wanted to give Simply a fair shot so we decided to order 3 small menu items to get a good overview of their menu.

1)  Small Falafel with housemade Tzatziki = PHENOMENAL 5/5 stars for sure!

My hubby and I LOVE, and I mean LOVE falafels; Simply Donairs did not disappoint!  The chef said that he orders the spices direct from their naturally sourced origin and makes them from scratch.  They were DIVINE!  

2)  Small Mixed Donair (chicken and beef) = 3/5 stars.

The Chicken and Beef Donair was good... but it was a little too greasy for my tatste and over sauced.  We had the sweet sauce which was good - but a little too fruity for my liking.  Almost pineapple like?  The mushrooms are canned - not fresh :-(  And no banana peppers or jalapenos - but yes to Frank's Red Hot Sauce.  Everthying was prepared with love and grilled to perfection but the meat was greasier than I like and not seasoned as much as I prefer.  Don't get me wrong - if this was the only Donair I had ever had it would still still be a winner but it just didn't hold a flame to my original love, Joe's Famous Donairs and Burgers.  

3)  Small Donair Poutine - OH my God - Oh my GOD - Oh my God!  5/5 Stars!

The Small Donair Poutine was out of this world delicious!  First, he used crinkly fries which really held their texture and didn't get soggy.  There was enough meat to more than last through every bite!  And the sauce--- Mmm... Can you say heavenly?  He mixed sweet sauce with the Gravy!  Now, it was mozerella, not cheese curds - but that is what I'd expect at a Donair House anyway.

HEAVENLY - did I mention heavenly?

The prices were bang on, too!  Smalls were about $6 and larges were around $8.  Hubby and I were unable to finish all of our food and he even threw in 2 baklava for us, as it was our first visit!

The place was clean, bright, and even had two well kept washrooms - a big plus in my eyes!

If you are in the mood for a Falafel or Donair Poutine - this is the place to be!  And if you like your Donair to be a little on the reasy side - you will probably gtive thes place a 45/5 for their Donairs, too.

The owner couldn't have been more hospitable or friendly!  Love this place!  So even though they did not replace my longstanding love affair with Joe's Famous Burger and Donairs, this place is still a 5/5 in my books!

Better yet... Do a taste test and compare the two!  They are both loacted in the same parking lot!  Yep, that's right - in the same parking lot!  Simply Donairs is next to Dairy Queen and Joe's Famous is next to Klondyke Flowers.

Simply Donairs, you have made a FAN out of me!

Ignore every review of Hole's Greenhouse prior to May 1, 2011.  Also ignore the address that Yelp gives.  Prior to that date, Hole's operated out of a cramped but user-friendly greenhouse on Bellerose Drive.  Yes, you had to put up with someone's cart running over your toes but that was a good way to meet fellow gardeners.  The stock was well-marked and easy-to-find.  Furthermore, the old Hole's was easy to locate and get to from Edmonton or any place in St. Albert.

Everything is wrong with the new Hole's, beginning with a name only a salesman in a lime green suit can relate to, Enjoy Centre.  The reason for the meaningless title is that the new Hole's consists of a greenhouse, a restaurant (more below) and a spa (currently unfinished).  One reviewer compares the new Hole's to IKEA.  This is a fitting analogy.  The place is humongous (4.5 hectares) but without the charm of Swedish names with o's with slashes through them.

The new Hole's is located in a hard-to-get-to industrial park at 101 Riel Drive in St. Albert.  My GPS took me out the Yellowhead, up 178 St through half-finished overpasses and residential areas before finding 101 Riel Drive.  There's a much more direct route via 170 St.  Parking is ample, possibly the only charm of the new Hole's.  

The entrance showcases the restaurant and the unfinished spa. To get to the plants, a disadvantage for elderly gardeners.  I didn't see any wheelchairs for seniors with mobility problems.  The plants seem to be arranged randomly under designations so meaningless that I had to ask another customer where she found the tomato plants.  Don't bother the people at the information desk because they seem to have important business on the telephone.  The staff on the floor try to help but they can't seem to find anything either.  The only solution is to walk around and keep looking.

Two weeks after we went for our plants, my wife's girlfriend took my wife to try the restaurant.  My wife reports that the food is pricey and not worth the price.  She reports that the dumplings with the pork and apples ($15) were hard and colud be used as decorative rock in the greenhouse.  Her girlfriend had an omlette with vegetables ($13 and on the menu with some fancy forgettable name) and reports that it was satisfactory.

I wish Yelp would update their listing for Hole's to the new address and add a separate listing for the restaurand and Spa.  Overall, not worth the gas to drive there.
Very impressed with this restaurant. Lots of sushi options for gluten and dairy fee and they even have gluten free soy sauce! A great place for lunch and they have good customer service.

At the end of May, 2011, I took my mom to the new Holes Enjoy Centre.  "Enjoy" is the not the word I would use for this monstronsity of an industrial building. They moved from the homey greenhouse on Bellerose Drive to an industrial section of St. Albert.
My first impression as I walked in was "Ikea". Big, impersonal and so busy, but with many people walking out empty-handed. The prices were absurdly high - $22 for a six pack of annuals - are you kidding me? I overhead a lady telling her other half while looking at a bag of dirt "We can't afford that". I guess they have to pay for the multi-million dollar complex they are in.
There is a very large area full of plants and hanging baskets, but the baskets are on a trolley system (something like you see at the drycleaners).  This room had ropes across the entrance saying it was for employees only - so I witnessed ladies standing at the entrance watching these plants slowly moving - wasn't sure if one was supposed to grab one as they floated by or not.....and the baskets were not that big - they were quite small in growth. I didn't see a good selection of baskets in the main shopping area.
What happened to the personal shopping experience of wandering admist the hanging baskets and having the pleasure of picking one. This industrial trolley system certainly takes that away. Lois must be turning in her grave.
Also, what is up with a huge cafeteria/food area - definitely Ikea'ish.
My mom and I walked out - there was not one thing in there we wanted to buy - instead we drove down the highway 15 minutes to Morniville Greenhouses and ended buying several beautiful baskets and fillers for half the price of Holes. (Disclaimer: I have nothing to do with Morinville Greenhouses - I live out of Province and was just taking my mom greenhouse shopping for the day.)
Holes is expensive, massive and very industrial.
Jim Hole and family certainly did their mother no favour by expanding to this extent and only time will tell if they bit off more than they can chew. Holes may have the name in greenhouses, but such an expensive place will not be sustainable, even with Alberta's economy.

Here's why this restaurant gets 1 star only & why I will not be back & will not recommend it to anyone.

1.  It took approx 1.75 hrs for my table of 2 to get our dinner order.  We did however, have an order of bruschetta, that arrived in a timely manner early on.  Turns out our dinner order fell off of the clip onto the floor, so the kitchen staff did not see it.  Our very young & seemingly inexperienced waitress told us that she kept "wondering what was going on", but seemingly, made no inquiries in the kitchen as to why her clients weren't receiving their food, while all the other tables were.  The nervous, shy waitress mumbled an apology, but nothing from the kitchen or manager & no offer for even some sort of compensation.  Very unimpressed with this.  It was really unacceptable.

2.  My pasta (chicken penne in vodka sauce) was OK, in an ordinary way.  The kind of thing I easily & routinely make at home though.  My main complaint was that there was no salt or pepper at the table & our waitress did not come around with a pepper grinder (or grated Parmesan).  That made for a very bland pasta.  So, I packed my supper home, added salt & pepper, reheated it, and then I enjoyed it.

3.  The 1 star is for the bruschetta, which was very, very delicious. 

I will never go back here again.  There are so many more much better restaurants out there that I would rather visit.

Being new to town, I feel that we just discovered a gem. The service was superb, the food was great. I left so full I couldn't even eat dessert.  I loved the smaller cozy feel of the restaurant. Fantastic place, fantastic food, excellent staff!

So this has become New Asian Village now, 

Same food different name I suppose. 

I did find much of the buffet very tasty, but I felt like they were holding back a bit on the spices for their western audience. I couldn't help but feel like there were so e spices missing as I ate each item.

The butter chicken had more of a tomato taste then I am used to and I just didn't get the same heat I was looking for.  The naan bread seemed like it was cooked almost carelessly,  and it was somewhat difficult to get service. 

My 8 year old daughter who,just found her love for spice was sitting there with her mouth burning for a very long time before water refills came around, even though the restaurant only had 3 other tables going while we were there. 

The food was good but not great, and the service was serviceable I guess, I am only rating it four because I can't give it 3.5. It's priced too high for what you get, if the service was up to par it would be an easy 4 maybe higher.
Loved it. Best Italian food in the city! Great prices! Nice family atmosphere, a charming ambience. If you're searching up Italian places to go to in town, you can't go wrong with Luisas!

The food here is great, and the atmosphere is wonderful! Lots of soft lighting, draped fabrics, and brilliant hints of India... 

And then, there's the food! We had the shrimp tikka, OmG what a treat (try it w the mint sauce to add a bit of bite), paneer crusted w chickpea... and that was just for starters!  We left the deciding to our server, and he didn't disappoint at all!  Thanks again, Haweli, for a wonderful night!

PS Try the coconut naan for dessert... :-)

Our local mall has some great stores, awesome staff and a great location. Although they can't compete with the larger shopping centers it is super handy for locals. I like many others miss the larger brand store, Target, but am confident that soon the inventory available will be competitive with the variety of stores coming in. 

The renovations are coming along and I am looking forward to the final result with much anticipation. They are not disruptive to the shopping experience and show the centers commitment to staying fresh and vibrant to both the client and the community.
The BEST pad Thai. Huge portions (they're so big I can never finish it, who doesn't love leftovers) and the price is awesome. The owners are so sweet & the service is great.

Hawelli ( now known as New Asian Village ) is really a secret gem! The food, service, and atmosphere is wonderful! Everything I have tried has been amazing! The staff are so nice, and offer great recommendations. I have also picked up takeout which was wonderful!

We have tried 5 times recently to go to this retaurant for a meal. They have been closed when their door sign says they should be open, they close on stat holidays with no advance warning, and two days ago, I phoned to make sure they were open, ask to make a reservation, told none needed no problem, got there 20 minutes larter, first question, do you have a reservation. Thjis is the SAME lady I was talking to on the phone and she admitted it.

Only table is by the bathroom and you are sitting 3 feet off the ground. Now the decore int this place is strip mall chique at best so sitting by the washrooms is not on. Apparently business is good enough they can operate in such a cavalier manner but this is our last attempt to go here. Will drive a little farther to make sure the service is up to par.

This was my first time trying Thai Mekong and it was perfect. My boyfriend and I were quickly served and the staff were excellent with my food allergies. I could eat most things on the menu, curries, entrees, noodles, almost all the dishes! The service was attentive and helpful, the place was clean and the plates were a fair size. We split two dishes and still had leftovers to take home. The restaurant has a nice ambience and a friendly feel. We will be back in the near future!
Excellent service and great food. Great family platter and good value. Chef visited table. Complementary bruschetta
We just ordered a modest meal from this establishment. $74. Meager portions. Pretty good but you will feel like you payed too much.

Absolutely the best Donairs I have ever had! It's always pretty busy in there but well worth the wait. Love the chicken Donair too! The meat filling is always very generous and they're never dry. Lots of tasty sweet sauce in the Donair. I have tried many Donairs but nothing beats Simply Donairs.

This is an Italian restaurant in the heart of downtown St. Albert.  Absolutely amazing food. Actually the best Italian food I've tried. Everything is fresh and tastes homemade. They are very accommodating with the menu. This visit I tried the mushroom soup, which tasted heavenly (I'll admit I am a mushroom snob and this exceeded my expectations).  I also had the pizza which had the perfect crust and the perfect flavour.  Service was so attentive and friendly.  Seriously there is nothing to criticize in this place.  Prices are very reasonable and quality is exceptional.  The website is also accurate and has the menu posted on line. Definitely worth making a trip to this place.  You will not be disappointed.

There are two very good reasons to have a Shoppers like this one nearby.  First, it's open from 8 a.m. to midnight every single day, so if you have a sudden need for medication or even the munchies, they are there to help when other places are closed.

Second, even though their prices are often a little higher than elsewhere, they have an Optimum Points program that is simply spectacular if you learn to play the game.   For every dollar you spend, you get points, and can then shop for free.  Okay, so other places have similar plans, but there are tricks to really multiplying your points at Shoppers.  Watch their weekly flyers and get on their email list, and you'll be notified of special days when your points can be multiplied 20x, when different products give you bonus points, and when they have an Event Day where your points are worth even more.   Last week I had a $200 dollar shopping spree and didn't pay a penny.   A few days ago I earned enough bonus points from a coupon they mailed me to save $40, plus got a $10 gift card for free.  Something about FREE makes me giddy!  :-D

They also have weekly loss-leader sale items that truly are a bargain.  I'm a diet Coke addict, and when I can get a six pack of 710 ml bottles for $2, I'm delighted!   My grandson loves pepperoni (or "pockey moanie" as he calls it) and it goes on sale for less than Walmart charges.   Milk and cheese are other good sale items, plus lots of other food, beauty, and health products.  Just watch their flyer, either in the mail or in your email, and plan which days to go to combine the best deals.
