Hmmm... I sound a bit like a fanatic over savings .... little things make me happy!
Outstanding food, ambience, and service. Well done Luisa Ristorante and a special shout out to Ed!

Went here with a donair lover and decided to sample their offerings. I had a small poutine, which was such a delicious, junky poutine with enough salt to make your tastebuds stand at attention. Also: the small was quite substantial and I could never ever imagine finishing their large. 
I also had a regular chicken donair. FYI: super spicy, bit too spicy for me but just barely. Really, this is so much better than the tasteless options I have had elsewhere. I really love the customization options for toppings: I had the garlic sauce, tomato, lettuce, and pickles. Again, massive serving for just the regular size with a generous helping of the chicken. 
The baklava here may be the best I have ever had - a great addition for just $1 each. We had to get a second. I will totally go back for the poutine when I am in the mood for the ultimate Canadian junk food (and get baklava too). Yum yum. 
Service was hit and miss: took 5 minutes to get any service but the guy who assembled my donair was really nice. :)

Was directed here by my bike manufacturer's website, as I was looking for some branded accessories to go along with my bike (which I had purchased elsewhere).  Anyway, I was very impressed with the customer service here.  I was immediately greeted and approached by staff not once, but twice, to see if I needed any assistance.  

Looks like they have quite a wide selection of bicycles and other bike-related accessories, all of which are priced fairly reasonably, given you are shopping in a specialty bike shop.  

Free parking available behind the store.

The Candy Bouquet is located on Main Street downtown St. Albert. This gem of a little shop specializes in British imports. But has loads of other options of delectable sweets to choose from. 

Most of the candy is just mixed about the store randomly and it's a lot of fun checking out all the yummy things you might not have seen since your childhood. 

Behind the counter they sell a variety of candy in bulk. A lot of which is also specialty items that you won't find in a grocery store. But beware there are a few items that are outrageously overpriced.

Happy shopping.

If you think of this only as a mall, it's admittedly not first-rate as far as size and selection go.  It's anchored by the Bay and Target stores, and includes smaller shoe stores, Winners, jewellers, food court, etc.   It's very clean, usually quiet, and I've always had good customer service, but it's not the optimal place to shop.  As a Centre with a small town sensibility, however, I've come to really appreciate what it adds to the community.  The staff keeps an active web page going, with contests, info, and quick responses to questions or requests.  In the summer they turn part of the parking lot into an outdoor movie, with free popcorn, candy, balloon animals, and activities for the kidlets prior to the free family-friendly movie on a giant inflatable screen.  They are also the site for shuttle busses to the Farmer's Market, traveling shows, etc.   It's been a long time since I've lived in a smaller community and I'm enjoying what the Centre adds to it  :-)

Lots of new stores in St. Albert Centre, some stores moved to different locations in the mall. 

I like that the bulk barn is finally in St. Albert and more shoe stores to shop at.

My friends recommended this place for their lunch special ($25 for any ramen and any roll on the menu).  I like cheap,  so I agreed to it.  I ordered the seafood ramen,  which was ok. The egg was a bit overcooked for my liking, but the noodles were decent and the broth was fine; all in all,  nothing particularly memorable about it. I then had a mango roll (can't remember the exact name), which wasn't bad if you got past the roll being too mushy/ soft.  The mango mayo was pretty solid.  I tasted a friend's grilled eel roll and same issue: it was too soft/ mushy, but tasted fine otherwise.  This isn't an authentic Japanese establishment though,  it's Chinese run, hence the subpar texture of the sushi rolls.  All in all, this meal was nothing special, other than it was cheap.  I'd go elsewhere for my Japanese food. 

Free wifi available. 

Lots of free parking in the plaza.
Good food. But why no music? So quiet inside I can hear other people's conversations.

Just left Ohana-Ya for the first time ever going there; have heard mixed reviews from people that I work with. Good food, good portion sizes. The wait time was a little longer than I expected but other then that have no complaints!

This is my 1st review of this location, I think. Stop by here for quick shopping of skin products and my refill of prescription on a quarterly basis and use of the Canada Post branch inside. Sometimes I will grab groceries from here, as it is close to home after work. Staff are always willing to help find things for you. Self check out is easy to use.

Ever since my old Donair go to closed, this has become my new have.  

You haven't lived until you try their mixed Donair, consisting of both chicken and beef.  How did I ever survive until the age of 43 without trying this marvellous concoction. 

Best Donair in St. Albert, bar none.

I also recommend their Donair poutine.  They use crinkle fries which keep them crunchy unlike joints that microwave their fries to soften the cheese.

I double dog dare you to try the large Donair and leave hungry.

Great shopping centre on St.Albert Trail have expanded the number of  stores since Target left Canada after 2 years. Finally a Tim Hortons in the food court. St. Albert Kitchen has being here for 20+ yrs. St.Louis Bar and Grill and Bulk Barn on the outside of the mall.

Was craving some Thai food so I tried out Thai Mekong which is within walking distance of my place in St Albert. I've seen other good reviews so I was looking forward to trying it out. We ordered 3 dishes: Tom Yum Soup, Pad Thai and Panang Curry. 

The food was quite tasty in general but the Tom Yum Soup was sweeter then I expected and didn't have enough coconut milk. The Pad Thai was a little disappointing because the noodles were too dark from the seasoning but my dining partner thought it was the best tasting dish. I have to say I really enjoyed the Panang Curry. The actual curry was flavorful, the vegetables still had crunch and the beef was tender. The curry didn't come with rice however so we had to order it on the side.

The pricing was my biggest issue with Mekong... Everything was at least $2 more expensive then it should have been. A single serving bowl of coconut rice was $4! We each had a beer with dinner and the total bill ended up being over $60 before tip. That means that I won't be coming here as often as I would like and I think they may be turning away customers by the high price point.

Stay away if you can. First time I tried to get my truck in for two codes that were coming up on a friend's OBD2 scanner. I took morning off work to go in and the ridiculous guy at the service department said if the issue wasn't happening right than at that moment that there was nothing he could do.
I was confused isn't that what the codes are for. He told me that they might only be what was wrong than and not now. Well should you attempt to fix that since both codes where for the T.B.S.(throttle body sensor). He said we may replace one thing but it may not fix it. I thought mechanics attempt to fix an issue and if that doesn't work, fix what the next issue is until it is repaired. 
There was no safe way to engage this problem without driving highway speed for an hour or so. Than what was I suppose to drive back 100 km at reduced engine speed of about 40km down the highway. He didn't care and said sorry, than turned to next person. 

I left missing half a days pay, and wondering what to do. So a week later I again made an appointment online. Made the arrangement's to miss work again, and the night before I got an email from them changing my appointment to 2 weeks later WTF. That was the last straw for me. I never got my truck fixed by this dealership and really just want people to know that if your vehicle is not on fire when you bring it , don't bother. They don't care about your safety or your families.

Our first experience at this restaurant.  We made a reservation to celebrate our anniversary well in advance.  When we arrived the place was smoky and hot.  We were seated at a small and cramped table.  The waitress apologized over and over for having been seated there.  We were told this was their last night as the restaurant was closing.  Several items were not available.  The food and service were good, but found the menu overpriced.  Disappointed.

Great location in Village Landing with a post office inside. Pharmacy is open until midnight 7 days a week.  This is a medium sized Shoppers Drug Mart location.  My family has had both great and quite disappointing experiences with customer service throughout the store and pharmacy department.  None the less, it's nice to know that in a pinch you can hop in and out of here in only a few minutes late at night when someone is sick.

Awesome donair spot in St. Albert. The beef donair with cheese is my go to. I always order the medium, it's more than enough and I'm a big eater. Have had the donair poutine before as well and it is delicious.

I am not a fan of the chicken donair. It looks delicious and I have tried it twice... both times I found the meat to be very salty and lacking the flavour of the beef. As well, the fries and onion rings tend to be hit or miss. Last night we ordered a half & half of fries and rings and they were very overlooked. This has happened before. 

Stick to the beef donairs or donair poutine and you won't be disappointed. Rivals anything in Edmonton... the only spot I like as much in the city is Simon King.

If it was possible to give less than 1 star I would! I received a funeral arrangement from Holes, that was to be used at my daughters funeral service, with several damaged and broken flowers. These were totally destroyed and smooshed! I contacted Holes customer service and asked them to send a few replacement flowers so I could fix the arrangement , or to please send a new one. The customer service was terrible and rude. Eventually they did end up sending a new arrangement for the funeral service but not without a very nasty comment from the person who dropped it off. This kind of terrible behaviour to grieving parents of a small child is not acceptable.

HUGE shout-out to their pharmacy - I took in a prescription for someone else who needed it filled and back to them within 40 minutes (on their way to the airport).  Five people were in line in front of me to turn in their requests, and I heard #2 told it would take 20 minutes.  By the time it was my turn, I felt nearly frantic.  I explained to the pharmacy student and she assured me we could make it in time.  She quickly did the computer work for a new customer and expedited my papers to the pharmacist, putting me next in line, and a few minutes later I was out the door in record time to deliver the medicine by the deadline.   I stopped by later that evening to thank them again, and exchange happy smiles.  I so much appreciate the special service and great attitudes.

I like to drop in here often, all of the people here seem great. I have not purchased a vehicle through them but I am sure in time I will.

 I buy some parts and accessories from Surfer Joe in his hut... that's, right, he has a surf hut set up inside. The knowledge he has was what lead me to him in the first place, if they make it he can find it for you! 

If you are looking for a great selection of some very cool GM products don't hesitate to stop here, no pushy salesman, and a very comfortable atmosphere. They even have some rare cool vehicles on hand, check out the Hawaiian while you can, this vintage dragster has a ton of history.

Great little Japanese restaurant tucked into the Gateway strip mall area, easy to overlook but definitely worth a visit.  We stopped in less than an hour before closing but were not treated like a nuisance and everything on the menu was still available.  The menu itself is extensive and well-written, making us starvin' marvins wanting to order everything we saw!  We of course over-ordered and had leftovers to take home and enjoy later.  Will absolutely be returning to try out more items.

This is kinda your classic mom and pop place. The staff was laid back and cool yet informative. The food was delicious. I always like to try the bruschetta first and they didn't disappoint. Luisas was made with fresh tomatoes and nice crispy bread. Yummy! Next we got the shrimp! Totally worth a order! After that we ordered a pasta with sausage which totally hit the spot and we were too full for dessert. This hidden gem is where you should head for your next date night.

This update is strictly regarding the Black Friday Gives Back event, one of the biggest disappointments of the shopping season.

I want to acknowledge first of all that this event was to raise money for five charities, and that is great for the season.  I never want to lose sight of that.  However....

The first posting on Facebook to advertise for this event stated that the mall would close to the public, that there would be special sales available only for ticket holders, that there would be a V.I.P. room with treats for us, etc etc etc.  Sounded like a lot of exclusive fun and a chance for special shopping.  Told that only ticket-holders would be admitted to the mall, we even bought additional tickets for the kids so they could participate.

Now the reality...

The mall remained open to the public.  Kids didn't need those $10 tickets after all to be inside, only if they wanted to enter the "special area," which turned out to be a roped off section of the hallway in front of Winners, with some sparkling juice, meet and cheese board, and chocolate bells from Purdys.  Yep, that's it.  To add insult, we were refused "re-entry" for another glass of juice at the end of the evening, even though there were no more attendees waiting to enter for the first time and there were over a hundred glasses of juice sitting there already poured out.

Employees, whether paid mall admin people or perhaps some helpers, seemed frustrated, frazzled, and totally out of patience to address any concerns.  One in particular was extremely rude, and I mean extremely.  Maybe things weren't going well for them, or maybe there had been some disagreements before we arrived, but regardless, we paid the penalty for their bad attitudes.  

All in all, we would not participate in events in the future and regret roping in friends to come with us to this one.  

Oh - and the frosting on the cake??  There were NO special sales for us.  We were handed a sheet that purported to give us the skinny on sales, but they were clearly posted for the public at each store - not one special for us, except for free mints at one location if we spent $25 first.  Uh, no thanks, and thanks for nothing.

Do I sound jaded?  Yes.  Based on the letdown from expectations raised in the beginning.  Beware -- lesson learned.

Today was my first ever visit to ThunderGround I was invited to attend an X-Wing miniatures Tournament. 

Roy (owner I believe ) hosted this event with so much class, he made everyone feel welcomed and valued ( he called out most by name).  

There were deals available for Xwings at the time

Parking was shared amongst other businesses in area but seemed to be fine, even for the event 20ish ppl I think. 

They had all sorts of board games , card games, miniatures such as war machine etc.  I would for sure recommend to check out for any of these needs or even to learn about a new game.

Holy crow, I did not expect This.

Having lived in St. Albert for almost seven years, Ohana-ya was a place that I passed by a thousand times. It's only now that I decided to finally try it and I am upset that it took this long. 

Over the course of two separate visits, the Trophy Wife and I got to partake in the jalapeño hamachi, the ABSOLUTELY INCREDIBLE avocado salad, Tan Tan ramen, Mangocado roll, miso soup and the house Bento.

Everything really was absolutely amazing and would order it all again. However, I was completely blown away by the avocado salad. Describing it can't even do it justice. It must be ordered and experienced to even begin to describe it. Let's put it this way... mildly spicy dressing and tempura avocado is just the beginning. 

The staff is very friendly and accommodating and truly work as a team to make your visit extra special. I really like the addition of a motorized sesame seed grinder for the ramen. 

Keep the doors open, Ohana-ya... I will be back.

Soon.

Very soon.

This is a fun little store to check out, with shelves absolutely loaded with everything from high-quality chocolates to total junk candy.  I was quite impressed that the kiddos with me held themselves to a reasonable amount of temptations.  It helps to be aware of what's available at your local grocery, as those items seemed to be priced higher than I would normally pay, and a few boxes that evidently aren't too popular had dust on top of the wrappers, but in general it's worth browsing and you'll find yourself smiling and reminiscing as well as discovering new items to try.

I love Cranky's they always get the job done right and fast. Their bike station at the farmers market is amazing. I went in there for 20 minutes and asked a few questions, I got all the help I could've needed! Only bike shop I go to anymore! Plus no one minded I brought my puppy in (on a hot day).

Uhhhh, I think something happened to the quality of this restaurant. Did I come at a bad time?
We ordered the appetizer assortment plate, which was so obviously left over from long ago and reheated.
The one dish that was "fresh" was mediocre, the shrimps were the smallest available and tasted very poor or "off"  and the bean sprouts and carrots were just that and nothing more. Total was over $60 with one beer. I figure they made a profit of $57.
This was after 2pm and no one was in the place, so we either got someone's reheated lunch or this place has taken a huge dive judging from other positive reviews...
Not sure what happened but I expected fresh food and I got reheated microwave Thai food...right out of a safeway box, judging by the quality.
I won't be back.

Great Food, Great Drinks!. Just went to my usually hangout spot at Luisa's and another excellent meal I had. I like how they changed up their drink menu and started having drink specials, nice job guys! Had my usually bruschetta and shrimp scampi to start and changed it up from this time, from my usual tortellini and chicken to the lamb shank and veggies, no regrets there. I like how they changed up their drink menu and started advertising drink specials, nice job guys! Great cesare drink with the lemon sliced rim and the decorated celery to top it off. Once again, ill be back for more!

After dealing with the worst experience (bait and switch) at the Go Auto Outlet, I came here to find a used truck. Immediately I was put at ease, which is saying a lot after getting jerked around like that earlier. I had Bob Robbins help me, who was very knowledgable and kind. And when financing, Mike Erickson took extra time out of his day to get me the lowest interest rate possible with his wizardry. I had a great time buying my truck here and highly recommend this dealership to others I talk to.

Great Sashimi at Ohana-ya love it every time I eat there or take it out. Ordered off of skip the dishes as well same goodness. Rolls are so yummy as well as the sashimi salad. Keep up the great food Ohana-ya.

Their service department is a joke... I don't recommend bringing your vehicles here for anything... Especially detailing as they have incredibly low standards when it comes to detailing both inside and out. Won't be buying my new truck here for this reason nor will I be recommending this dealership to anyone. All respect lost.

My wife and I went here for the first time on a Friday night before a concert at the Arden Theater. From the minute we walked in the door until we left after our meal, it was obvious all of the staff were dedicated to making our experience amazing. We were looked after by Cindy who is one of the (new) owners and she provided some of the best service we have ever had, anywhere. Everything is done with class, and pride. 

The food was excellent (we shared a beet salad, both had the Carbonara and shared a Tiramisu). Everything was delicious with large portions at very reasonable prices. They have a great wine list and again, the prices are very fair. The ambience is cozy and welcoming. Overall, it was a fantastic dinner and we will be back soon. I really hope people support this wonderful, locally owned, non-chain restaurant run by people that are incredibly passionate about what they are doing. Outstanding!

Bought a bike yesterday and the girl who sold it to me was very nice. So im not venting on her it was after. 
The next say I took it for a rip and noticed a wobble on  the tire, called the service guy and he pretty much told me it's too bad that just the way it is with some pretty spicy attitude,  I guess the name cranky works in their favor. That's the second bike I bought from them and the last. Sorry for the lousy spelling.

Wanted to celebrate our Anniversary with a dinner out, but Covid changed our plans slightly, but it turned out to be one of the best dinners ever!
Ordered from Luisa's for the first time ever dining there and it was a wonderful experience. When I first called to place my order, they asked what time I would be picking up as they only allow one person in at a time. And they completely disinfect everything after each guest leaves (door handles, debit machine, counters, etc). After placing my order, he described the process of entering the restaurant, where to park at the back and the cleaning process, which I appreciated greatly. 

For our evening out, I ordered a side cesar salad, bread basket, lasagne and the chicken parmesan that they had for the special that evening. 
We took our meals to Lion's Park and had a lovely picnic instead of bringing the meals home. 

Our salad was a perfect sharing size and tasted great. The bread for the bread basket was a bit dry, but would have been perfect for bruschetta. So we'll make french toast with it at home. :) 

My spouse's lasagne must have weighed 5 pounds! The portion was huge and really delicious! The perfect combination of meat, pasta, sauce and cheese! 
I had the chicken parmesan special, which was a huge chicken breast marinaded over night, topped with italian meats (I don't remember exactly which ones...sorry...), sauce and cheese. It came with a large serving of pasta that had been tossed in butter, garlic and parmesan. I could only eat half of the chicken and pasta because it was so large. But that means leftovers for supper tonight!

The owner, Ed, and I had a lovely conversation while I was picking up our meal and he was very nice to deal with. Overall, our dinner was amazing and we can't wait to go back. Either for another pick up, or to dine in!

Thank you Luisa's Ristorante staff and owners for a great anniversary supper, Covid style!

The staff were dealing with 2 (two!!) anti-mask crazies while I was shopping. They handled the situation with confidence and respect for the surrounding costumers. I greatly appreciate the staff trying to maintain the safety of their community by attempting to remove the cov-idiots from the store.

I don't think it's fair, however, that two women had to stand up to two different grown men. I hope this location considers hiring a security guard or a peace officer until the population of St. Albert learns to behave like adults. 

(Also this place is always well stocked and has great prices compared to other drug stores.)

Went here last night under the new ownership. I had never eaten here under the old, so I can't compare. I can, however, go on and on about the DELICIOUS meal I had!! Started with the classic caesar salad, I could not shove it in my mouth fast enough, omg so good. For my main I had the gnocchi with housemade sausage and peas. The sausage had a nice hit of spice which was balanced with the sweetness of the peas. Nice big portion, I should've taken some home for lunch today but it was so amazing that I ate myself into a delightful food coma. The only thing I regret is that I had no room for gelato. The service was top notch, friendly and attentive. My water glass was always full (which is honestly what I base my tip on - don't judge, you have your own system too). My friend had a peach grappa over ice after dinner. I was driving so I only had a sip but I'll walk home to the west end from St. Albert next time so I can have one (or three). No doubt that I'll be back to try the carbonara, it looked to die for. Not one of us took a photo of the food ...we were too excited to eat!!

sushi was good but was very disappointed as we arrived at 8
;00 PM only to be told sushi bar was closed at 8:10 YET they say open to 9:PM some people wre actually turned away prior to 8:30 SO watch when your timing at this place

We just happen to be passing by when my sister and mom decided to check this store out! It's pretty amazing! I saw candies in here that I didn't realize we could buy in Canada! 

A couple of years ago, my friend asked me to buy her some Galaxy chocolate in London! I was surprised to see this store fully stocked with these chocolates! Totally saves me a trip to Europe!

There were so many kinds of candies in here! I was literally like a kid in this candy store! Some of the prices were a bit on the expensive side, like $2.49 for a tiny Galaxy chocolate bar, but I know this chocolate is imported! It even said 1 Euro on the packaging!

If you have a sweet tooth and want to try something new and different, come check this store out!

Wow, I really need to get back to the UK! Until then, this is as close as it gets when it comes to sweets! Keep in mind these are imported goods and as such the price is a bit higher than your convenience store chocolate bar. But is it ever worth it!

I have a sensitivity/allergy to soy. If you check the ingredients of practically everything chocolate in North America, it contains soy lecithin. It's horrible because I love chocolate! Gratefully in England they don't add unnecessary ingredients to their candy. Last time I was there, which was well over a decade ago, I fell in love with Cadbury's Flake bar. So, today I got one. I also noticed something interesting - you know Cadbury's Easter Cream Eggs right? They have them available in chocolate bar form! Seriously! The same filling and chocolate only not in egg shape. I had to get one simply for the novelty of it. 

An interesting tidbit for those with celiac disease, I've been told that only North American liquorice contains gluten. So, get some good stuff at the Candy Bouquet! 

This store is the real deal. I got there just before close and didn't even have a chance to see everything but what I did see was amazing. Besides, stores like these must have a time limit as far as my personal shopping goes.

This little shop has been our go to place to take our daughter when she has earned a treat. She is always excited to come check out what unique candies are in store and then agonize over picking just one of the large assortment.

There is a huge variety of candies, chocolates, biscuits and some hard to find specialty grocery items and drinks. I always end up finding something for myself as well and you cannot go wrong with the candy grab bags at the check out.

We like the good assortment of interesting candies and always can find a deal but it might be more than what you would find in other stores. Altogether a fun little store in the heart of St. Albert.

I am so impressed by the assistance that I got with the repot of my dear Ficus Tree, "Stephen". He is twelve years old and has been with me for a long time. He definitely needed some TLC as his roots were beginning too outgrow his pot.

I was emailing back and forth with Stacie about the repot and eventually it  got warm enough for me to bring him in. She gave some great advice and got Stephen in a nice new pot that was a more appropriate size. I had also gotten some previous advice about Ficus trees that she nicely explained was incorrect and gave me some great tips about how to care for him from now on. This is my oldest plant and I know he still has a lot of life in him so I want to care for him as best I can! 

One of the best things about this is I only had to pay for the pot. I was prepared to pay upwards of $100 but the repot and advice was actually free! What a nice surprise! I think more people should take advantage of this great service. I believe I will bring him in again in a few years but of course these trees are temperamental and don't like to be moved too much.

I also brought in my little prayer plant and we set him up for new propagation to keep him feeling good as well. 

Thanks to Stacie and the staff at Holes! It makes me feel like Stephen and my other plant were in great hands and I will definitely be back!

17 yrs I have been with this pharmacy. It's used to be awesome.I have A LOT of meds. A senior staff member left. And a bunch of new ppl hired abt 2 yrs ago. Nothing but probs since. This last year has been brutal. And I am often talking to different ppl or my husband does and repeating regularly instructions. I have 2 health coverages one AISH which is supposed to be secondary. They argue with me tgat it's not put it That way and affected my benefits for dental. AISH Wouldn't cover as they said they are secondary. Then it can't be put through at dentist again on their system so I have to wait for my dental work for 4-6 was while it is snail mailed for approval. I'm in pain. 
AISH, pharmacists assoc., and Sure Health all day my AISH coverage is secondary. They have also cost me $200 out of pocket bc AISH doesn't cover but they did not put through on Sure Health. 
Further issues this past year: 
- when trying to get health coverage issues addressed after explain, etc told to speak with my pull pack person. Who is the one who argues AISH is first and caused the issues. Apparently there is no supervisor for me to speak with. ( other than that Christine is great with my packs always on time) - give over the counter for 2 prescription meds Twice that are also avail over counter. Without a asking no authorization, my husband just picked up. You do not change a prescription. There is a reason that the doc writes a script. Taxes, delivery method of med, etc. 
- repeating my name and birthdate over and over in same call. Several times and not bc they couldn't hear. Inexperienced, not listening, not paying attention. ???
- notes not placed on file so have to explain situation multiple times to different ppl. 
- owner while addressing my complaints in person was running around, tending to other things, dismissive. I felt undervalued. 

There are a couple other little things, but not big just annoying. I used to love my pharmacy and brag how well they took care of me, managed my pills, knew both my husband and myself when they came in. The pharmacists themselves are great. The pharmacy assistants are the issue. I'm currently looking around to decide on a new pharmacy. It's sad. The owner doesn't care, the assistants are either too busy, too new, too something and they give me and my husband too much aggravation. And I hate to say it but a couple just can't get what myself or my husband are trying to explain. Yes... our coverage is more complicated, I have A LOT of meds and small changes not often. It shouldn't be this frustrating. 

If you are just going for the occasional  med, good. If your previous pharmacy was bad they may be ok for you. If you have moderate changes to your meds, lots of meds or specialists go elsewhere.

This restaurant is under new management and the difference is truly huge. Service is friendly and accommodating, food is excellent and pricing is reasonable for the quantity and quality. Had lunch there today, $15 for Spaghetti and three large veal meatballs. Pasta was cooked perfectly, sauce was full bodied and tasty and the meat balls were great for adding some protein to the carbs. A definite winner. The new owner even brought me a complimentary desert and it too was very good. 

Good wine selection at reasonable prices, some craft beers but no domestic stuff for those of us that prefer Molson Canadian to craft beer. I believe they are planning to add a few mainline options to their selection. 

I will definitely be going back to try some of their other dishes.

This was my first time trying their sushi and I was very impressed with the size of the nigiri as they were huge. Taste and quality was pretty decent, but I thought it could be better, price point seemed slightly higher, but overall, I really enjoyed my meal. Another decent sushi place in St. Albert, and I would absolutely order from here again.

Some of my coworkers and I go here every now and again; tempura is great, no issues with the sushi, salads taste good as well (which is nice as most restaurants have bland salad). I haven't tried any of the soup-based dishes myself, but other coworkers said they were fantastic.

Staff is always friendly and accommodating.

Luisas is the BEST.  They are very friendly wonderful people with a great clean restaurant and FANTASTIC Italian food. We have been there many times and will be back. Last night they were especially kind accomadating our 7 yr old granddaughter. One of the BEST

This is my first time at a Hole's Greenhouse. Judging from the reviews, I'd say I like this place a better than the other reviewers, but maybe that's because I never saw the old location.

It's true the Enjoy Center is located in a weird place. My bestie was doing the driving and I had to ask, "Where are we going? I thought we were going to St. Albert?" But we had no problems getting there.

We decided we would check Hole's out after the Spirit Expo, which was our reason for being there. I'm definitely on the fence about how I feel about this place. I kind of liked the open concept, but it also made me feel a little lost, like I wasn't sure if I was still in the store, and was the kitchen store part of it? (Staff there need to work on their social skills. Saleslady asked me in a booming snarl if everything was alright. Glared at me the whole time like I was going to stuff my pockets with mini spatulas and pepper mills.) 

Lovely merchandise. I picked up an air plant and several interesting stocking stuffer items like pickled sea asparagus. I'll bet this place is LOADED with awesome stuff in the spring, and I might want to come then just to see if I can find something special for my garden. Service at the checkout was polite, and she even gave me a bag to hold all the other bags I was carrying from the expo.

We were feeling peckish, and thought we might give the cafeteria a try. WRONG! Nine dollars for soup?! I don't care if it's gluten-free and organic. That's all we needed to know, and decided it was probably time to leave.

It's right around this time that the weight of snobbery became heavy for us, and we started to feel as though we didn't belong. It's a new place, and it IS St. Albert, so part of me expected things to be a bit pricey, but I think we were in over our heads a little. If I come back to Hole's, it will be strictly for gardening stuff.

They call it St. Albert "Centre" but it's hardly that. The only thing it's the centre of is literally the city itself. The mall is dead with stores I haven't seen for at least a decade, ie. Bootlegger and Northern Reflections. The Winners is the smallest Winners I've been to which means less selection, and Target is just a rebranded Zellers that has more employees hanging out than shoppers. Actually, I think "more employees than shoppers" resonates with every store in the mall, and I didn't come here on a Monday morning either. It was Saturday afternoon. I feel bad but the only thing the mall is good for is the free park and ride for the Farmers Market shuttle.

I went to Jack's after seeing many many posts from a local food blogger about the amazing burgers at Jack's. It also made a list of top 5 burgers in the Edmonton area, so I had high expectations. We ordered the shroom and poutine. My first bite was a surprise as I thought maybe the bun was under cooked and the patty was so thin. The whole burger was quite small for $9. After my second bite I said to my husband that the bun tasted like a grocery store dinner role, not surprising after just reading that Safeway makes their buns. The meat had a nice crisp on it but the patty wasn't substantial enough to get a sense of the quality. The poutine was a total let down- Costco makes it better and that's not saying much. The gravy was way too thick and lacked flavor. There was no commingling of gravy and cheesy goodness because the gravy wasn't the right consistency for poutine. All in all the burger tasted good, but not in my top 10 list at all. A small burger, small order of poutine and a milkshake was $20. Although the shake was tasty there was not enough bang for your buck overall.

we wanted to try Jacks for two reasons.  The claim of best hamburger in town and the fact that they used Darcy's Meats (out of St. Albert) for the meat.

I appreciate Darcy's Meats and what they do, so that Jacks was using their beef was good enough for me.

We got two burgers, the cobb and the peanut butter one.

they were good.

fries were good too.

lettuce wrapped option (sans bun) puts this on my YEG paleo list

we both said we got "jacks" out of our system and wouldnt go out of the way to go there again.

Food was priced decently.  Size of burger was average.  Meat was good.  flavors good.

Would pop in if I was in the neighbourhood again, but that's about it.  Not making a special trip out of Edmonton for them

I still enjoy the food at Wild Earth, but they're starting to drive me insane because of one thing: the lack of prices! Why on Earth would you have a bunch of products for sale without prices?! Want to know how much that square is? Either buy it, or ask an employee. How much is the chocolate brownie beside the til? I had to ask (and it's $5!!). Maybe they don't put prices on things because it'll scare away customers.

Please, Wild Earth, put prices on the things you sell! Yes, there are chalk boards with prices of some things, but I think about half the stuff they sell isn't priced at all. Grr!

This used to by my all time favourite cafe in Edmonton. I came here at least once a week even though i don't live nearby. Sadly it seems to have lost some of it's charm within the last year. The coffee isn't as good and there isn't the same selection or quality of food as before. It used to feel like the Wild Earth had something really special, but unfortunately has become just rather standard, which makes me sad because I really loved this place. I still visit but not with the same frequency.

Simply put, it's the best burger place around. 
A burger should taste great fully loaded and naked too, that's what you get at Jack's. The ground beef is perfectly cooked, and very flavourful, the buns are soft fluffy and chewy just as they should be. Really, I can't think of a better burger. 
Great fries too. Especially the jacked up fries.
Love the atmosphere at this coffee shop. It's cozy and comfy and the baked goods are incredible. I'm also a huge fan of the live music on Friday nights. It's my go to meet up place with friends.

We were pretty stoked to try Jade Village last weekend at the recommendation of our friends.  We ordered about 6 different dishes, 2 appies, and soup to go for a group of 6 of us and we were so disappointed.  Portions and prices were okay but quality was just not up to par for us.  In much rather pay a little more and get take out from the Lingnan express in the future.

A few example - green onion cakes were $5.95 and were flat and squishy little doughy pancakes.  We usually a lot an entire order for the kiddos and they wouldn't eat them! 

The Hot & Sour Soup wasn't spicy and tastes weird - like worchestershire sauce!

The ginger beef was blah as we're the salted jumbo shrimp - which weren't so jumbo.  We had some sort of cashew chicken but there wasn't much cashew or chicken.  A lot of filler foods and bland flavors.  

Spring rolls were standard as was the steamed rice.  

Hubby and Gramma were not impressed and they usually are pretty going.  And as a side note - 1 fortune cookie in an orde this size was definitely a little odd.

We will NOT be doing takeout from Jade Village again.  I feel badly giving 2 star as the restaurant appeared clean and the staff was friendly but the food left so much to be desired :-(
Burger was really good.  Enjoyed the food until I grabbed my last bit of fries and bit into a small rock.

Now THIS is a burger joint. Pretty much everything at Jacks is made from scratch, and it really shows in the quality of their food. My favorite is the BBQ Crunch - with potato chips and an Orange Pop BBQ sauce - it's a thing of beauty. 

Staff was amazing, place was clean, and the milkshakes...OMG. This is my favorite burger place by a mile. Where's the 6 star button when you need it?

This place it's a true gem for casual comfort food. It's a creative and delicious twist on your traditional burger joint. Fast and friendly service. The daily specials are always something to look forward to.

I enjoyed a blueberry tart and lavender tea from this little cafe. Most of the baked goods were sold out when I got there. They should top up on their selection throughout the day. There was a good selection of loose tea leaves to choose from as well. My lavender tea was aromatic and light tasting. 

The cashier was new. She made multiple transaction mistakes. Hope she gets better at her job soon.

The food is good but they are often not open when they say they are. Checked the website menu and it said open Friday 11 to 9. Went there at two o'clock and although I could walk right in the unlocked door, I was told they're closed. It would be courteous to customers to update the operation hours on the website. If you're expecting a tightly run operation like CFL and Lingnan downtown, this is not it.

Well, this place is quaint! Ok, it's teeny, it's tiny, it barely has standing room, but By George it has delicious ice cream, sorbets and gelato! 

With all the product coming from Foothills Creamery, Chapman's (the premium label, not the stuff that is available to buy at Save-On), and of course the insanely insatiable Pinocchio's products - this is most definitely a wonderful little Mom n' Pop place to take the kiddos for a cone. 

While I was in though, I actually never saw any kids (nor families)... I did see 3 separate elderly couples come in for "date night" (adorable!) What I am trying to get at is that this place is geared towards the very young and very old. It is not 'cosmopolitan flavours' that you find at Rosso, Cafe Leva or Cravings Gelato. Nor it is 'On Fleek' and uber trendy like Pop Bar. It is lovely, and worth your time St Albert - so enjoy!

Partially salt water pools - hip hip hooray! Family change rooms available, a toddler pool, 2 deep pools, giant slide, and a large hot tub - Love Fountain Park! 

My toddler just finished her first unparented swim lessons here & adored her coach, Taylor.  This is the facility for group swim classes/lessons ranging from parented with babies all the way up to adult!

Because of the large number of swim lessons & schools utilizing this pool, open swim time is limited.  Be sure to check the schedule before showing up!

I had originally given Wild Earth 4 stars because I enjoy the atmosphere of the cafe, the selection of loose teas, their homemade soups, and delicious baked bread. Recently I have had some disappointing experiences at this location. The cashiers seem to be uninterested in taking orders/helping customers. I have had my drink order forgotten twice the last two times I was there (just ordered brewed coffee to go). After trying vainly to get the attention of a barista, I finally managed to ask if my drink had been skipped and was given a look that could be described as "So, what?". 

I would also add that the sugar-free muffins near the front of the till are often put on display while still frozen inside. I bought one to go, and was let down when I found it to still be an ice chunk. A bakery serving frozen pastries? Come on guys, you used to have this place down to a tee, and now it feels like it's heading down.

Jack's is awesome!!! Love the burgers and that sauce they give you with the chips..OMG!!! The Nutella milkshake was divine as well! The only bad thing I can say is that you have to get there early enough to get a seat(which there aren't enough of) and they seem to have a certain amount of food per day so you may have to have a gluten free bun or no bun with your burger! But I'd say Jack's is one of the best burger joints in the city!

The place is kind of a hybrid between a bakery and a cafe and there are  lots of gluten free options which I think is great. My drink was delicious once I stirred it, though i'm not a fan of their whip cream. My biscotti was as hard as a rock... I couldn't bite it unless I put it in my coffee for a good minute or two. That's a little too hard for me. Staff were pretty friendly although it felt like the lady was rushing me to get to the next non-existent customer.
Love Jacks burgers! I just wish they weren't sold out of ingredients, this has happened more than once.

Got the regular basic burger with cheese. The burger patties were extremely thin and so the edges were burnt. The bun was also very thin. Maybe it's just the style of burger but I prefer the patty thicker and moist. It was quick service though

I consider myself to be an ice cream aficionado and this space is unfortunately just a glorified lemonade stand. When we went in today there was ONE kind of gelato! That does not seem reasonable if you actually use the word "gelato" in your business name. We settled for 2 regular ice cream cones in waffle cones... for $12!  They do not make this ice cream, it's the same typical ice cream that everybody else sells or you can buy for yourself at the grocery store. They have the audacity to charge $12 for two very small portions.  

I can't wait until the craft ice cream model from Calgary arrives in Northern Alberta. Until that happens I think I'll save my money and my waistline. 

*Please note that the only reason this was not a 1 star review was because of the friendly service we received.
Never fails to impress me.  Their beef patties are flavourful in whatever burger your choose. Jacks fries are delicious.  Only wish it was open later so we could go more often!

There are several vietnamese restaurants in St Albert, and we've eaten at many many viet places, so we looked forward to trying this one especially since it had been closed for renos.  The food was so so so severely bland.  It was disgusting.  Our table had a variety of food too, a vermicelli bowl, salad rolls, soup... Fish sauce tasted like water, peanut sauce was watery and lacked flavor, meat wasn't seasoned, broth no flavor...we were so disappointed. The service was crap too.  A large party of 8 came in just as we were paying, I felt like telling them "don't bother, walk out now and save your money"  I will never ever go back, you couldn't pay me to.

I've found my new favourite coffee shop in the city, I think. Just maybe.

Swung by last weekend for a morning date with Sarah J. Now, after reading this review, you can't say I didn't warn you when I tell you that it might be awfully tricky to find a seat here on a Saturday morning. Or Saturday afternoon. Or anytime on a Sunday, at all. Busy busy busy!

My muffin was fresh and delicious and full of berries. My coffee was fresh and hot and just what I needed!

We snagged a seat the bar by the window, luckily. Even though the joint was hopping, it never felt too loud, or like we couldn't have a conversation. I really like that about this place!

When I really feel like splurging, I'll try one of their infamous cinnamon buns. And when I have a Friday night with nothing to do, I'm going to check out their live music scene - NO COVER!

The food is not near as good as the Express downtown nor the main restaurant. Also, the posted hours on the door are always changing so you have NO IDEA when they will actually be open. Even when the sign says they are open they are often closed with no explanation. 

I am a fan of Lingnan's main restaurant but this place is hurting their rep big time. Run it right, rename it to something else or close it .

They do a good job here. The other franchise near the mall is not as good. I've always been impressed with this location, consistent for fast food. My kids, the only reason I go, like this location best too. They are busy and sometimes there is a wait but when we get our orders they are complete. They are also friendly which is a really special feature these days.
Biblical burgers. I got the standard and it was, hands down, the best burger I have had to date. It's everything I hoped for. Everything I dreamed. This burger was so beautiful to me
Excellent burgers and shakes. No sloppy over filled burgers, fresh and delicious. A must visit for burger lovers!!

My review is solely based on service. If you love a good London fog, you will never be dissappointed and the baked goods are incredible. 

Let me preface this by saying, I have worked in customer service for my entire adult life and I was very dissapointed with the cashier. After making my order, I noticed a sign saying that they now offer coconut milk. I politely asked the cashier if I could change the latte to one with coconut milk. She rolled her eyes and sighed.....oh I'm sorry, did pressing that one button really put you out that badly? Let's chalk this up to a bad day, perhaps.

After I order she points to the end of the bar with a straight face and says, you can wait over there. 

No thank you, no smile, no nothing. I will think twice about spending 6 dollars on a latte here again.

Amazing burgers! The BBQ crunch is my favourite and hangover-styling it makes it even better. The fries with aiole are amazing too. The prices are fair for the portions and staff is friendly. My only tiny complaint would be their opening/closing times and things sometimes running out early.

Wild earth is more then a bakery, more then a cafe, more then a quaint environment. It is a fairy tail of delectable goods and darling spots to be inspired in life again or to reconnect with friends and family. This adorable South side spot is the bar to which I measure all other cafes, bakery/coffee houses. I can't even put into words what it is, there is just this air about Wild Earth that makes me happy to be alive, to be me, to live where I live. It takes me away and brings me home all at the same time. 

The staff are so wonderful and make me laugh. The drinks are lovely, the food good but we all know why we go... The insane, delicious confections! From cookies to squares, tarts to cakes and everything in between. I love it all! I especially love all that is made with the word lemon in it: Hello lemon loaf, ya, I h-e-a-r-t you soooo much, but not as much as your square brother.... Need I say more?
Low to no staff and whenever you call store for product info no one ever answers the phone. It's impossible to reach them by phone !!!!!!

I base this on the service not the actual baking. The baking is amazing. The cakes moist and not too sweet . However, the last time I was there, it was just painful. I waited for about 20 mins. After they served everyone around me and the "servers" simply forgot that I wanted to purchase a cake and order another for a event. It was the actual Baker who was helpful. Doubt,I will return due to the terrible service.
Very tasty salads and soso BLT. Would have lunch there again if we find ourselves in the neighborhood. Cozy and comfort with interesting array of furniture, too.

I love myself a tasty burger, and that's exactly what you'll find here! My only regret is that I live on the south side of Edmonton, meaning I'll miss out on many of the "daily burger" specials. Oh - fries were also superb!

Oh my god, these are the BEST burgers ever!!!!!!! I cannot wait to go back here and eat again. I had the chick pea burger and it was amazing and my husband had one of the meat burgers in between the grilled cheese sandwiches which is said was delicious. Seriously just thinking about it I want to go and order it now!

This is one of the best place to come and have breakfast. The location and where this cafe is situated brings such a relax and inspiring feel to your soul. 
When you enter into the cafe, you are delighted by how all the pastries are neatly placed in there appropriate station. Choices here is abundant and you will definitely want to give everything a try.
It's always busy here in the mornings and trying to find a place to sit might be a little difficult but if you wait just a little while, something will always open up unexpectedly and you will be surprise how quickly you will find an open seat. In the end you will get to enjoy your breakfast with you friend that you invited.
The staff and even the customers here are upbeat and friendly. Great place to meet new friends.
I'm a coffee drinker, so I usually get a latte here. It's nice and smooth tasting. 
The sandwiches, salads and soups are always fresh.
I usually get the croissants and sometimes it's over baked. I haven't tried to many of there other baked goods, but they always look so good on the display.
You will never lose interest of this place. There's so many homemade varieties of sweetness...you will find yourself coming back for more.

Today was my first time trying this place with my dad. The burger I ate was "The Standard" it was pretty good. The meal we both order together came to $22.00 cheapest meal I think I've ever had haha. I'd go again and try something else.

Hands down my favourite cafe in Edmonton! Their baked goods look amazing but I have yet to try any; however, their coffees and teas are amazing and you can feel great about ordering them as they have some healthy options (e.g. organic almond milk, can ask for real honey instead of simple syrup). I love the feel of the place: very natural decor and good energy from the staff; however it's usually pretty busy and I can never get a seat in front of their amazing fireplace!
Good quality food. Nice lattes.   The only downside is the prices which are pretty steep.  I had a small latte and a square and it was over $10.

Was going to go to soda j erks but they close at 9 o'clock so instead I yelped ice cream and found Geppetto's gelato camera.  got here 5 after 9 and they were pretty much closing shop even though the website here on Yelp says 10 p.m. So my wife went in and asked if they would help us which they re open the whole store let us sample everything we want a sample were very polite and pleasant didn't make us feel rushed didn't impatient or rude that we were there 100% customer service fantastic I got some gelato my wife got some ice cream absolutely amazing price is completely reasonable especially if you wanted a bucket of ice cream as you can see by the picture I posted job well done thank you very much for not making my night wasted

Been there in the last 3 weeks; food was fresh, tasty, prepared and authentic. Portions are generous. Just excellent. Prices are about what you'd expect for the amount of food, style & preparation. Very clean atmosphere. Definitely worth going to again.
Horrible. I only download this yelp app to deter people from making the same mistake I have made.

Almost prohibitively expensive, though I guess perception is key. If you, unlike me, decided to embrace the responsibilities of adulthood as quickly as possible and got a well-paying job in your early 20s, ten dollars for a cup of coffee and a slice of cake is totally reasonable. As for me, I can make better baked goods, sandwiches, and salads at home, and have a hell of a lot more fun doing it on my own. 

Though past visits have been costlier, I came in at just under $5.50 for a cup of coffee and a lemon meringue tart yesterday afternoon. The tart was okay, but meringue isn't supposed to be chewy, and the crust was similarly textured--the effects of refrigeration, perhaps? The tart was less than $3, so I had no reason to be too pissy, but my friend paid $7 for the driest slice of carrot cake I've ever tasted.

Yesterday's (Sunday) clientele at 4:30 in the afternoon was a weird mix of seniors, young families, and scene kids. We had to bus our own table before sitting down because the previous occupants hadn't done so, and neither had the staff. 

In sum, a bit too pricey for the quality of food. Your money likely is better spent at other fancy bakeries around town. I will, however, say only excellent things about their chili varieties, which are delicious--and generally the reason I come here.

Found this gem of a place that makes vegan rolls (awesome!!) and muffins. The lemon poppyseed is my favorite. Girls are efficient and friendly, even a long line moves fast. Go try and decide for yourself.

For a small recreation centre - the pools are amazing!

And it's a Saltwater Pool - HOORAY!

When I had my first baby, I did the mom and tots baby class there - great facility, great instructors, great pools, great equipment.

We continue to enjoy the rec centre.  The toddler area pool is particularly great for families because it is separate from the other pools for aquasize, lessons, deep end, and lap lanes.  

The toddler pool has lots of toys for wee ones and is large enough to easily accomodate 30-40 people without being squished.  The toddler pool has three small slides that the parents can catch the little ones as they slide into the water.  The toddler pool has varying depths suitable for infants up to preschool.  Unlike the bigger rec centres like Millenium or Service this one is smaller which is great for wee ones who might not want all the action of teenagers running around.

There is a nice tube waterslide, diving boards, and a standard ladder slide in the deep pool.  There is also a large hot tub area.   

Excellent for young families!

Aweful service , I came to buy some labels. First walk all the store to find them , then came to pay and the manager tells me they don't have debit working. Not even apologize , just said sorry can't help you then. If your machines are down debit at least make sure to put a note letting customers know BAD service the manager was a woman with short shoulder hair length and glasses. She needs some training this was at 8:30 pm
Best burger I have ever had. This place never disappoints and the service is great. Lots of choice for the adventurous but the BBQ crunch is my favourite

This is one of my favorite bakeries in Edmonton. It is nice, cozy and customer service is great. I've tried their strawberry rhubarb and creme brûlée tarts ($3 ea.) and they're fantastic. Also, if you order some chocolate milk ($2.50), they will make it for you and you will get it in a nice mason jar. I've also tried their chorizo scramble and iced coffee, which are pretty descent if you ask me. 

I'll definitely be back to try more of their baked goods. I've heard their raspberry white chocolate scone is fantastic so that'll be next on my list.

I seldom review places that have a lot of reviews unless I've had a contrary experience and feel a need to set the record straight.  That's not the case with Jacks as I agree with the strong ratings. It's just that the customer service was so good here that I felt compelled to chime in.  

The food is excellent and they offer chicken and vegetarian alternatives.  But from the time you walk through the door to the time you leave, you'll feel truly welcome and cared for by the overwhelmingly happy staff. 

Everyone is happy at Jack's! This place is a must for burger fans in St. Albert.

Best burgers around! They have some awesomely unique daily specials, along with my faves: All Shook Up, The Hangover, and BBQ Crunch. My husband loves The Quebecer....it's got poutine right on the burger!  Don't forget to order the Cap'n Crunch shake!

It's a good place to grab a burger to support local business. The food isn't over the top, and neither is the atmosphere. I got a little peeved when I went in the middle of the afternoon to find they close for a couple hours between meal services.
What a great place to eat at.  I have yet to try something I didn't love.  This is a great place to go and relax with friends.

These are probably the best burgers i have ever tried in my life no joke i keep bringing people here and no one believes me till they take that first bite and you can see the look of complete SATISFACTION in there eyes! So far ive tried the Shroom, BBQ Crunch, Inferno, and Hangover honestly each burger is amazing in its own way i have yet to eat a burger there that i regretted and im a very critical person when it comes to food. The only negative i got on this place is the fries.. pretty gross i would do a complete overhaul on those, they were thin, stringy and kind of soggy also tried a creamsicle shake once and it was really runny i prefer my shakes a little thicker!! But this review is for the BURGERS and for that i give a solid 10/10!!

Fantastic burgers!! The Inferno burger with an order of "Jacked Up Fries" is a great treat on a summer afternoon. Outdoor seating when the weather is nice is a huge plus. Interior seating is a bit cramped, and you may have to share a table or wait for a spot to open up. The atmosphere is pretty simple, but it works. 

Jack's Burger Shack is well worth visiting.

Not that great! I used to come here often. But for the past few years seems like the service and the food is getting worst. 

What's good about this place: The selection of teas, the coffees and the scones. 

So why only 3 stars? Well the service is not great! I've never once been greeted with a smile. The staff don't seem to care and be willing to help...  The food is ok. Nothing special. The space can use more sitting areas for sure. The worst is if you wait for your food and don't have a table, you find yourself waiting in the middle of traffic right in front of the milk and sugar station... and that's unpleasant and very awkward.

Great food, best cakes and great service!!! Last year, I ordered a cake for my son's birthday but due to some staff illness and holiday blur, my cake was forgotten. I was sad. But the upside is that I was reimbursed immediately and offered a free cake. I came back to them this week and they remembered me and honoured their offer! That's what I call good service! And the mocha cake is delicious!!!

I love Fountain Park Rec Centre.  It is never busy (well rarely), you can ALWAYS find a locker - i use a lock and find some facilities do not provide enough lock lockers (ladies change room).  The staff are great, they do a great job ensuring the safety of all people/kids in a friendly professional manner.

As a family of 4 I find that Servus fees are $25 when Fountain Park's is under $20.  When we go my kids (3 and 5 years old) spend the majority of the time on the diving board, deep water slide and the big blue slide.  I highly recommend bringing your kids to the weekend late afternoon family swim - they sleep AMAZING after, its not busy and you can end your night with a soak in the large NON FOAMY hot tub!  

The facility is always clean, we have gone many times when the life guards were spraying down the change rooms - which gives me peace of mind that the facility is clean for a public facility.  I also remember the days of full chlorine water and find it easier to swim with the salt water - for eye health.

OMG!  I've died and gone to Heaven!  Our own local Gelato, sorbet (REAL SORBET), and ice cream shop in St. Albert serving locally made frozen heaven from Pinocchio!  And no my nose isn't growing ;-)  Pinnochio's uses all natural ingredients - You won't find anything artificial in this goodness!

http://www.pinocchioicecream.ca/

Prices are SUPER reasonable - I think it was $3.50 for one scoop or $5.75 for two.  They offer house made waffle cones, waffle bowls, and toppings!  Though, the stuff is soooooo good - who needs toppings?  

We opted for Gelato goodness - a chocolate hazelnut and amaretto in one bowl and lime and raspberry sorbet in our other bowl - MMM... Good!  

And then we picked up 2 pints of sorbet to go for only $6.50 each - and if you know your real sorbet, that is a STEAL of a deal!  They offer larger sizes for $9.75 I think - next time, we will save even more $$$ and just get the giant ones to go!

We opted for lemon thyme and raspberry tarragon.  Not your average run of the mill flavours - a treat that is for sure!  Pinnochio's ice cream makes their treats custom made for local restaurants and these funky flavours are recently made for Blue Pear if I remember correctly and that is why they are so funky!  Gepetto's Gelato orders extras for their customers since Pinnochio's is already doing up the custom batches for the restaurants.

There was also a cucumber mint in addition to all the normal sorbet flavours in the freezer - lemon, blueberry, raspberry... Mmm... My mouth is watering at just thinking about it.  

I can't wait to go back and try some more!

I uploaded pics - Check them out!

PS - Oops... I forgot to mention that the staff were super nice, too!

The place is one of those premium priced burger joints. A buck for cheese , $7 for a 5 oz burger and $4 for fries. A med chocolate shake was $5. 

Shake was nice and thick but not that heavily chocolate flavoured. Burger and bun were excellent. Good crust on the burger from the flat top and a nice beefy flavour. Bun was fresh and flavourful. Ketchup and vinegar on the table along with salt and pepper. 

I did not like the fries. They are double  dunked and crisp but they are the peel on type and most of the plate had absorbed so much grease they were dark colored and unpleasant to eat. 

I would have a burger here  again but I would stick to water or a soda to go with it and I would never do the fries again.

I am impressed with the consistently great food and service here. Even when they are swamped and people are fighting for seats, the staff stay friendly and food is great. They don't cut corners just because they're busy. On top of that they remember my name every time!

Try the burger of the day for something new. I get it almost every time I'm here and have not ever been disappointed. They're always trying out new cool toppings you won't find anywhere else. 

Keep up the fantastic work!
The sandwiches were not bad. The creme brûlée was horrible. The sugar crust was completely charred in some places and raw in others.

This was my first visit so I thought I would try their special of the day.   A hamburger with burnt ends, a spicy cheesy spread (not really that spicy), barbecue sauce and lettuce.   Ordered up a poutine (fries topped with cheese curds and gravy), and a shake "Malteaser" -basically a vanilla shake with some chocolate malt balls on top.  (The shake was a bit thin, so-so)

All in all, however, very good.  Order at counter and sit down type service.  Friendly place for a quick bite.

Another amazing bakery/cafe in Edmonton. Recently expanded and renovated with a warm earthy, cottage feel, there's now more seating, larger selection of goods and you can also order a "build your own cake". Always fresh, amazing quality. Mini scones are the best, sausage rolls, cake bites, salads, tarts and pretty much everything is fab!

The white chocolate raspberry scone is amazing but haven't really enjoyed much of anything else. The cinnamon buns are dry, the breakfast sandwiches use some sort of crazy egg mixture, and the panini is a loaf of bread with a sprinkle of stuff in the middle. This place could be great it's just missing a little in the execution of a few things.

Jack's burger shack is literally in the corner of a building it's tiny you have to wait in line and it is not fancy, but they have amazing burgers and that is the reason why people lineup for them. my personal favorite is the shroom burger. Tender morsels of mushrooms sautéed in something amazing then topped with creamy Boursin cheese. The Patty is simple has a great crust on it and a bun is soft and fluffy if you dare add a side of fries and a milkshake to it you'll think you have gone to heaven. I highly recommend this place

Update: went back twice since my last review. The second time we went the shop wasn't open even though it was within the times posted on their website. You might want to phone first if you're coming from any distance. The third time we went their soft serve machine had gone out for servicing and would be gone for a week...disappointing.

I don't like coffee and I generally don't like cafes.

So for me to like a place like this says something.

My girlfriend loves to come here, so I end up going more often than I would just by myself, but it's still pretty good!

As I said, I don't really like coffee, so I can't tell you about that.   What I CAN tell you about is the service- everyone who works there seems friendly and attentive.  The pastries tend to be hit-and-miss.  Some of them are DELICIOUS, like eat 10 of them in a row delicious.  Some pastries are crusty and don't really taste like anything...

The trick is that they all LOOK good.  So you can't judge the food here by how it looks, at least not in my experience.

For example, they have this raspberry jam and white chocolate cup thing (my list of words for baked goods ends at 'bread', so bear with me here...) that's ultra-yum-licious, but they also have some tasty looking banana bread that ends up being something akin to eating banana-flavoured crumbly sandstone with nuts in it.

So you gotta experiment a bit.

The hot chocolate /w vanilla and chili is what I get all winter, and it's a failsafe recipe for instant warmth and tastiness.

There are a couple complaints about this place though:
First, the way they've set up the counter is.. interesting.  follow the (not-so-visible) signs and you'll find where you need to go
Second, there are no plug-ins anywhere.  I suspect this is on purpose, so they don't get people parking themselves somewhere for hours on end.
Last, it's hard to tell how much you're going to be paying for something.  Price tags are hard to find!

Overall, this place ain't bad, as long as you already know what to get, how much it is, and where to line up to pay.

Ken says 5 stars! It was busy but the food was fresh and came out fast. Te five year old ate a whole burger and that never happens. We tried the Shroom burger (standard with Boursin and mushrooms) and the Hangover (beef party, pickles, ketchup and mustard between 2 grilled cheese buns) and the poutine. Immediately followed by working out double afterwards, but it was soooo worth it! Would drive out here for a burger again!!!
We'll have to try the Nutella milkshake next time ;)
Mmmmm so good!
Yum yum yum! Always so good and everything on the menu is on my try list! Most imaginative menu I have seen ever, and delicious too! :)  Thanks Jacks Burger Shack!

When we moved to St. Albert we were really excited to discover a Vietnamese restaurant in our neighborhood! 

We gave it a try the first week after moving and were unfortunately disappointed.  The prices were high and the food lacked flavor.

Whever fish sauce comes to the table unseasoned... I generally take it as a bad omen for the rest of the meal... and this held to be true.

We had two different vermicelli entrees with grilled meats, spring rolls, and an appetizer of salad rolls (even the peanut sauce was bland...)

I've been going to Wild Earth for probably 3+ years now.  Like Gord L., I'm not a coffee-drinker, so I don't go there for that.  However, I'm told (by reliable sources), that their coffee is quite good.

The ambiance of this large coffee shop is wonderful.  Lots of comfy seating, nooks and crannies make it quite a nice spot for a chat or a quick bite.

To me, however, Wild Earth is more a bakery than a coffee shop.  I can't say as I've tried everything there, but I've tried a good chunk.  As others have said, their wraps, sandwiches and salads are quite good.  But it's their baking that sets them apart.  My perennial favourites are the Raspberry-White Chocolate scones and their cinnamon buns.

I love their cinnamon buns and they seem to have something for everybody.  Whole wheat or white dough, raisins or not.  The dough is wonderfully flavored and the buns themselves have a great, up-front cinnamon flavour.  They way they bake them turns some of the cinnamon, raisin, butter and sugar mixture into a toffee like consistency.  Love it.

The only knock I have on Wild Earth is the service.  Sometimes I find the staff to be a little short or disinterested.  This could be a factor of being understaffed or just tired.  Not sure.... 

Overall, though, if you're looking for a nice place to have a quick snack, coffee or chat, this is one of the best in Edmonton!  Check it out!

Wild Earth Cafe and Bakery is a Millcreek institution. However, you don't have to live in Millcreek to enjoy it. 

Situated on 99th Street and easily accessible by bus it's centrally located between Whyte, downtown and the always wonderful Saskatchewan Drive. 

I particularly enjoy the Bacon Sunrise sandwiches but you'd be hard-pressed to find something that wasn't extremely agreeable. They have a massive selection of extremely delicious baked goods. I'm a fan of the carrot cake but you could come here every day never exhaust their menu. 

I don't drink the stuff but I'm told the coffee is delicious. They also have compostable, bio-degradable to-go packaging, something that always score a few brownie points from me. 

They've just undergone a recent renovation which has added a lot more seat space space both and room for the kitcken/bakery as well. I'm not the biggest fan of the decor, it feels very showhomey, but this is my go-to spot for warm drinks within walking distance of my house. 

If you're close by, driving by or biking by you should probably check it out.

We recently moved, and I was very fondly attached to a family owned cafe in my old neighborhood. Wild Earth is now my closest cafe, so I went in the other day to scope it out.

First of all, it's pretty big- which means lots of seating and you're probably more likely to get a table. Windows everywhere, lots of natural light. Gotta love that.

The staff member who helped me was new at his job, and was enthusiastic, friendly, and immensely helpful. I wanted a tea and he knew everything about all their available tea. My jasmine tea ended up being super delicious. 

They also have a huge spread of bakery treats!! I didn't try anything this visit, but next time I plan to pull up at a table with a coffee and one of those amazing looking treats. Looking forward to this being my new haunt!

The service leaves a bit to be desired.  Staff can't answer any questions because they are just there to pump out pre-packaged foods and overpriced cakes.  
The special brew coffee that my friend ordered had been sitting in the earn for a while.  He assumed that he was getting a fresh cup of coffee.   My tea was fine, but my cup had a large chip on the rim.  Not cool.
I like the music and the seating.  In warmer months, you can sit outside.  There is plenty to read and it's clean and spacious. 
I like it better than chains like Starbucks. The hours are decent.

A very bohemian atmosphere with reasonably priced, light food such as sandwiches, wraps, and baked goods of all kinds. The displays looked absolutely delicious. I just stopped in to grab a coffee - the medium roast was excellent. I saw lattes being prepared, with art on top (this always impresses me). I definitely want to come back to try a treat and maybe have a latte.
Great tasting burger and fries. Friendly staff. Only thing that could be improved is the bun. They need to stand up better especially if you do take away.

I came here for a good friends concert just yesterday and was really impressed. It had a great atmosphere. I had a grapefruit drink from their fridge, skipping the small portions of coffee, and a turkey panini. The sandwich was the most I've ever spent on a sandwich (almost $8), however it was the best I've ever had too. Absolutely delicious and if I had the money I'd be going back often for more. However Im a college student, so I don't see myself going back here unless my friend plays again.

Our family loves this little place. Last time we came there was a very nice girl working who explained the Gelato has no additives, explained how the sizes worked and was very patient with my kids while making their big decision. Tonight however a different girl was not friendly, not patient and scolded my kids to stay out of the open door that is ajoined to the ice cream place. They were just peeking as they were curious what was in there. She then actually "shushed" my daughter who is 4 and was excited and overwhelmed with all the ice cream flavours. She then snatched the money out of our hands and couldn't smile to save her life. I get kid's can be loud and annoying but when applying for such a position you must know you will be dealing with little ones. Customer Service is key and over at Midtown Apothecary the owner is super friendly and patient with my kid's as they decide. That goes a long way. Will try again and hopefully she cheers up. Maybe close the door to the hair salon next door which was closed and youwon't have little curious kids peeking.

I LOVE the food at Wild Earth however, like many other reviews I find the service lacking.  If this place had better service I would definitely give it 5 stars.  The latte's and beverages here are amazing as well as the food.  The breakfast sandwiches are delicious and Fresh.  I also love that they have a vegetarian soup option daily and veggie chilli.  If you make a trip make sure you order a scone as they are unfreaking believable.

I've been driving by this café a lot lately and because I've heard such good things about this place I decided to go in and check it out.  Right of the bat I loved the atmosphere; they have some nice seating by the windows and they have this one really nice wooden table with nice wooden chairs.  That just happens to be the one spot everyone wants, so get there early to claim it.  The place was pretty busy when I went in; there really weren't any more places to sit but I was lucky that one opened up by the time my latte was ready.  My friends come in to this place all the time and they told me to try one of their tarts; well I have to say the apple and raspberry butter tart they have are really good!  They have a few to choose from if you don't like apple or raspberry.  They also have a lot of other yummy items to taste.  They have a couple different kinds of banana bread; one with just walnuts and the other with walnuts and chocolate chips.  They have cakes and different kinds of bars; they have this one chocolate overdose bar that is really thick and looks so yummy; that's a good item to share with someone.
