Their lattes are really good and I've heard magical things about their hot chocolate so that's the next thing I want to try.  I also want to check out some of their good items.  They have yummy sandwiches and other great things too much on.  They also have a couple of salads to choose from.   

And the best thing about this place is that they café for planet earth so they use nothing but bridgeable coffee cups!  Oh, if you happen to be an artist or a photographer you could sell some of your work from their store; I'm not sure how you would go about doing this but I'm sure the staff members would be able to fill you in.

This is by the far best place I've gotten a burger in a very long time. Everything is delicious there. The inferno burger is my favourite and their pountine is to die for. I've only had a taste of the milkshakes but they sound amazing. The service is excellent and even when they are busy they make sure the tables are clean and your food comes as quickly as possible.

I only stop by to make some photocopies and I was surprise of the expensive prices they have $1 per copy black and white, color was $2 per copy (while you can find the same service for $.15 B/W) Using a computer connected to a scanner was $18 per hour or $.30 per minute, An easy and fast way to rip people, for sure I wont stop by that business anytime soon.

I love the food at this restaurant. I don't eat in I take out. I practically eat the food every other weekend and does not dissapoint always hot and tasty. This place has been around a long time and been my only chinese goto.

Do you need a birthday cake? From Wild Earth, yes you do!! :) My favourite, and IMO, best cafe in Edmonton. Fresh food galore!! Delectable baked cakes - moist and decadent!  Espressso deep and rich. Baristas wonderful morning people. Brightly lit, soft music. A place you can write a novel or catch up with  a friend, or indulge in a perfect croissant.

Bring your hotspot if you'd like to catch up on the laptop. This is a wonderful place for people who actually read the morning newspaper or a new novel.

My friend ordered 2 cakes from here for her husbands birthday. One was vanilla with strawberry filing, and the other was chocolate with peanut butter filing. Both cakes were extremely dry and not even worth the calories of my first and only bites. Cake should be moist, not bone dry.

If you enjoy fresh homemade treats this is the place for you.  My favorites are the cinnamon buns, you can choose from plain or whole wheat and with or without raisins!  The scones are on my list to try....lemon squares are yummy.  Cakes are a bit hit and miss I have ordered a couple and they can be on the dry side.  I love the London fog varieties for drinks and my go to is the Mathca latte.  You will have to wait a little longer as they prepare your delicious treats and it is usually busy but the wait is worth it.  You will also pay a little more my latte is over $6.  Staff is usually friendly but sometimes indifferent.

First time here, but I've heard all about it.  Good flat pressed burgers, about a 1/2 inch thick.  A few options for burgers, milkshakes and fries.  Food comes out fast and the service was really really friendly.  
Fries were piping hot and delish, and the burger was good and fresh,  not the best ive had, but good.  (I had a standard cheeseburger). 

My only gripes would be that I wished they had more Jacks sauce on the burger and they used something other than iceberg lettuce as if it's not fresh its resulting metallic taste can really affect the rest of whatever it's on.

My now husband and I ordered the Queen Bee cake just because we needed something for the cake cutting. Thankfully the cake was only $30 because I was under the impression when my order was confirmed after I input my Visa information that my card would have been charged accordingly but was not. When the cake was picked up, the person doing so had to pay. No big deal. I just wish it had been outlined because I told the person the order was paid for already. My biggest complaint was that the wrong cake had been prepared for us and I kind of wonder if they made the one we ended up getting last minute in the back because it did NOT look like the cake online. There was next to NO burnt honey on the top and this was a major reason for choosing this cake because it went with our fall colours. The head table and family loved the cake, although it was nothing what I expected, so at least everyone else was satisfied.

The chickpea patty was incredible!  I never typically enjoy anything with chickpeas but it was outstanding and they let me sub the patty on whichever burger I wanted. The fries are also fantastic. It was busy on Canada Day but the service was fast and friendly.

Amazing Food!

When we found Jack's 2 years ago, I fell in love with the place.
The staff, the owners believe in great tasting food and great service!

If you haven't had a chance to make your way down, try it today!
Great food .... and service, the ginger chicken is the best I've ever had.... quality food and no msg....

The only time I'd wait in a line for 15 minutes for a burger an not complain. A St Albert institution that makes amazing fresh daily burgers... Hang out with all the locals and enjoy a relaxed, casual freshly homemade burger.

You will be back

I'm not a coffee drinker, so my trips to Wild Earth Bakery are focused on the sweet stuff... their wonderful squares, or other delicious delicacies.

Things I like from Wild Earth include: anything with chocolate, their sausage rolls, their wraps, the decor, and the service. It's a place I need to visit more often, the location just isn't convenient to walk to (I don't pass it while walking somewhere else, I have to walk to it specifically).

My only complaint would be that some of the prices seem a little bit high for what you get.

Well after boycotting this place for awhile ....Because it is so close to my house I caved and decided to give it one more shot.  Big mistake....same problems as before the boycott...disconnected staff that for the most part don't care....there must be huge staff turnover as I never see the same face twice...and they run out of baking by noon...how do they keep the doors open after noon if they don't have fresh baking available? ...and is it really fresh? Is it really a bakery? The date square I had to opt for, because there was nothing else, was hard and dried out and prices are just ridiculous. Dinner hour is no better, often running out of food or replying irritably that they "could" dig it out and microwave it. Don't stay open til 9 if you are packing up at 7:30

This is probably my favourite place for a moccacino. Like most places there are several options of milk to craft the concoction. Unlike a lot of places Wild Earth has the option of almond milk which when mixed with the chocolate creates this nutty-choco taste that keeps me coming back.

It is also surprisingly spacious. With table and bench seating throughout. Great treats as well to go with superb drinks. 

I also enjoy the questions of the day. Apparently, Finland is the country that has the most islands in the world. Go figure!

You know what I love about Sobeys?  You don't need a stupid card for sale prices.  Yes, you need a card to collect points but not for sales.

Also, they have super cute little shopping carts for your toddler to push!  Just beware of your ankles a d those around you as the cart is metal ;-)

Reviewing a lookup restaurant, c'mon I can't be serious. Well, actually I am.

First, what the heck is a lookup restaurant? This is the type of restaurant that when you walk in, you have to stand in line and look up to see the menu.

Now, back to McDonalds. This isn'tnecessarily specific to this location, it is a one size fits all kind of comment.

They have really decent coffee! Now there are a lot of coffee snobs out there who won't agree, but if all you want is a decent cup of coffee and maybe a breakfast sandwich to go with it, McDonalds should be a place to consider.

I am all for the coffee house, but don't overlook some of our other slightly less obvious options.
Reduced portion sizes five times in two years. Using cheaper ingredients. Trying to be upscale but falling down on the basics. Fail.

This store works hard to lose my business.  I needed a photo ink cartridge for my HP printer.  Sales associated insisted that 'this one' was the right one even though it didn't say photo anywhere.   Got it home, nope this is the black ink not black photo.  It's going back and an hour of my day wasted. Hello Costco.

I don't think I could ever say enough good things about this bakery. I've used them several times so I decided to go with them for my wedding. They were so amazing about our allergy concerns (eggs, gluten), and the cakes were out of this world amazing.

Greta put up with my crazy mind-changing ways for a good year and never took the smile off her face. Thank you so much

What a great place! Had lunch there today and was very pleasantly surprised. I usually end up eating only half my burger but ate the whole thing today.  I really like how the patties are thinner than usual.  I like my patty well done and it was perfect. The buns were so soft they were almost like a croissant.  So good!  My friends loved theirs as well. The fries were really good too  The staff were friendly and cleared our table up when we were done. They also serve Pepsi which is my choice over coke. So I was very happy with that. We will definitely eat here again.  Thanks!

I like the atmosphere and vegan options they have here, just wish they had more. It's cozy, has a fireplace, and comfy chairs to sit in while enjoying the varied menu. 
The staff are generally friendly, really no complaints. :-)

Ok it's time for a re-yelp. Now I know that I have professed my distaste for yucky coffee and my interpretation of bad service about Wild Earth in my previous yelp, I feel the need to clear the air because there seem to have been some recent changes.

1.The beans. Recently Wild earth changed their coffee beans and even the decaf Americano is to die for. Yes, the coffee has gone from awful to amazing. Thanks WE!

2. In the past I expressed disappointment about the unappreciative service. Well, not sure if it's the end of 99 ST construction nearing or the new coffee beans but my local barristas and the owner of WE have been very polite and even chatty. It's appreciated because I like to feel that my regular business and hard earned dollars are going to a good place with nice people. 

I take it back. Re-Yelp! WE is a decent place and it's the only place to go for a good coffee in Mill Creek. Try the Thai wrap grilled too, it's delish!

Stopped in for a quick lunch and so glad I did! The line was to the door but moved super quick and the staff is on top of getting recently vacated seats cleaned off and ready again. 

Since it's my first time here is thought I'd start with the basics - the "standard" burger with bacon, side of poutine, and a coke. The burger was fantastic, just the right amount if salt, super tender, and the gun was so fresh I looked around for the bread oven! The bacon was generous and crispy enough that it didn't all pull out if the burger on the first bite but not overdone. 

The poutine was great too. The fries most definitely hand cut and brown and crispy (no white soggy shoestrings here!) the gravy had great flavor and just enough not to drown the fries. The cheese curds were good but not "squeaky". I'll have this again -  maybe even for dinner!

So much for the weight loss plan, Jacks is only 5 minutes from work!

Definitely a step up from Tim Hortons, I ordered an iced chai latte and a peanut butter rice crispy roll and they were both delicious. Also grabbed a Nanaimo square and chocolate banana loaf to go. The base was pretty dry and sadly not that great. My SO loved the banana bread, said it was wicked.

Bottom line, good place to stop for a drink. Just not that big of a fan of the treats.

I was there a few days ago, they couldnt make fries for some reason
I ordered a single burger and patty waspretty thin
Tasty though

Located on the south side of Edmonton.  A hangout for the yuppy crowd with their lattes and muffins.  Nice neighbourhood atmosphere with brick and nooks and stools to see the street and leather chairs. Popular place and they have live music on Fridays.  Food wise I have had no luck with their muffins or cinnamon buns or scones as I found them fatty and or tasteless. But I do love their banana pecan and lemon seed loaves.  Their soup was good but chili was  only big chunks of hamburger and a can of mixed beans, very blah.  Sandwiches and bread are fine.  I don't think they taste their own food.

I like Wild Earth.

I like the location of it and I like the atmosphere.  I don't like how busy it can get.  There have been a couple times where I have gone in and there were no tables available.  I guess that's inevitable though.

These guys have pretty decent coffee and the definitely have some tasty treats.  The baking always seems pretty fresh which is why it is always good.

The prices are typical for a coffee shop these days. 

It's a nice place.  If you haven't been, give it a shot!

Open 24 hours, basically a normal McDonald's, staff is mostly young kids/adults. 
But I'm a huge fan of the $1 drink special they have on now!
Way over priced that is why the 2  star rating ! Pictures will follow after food is served !

Wild earth has to be my favorite cafe shop in the whyte ave area.. As long as my favorite spot tucked in the back is open! I have enjoyed their cappuccinos as well as some of their teas. The baristas allowed me to smell each of the teas until I found one I enjoyed. I have always had great service with very pleasant staff here... Though I do wish they stayed open until 10.

When I go to St. Albert and I have any amount of time, I'm going to Jack's burger shack. 
I love all there burgers but my favourite is the Shroom burger it has that herb and garlic Boursin cheese on it and it's like Daaaaaaaang good! 
I really enjoy their shakes a lot! They have a cola shake, it's great! Oh yes and they have a malt vinegar aioli that comes with their fries! It's delicious! My one suggestion is to get maybe one fries for two ppl because they're pretty big. They only reason they don't get a 5 out of 5 is because they sometimes don't have enough seats but what are they gonna do? It's a busy place!

My reviews are usually short so the burgars
We had were good flavour thin patty  though but alright , the bun was super fresh , fries and the dip we had was real good  ( fries similar to new york fries we also had a lettuce Wrap with chicken ( it was a very small piece of meat but good taste , milk shake there was thick 
Good taste and would order again they also had some neat flavours seating was limited 
Due to it is not a huge location and it is tucked in a bit off main street. Pricing for three burgers 2 fries and threes drinks pop and shake was forty i guess next time i would order a double patty but overall it was 
All good

Wifi never works for anyone Doesnt Let You Sign In 
Both St.Albert locations  aside from that 
Regular mcdonalds

Decided to head to Jack's, they don't have skip the dishes or deliver ,so I took a drive to see what all the fuss was about... Staff were extremely friendly and service was very fast.. Which I can truly appreciate : )

The food was amazing with the real beef pattys, with a homemade taste!! I was hoping for a mountain of toppings and was not dissapointed nor blown away..

My gf and I decided to get some take out to give us a break from cooking. We ordered two double burgers  (we're of average size people lol), 2 poutines, 1 milkshake  

Total = $51.00 GST incld. 

It's probably the hallmark of burgers if your gonna decide on burgers. So be prepared to pay, they don't combo anything. So for fries and a drink with a 2nd beef patty, look at hovering around the $25 Mark/person. St. Albert Perron street tho , who am I to complain!!!

Great food, great people, highly recommended. Had an Italian Stallion, an espresso shake with biscotti bits on top. Don't remember what burger I had, but it was spectacular as well.

Why are you still reading this? Get over there!

I love the selection of pastries and loose leaf teas available at Wild Earth. Their scones and muffins are delicious, and their daily soup creations are usually amazing. 

The only gripe I really have with Wild Earth is that their cafe can be quiet messy, and the staff can be inconsistent with service. I've gone in and had the baristas make me the best Americano I've had in a long time, but I have also gone in and had the staff be extremely snotty and rude to me. 

A little more consistency and customer service, and I'll be an extremely satisfied customer! 

Keep it up guys, you're on your way to being  awesome!!

have made the trip to jacks a couple times, and every time is worth the drive out of edmonton!! Amazing food and amazing service!!! Hands down the best burger i have ever eaten!!! 

The last time I was there was near the end of the day, enjoyed an amazing burger, then went next door to the lounge for some cocktails to end the night! Definitely a great way to finish off the meal was with a nice cocktail.

While Jack's Burger Shack offers both good food and good service, it's seriously overpriced.  If the items served there were one-third less expensive across the board, then it would represent good value for money.  I'm unlikely to return until the value proposition improves.

this place I can go on and on about.

I always have the one with peanut butter. and the pontine is also fantastic. I'm
not a burger person at all but these ones are to die for! so good. best burger I've ever had!
Best burgers in town friendly staff prompt service definitely a must when you have time to visit St. Albert

I've been to burger joints all over this fair continent. And I can say without a shred of hyperbole that Jack's is the Perfect Burger.
Now, may other burger places have fancier toppings, or more options, or bigger patties, or or or. But Jack's doesn't concern itself with such frivolity. 
The standard burger is anything but - each piece is perfection in and of itself. The bun is soft but sturdy, and just the right size for the patty. The patty is seasoned just so - and not too big or too tiny. The veggies are fresh, and somehow the tomato is always JUST the right thickness.
This is Michelangelo's David if ol' Mike made burgers. Make a trip today.

Legitimately the best hamburger I've ever had! The bun did get a little soggy and messy but over all the quality of the meat was perfect. I got the standard burger with LTO and Jack Sauce and the guests I came with got the Barbecue Crunch burger. All of us were very satisfied. The poutine was similarly excellent. I'd recommend this place to anybody visiting St Albert! Reasonable prices as well!

I love this gem of a cafe!  When I moved to the neighbourhood and saw Wild Earth on the corner I knew I was going to love living here and I was right!  I've been frequenting the cafe for over three years and love that it is such a vibrant gathering place that really enhances the sense of community in the neighbourhood.  The baked treats are sinfully good and the selection of snacks, soups and sandwiches are always top-notch.  I, myself, am addicted to their ginger cookies, and I'm also a fan of the matcha lattes as well!

I'm feeling a little nostalgic as I write this post since we don't live in Edmonton or St. Albert anymore. But, all our happy birthdays were celebrated with a delicious and beautifully catered GLUTEN FREE cake. However, if you are super allergic to wheat, this is not the place for you. I have a mild wheat sensitivity and, in general don't eat bread, etc. made with wheat flour. They can't guarantee that the cake is free of wheat since their facility primarily bakes standard cakes. 

What I do love about this place is the cozy, wood-burning fireplace at this location. When we moved to St. Albert, we had our cakes ordered here and delivered to that location. We were excited when another one opened at the zoo (a place we frequented often with our little girls). However, the food itself or lack there of at the time left us a little dismayed. I'm sure things are different now since it's opening.

It seems like everybody in St. Albert knows everybody. Thus, they've known about Jack's for awhile now. There really isn't much i can add here ... maybe some profanity for emphasis? We made Jack's our burger quest episode 6 so expectations were high. And I have to say they cleared the hurdle with room to spare. 

I had the shroom burger (not magic) for 7$ and the Darth Vader shake (vanilla and coke) for 5$. I also shared some fries. Everything was stellar! Shrooms were fried well. Patty was tasty and juicy. Darth Vader made me want to join the dark side (assuming it tastes that good). Fries were nice and crispy. 

The reputation did not disappoint, but what I didn't expect is the atmosphere! It really feels like a part of the community. Kids running around all over the place. Grandma and granddaughter out for lunch. Love the outdoor tables in the sun. I felt like a lizard basking in the sun, soaking up those June prairie rays! 

Nothing really left to say here except that this place is effing great! I look forward to my next trip to St. Albert.

Love their chai latte. Never fails me. Creamy, tasty, yummy. Almond milk and they can still create some foam for me. Tickles me to my toes. 
And yes, I concur their pumpkin white chocolate or raspberry white chocolate scones are brilliant - they sold out just as I was paying so I got a raspberry white chocolate tartlet. OMG. 
Hello little sweetie, where you been hiding? 
No better way to warm up on this cool, grey fall day.

I stopped into the Wild Earth Bakery one day by accident when the line-up at Route 99 was too long for my liking. I needed something fast to quell my mood-debilitating hunger, and I lucked out here at Wild Earth, where the make a quick, mean egg, ham and cheese sammy for under $4, cooked on a fresh bun to boot! Impressive. I'd kinda been avoiding this place because I find the "Wild Earth" name somewhat misleading. It's next door to the Wild Earth Food store, yet another grocery outfit that's pretending to be all enviro and earthy, when it's just a gimmick to get people in the door. At the bakery they're "striving" to be organic - but they're not. That's not to say that they don't make delicious baked goods: cinnamon buns, raspberry & white chocolate scones, butter tarts and more. If they've got something good, why do they have to do it under the pretext of something else, which they're not?!
DO NOT EVER EAT HERE!  The food was beyond disgusting, and service was even worse.

Yummy!  Came back to Jack's burger shack with a group of fabulous Yelpers for Arc's fabulous Burger Quest!

The All Shook Up Burger was DELISH with peanut butter and bacon!  I think a dollop of grape jelly on it would take it to the next level!

LOVED the garlic aioli with the fries... Oh. Em. Gee.  Get in your car RIGHT now to go have their fries!

And the milkshakes today were perfection! Clearly my first visit was a fluke - they totally hit the spot this time! And to their credit, my first visit was during their infancy.  I highly recommend both the Darth Vader & Creamsicle!

Mad props for Jack's sourcing lots of local and only using the Best of the Best!

Looking forward to their expansion opening up into the space next door!

Jack's, you've made a fan out of me :-)

PS - Cutest takeout/leftover bags ever!

I'm not a huge fan of Staples, I find it very over priced. They have a great selection of office/school supplies but they are definitely limited when it comes to other things. Like any big department store finding staff to help you is impossible. I'll continue to go to Staples just out of convenience but it's not my fav.

We came here for the first time a couple weeks ago -

The food was fantastic. Service was quick - and to our surprise, they had a very delightful selection of milkshakes. (We tried the Cinnamon Toast Crunch and it was a delicious treat!) 

I had the Inferno burger, and my boyfriend had the BBQ Crunch. Both were great - I would definitely order the same thing next time!

Hands down the BEST burger I have ever had in my life! Nothing even comes close! I need to stop coming to this place because it is happening way too often. The poutine is amazing, definitely too much for one person so consider sharing. My favourite burger that I've had so far is the BBQ Crunch but the Inferno comes in as a close second. Depends if you're in the mood for something spicy because it's loaded with jalapenos. Would definitely recommend checking this place out asap!

I love coming here on my spare time. It's clean and everyone that works here are so friendly. 
I highly recommend this place to everyone because they allow all ages  under one building to have fun. Whether it be working out or just for leisure.

What a delicious burger! I am seriously not a burger lover any means, but the mushroom burger was VERY good. The bun was fresh, and the hamburger was so most and fresh! It was nIce to see the fresh burgers grilled right before my eyes. I don't know where the beef comes from, but it's definitely fresh. 

The milkshake definitely brings all the boys to the yard. Or maybe the burgers get the boys there, but the milkshake is actually what brought me there and it was amazing. I had the nutella flavor. Liquid nutella. Mmmmmmmmmm.

I've always loved the food, desserts, and the coffee here. I also appreciate the fair trade aspect and the fact that Wild Earth is a good employer, from what I hear. 

My complaint comes from the lack of wi-fi - either the owners are such hippies that they're wearing tin foil hats (and probably don't vaccinate) or they're too cheap to pay for it. In my mind, coffee = productivity, and I would get so much work done here (especially late Friday nights) if they would just provide that one service to their customers. 

Sorry to say I would have been a loyal customer of Wild Earth all winter long, but this is a deal breaker.

Not many coffee shops were open at 8:30am on a Sunday, so we decided to grab some breakfast to go. 

The food and drinks were great! Everything was hot and tasted fresh. Now we know where to go when we're looking for something to snack on or have as a meal!

Best little burger shack. 
If you love a good burger - you should check this place out!  Not a lot of space inside and the line ups can get pretty big.  Not the place to go for a quiet sit down meal.

Our little Jack's fan loved his Grill'd Cheese and fries. My wife and I had the BBQ Crunch burgers which were delicious. Nothing beats putting potato chips on a burger. The fries were great. The price was reasonable. We would come here again when in St. Albert.

WHY HAVE I NEVER VISITED THIS PLACE BEFORE! This amazing cafe/bakery is in my hood. Last night, my PR gang suggested coffee at Wild Earth. I arrived early to get some reading time in. As soon as I entered I was blown away. This cafe is huge first of all. Secondly, it has this small mountain community feel to it. I felt like I was in Jasper or Banff.

I ordered a double chai soy latte. It was amazing. I then waited for my friends to arrive before I ordered a little something something to nibble on!

The choices were vast! There was lines of jars with yummy cookies. There were tortes, butter cups and even puddings in small jars that you could take home. There is of course a plethora of loaves that you can take home from bread to zucchini, chocolate chip, pecan loaf. If you want something more to fill your tummy there is soup and sandwiches as well!

I opted for the peanut butter chocolate cookie. It was glorious! The seating is vast. There is even prepared baking and cooking that you can take home and finish it off yourself: soups, cookies, cinnamon buns. 

I highly recommend this cafe for breakfast, lunch, dinner, a place to grab a coffee or tea and chat or to pick up some bread for the week.

I left with a beautiful loaf of banana walnut bread! YUM! You HAVE to go! Support local and healthy!
Ate here a couple of years ago and it was great. This time not so much. Food was disappointing and was not warm when it was delivered. Quality was mediocre at best. Would not recommend.

Reaffirmed what I believed to be the my favourite place for a burger and shake. Had the hangover (9$) and compared it to the Vatican (11$+) at Burgers priest. Essentially both have a grilled cheese bun. And although the Vatican has two patties and is a very good burger, the patty is just better at Jacks. Ultimately, this is still the my favourite place for burgers.

The darth vader shake was as delicious as ever. Not mention the atmosphere is very chill suburbia. And I like that!

I wish Jack's was in downtown Edmonton, but perhaps for my wallet it is best that it isn't. :)

flavor=10 $=8 service=9  atmosphere=10 menu=10
avg=9.4

so far the only 5-star place to me.  they got a mad amount
of sweets and bread and i never get tired of this variety.
coffee is always bold and great flavor. the cakes.....vanilla
bean chai was delicious i remember. seems slightly expensive
but when you start eating it you feel its size...and it is huge.
fell in love with their jalapeno cheddar bread too!

atmosphere, seating, and music is very relaxing. service
is friendly. a lovely mini vacation to me.

thanks wild earth and please keep it up!
(slightly worried about the owner's attitude according
to another person's review though.....)

Fairly decent Vietnamese place. Not spectacular, but better than I expected for St. Albert. Outside of Vietnam itself, all of my experience with Viet food has been Vancouver and Toronto, so considering I'm spoiled this little place fared me well. My only complaint is that they serve Chinese style spring rolls, not the Viet rolls made with rice paper. I can't stand the flour style rolls. Only about 50% of restaurants serve the right ones, so I can't  criticize too much. All in all, a pretty good spot.

Round eyes in Edmonton desperately need to try good Chinese food so they can identify it when it is served to them!  Lord knows that the Lingnan Express does not offer it.  I know now to avoid its sister establishments, the Lingnan and Chicken for Lunch.  Do yourselves a favour, folks, and take a pass on this over-hyped, over-rated establishment.

This little gem is really hard to get to on a Saturday afternoon when the Farmer's Market is in full swing, but I assure you it is worth the extra effort to find the parking spot! 

Lunch ends at 2:30pm so make sure you get your order in by then.  They are closed between 2:30 and 4.  

This is a cafe style venue where the menu is on the chalkboard overhead.  You put in your order, pay for your meal and someone will deliver it for you.  They have a patio setup just outside the door so you can enjoy your meal outdoors if the weather permits.  

The "All Shook Up" has quickly become my favourite Peanut Butter and Bacon burger in the Edmonton area.  I don't know what they put in the "sauce" but it is delicious.  The buns they use are fantastic as well.

Sides are separate.  Their fries are fantastic served with the malt vinegar aioli.  

The "Creamsicle" milk shake is a lovely way to end your meal with Jack's.  They have several flavours to choose from.

I was looking for a place where I can buy decent gluten-free bakings in the city, and my mother-in-law recommended this place. I have tried their gluten-free cakes, which you can pick and chose what you want in your cake, and they were great. You cannot really tell the cake is gluten-free; the cake does not taste like cardboard and its texture is soft and moist. I would go back to the bakery when I would like gluten-free bakings in the future.

Great burgers here.  Really like the small diner feel.  But now that the secret is out, time to expand and get a second flat top for quicker turnaround.  Because 30 minutes to wait for a burger might be pushing it.
The meat tastes fresh and has great ( as Guy Fieri would put it ) "crustification"...that is why I usually do 2 patties in my burgers.  When I do, definitely do not need fries.  All good so far : cobb ( blue cheese sauce ), bbq crunch ( chips & orange soda bbq sauce ), shroom ( boursin sauce ).  
Buns are fresh & soft.  
Good meat & good buns, sounds like food porn.

For the record, I've never actually been to Jack's Burger Shack.

But their food truck parks outside my workplace once a month or so and let's just say it's the best burger in town. I keep a calendar of food truck dates at my desk and make sure to never miss a Jacks day.

Their burgers are thin but large, and are very juicy and flavorful. Their buns are huge and have that perfect level of 'squidge'. And their toppings are just perfect. I also really recommend trying the option with a boursin cheese/mushroom topping. So flavorful and indulgent.

One of these days I'll make the pilgrimage into St Albert to try the real deal at their shop, where they seem to have a few more flavors.

I am still have taste flashbacks (in a bad way) to the brontosaurus burger. The chickpea burger tasted raw, and it was absolutely smothered in white sauce. The first bite toward the edge where it was likely more cooked had some promise, but it went downhill from there. On the plus side, they gave me my money back, and my two meat eating dining companions thought their burgers were good.

Looking for a place to grab a hot drink and treat, we opted to try Wild Earth Bakery.

I had a strawberry rhubarb tart which was sweet and tasty and a loose leaf white tea which I would order again. Wild Earth has a pretty large tea selection if you like a lot of choice.

My friend ordered a macchiato and slice of London Fog cake. The cake was a big disappointment. It was dry and the icing far too thick with a greasy taste to it (likely made with shortening).

The cafe has a cute, cozy vibe with different seating options (tables, bar seating & lounge chairs). We opted to sit outside because if that's a possibility in April, you don't pass it up. :) They had a nice little seating area on the south sidewalk and the tables and chairs were comfortable (which isn't always true of cafe furniture). 

There is also an expectation you will bring in your dishes and put them in a dish bin. I don't have a problem with picking up after myself. However, it does bother me when there is a tip prompt on the credit machine and there is virtually no real service being offered. Who am I tipping and for what exactly?

It's not how I remembered it. Stopped by on a Wednesday afternoon to pick up a simple 16oz mocha. Aside from the fact that my order interaction felt robotic, my mocha was forgotten during a crazy rush of three people! The whipping cream was sloppily plopped on top. And the temperature was so hot I almost burned my mouth. For $5.25 the least I can ask for is a decent temperature, no? I usually treat myself to nice coffee once a week which makes me happy. However, I didn't enjoy my experience this time. :(

It seems like there is so much less energy here now. More than half of the space on the pastry window was empty. Wouldn't you want it to be full for the morning rush? I don't know. Is it that a Starbucks seems more appealing now? I didn't ever think I'd say those words. 3 Stars instead of 2 because I know they can do better.

It's about time St Albert gets a decent place to eat.  

Jack's is a really casual little place,  great for the family or great for a first date.... its very clean, neat and tidy and the staff are really friendly.

The menu is fantastic, not massive but very creative with ingredients.  

Milkshakes are to die for ....

Price is great and really affordable for everyone.

The line up can sometimes mean a little wait, but honestly its worth it.

Went to Jacks today in st albert.Got the shroom burger and the peanut butter one.The shroom burger was really good but wheres the beef.The meat was so little its hard to call it a burger.The peanut burger wasnt that good.really dry.Over all I would try this place again with double patty next time and a different burger

We went again the other night to Fountain Park Rec Centre and it was the first time I had ever noticed that they have a large flatscreen tv on the wall in the hot tub area!  My husband thought that was pretty cool... and a way I can get him to go to the pool even when a hockey game is on!

We also found out that they have a rumpus play room for children 6months to 6 years of age that is padded with play structures - great for letting your kids get completely dry and run amok after swimming before going outside - especially in our cold & frigid winter months!  Socks required for entry!

Sobeys doesn't exist in BC so I wasn't even sure what they had to offer. I peeked in to check it out and found that it's pretty much like Safeway, Save-On or IGA. But I must say that they have one things none of the other grocery chains have... cheese curds! I searched high and low for these because I love making home made poutine. Sobeys was the only one who carried it so I'm glad there's one in walking distance!

This place is my favorite best burgers anywhere I take anyone who comes to town friends family whoever every single burger is delicious the fries are just right and the milkshakes are amazeballs. GO HERE! I can't wait for the new pub to be open

Placed an order for takeout tonight at 5:40, it's now quarter after eight and still haven't seen my food yet. I can't say whether the food is good or not, but I can say the delivery sucks.  Cancelled my order.

Great atmosphere, great food if your a vegetarian, (I forgot until after I started eating the Mediterranean panini). Didn't have lactose free milk which sucks, and soy or almond ruin the taste of a latte. Sat outside reading my book on a lazy Monday afternoon! Great afternoon spent.

I don't have a dog, but I love the fact that there are water dishes outside for them!

We are over the moon that the Lingnan Chinese restaurant decided to open up their first Express location in St. Albert!

My husband and I have been patiently anxiously stalking their twitter and Facebook site awaiting the grand opening!  Much to our surprise, we were driving by the location on Hebert road yesterday and thought we saw an Open sign!

Upon arriving home, I immediately checked Facebook and twitter but there weren't any updates yet.  So I phoned their downtown location and spoke with Mandy who confirmed they opened yesterday!  Hip hip hooray!

I called my hubby at work and we set the wheels in motion to plan for our inaugural Lingnan Express Lunch for the next day!

One of the reasons we are OVER the moon is because we have a toddler and a baby who has been sick for a few months, so needless to say, we haven't gotten to enjoy a Valentine's or Birthday meal out in a few months!  Let alone a normal date night... What are those?  At least now we can bring home the city's BEST Chinese food to the comfort of our home!

Flash forward...  It's today!  Today is the day!

Went down to Lingnan Express this morning when they opened at 11am!  I was so excited to see Amy, Miles, and Mandy there!  (If you haven't seen their television show, check out Quon Dynasty on the Food Network and get to know the family!) Mandy quickly came out from the kitchen and greeted me upon entering the restaurant.  I had to tell her how excited I was that they opened up in St. Albert.

While perusing the menu, which includes 5 different $9 lunch combos (available daily from 11am - 2pm), Amy (the Mom) arrived at the restaurant.  She is just as bubbly in person as she is on the TV show and we have been going to their restaurant in downtown Edmonton for 10 years now.

I expressed my undying gratitude for the new location and Amy and Mandy explained that they have always loved their St. Albert customers and knew that St. Albert was the first place they wanted to open an Express location - I feel so lucky!  They let me take pictures of the restaurant for the Yelp review and Amy even insisted I take one with her :-)

I ordered Combo #1 and Combo #4 to go - and I apologize but their take out menu doesn't break down what exactly all I ordered.  I know Combo #1 was Amy's famous Crack Chicken (Dry Chicken) with Ginger beef, fried rice, mixed veggies and a veggie spring roll.  Combo #4 was Beijing style Kung Pao Chicken and I can't remember the 2nd item - sorry!  Also with mixed veggies, a spring roll, and chow main.

The Crack Chicken/Amy's Special chicken in #1 was perfect!  Just as addicting as ever - and perfectly moist and dry!  The ginger beef was a little over done - a bit difficult to chew - but I'm not complaining!  Still some of the best darn ginger beef in town. 

Amy was so cute, she warned me that all their equipment is brand new and it takes a little while to get used to cooking on new equipment - to essentially break it in.  She warned that it might take a little while to get up to her standards.  Just love that woman!  The mixed veggies were cooked perfectly and the rice was also perfect - not an easy feat for Chinese take out.  I LOVED all the stir fried broccoli - LOVE LOVE LOVE it when the mixed veggies isn't mostly onion and celery.

Combo dish #4 was awesome and I we loved it!  Although, I will double check the picture next time in the restaurant because the Kung Pao Chicken was Beijing style but it was only the chicken on top of the noodles in my dish - no peanuts or veggies with the Kung Pao?  I was the first customer of the day so it may have been in the transition of being completed since I did go at 11am :-)  But the sauce was spot on - Delish!  Hubby loved the 2nd meat item in Combo #4 - Wish I could remember what it is.

And the best part of all?  The EGG ROLLS are to die for!  If you haven't had a Lingnan Egg Roll you are in for a treat!  $2.50 each and well worth it!  They are GIANT and filled with savoury curry goodness!  You will love them!

So very, very happy for the Lingnan!  And looking forward to our Saturday cheat meal more than ever now that we can just pop out and grab some of Amy's Crack Chicken and an Egg Roll to go!  

And before I zipped out the door to take my delicious Lingnan Express food home to the fam, Ms. Amy gave me two gorgeous chopsticks that my daughter fell in love with the minute I got home!  And for a 3 year old, she's pretty darn good at picking up rice with them!

Next time we will order off the dinner menu!

Hip Hip Hooray!  The Lingnan made my family's day!

*Check out the pictures I uploaded*

This has to be my favorite location...the last stop on the way out of town!! Coffee? Yes please!! Fries for my kids?? Why not!! A smile from everyone in the car ?? Sign me up!! 

My only REAL PROBLEM is small but becoming larger with every time I stop!! When I get my free coffee sticker card full and then go to cash it in they charge me .20 cents for a LG and for this who like an XL it is .40cents!! What is the idea of a free coffee then?? They give free refills, $1 drink days and numerous other opportunities to earn that percentage of income for the company...but instead they take a free coffee and charge me for it. 

This seems like bad business all around and leaves a bad taste in my mouth no matter how good the coffee is! Then when I pointed this out I was asked to pull over and wait for my coffee for at least ten minutes. It seemed like it could have been bad timing or maybe passive aggressive behavior I can't tell!

My wife and I walked in this afternoon for a late afternoon snack.  Nice selection of interesting sodas in the cooler and we each had a side salad.  She had a Greek salad, and I had the Vegan bean salad.  
Both were nice servings for the Small and it was very pleasant to eat outside and around the corner from the very busy 99 Street.
Comfortable looking place, the washrooms were downstairs and everything was interesting and clean.  Part of a little string of interesting places with the Organic Market, Ristorante and Wine Bar all in a row.
When in the neighborhood, would stop in again.

Very disappointing.  We have ordered before but it been a while, but it will be a long while before we do it again. The fried rice was white, with white chicken, and nothing else...sorry, we did have one pea.  We live 5 minutes away, still wasn't really warm either.  Had the almond chicken and needed a steak knife to cut it.  The won ton broth was like dish water.  I could go on but won't, you get the picture.
Some very interesting and flavor packed burger options, although I find them a little soggy most times I've had one. Keep the napkins close by!! Great fries, and AMAZING milkshakes!

Great little local coffee shop. Everyone is always so welcoming and nice. Delicious baking and great little snacks, recommend the scones! Their White Chocolate scones are amazing and so are the cheese scones. Good vibes in the place.

This is my neighbourhood cafe, so I admit that I'm probably a little biased, but I love this place! However I do have a complaint: they don't have a good selection of cold coffee drinks (I can't tell you how often I would be here if they had a rockin' Vietnamese iced coffee on their menu). 

Their cakes are super tasty, and the service is always awesome. It's nice to see them so busy at nearly all hours of the day (even if it means I can't find a place to plop down and read a book).

Wow this place is great . Happy staff great food , The buns and burgers taste so fresh . I never had a good poutine and burger since I moved out here till now and the shakes here just tops it off n I will most definitely be coming back here

First time visit today. The cappuccino was pretty darn good though there was a lengthy wait for it. Employees were pretty decent to deal with. 
The atmosphere and vibe were great though I imagine it may be challenging to find a seat during busy times.
Never tried anything to eat, but it all looked pretty good.
Will go back for sure

A friend and I come here on Monday nights for the deep-water aqua size class. The class is fun and actually a good workout (especially if you struggle with joint problems). The pools are clean and well-maintained. The water is also partially salt water so it's better for your skin! The change rooms can be quite busy if kids have their swimming lessons but I've never struggled to find space or a locker for my belongings. I appreciate that they also keep the floors as dry as possible (it can be pretty wet at times but it's never dangerous). The change rooms also have a dryer for your suit so you don't have to go home with a dripping wet suit! The prices here are also much cheaper than other pool facilities I've seen. Overall, a good experience :)

Have you ever had a burger at Shake Shack in NYC? If not, get on a plane and go have one. If that's not an option, just get in your car and drive to Jack's Burger Shack in St. Albert. It's the next best thing. It's about as close as I've found to a Shake Shack burger anywhere, and I eat a lot of burgers in a lot of cities.

The burger is perfectly seasoned high quality meat, simple fresh ingredients, and an awesome bun. No need for fancy toppings, just keep it simple with cheese, tomato, lettuce, pickles, ketchup, mustard, and Jack sauce. Add bacon if you like bacon. 

The fries are great. The service is great. Jack's Burger Shack is awesome. Best burger in Edmonton area. For reference, my fav burgers in order of preference are:

1) Jack's Burger Shack
2) The Next Act
3) Five Guys
4) Burger's Priest

Go get one!

I came in to have my lips done, my mom has been coming hear for years and swears by it. Everyone was so friendly from the second I walked in. Marnie the nurse I had do my lips did an EXCELLENT JOB I love them! She was so patient with me because sometimes I'm wormy, but she took her time and walked me through everything and in the end I'm so satisfied with everything!

Lovely little place with gelato, sorbet, and ice cream. The staff was super friendly and willingly offered samples. I picked up a medium (4 oz) lemon sorbet for $4.95 + tax. The sorbet was good though the texture could be improved. Overall, quite enjoyable for someone who is trying to avoid dairy. I do find the pricing a bit too high for my tastes - so this will stay in the realm of a rare treat. 
I will be back to try their soft-serve, which is also dairy-free and only costs $2.95. I am looking forward to that. :-)
Best burger joint anywhere! And the brontosaurus patty is crazy good when you get a menu burger and then sub the patty. The staff is friendly and the place is clean.

I came in with my sister on a hot Saturday afternoon...

When we arrived there was a line up all the way out the door so it must be good :) 

I decided on keylime because I love citrus flavors. My sister ordered the colorful one ( I can't remember the name).

It's a cozy ice cream shop which is cute but can be quite tight when there's so many ppl crammed in all at once. 

The ice cream was great! I love how cold and flavorful it was, you just can't go wrong with ice cream lol .

I will definitely come back whenever i'm in St. Albert.

Sorry, no pictures this time as I thought it would be rude to take food pictures in the presence of company.

A group of us made a burger pilgrimage to Jack's.  Been there before but it has been a while.  The location is central in the middle of the quiet area which St. Albert called downtown.  There is no parking lot but then, the entire area is filled with hundreds of street parking spots.  

We walked in and was greeted with smiles; yes, every employees had smiles on their faces.  In fact, every lady who works there was so cheerful, we couldn't help to be cheerful ourselves.  I ordered the Schroom burger, omg, it was fantastic.  The small prints below the menu stays that the beef is grind fresh daily, you can definitely taste it; the patty was fantastic.  Topped with just the right amount of mushrooms and Boursin cheese; then lettuce and tomatoes; extreme yumminess.  As soon as you bite into it, juices gush out of the patty, my napkins and my plate were soaking with meat-juice after the meal.  Not sure what kind of bun they use but it was soft and tasted extremely fresh.  Burger wise, for $8, definitely 5/5.

Then there are the fries, well, I have tasted better.  It is skin on skinny-cutted fries.  May be because a large group of us arrived at the same time, the fries were not crispy and a little on the greasy side.  The aioli dip was good though, move over ketchup, aioli for the win with these fries.  Fries, $3, even with the strong aioli dip, 3/5.

I am a water drinker, the healthiest drink around.  Two large glass dispensers of ice lemon-flavored filtered water (filtered? at least that's what the sign says) available for all patrons to take freely.  Love it.

5 young energetic employees working today (okay may be 4 youngers and one that looks like the owner; he acts young, that's all that matters); everyone smiled, at least 3 came by to say hi and how is the food.  Totally unlike any fast food place I have ever dined it.  Last I checked, no one from Fatburgers, Five Guys etc. ever came to check on the patrons after the food has been delivered.  6/5 for service.  High score because this is a fast food burger joint, not fine dining.  I would have expected more at a 3 star restaurant but not from a burger joint.

Overall, definitely not the healthiest meal I have ever eaten (looking at the meat-juice on my plate afterwards, lol), but then, I am on my Christmas break, I am allowed.  The burger was dang tasty; definitely satisfied my beef craving after a few days of turkey eating; almost ordered a second one, wanted to try the Quebecer (poutine on burger).  This meal definitely reminded me why it is worth the drive to St. Albert occasionally for lunch.  All the tastiness for $11, what more can you ask.

I have always enjoyed this bakery/cafe. Easy to access, there's street parking along side and through the neighborhood (i don't mind walking) as well as parking lot shared with their other neighbors and grocery store. There's comfy seating and lots of tables and chairs. I like the fact that you can sit in or take out. The atmosphere is relaxed and pleasant and i especially like the fact that they feature local talent on open mike. It feels like you are in your living room sometimes where you can just sit back, sip on some coffee, eat some yummy baked goods and listen to live music and poetry. Recently we had a wedding bridal shower and had a cake ordered. It was delicious and a hit at the party.
 I find the service friendly, however, when there's a line up, expect that they are working hard to move that line fast. 
They always put our their fresh good but also sell their later-in-the-week goods for lower the price which i still think its awesome because it seems fresher still, than larger grocery store bought bread. 
Hours open are reasonable and worth the visit. I cannot comment on the other location as i have never been.

This place is amazing! Burgers are made fresh to order and so many different options for your burger.  Poutine and milkshakes so great as well. Best part was 2 burgers, 2 milkshakes and poutine for under $40! FANTASTIC!!! Also the staff was super friendly. Why go to a fast food joint when you can come here

This is my favourite burger spot, period. I was never really a fan of smashed burgers until I ate here, which l will admit took me far too long. Everything is good. The Nutella milkshake is exactly what you want in something that's suppose to taste like Nutella: smooth and creamy, and reminds you of a Ferrero Roche. We've back multiple times now, and were not disappointed either time. During school hours, and the summer, expect the lines to be long. They have rules posted, and one of them is "Don't linger" for a reason. The fries are to die for, and last time I was here I had nothing but the poutine. It's simple: fries, curds, and gravy, but you don't need anything else. If you haven't been here, get here.

A good place to people watch, very busy with views of 99st as well as the Route 99 parking lot.  It can be hard to get a spot on the bike rack if you peddle over.

The soup is usually good, but the sandwiches are unappealing.  The scones are delicious, especially the ones drizzled with chocolate.  The coffee is ok, as is the service: not wow-worthy but adequate.

I enjoy grabbing a stool by the window and enjoying the scenes unfolding around me. A good place to write.

Great baked goods, you must try the raspberry white chocolate scones!!! This cozy cafe is one of my favourites in the city, they offer a wide selection of tasty treats, coffees and teas. 
They have great outdoor seating in the summer and a warm and cozy environment inside for the rest of the year.  
Very friendly staff, and fresh baked goods made in house. 
You must check it out, but get there early especially on weekends as they are very busy.

Been here a couple times now.  Odd how I missed this originally being it is down town St.Albert...but I did.  My wife had it recommended and the disruption dounded great.  Loved the many choices, and the local sourcing.
My only complaint, and it is minor... It is smallish, and not exactly comfortable seating.  I can deal though, just to wrap my pie hole around those burgers!

If you want burnt buns on your breakfast sandwich, this is the place to go! I ordered a mc muffin and got this (see pic). When I had it replaced i was told "oh, our buns come toasted". Lady tossed it to another coworker at the back and said "lady wants her bun not toasted". Geez. There's a difference between toasted and burnt! 

Also, on the same trip, we ordered 2 happy meals with Nerf toys. Without any explanation, they gave enclosed 2 books of the same titles. When i approached the counter to ask whether they might have missed that we ordered different toys, the manager just said dismissingly said "oh we ran out of them". I said why werent we told this, she just smugly said "you can just come back and have it replaced when we have stock" and quickly turned away heading to the kitchen.
Wow. Just WOW!

Sadly, the shack part of the name is a misnomer - Jack's is located in a strip of stores in downtown St. Albert.

The beef burgers are pretty good - certainly the best fast food style burger I've had in Edmonton, aside from a slightly undercooked one from the Next Act's truck. I got the "crunch" burger, which includes potato chips.

The veggie burger needs improvement, according to my wife. It's flavourless and limp.

But we both enjoyed the fries and their delicious shakes. While a milkshake topped with Cinnamon Toast Crunch sounds disgusting at first, it's actually quite delicious!

Kinda weird that there's a manager standing there watching people eat every time I come in. Makes me feel uncomfortable. Also every time I go through the drive through they forget part of my order. They're nice enough about giving me the correct order when I walk into the store, but when this has happened for the fifth time in a row... the place is clean enough and staff are friendly, but it just has a weird environment.

I must admit I only come to McDonald's for their $1 any sized iced coffee (caramel) all summer long and the occasional egg mcmuffin.  I'm pretty thrifty when it comes to McD and only come when I have a coupon. 

The reason I'm taking the time to review this location is because they are always pleasant and efficient. On numerous occasions when I have come through the drive thru and used a coupon the lady behind the till has cheered, "woo hoo!" and they have let me keep my coupon to be reused on several occasions.
The best burgers in St. Albert or possibly Edmonton, and the milkshakes are amazing - the Nutella shake is my favorite!

The loss of two stars is due to the stern-faced, you are in trouble for something and you don't know why, cashiers at this cafe and bakery in old Strathcona. If it wasn't for the vegetarian options and the excellent coffee I don't think I would come back here on a weekly basis, just based on the front of house service. However, when I've ordered cakes in the past and spoke to the bakers or when chatting to the baristas they have always been cheery and helpful. It's almost as if they have it backwards; lovely friendly people hidden in the back and the crabby "I hate my job" staff doing the ordering. I would give you lots of examples but I get shaky and clenched fisted just thinking about today's episode alone, where I was made to feel stupid more then once in a 60 second time frame. 

The gluten free brownies are unbelievably moist and delicious though, and the veggie wrap is tasty. My son , who is like a little foodie but only when it comes to banana bread and has tried every place in town, thinks wild earth's banana bread is too dry and doesn't taste like bananas. He's 3 but he knows what he's talking about on this topic! 

So while the decor is warm here and full of charm and wood furniture, the cashiers are wooden and charmless(For the most part, but occasuonally we've had a friendly person up front) . 

The other thing I should mention are the made to order cakes! We ordered one for my sons birthday online and then spoke to a baker who was exceptionally lovely and accommodating! The cake was beautifully decorated and monogrammed, and really a steal at $32.00!

Depending on what you are going to Wild Earth for, I'd say it's hit or miss.

I was in the neighborhood this morning and finally had a chance to step into the Wild Earth Bakery under the pretext of satiating my morning caffeine craving. But once I laid eyes on the cooler filled with delicate tarts and cakes, I knew I'd be leaving with more than just a small dark roast with cream and honey. 
Cinnamon buns, scones, and muffins vied for attention in baskets on the counter, but I went for the almond croissant and was transported to instant heaven. It was that rare perfect combo of moist and flaky (meaning the layers peeled off beautifully - is there a word for that?), with a light sugary glaze on top to secure the sliced almonds in place. I followed this pure delight up with an even tastier treat - a tart. Pumpkin caught my eye, but creme brulee couldn't be passed up. My first contact with my favourite dessert in tart form was as dreamy as could be imagined - the thick pastry shell was almost creamy, and it was moderately filled with an even creamier custard-style concoction, requisitely charred slightly on top. 
Had I any inkling that Wild Earth Bakery was such an absolute delight I would've been frequenting it long ago. As it stands, I'll be back to claim that pumpkin tart shortly.

Wild Earth is a neighborhood bakery with a number of delicious baked goods (like the white chocolate pumpkin spice scone!) for you to enjoy while you sip a beverage of choice (try the chai latte!). They also have sandwiches, wraps, breakfast buns, and other things you'd expect a bakery to have.

Seating is sort of limited because it get's pretty busy, but if you can't find a comfy chair in the back room and don't want to awkwardly stand around, they also have take-and-bake prepped goodies in a cooler for you to take on the kitchen and bake like a boss at home.

ps. 
Their Chili is pretty fantastic.

Also, the Wild Earth grocery beside the bakery is pretty awesome. A lot of the inventory sold there is local, organic, and delicious with comparible prices to Big-Box Stores. They also sell Dinner-to-Go containers for those on the fly!

I want to like Wild Earth Bakery, I really do. I think the owners are cool/interesting people and I love the location in Edmonton, but there's just a couple of things that irk me about Wild Earth.
Firstly, no wi-fi. I have to write this review from home because there's no wi-fi. Who knows maybe if i was sitting in the cafe updating my Instagram and checking my email I might also throw in a positive review for Wild Earth but I can't because no wi-fi. It seems like a petty complaint but really a hipster coffee bar should have wi-fi. Next, didn't really enjoy the food all that much.. I don't want to say the food wasn't made in house but something just didn't taste good about the breakfast burrito (I'm hoping it wasn't a Sysco product but it tasted a little like opened from a bag and put on the grill) with all that said I do think it's a pretty cute place. Small tweaks and this place could move up to a 5 in my books. Oh ya and it needs air conditioning!! My heart breaks for their sweaty staff on hot days!

All Shook Up Burger w/ hangover style buns $11.75
Beef, Bacon and Peanut Butter. The hangover style buns include a grilled cheese, an extra patty and extra bacon.

A beautifully monstrous burger. Calorific degeneracy in the form of peanut butter, beef, bacon and grilled cheese buns. It takes time to get used to the chunky peanut butter, but this is a fine burger. It's an acquired taste, though - you have to be a peanut butter fiend. 

The dining experience was coloured by an inordinately saline poutine, featuring lacklustre gravy and over-seasoned fries. And the Cap'n Crunch milkshake was uninspired; just a minimal blend of cereal with pieces on top to disguise a mediocre creation. I was expecting more, but Jack's burger game is strong. The service was also exceptionally kind. 

My Rating: 3.75/5

Facebook.com/RamneeksFoodReviews
Awesome homemade burgers! Great frys made with fresh potatoes from Washington State. Definitely coming back!!

Came here for some pho. I ordered a beef noodle soup (Pho) and asked for no beef. I dont like the beef they serve because they dont trim the fat off. The entire time the staff was double checking the order and laughing. Even the server couldnt stop smirking the entire time I ate my meal. Very disrespectful and unprofessional staff. Run by kids.

During a time of so many unknowns Sobeys has really done a great job at keeping their store stocked (as best they can) and very clean.  Today when I popped in after my shift there were no baskets to be used, but a lovely lady was there to clean a cart for you to use.  I used my own grocery bag (which felt funny at first, like I was looting).  

I was able to find everything I need to make a lasagna and breakfast sandwiches.  

The other reasons they get 5/5 stars is due to the workers.  Every single person I saw today in that store had a smile, was helping someone if that's what was needed and were friendly.  In a time of so many unknowns it was wonderful to see such amazing Humans working to make sure we can provide for our families.  

Even the customers were kind. The lady ahead of me (2m away, nicely marked on the floor) asked me (I was behind her) if she could go get milk that she forgot.  I of course said yes.  I'm in no hurry.  Then I moved to another line with fewer people as I didn't have much.  And this wonderful senior gentlemen wanted me to go ahead of him, even though he had been waiting much longer than I.  

The lady at the lotto counter who rang in my groceries was funny and kind.  Way to go St. Albert Sobeys.  Truly wonderful place to shop and be greeted with friendly faces. 

In my books you get 6 stars.

What's not to love about jacks. The meat is pressed and excellent. But the buns they use are supiorer. Can be a bit of a wait during the rush but it's worth it and they are always getting better. On the vegan side it's a pleaser. Their meatless burger is easily one of the best in Edmonton and surrounding area. The fries are excellent but jacked up fries was better to share than go it alone.

I love this place and have been popping in regularly for years for breakfast and tasty baked goods. This morning I needed a good pick me up after the gym and no weak drive through coffee would cut it- I needed the good stuff! I went in at 6:45am and it was already busy with morning rush. The crew there are awesome, and despite the rush, I was in and out and on my way to work on time. Candis makes a MEAN latte! I love their selection of vegan and gluten free options, as well as yummy treats for my mutts. So many things I like, all in a cute neighbourhood cafe! Thanks for helping me start my day! :)
This place is worth the drive to taste their burgers. Lots of choices and really cool special burgers. I went there 4 weeks ago and have been back x10 to try everything on the menu.

We've eaten at Jack's several times now and their burgers do not disappoint! My faves are the BBQ Crunch & the On the Cobb, both are delicious flavour combinations. I would give them 5 stars if it weren't for my attempt at their Jack'd Up fries... I guess I should have read the menu more closely because I was totally grossed out by the plastic cheese slice melted on top of my fries.  The Jack sauce is awesome but skip the fake cheese! 
It's always been busy when we've visited and seating is limited so don't be surprised if you have to order to-go and take your food elsewhere.

I used to come to Wild Earth when I worked super early mornings. I'd pick up a latte, and either some raspberry white chocolate scones, or a couple slices of banana bread. Everything is super fresh, and absolutely delicious. I prefer to go earlier in the day where there is more product and it's still warm, but any time is a good time for a treat!

Wild Earth Cafe has always been one of my favourite cafes. After the renovation and extension it's THE favorite one.  Awesome coffee and espresso drinks, good collection of teas, choice of pastries, cookies, sandwiches. salads and soups makes it a fantastic spot for weekday evenings and sunday afternoons. Little sections give you choice of space. You can sit by the window, in the main room, by the fire place, or in the more private space of the  small room they have in one corner. Decoration is nice and has a cozy cabin-in-the-woods sort of feel to it. if you decided to grab your laptop and work here, keep in mind that there's no wifi.

I love coming here. I swim every morning and its a great place to work out. Very clean and they have loads of free equipment for public use (flippers, water weights, flotation bands, flutter boards, etc..). Its great for families or if your looking for a solo workout. 

Plus the aqua-size classes are great! Its a good way to meet new people or go to classes with friends and socialize. Coming here has become an important part of my day!
SO good. best burgers! such a fun environment with fresh ingredients and incredible milkshakes. i love all the gluten free options. it's a must try!

I can't say enough positive praise about my experience with External Affairs. From the moment I walked in the staff were warm and welcoming. The space is absolutely beautiful and the staff truly make it shine. I had an initial consultation with Joanne, Dr. Briggs and Carol. Joanne made me feel comfortable and at ease and was very knowledgable about the service and products offered. Dr Briggs provided me more information  than my family doctor ever has, and Carol was able to provide me with a great treatment plan to suit my needs. I ended up getting services same day because I felt so confident with the staff. I truly look forward to my next appointment.
Awesome Burgers, fast service, Got there before they close at 8pm or run out of buns first

I came to Jack's with a group of Yelpers to attend UYE Burger Quest part 6.

I came.  I ate.  I conquered.

I am now a fan of Jack's Burger Shack due to 3 things:

1) Darth Vader Milkshake - Vanilla ice cream blended with coke
2) French Fries with Sea Salt and Malt Aioli - Simply fantastic
3) All Shook Up Burger - Who'dve thunk that a Beef Patty covered in peanut butter and bacon could be so wonderful?  Never in my wildest dreams would I have thought that this concoction would go together.

Honorable mention goes out to their, as of yet, unnamed coffee milkshake with crumbled biscotti on top!

It's been a year since our last visit and after such yumminess the next one won't be so far away.

The food is okay, the fries have never been fresh every time I've been there though. It's always a super long wait, it's nice that they cook everything (except the fries) fresh but even when it's not busy it takes forever. Most of the staff I've encountered are not friendly at all.

I am not exaggerating when I say that this place has THE BEST burgers you will ever have in your life. I'm not much of a burger fan, but this place is the exception. I could eat their burgers everyday. The patties are extremely juicy and flavourful. And don't even get me started on their signature "jack sauce"... it is HEAVENLY, I don't even know how to describe it. It completes the burger. If you are going to order a burger you MUST have the jack sauce on it. I highly recommend ordering the "standard Jack burger". It's the best.

I have never had such disgusting food in my life
 One bite and I threw away the whole container. The chicken was covered in sauce to mask the fact it was days and days if not weeks old. DO NOT ORDER FROM HERE.
Bun was stale.  Asked for on my fries.  Put on a slice of cheese on top and put it in the microwave . Will never go back

I unfortunately live in vancouver now and let me tell you I MISS THIS PLACE SO MUCH! anytime i'm home for a visit i always make a point of going in to my favourite spot. BEST BURGERS AND MILK SHAKES EVER

This is my second time here and definitely a massive improvement. Fantastic customer service, every employee went above and beyond ensuring we had a great experience. The burger was amazing and came between two grilled cheeses. The patty was crispy on the outside and super thin. The cap n' crunch milkshake was that perfect balance of not overly sweet. Definitely recommend if you're ever in St. Albert!

Great service and great selection. I always buy my work and home supplies from Staples. I especially like online ordering and delivery.
Just made a mistake on a purchase and the return was super easy.

Super solid place to have a meal. Specifically burgers. Because obviously? 

I've been here twice now. My first and second visits were within two weeks of each other. This must mean it is delicious. It really was. The burgers are quite significantly sized. I went in so so hungry, ate a burger and shared an order of fries and was satisfied. 

I really loved the atmosphere. It's cozy and welcoming. Everyone is really great. It can get busy in there so it can mean no table, but order anyway. Eat outside. Eat on your car. Whatever. 

I really enjoyed sitting at the counter. I like watching kitchens operate.  

I haven't had a chance to have a milkshake yet, but seeing people come in and order just milkshakes makes me a bit excited. You wouldn't show up for bad milkshakes.

They are consistently excellent, simple as that.  I think one of the best Burgers places in St. Alber
t
The staff are always friendly and these are the best damn burgers in town! Don't believe me? Order a bbq crunch and let the good times roll

I love this place. The burgers are fantastic! I fell in love with the nearly perfect poutine with real curds and fantastic gravy! A Darth Vader milkshake was the perfect dessert to end the meal. 
Really friendly staff. I got there just before lunch closing at nearly 2:30 p.m. and instead of rushing my meal and pushing me out the door for them to close...they let in another five starving customers. 
Great service and I will definitely be back.

Would I eat here again? Probably not. Am I glad I tried it? Absolutely. 

The first time I came here was with my girlfriend at her recommendation as she had heard positive reviews, in particular concerning the milkshakes. So we had gone to explore St. Albert and have some milkshakes. Yesterday was our first time eating there - our fridge was empty and work ran late so we were looking to eat out. I was underwhelmed by the food. I ordered the veggie option, the Brontosaurus, described as a chickpea and blue cheese patty served with lettuce and jack sauce. That's definitely what I got and although it wasn't as expensive as your typically burger, at $9, I don't think this burger was worth more than $6. The patty itself was nothing special and the bun was so cheap; I get better quality buying the cheap stuff at the supermarket. I was surprised at the lettuce and how it exactly tastes like that of McDonald's. The jack sauce didn't make any difference other than to spill off my burger and onto my hands as I ate. To compliment our burgers we shared a side of jack'd up fries. At the first few bites we were pleasantly surprised but after awhile we became displeased. The amount of jack sauce was nice considering how many places these days are stingy with their toppings but the taste began to be bothersome after awhile. The fries themselves were just a tad below average and the menu stated there is cheese on the fries but I could only find two small curds amongst the swamp of jack sauce and onions. 

I'm happy I tried the food after seeing all the good reviews, but I should have just stuck to the milkshake.

Signing up for a yearly membership at Servus Place enabled me to also participate in water exercise classes at Fountain Park, closer to home and a whole lot quieter.  I am HOOKED by the warm water, friendly staff and patrons, and an activity which is kind to my ancient joints.  I've attended both shallow water and deep water classes (although I'm a bit chicken - no, more like PETRIFIED - if my toes can't touch bottom - I'm working on that) which are 45 minutes long and energetically coached by staff.  If you've never tried deep water exercise, I do recommend it - there are buoyancy belts that I'm promised won't let me drown.  I'll keep working on believing that  :-)

This continues to be my go to pool 5 years later.

The staff are friendly.

The pool is pretty darn clean.

The swim instructors are nice.

The water is partial salt water.

The entrance fee is almost 1/2 of Servus' fee.

See you Sunday, Fountain Park!

I have heard about Jack's for years. Apparently it is the place to go to get the best burger you will ever eat. 

It was meh. It was not horrible by any means, and the burger was "St Albert good".  Will I go again...as a foodie it is unlikely. There is definitely better burgers in the area. Is it better than McDonalds? Absolutely. The atmosphere was fun, the fry's were good, but it definitely has a long way to go before it becomes a foodie's dream.

I went into External Affairs because I've been struggling with really horrific hormonal-cystic acne. When I made the appointment I asked if there was a dermatologist on staff and if I could see them, the lady said she would book me an appointment for that and I would be seeing a technician and I just assumed that was totally normal and was really excited. 

When I got the appointment I went into the room and the technician (I won't name her) came in. She asked why I was there, I told her about my acne problems. She then gave me a sales pitch for all of their skin care line and left. When she returned she was carrying a bunch of bottles and told me I needed all of it. She didn't even look at my face and was pushing all of these products. I told her topical treatments don't work because my acne was cystic and hormonal. She said their products were "Medical Grade" and should work. She also gave me these "Hormone Balancing" pills and said they should fix everything. 

I was so desperate, so so desperate that I just went with it. She successfully sold me $400 worth of product and I'm sure that went to her commission or bonus. 

It's been over a month, and there have been no improvements, not even a little bit. My face is so dry and the skin around my eyes and mouth is peeling off. My acne has actually gotten worse. This is my face, I have to walk about with this every day, I've cried endlessly over this. Last week I went to the grocery store without makeup and I cried in my car because my face looked like a war zone. I thought after spending $400 I didn't have, I would at least see something. I trusted the technician.

I finally did research on what she sold me, and the pills she sold me (For $57) are only 10mcg of the ingredient that supposed to help acne, and 200mcg of broccoli extract. I found something proven to fix hormonal acne, it has 200mcg of that ingredient for $27. Another product she sold me for $47, I found an equivalent for $16.

I feel ripped off and it's totally my fault. I shouldn't have trusted her, no one forced me to buy the products, but she made it sound like they would work. I feel so hurt, I spent so much money, and it just really upsets me.

I was really nervous to write a review because I've seen how External Affairs as responded to their negative reviews. They always seem to respond angry and with a "well go somewhere else then", and that just makes me so anxious.

This Staple's location is smaller with fewer choices in each department than what I was used to in the U.S. - it's the only one I've visited here so don't know if it's typical or not.  I was disappointed not to find items I wanted, but on the other hand, I was impressed how organized they were for parents shopping for back-to-school supplies, with lists for every school in the area.  It's not necessarily easy to save any money here, except on their specials, but at least it's stocked and all in one place.

As another reviewer mentioned, no one seems eager to check on whether you need assistance - I roamed the aisles trying to find an employee without success.
