I had to recently return an item and commend that employee for making it a quick and easy transaction.

Terrific food. We had the Big Jack, a massive charbroiled double paddy burger with poutine fries nestled inside. You will need a fork and knife for this massive burger. My husband loved it, but I prefer a juicier burger. So I will not order again, but he will. 
As to the milkshakes, I broke a two-year ice cream fast to have a "Malteaser." Delicious!!! And I appreciated that the portion was smaller.
Jack's rocks like no other burger place. Working just up the street makes it my main go to when I'm hungry and pressed for time. I would give it 6 stars if I could.

Was at this location yesterday around 6 P.M. to shop for a new desk top or lap-top. There were 4 or 5 employees all chatting when I entered the computer section. After over 15 minutes of mulling around, I was surprised that not one person came over to offer assistance, especially since I was the only customer in the entire section. I inadvertantly sounded an alarm on a lap-top when I touched it, prompting a young sales associate to come over. After he apologized, I remarked that this was one way to get someone's attention, yet he returned went to his social gathering of fellow employees. I left the store, likely never to return.

No doubt one of the better burger places to eat at in St. Albert. The burgers have a homemade feel to them and the fries are crispy, golden brown, and delightful. The restaurant also boasts an impressive selection of milkshakes.

St. Albert surprisingly has a decent amount of restaurants in the 'hood. A co-worker and I wanted to try something different for lunch so we decided to check out Jack's Burger Shack on a Thursday. We just missed the lunch rush (score!) and were able to grab a seat at the counter. Good spot as you can see everything being cooked and the fries being blow-torched (what!).

I like how all of Jack's burgers can be substituted for a chicken breast if you say don't eat beef and they also have one vegetarian patty on the menu. All the staff were very easy going and it's always great supporting a family run joint.

We took a look at the chalkboard menus up on the walls and decided to go with:
- All Shook up ($8) - Beef, bacon and peanut butter. Interesting idea with the peanut butter. My co-worker said it was very good and that the beef patty was tender and juicy.
- Brontosaurus ($8) - homemade chickpea patty with LTO, jack sauce and bleu cheese. I'm no vegan (clearly) but the brontosaurus sounded interesting so I gave it a shot. The chickpea patty was surprisingly very flavourful. As many people have said, the patties are bigger than the buns, which I don't mind one bit. Also an interesting tidbit I found out was that their buns are made specifically for their shop from Safeway (who woulda thunk)!  
- Jack'd Up fries ($5) - hand cut fries with jack sauce, cheese slices and onion. It's interesting how they blow torch their cheese slices - can't say I've ever seen that before on fries. The jack sauce is what makes these fries good!
- Poutine ($5) - hand cut fries, cheese curds and gravy. I'm not the biggest fan of poutine but this one was very average. We both found it to be a bit too salty for our taste buds.

Overall, Jack's is a quaint little spot - nothing mind blowing but tasty burgers, fries and shakes.  Speaking of shakes, I will have to try one next time as everyone else seemed to be ordering them. They also have a sister pub restaurant, right next door, called Feast & Lounge. Patio looks pretty sweet for the summertime.

We had stopped in this bakery before, but this was our first time eating here...well, kind of! It was after 3:00 and knowing we were in the middle of our day's adventures, I begged my husband to pull over so I could get something to eat.. I ran in, picked up a couple of sandwiches and a peanut butter cookie  and was quickly back out the door - after paying $16.00, that is. The staff were helpful and there wasn't a lineup although there were several people enjoying the great weather at their tables outside. As for the sandwiches and the cookie, they were tasty, but the price seemed a bit high. If I'm in the neighbourhood again, I'll surely be back for other bakery items. I also noticed a bit too late that they sell dog biscuits for $0.49 each and would have loved to grab two for my furry friends. Next time!

I came to Jack's for the first time the other day with my father-in-law, hubby, and 5 year old in tote after hauling some furniture - we were all in serious need of a refuel!

Off the hop, the place was a little hard to find because they don't have their sign up yet (they told me they are awaiting the city permit approval to install it).  They are on Perron street in a little alcove with Wine Kitz and Trendy Home by the Community Hall.  They have an awesome patio with brightly coloured orange and red metal patio tables and folding chairs.

The staff were awesome and decor was bright and clean but that's where the buck stopped for me unfortunately.

Okay the food:

Menu looked great, reasonable prices, fresh and new creations.

We ordered:

Inferno: standard 1/3 lb. patty with jalapenos, cheese, and a allegedly spicy sauce but I didn't find any heat on this burger.  Seriously, it would be a 1 out of 5 on a spice scale.  $8 (does not come with sides)

BBQ Crunch: standard 1/3 patty with bacon, cheese, potato chips, orange pop BBQ sauce.  My counterparts (men) loved this burger. $8 (does not come with sides)

Kids Meal - Burger, fires, and small fountain pop $6.  My daughter was happy - but what's not to love about a cute little kids meal for kiddos?

On the recommendation of the other reviewer, we tried the poutine but uh.. No, those were not cheese curds the day we were there.  They were curd shaped but not squeaky at all and definitely your standard mozerella - the same cheese you find at Costco in their poutine.  Yummy, but not traditional.  The fries were fresh and the gravy decent but nothing to write home about.  $5 was a good price and I'm sure if we are here again, this would be on our table.

As a total aside - the cheese here is processed.  Hubby says he prefers that on a burger but I don't - I like real cheese (not the stuff made from oil).

And then we ordered 2 milkshakes: Malteaser and Cinnamon Toast Crunch.
We were so disappointed in the milkshakes that it makes me sad to relive it.  At $4 a pop, the price is great but the taste and consistency really let us down.

All of the milkshakes are vanilla ice cream based and then the toppings or cereals are blended in and then garnished on top.  They looked gorgeous but the taste was overwhelmingly vanilla and the were so runny that I wouldn't even call it a milkshake.  It was more like milk with a splash of ice cream :-(   

The staff were super friendly and offered to remake our shakes but I didn't see any point and I'd hate to waste another set of milkshakes.  My daughter happily slurped them and my father-in-law never complains but my husband agreed with me that he wouldn't call what we had a milkshake.  More like a ice cream inspired milk beverage.

The burgers were definitely the highlight - fresh ground beef smashed right on the grill - kickin' it old school.  And I liked the serve yourself water bar :-)

Beautiful patio, friendly staff, fresh burgers, but a fail on the milkshake department which is a dealbreaker for me at a old-school burger shop.

My favorite place to eat in St Albert. Pretty much a weekly tradition. Love the burgers and the fries are super good too!  BBQ crunch is a favorite of the hubby while I like the regular with cheese. Thin patties and fluffy buns make the perfect combination.

Yum, yum, yum! Oh St Albert, you have got it going on!! I am so in love with this Burger Shack (and soooo happy I don't live close, 'cause my bathroom scale would bust). Lets do the check list:
Decor: Adorable.
Patio: Decent. 
Shakes: Phenomenal. Try the Darth Vader, I loved it!
Fries: Crispy and delicious. 
Burgers: Crazy good - oh, and I had the chicken. 
Dessert: Ya right... I'll never have room! But good for you if you can do it. 

Jack, whom ever you are, you should be very proud of what you've created.

Well I've had 3 experiences with Jack's now, so I feel really confident with the 5 star rating.

My first experience was when my office did a large order for takeout.  The packaging was fairly greasy by the time it made it to the office (about half an hour away) but everything was absolutely DELICIOUS!  It was most of our first times trying Jack's and everyone was really happy.

Second experience was at the end of a road trip, i was craving a milkshake so bad.  So we stopped and picked up a couple of Malteser shakes to go.

Third experience was right around lunch time on a Saturday after wandering around the market.  We somehow managed to get there right before the rush.  There were 3 of us, and we all ordered the standard with cheese.  We shared an order of Jack'd up fries.  2 of us got milkshakes and the third got a pop.  The total was $51.00 which I expected and really wasn't that bad for 3 of us.  And we were all painfully full by the time we left.

Things I've noticed with the 3 very different experiences:
The staff are always incredibly friendly.  They are a young bunch, but they appear to work hard.
When they say the beef is fresh, they mean it.  I think I read that they get it from D'Arcy's, which wouldn't surprise me at all.  it's amazing.
The buns - oh man the buns!  I usually take off my top bun because there's just too much bread, and although this one looked like it was going to be very heavy, it was not at all!  It was the lightest bun I've ever had with a burger.  
The milkshakes are delicious... I almost wish they had more flavours!  But who am I kidding?  Both times that I've gotten a milkshake, i've stuck with the malteser.
The fries are seasoned perfectly.
The Jack Sauce..... what is it?  It's what dreams are made of, that's what.

So yah, I recommend it...

Drove out to Jack's today to try their famous crunch burger.  I live in Sherwood Park, so it's a bit of a hike out to St. Albert for lunch, but today we loaded up the family for a pilgrimage for what some say is the best burger in the city.  When we got there, there was lots of free street parking and the patio was perfectly half in the sun (for us) and half in the shade (for the kids) even while sitting at 1 table together.

After staring at the menu for 5 minutes, my suspicions were correct, the crunch burger was what I wanted.  My wife ordered the same thing, while we got my son a $4 kids meal with grilled cheese and fries with milk.  The crunch burger was surprisingly small.... truth be told I have a pet peeve against burgers that are stacked taller than a persons mouth (even when squished).  This burger was the perfect height.  My favourite part of the burger was that every bite was the same.  The distribution of ingredients was perfect.  I have put chips on burgers at home, but have never ordered it at a restaurant.  The surprising thing for me was how few chips you actually need to add in order to get the desired crunch.  For our fries I asked the girl behind the counter if the "jacked up fries" were any good.... she said she had never tried them.  How can you work at a place with 3 types of fries on the menu and now even had 1 bite of all 3?  I opted to skip em because it was weird that not even she wanted to try them.  We opted for 1 side of fries and 1 side of poutine.  The poutine was great, but to be honest, the fries were what made it good... you didn't need the gravy and cheese.  They are cooked perfectly, so there is no need to pay extra for the poutine, just stick to the fries if you go.

The grilled cheese we ordered for my son was cooked on a panini press, not a flat top, so it had deep grill marks in it.  My son took 1 bite and wasn't interested because the grill makes make the bread feel more like crust than fried bread (what kid likes crust)... luckily for us he liked the fries, so he filled up on those.

Overall a fantastic experience, I can't wait to go back.
LOVE these burgers!! These guys are burger geniuses. Fresh ingredients, very friendly staff. I recommend this place to people all the time.

Wife is celiac so must eat Gluten Free ! I on the other hand can eat just about anything ! Tried the Jade Village food quality was ok ! My egg foo yong was shy on the egg and sauce a bit thin ! One disappointment they do not deliver to north Edmonton ! Had to pick up , seems odd with everyone and their dog doing deliveries now a days ! But it's only 20 minutes to drive there so not an issue today ! On the plus side Jade village has small pub attached a pint was only $5.75 while we wait ! Service was top shelf here !! Park behind the save on , the entrance to restaurant was a bit confusing !

Food is always good. Burgers are made fresh and always taste great. 
Owner is friendly. Staff is helpful and always working hard.

Please do not go to external affairs for any type of injections!! They will try and tell you that they only offer things via the cannula method because it's safer, but don't mention they do this because you need very little experience to inject the filler and don't need to know how to shape and do the proper injection techniques! I had a horrible experience getting lip injections from a nurse that didn't know what she was doing and put me threw extreme amounts of pain and even poked the needle straight out of the inside of my lip. It was so painful even with the numbing cream to the point where I left tense, sick to my stomach and in a cold sweat! I got a full syringe of Restylane and paid higher then what most medical spa's are charging, because I thought I would be in good hands but instead I left with very poor results and traumatized.. I shortly after went to a completely different establishment looking for answers as to what went wrong with my experience at EA and to get the results I should have been given in the first place! After having a consult, and being examined it was confirmed the filler wasn't even put in the right parts of my lips witch was why the results were sooo little.. I had them re done with the same numbing cream and another syringe BUT via direct injection by a nurse who had the right amount of experience, and my results were perfect for what you'd expect after one syringe! Nothing dramatic but still noticeably fuller!! Finally what I wanted and most surprising to me, IT WAS TOTALLY MANAGEABLE PAIN and nothing even close to what I was put threw by external affairs.  I never wanted what they told me was " the dreaded duck lips" all I wanted was to get what I was paying for and to have it done right!! I was offered not one explanation or reason as to why this happened to me, instead I feel I got the typical customer service rant from someone who felt she was better then me! Please take my advice and don't become the next victim

We just ordered chicken chow mein, beef broccoli, chicken balls, green onion cakes and deep fried won tons. The chow mein was tasteless and the noodle crunchy. The chicken balls weren't fully cooked inside, the green onion cakes were dense and greasy. The beef in the beef and broccoli was rubbery. Basically the only thing we could eat were the wontons. We'll never order from here again.

The atmosphere was great. Really interesting people with a good vibe. Seating was comfy and staff customer service was awesome.

Nice mix of people of different ages 25-55.

Nice selection of baked goods. Will be back :)
This was our first time coming here and the service was very friendly. They have ice cream, gelato, and four selections of dairy-free sorbet. We had a lemon and orange sorbet. Both were delicious.

Whenever I come here, I don't even look at the menu board anymore. I'm on automatic pilot for the BBQ Crunch Burger. I order, get the food and then it gets into my stomach, in record time.

It's that good.

The BBQ Crunch burger has standard cheese with bacon, cheese, potato chips (inside) and orange soda BBQ sauce. The bun is soft and easy to bite into. I'm salivating just thinking about it. This is no ordinary burger.

The hand cut and triple fried fries are crispy and are the perfect side to complement a  burger. The icing on the cake is the malt aioli to dip the fries into. So yummy for the tummy!!

Bottom line: Come here for the most amazing burgers!

First impression of this place is cosy and homely. Loads of seating by fireplaces, corner sofas and nice cast iron details on the windows. I bet this place looks super cute at Christmas time. 

I didn't realize they don't have wifi which was inconvenient for me as I wanted to work while I was there. The service seemed a bit off too. I had to ask the servers too many questions including heir loyalty card which is answering a different question each day. When I went he question was about GOT so that's what sucked me in. No one offered any info... it seemed a bit odd.

I just wanted coffee and a breakfast scrambler. My coffee was sitting there for ages because they never shouted my name until the food was ready. The scrambler was good but it was meant to have chorizo in it and I didn't taste it at all, so I think they gave me the wrong one.
Three stars for good food, coffee and setting.
Amazing. Certainly one of best burgers I've had ever in the world! Fries are outstanding as well.

The burger Nazi lives here. Fantastic burgers, the best poutine in town and the rudest owners. I saw the guy reprimand a customer in front of the customers kids and my grandchildren. When I challenged the guy he made up a story about me pushing his mother!!! 

So, now I sneak in incognito and still enjoy the burgers. Go here, eat the burgers and watch out for the burger Nazi!
Great service at the cashier, stock inventory, and pharmacy. Be here at this location in the near future. Different products then Safeway at times, even though there the same company now.

The hubs and I went to External Affairs yesterday for the first time for a his and hers pedicure we won on their Facebook page for Valentine's Day.

We had the EA Signature Pedicure - includes exfoliating scrub, paraffin treatment and a complimentary polish to take home (regularly $75).

First off, the location is beautiful just off the Sturgeon River in the beautiful River House.  (12 Acres is also located in the same building which makes for a great combo for a lunch or dinner date #PatureToPlate).

External Affairs is located upstairs (I don't think there is an elevator) in the gorgeous River House.  I loved walking up the winding wooden staircase.  The staff greeted us an immediately offered us water, coffee, or tea and there was a variety of complimentary snacks and treats available while we waited for our appointment.

I really wish I had caught the name of the 2 young ladies that did the pedicures for my husband and I but they were a hoot!  The owner, Larry, even stopped by to say hi.

Everyone was so pleasant and full of vibrant energy everywhere you turned.

The pedicures were done in a beautiful turret (does that make sense? You know like a castle turret with windows all around the tower?) room overlooking the Sturgeon River.

The paraffin treatment was awesome!  I had never had that done on my feet before.  The hubs was still talking about how soft his feet were last night.

The Hubs even got his toes painted in alternating Oilers colours (blue/orange (well orangey/red).  It was an absolute hoot!  They have disposable thin foamy flip flops if you forgot to bring sandals (like we did!).

I would definitely recommend External Affairs for a couple's pedicure or a girlfriend date.  The atmosphere is perfect and it feels private as there are only two pedicure soaking stations (perfect for a duo date).

And I've heard great things from girlfriends about their other services and I don't doubt it for a second from our experience there yesterday!

Just alright for me. I know people rave about jack's but I am middle of the road for a recommendation... I wouldn't not, not recommend but it isn't where I head to first. Very cool choices/creative burger menu, but limited seating and that is a turn off for me. Service is just ok for me too.

I met with Kristen who right off the bat so friendly.  I was there to ask about some sun spots. She walked me through all my options.  I was really happy to not feel any pressure to leave with any purchases or products.  

She explained their line of moisturizers and more and told me how they would help me.  She even provided a couple samples of what products she mentioned. I have been using the vitamin C stuff and love it 

I will be back in the fall when I can get the procedure she and I discussed.  

The place is also clean and bright.  Ladies are so welcoming.  And they follow all covid protocols.

This place truly lives up to it's rating. The burgers were phenomenal! They have such a fun mix of flavours on the menu, a group of folks having to pick would surely be able to find at least one of the options to satisfy them. The fries and shakes were also on point. 

I wish the hours were consistently open vs a partial mid-day closure and closed Sunday's. Just had to reference the hours because we can never know when we are around town if they will be open or not.
Everyone raves about Red Brick Wall but I honestly think Saigon Cuisine is superior. They give you a decent amount of food and their peanut sauce and fish sauce are way better.
Awesome Burgers, fast service, get there before they close at 8pm or they run out of buns first
Went to the St.Albert Sobey's today for my COVID Vaccine at the Pharmacy and the Pharmacist was so kind and friendly.  I have always loved this Sobey's and today I love it even more!

I haven't had a good burger in a long time, Jack's changed that. I am thoroughly impressed. 

The best part about the burger was it didn't leave you with the gross feeling that all your arteries were clogging. It was very light, while still very flavourful. 
The fries were downright crispy deliciousness. 
As for the shakes, if I could've tried them all I would have! Because the Italian Stallion was so yummy. 

Price wise I found it relatively inexpensive. 2 burgers, 1 shake, and a side of fries came to $26. For an extra couple bucks it is well worth coming here instead of some fast food chain. And there service was very fast, I think we waited 5 minutes for our food. 

The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars was because there is something to be said about the ambiance of the place. The inside leaves a bit to be desired, I found it stuffy, and a little claustrophobic. Their patio is lovely if you can dine out there, but with winter approaching patio season is coming to a close. But that wouldn't stop me from coming to Jack's again, and it shouldn't stop you either. This place was exquisite. I certainly will be back.
I like the burgers. Bit pricey but good food. Good gluten free buns. Fries aren't included.
I love the shroom burger. Lots of delicious mushrooms. It's  always a treat eating here.

At this location their debit machine has been broken for a week and does not accept tap. 

The worker was pretty flippant in telling me that their machine was unable to take tap. I asked politely if there was any way to use another machine and he said yes "but I don't want to go back there to it."

Given everything going on with cleanliness, and this workers rude approach, I left the location. 

Hopefully they can remedy the machine and help their teams approach. I can be empathetic that some people were likely less kind than I was but it was still sadly a poor experience.

5 COVID free stars!
Jack's is doing call-in/walk-in business with temporary hours, so please check the website before going. 
There's no dine-in or washrooms available, but I'm NOT complaining and you shouldn't either. 

We walked-in, and our order was taken quickly and efficiently. We waited outside and sat on that big metal hinge while we waited. Jacks staff brought everyone's order out to them which was great. 

I got the shroom burger, hubby had the BBQ crunch burger. We both loved them. The patties are thinner with a nicely grilled exterior, which reaches the edges of the enormous, pillowy, fresh & delicious bun. I had a generous pile of thinly sliced & grilled mushrooms on top for a big umami punch. Fresh ingredients, and FAST & friendly service make this place a stand out. 

Jack's is really good value, as opposed to other "specialty burger" places in Edmonton. 

We'll defiantly be back, and try some sides with our burgers. 

Ps. I wish there were tables outside to sit at. I'm sure they would have some if they could. Oh well.

Fuego! Top burger joint in the city of stalbert for sure and even Edmonton and area , I usually get the hang over but the shroom is nice if you're not wanting to be stuffed after leaving , very filling burgers.
Best burger joint in Edmonton (and St. Albert). Inferno burger is amazing and the fries and sauce are really great too.

Fountain Park Pool for a birthday swim with Covid-19 restrictions was well outlined to everyone who arrived from the lifeguard. Wear your bathing clothes under your walk in clothes, take those off put them in a bag on a trolley. 

And the lifeguards will bring them to you after your swim time, no showers. Leave the pool facilities after you have changed back into your clothes you came in, over your bathing clothes.
You won't find a better burger around. Hangover style it for sure. And the milkshakes are perfect.

This place is near my home, so my family has been patronizing this location for years.

We've finally given up on them!! The problems have gotten pretty bad. Last week they double charged our debit card.  The girl who did the transaction knew something messed up and she claimed she canceled the first transaction, but she didn't. We had to make an extra trip back with the bank records and our receipt to have a manager correct it.

Coffee through the drive through has been bad on many occasions. It is so weak it taste like hot water, not coffee. One time I took it in and the manager said they must have 'forgot' to put new coffee in when brewing (using old grounds instead) and the coffee he got out of the urn used for inside service was ok. The weak coffee has been given to me so many times through the drive through that it couldn't be an accident - I think they are too cheap to brew real coffee for the drive through, knowing everyone will be long gone before they taste it.

Oh - and I can't tell you how many times we've not gotten sausage in our hotcakes and sausage. Just hotcakes.

There is another McDonalds just north on St. Albert trail a couple of kilometres that doesn't have these problems.

Horrible horrible! I waited a while for their spring rolls which came out burnt. The lemon chicken was so over cooked it was unedible and the lemon sauce was so runny it didnt coat the chicken at all. The beef was as well overcooked and very chewy. The only thing not over cooked was the rice which was actually crunchy from being UNDER cooked!
I know it's technically fast food Chinese but they should take SOME pride in what they send out. Especially when you spend over $60 and not find out the food sucks till you get home where there is nothing that can be done about it.

This place is cute! I've driven past it so many times living in Edmonton but never actually gone inside. Today my Aunt suggested it so we decided to go. 

They have a lot of food and pastries, and of course coffee. I decided to try the roast beef sandwhich and the chai latte. Both were actually way better than I was expecting! My aunt had a toasted egg on an english muffin and she said it was really good. It is nice that they have a good selection of vegetarian options, which is good because my Aunt is a vegetarian. 

They also have a cute little patio that overlooks 99th. It was so nice today so we decided to sit outside. We had so much fun! I won't overlook this place anymore as a place to go and hang out. I was pleasantly surprised. :)

Innovative burger joint in a the heart of St. Albert's arts district. I enjoyed the peanut butter-topped burger I had and the shake was serviceable. If your in the area, it is a nice place to stop for a causal meal. However, I don't know if I would go out of my way to stop in again.

I've been coming here 3 years now for the medical Botox for migraines program.  I've suffered from migraines for almost 20 years and been on so many, many prescription medications. 

Originally I saw Dr. Briggs here (who was always fabulous) but he's moved to Ottawa with the military (thank you for your service).

I've seen a nurse and another doc that recently came into the practice in the past year and have continued to receive excellent care and treatment. 

The environment is always impeccably clean and the staff welcoming.  

They now are offering regular family health care here as well as female specialized.  So if you're looking for a new GP, you may want to consider checking them out. 

The Botox for migraines program has been life changing.  It took three visits over 9 months for my migraines to stop and I'm so very glad I didn't stop after the second visit.  Since starting this program, I have gone from missing 1-3 days of work, life, and fun a month to having only 1 or 2 minor migraines a year!  Seriously - like I used to get so bad I would have to see a neurologist and go into the ER for IV treatment to stop the throw up cycle :-(

I still keep prescription migraine melts on hand for emergencies but I could probably survive now with just Advil and ibuprophen.

Seriously, if you suffer from migraines, PLEASE inquire if this program is right for you.  

See you again in 3 months, External Affairs.

PS Love the email and text reminders for appointments especially as mine are 3 months apart.

I've been here a few times when I happen to be in the St. Albert area looking for fast food off the beaten path and I am a repeat customer whenever I catch their food truck at the hospitals. It's about time I share my thoughts on Jack's burger shack! 
Obviously I love the burgers! I've tried the shroom, bronto, PB & J, BBQ crunch. Honestly, I couldn't pick a favourite, they are all delicious but very distinct in flavour from each other. I appreciate that their beef patties are from a popular local butcher and I really like the texture of their bun...it makes the burger look massive upon presentation, but squishes down nicely so I can actually get a decent bite. Service at this location is consistently quick and friendly, I typically get my order in about 5 minutes after ordering. It's a small space, so I typically order to go, but that being said, if you choose to sit down & can't finish, they can also wrap the leftover to go too! 
I recently ordered one of their shakes and it was like drinking a frozen bowl of cereal! Yum! But, it's a lot to consume in 1 visit if you are also eating a burger. I'll maybe pass on the drink and just have a tumbler of water that they have available near the till unless I have someone to share with. They also have some beer & soda options to wash down that burger if that's more your style. I'm also happy they have a kids menu! It gives my munchkins some options when they are in tow!

This is a tiny little shop with amazing food! We take out of town guests here often for great food and a tour of the little downtown area. I love the vegetarian burger option (called the brontosaurus burger). Milkshakes have all been tasty. Even the burger buns are amazing. Absolutely recommend this restaurant to everyone!

I went to External Affairs and what wonderful staff there.They were very kind and quick to greet me. Joanne was great at explaining the Juvederm and helping me choose the right one for me. I would deffinatley recommend External Affairs.

Such amazing staff, incredible owners and such a forward thinking, knowledgeable place. I go between the St albert and Edmonton location and they are both absolutely incredible. I won't go anywhere else other than external affairs for any of my services!

Awesome, awesome, awesome.
My girlfriend took me here when I was starving and ready to just hit a drive-thru. I like burgers but I don't go nuts for them, it's just a burger after all.
Well not this burger!  This burger is DELICIOUS. 
I super appreciate the thin patties. Every burger you get these days tries to be a monster and that doesn't appeal to me.  I had the standard burger and it equates to just a straight up tasty burg.  Also had the fresh cut fries with gravy and in house aioli, yum all around.
It's currently only takeout which is A-OK by me. The takeout is as fast and priced comparably to any fast food joint.

Been going here for more than ten years. Friendly, affordable and tasty. Driving by would not grab your eye, in fact a neighbour took me there the first time... not some place I would have tried on my own (hole in the wall-ish). It is always busy and I have always been satisfied.

So in case you were wondering Jack's now has a food truck and they just so happened to be parked outside my work place today. 

I've been to the downtown shop a few times now and the food truck is on par both for service and taste. Jacks burgers are somehow always cooked to perfection. Crispy on the outside and tender and juicy everywhere else. The crispy outside gives that deep grilled flavour you crave when eating a burger. At least that's how I like it. 

Today I had the mushroom and Boursin cheese burger. This burger packs a big punch of flavour. Honestly I don't think at this point I'd order anything else. But be warned it is a bit on the messy side. Also can't forget to mention the amazing brioche style bun that all these delicious ingredients are pulled between. It's oh so soft and light. 

Mmm. I kind of want another already.

So last year I would have said, definitely go to this place (4 stars)... This year, methinks not. 

Last year I ordered a Red Velvet cake for my wife's birthday.  Ordering process was a bit wacky, but ok, they are a small shop, they don't have their process for getting orders quite right.  However the cake was fabulous.  Very moist great flavour.  Icing was done perfectly.  So willing to overlook wacky ordering process.

This year, From the start, it was all messed up.  Phoned to order cake hoping that they would replicate last year's success.  Apparently I called when the bakers weren't there and the Front Service staff weren't allowed to take cake orders due to screw-ups in the past (maybe I should have paid attention to the foreshadowing here).  Was also told that I wouldn't be able to leave voice mail so, after I got off the phone,  I had to place order online.  The next day, I heard nothing, so I had to call the following day.  The baker says, "ya we got your order" and then proceeds to ask a number of questions that were not on the website order form, including requesting full payment.  Well, if you got my order, could you have at least acknowledged that ?  apparently they don't do that.  And oh by the way, I'm not totally cool with paying for something in advance when I don't get any assurance of quality.. anyway... (in retrospect, this is the point I should have run the other way) 

I picked up the cake, and they let you inspect it prior to taking it away, I would say paying for it, but I already did that.

I get home and the icing is so thick that it's already slid off the side !  Seriously... that's disappointing !  Oh well, I guess I'm forced to overlook that.

I present this to my wife, she cuts into it and....

It's Fuchsia !  WTF !

I've never seen a Red Velvet cake that is Fuchsia in colour before.  
Trying to be objective, about the colour, I try it.  Ok, it's moist, but it's flavourless.  The cake is definitely missing something.  I'm not sure what, but this is an effort where if I made this, that would be somewhat acceptable.  However coming from a professional baker.  Wow, all I can say is, "that's really disappointing ! "  My wife concurs, and voices her disappointment as well.   

After paying over $30 for a small cake.  Really ? is this as good as it gets.  

Wild Earth, I just hope your other products are better than your cake.

Thanks but no thanks !  I think I try to make this on my own next year.... 
See ya, because I'm not coming back.

When searching for bakeries to try this hidden gem showed up on Google Mapa. Located literally hidden in the garden centre it was a little hard to find but I did get to take a very cool flat escalator. I forgot how many cool nich-nacks were in this store so walking through it to find a bakery was a blast. A large variety of goodies with clearly marked flavors and prices was nice to see. I ended up with a mint choc chip meringue and a caramel square. The meringue was large and impressive looking. Definitely a looker but I wish the flavor was stronger and that there were Choc chips throughout and not just on-top. It was melting your mouth as expected. The caramel square was Amazing. Soft definitely homemade caramel on-top a soft cookie crust. The proportion of cookie to caramel was spot on. I would definitely buy the Carmel on its own if that becomes an option! 
Definitely a great spot to kill some time or look for unique trinkets and grab a tasty snack.

If you are used to the food at the original Lingnan you will be very disappointed.  We have enjoyed Lingnan for years and ordered from Lingnan Express as it is much closer for us. The food was lacking in flavor, the pineapple sauce was very thin and tasted watered down. The chicken balls had chunks of fat and we're very greasy. The spring rolls were dripping with grease but the flavor was ok. The fried rice was completely lacking in flavor as well. The green onion cakes were fairly tasty and the dry spicy chicken was close to as good as the original.  The schezwan beef was not good, no flavor or spice at all.

This meal was not quite as good as a food court Chinese food meal but the price is the same as at the original Lingnan.  Save your money and order elsewhere as this was a huge disappointment.  We will not be back!

Wild Earth Bakery and Cafe on 99St is an awesome little bakery and coffee shop.  They have some great seating inside and during the warmer months some outside spots as well.

I have tried many of the muffins, croissants, bread and non-coffee drinks (sorry can't comment on the coffee as I don't drink it) and have always been impressed with their products.

You can buy fresh loaves of bread here and they have always been fantastic!  They also have vegetarian and gluten free options if you need that.  At the front till they usually have a basket of dogs treats as well that you can pick up for your furry friends.

If you are on 99 St. and want to stop for littler food or coffee break this is a great choice!
